Its per-tab scope is keyed by `window.name`, so it *survives* F5 (same tab, same name) and its destroy listener fires only on a *real* close — the library already solved the F5-vs-close discrimination a hand-built UI-detach detector would have to. `vaadinx.swing.app.SwingBridgeEmulatorsBootstrap` (a `VaadinServiceInitListener`) calls `TabScope.setup` and hooks `addDestroyListener` → `AppTab.onTabClosed` → `session.close()`. **The app registers it, never the library** ([R_no_spi_selfregister](../CLAUDE.md)): a library-SPI `VaadinServiceInitListener` conflicts with Spring's bean discovery, so `:emulators` ships the class and the app wires it (Sampler's SPI file; a Spring app as a `@Bean`). `SwingBridgeEmulatorsBootstrap` is the *single* mandatory init listener — it also wires `BrowserTimeZone.fetch()` per UI-init (SD_browser_timezone), so one SPI line covers both. **Active-tab guard via the [AppTab](#) identity:** `MainWindowRoute` binds the app to its browser tab (`AppTab.markAppUI`, which records the current `TabScope`) on first load and every F5 rebind; the destroy listener closes the session only if the destroyed scope *is* that app tab (`AppTab.ownsTab`) — so a *curtained* (non-app) tab's close leaves the app alive in the active tab. **Wired unconditionally, browser or not.** The leg once skipped under Karibu's `MockService`, behind a `SwingBridgeEmulatorsBootstrap.activateUnderMockForTesting` opt-in, on the premise that the handshake needs a real browser. That premise was wrong: Karibu fakes `ExtendedClientDetails`, so `TabScope.init`'s callback fires and a scope is created browserlessly. Both the skip and the seam are gone (2026-08-25) — `:emulators` is 1795/1795 green either way on tab-scope 0.3, and `JFrameTabCloseTest` now drives `MockBrowser` with no opt-in. Two failures surfaced while measuring, neither a design objection: upstream [vaadin-tab-scope#5](https://github.com/mvysny/vaadin-tab-scope/issues/5) (fixed in 0.3) and a `ToolkitTest` fixture that inherited its no-browser-details premise instead of asserting it (since fixed). Removal was *required* rather than merely tidy: [M1D_former_singletons](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_former_singletons)'s tab-scoped holder must resolve under Karibu too, so a test with no scope could not reach it.
2. **`WINDOW_CLOSING` fires from the `VaadinService` session-destroy listener alone.** session-destroy is **F5-safe by construction** (the session is preserved across a refresh — the same property D_session_scoped_pools/D_active_ui_pointer rely on) and fires **exactly once**, so it is the single authoritative dispatch site. The `@MainWindow` (InlineStrategy) frame registers itself as the session's main window at ctor (a session attribute — `getWindows()` can't find it at destroy since it walks the now-gone live UI tree); a once-per-session `addSessionDestroyListener` (mirroring D_callswing_loom/D_session_scoped_pools's `forSession` wiring) then runs the existing `JFrame.processWindowEvent` → close-op dispatch synchronously (Vaadin wraps the destroy listener in `session.access`, so `VaadinSession.getCurrent()` is set for the throw-seams). Session-scoped machinery (D_callswing_loom executor, D_session_scoped_pools pools) is disposed by its own destroy listeners. Because there is one call site firing once, **no dedup flag is needed.** **Dispatch dedup with the programmatic-close path is by visibility:** a `dispose()` (e.g. `EXIT_ON_CLOSE` Quit menu → `session.close()`) already ran `WINDOW_CLOSED` and dropped visibility, so the dispatch fires `WINDOW_CLOSING` only when the main window is *still visible* — the display-yanked kill — and skips it when the app already tore itself down (out-of-order/redundant otherwise). A buggy `WINDOW_CLOSING` listener is caught and routed to the session `ErrorHandler` so teardown continues (D_close_operation_dispatch).

   **Trap for anything that later reads the main-window pointer:** `dispatchShutdownClosing` nulls the `MAIN_WINDOW_KEY` session attribute *before* firing `WINDOW_CLOSING`, so an accessor built on that attribute answers empty exactly during the app's own cleanup handler — the one place migrated code is most likely to call it. Harmless today because nothing reads it (the window registries read [D_window_registry](#D_window_registry)'s registry, `getFocusedWindow()` walks the emulator chain), and it is why both of those deliberately do not. Re-check this ordering before basing any new accessor on that pointer.

**The shutdown throw.** Every browser-round-trip await in the codebase funnels through one seam: `Dialog.parkUntilClose()` → `EHelper.awaitModal(peer, future)` → `UIFibers.parkAndAwait` (all blocking dialogs — `JOptionPane.show*`, modal `JDialog.setVisible(true)`/`show()`, `JColorChooser.showDialog`, `JFileChooser`, AWT `FileDialog`, modal `JInternalFrame`). At shutdown `WINDOW_CLOSING` runs off-VT (no live UI to `callSwing`/`ui.access` into), so `parkUntilClose`'s existing UI-fiber check (`UIFibers.checkInUIFiber()`) *already* throws — the hang is prevented today. What D_shutdown_lifecycle adds is a session-level `shuttingDown` flag (set before dispatch) checked *ahead of* that guard to swap the generic "must be on a UI virtual thread" message for an actionable one ("Application is shutting down — modal dialogs and browser round-trips are unavailable inside `WINDOW_CLOSING` listeners; do server-side cleanup only"). The server-side-await primitives that don't hang but block on a torn-down resource — `SwingWorker.get()`, `SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait()` — also read `shuttingDown` and throw a shutdown-named message (cheap; priceless when reading shutdown logs) rather than their cryptic "no current UI" fallback.

**Rejected alternatives.**
- *Hook `beforeunload` directly.* Rejected — unreliable (dropped beacons), its dialog is browser-controlled and uncustomizable, and it fires on F5. Nothing it offers survives the reframe.
- *Fire `WINDOW_CLOSING` directly from `beforeunload`/UI-detach, dedup against session-destroy with a flag.* Rejected — it fires on F5 (a refresh detaches the old UI identically to a close), so it would need its own F5 filter *in front of irreversible listener side effects*; a `WINDOW_CLOSING` fired-then-retracted-after-F5 has already run its saves/audits. Routing through `session.close()` puts the F5 filter in front of the *close*, not the side effects, and collapses to one dispatch site.
- *Hand-build the detector (UI-detach + grace timer + D_active_ui_pointer-pointer reconnect check).* Viable, but `vaadin-tab-scope` does exactly this, is F5-safe, and doubles as the per-tab scope primitive the multi-tab option-3 path will want ([multi-tab-and-session-scoping.md](../ideas/multi-tab-and-session-scoping.md)). Adopting the library is less code and de-risks a future direction.
- *Narrow session-close to `EXIT_ON_CLOSE` (keep D_close_operation_dispatch's per-close-op tab-close row).* Rejected — the tab *is* the app's only display and one-app-per-session means no other window keeps it alive, so a tab close is always a kill; `DO_NOTHING_ON_CLOSE` can't "do nothing" when the tab is gone, `HIDE_ON_CLOSE` has nothing to hide. Always-closing the session also makes the new-tab story clean (fresh session → fresh `bootstrap()`) and sidesteps the option-2 singleton-desync trap that re-`bootstrap()` into a surviving session would hit. The close-op distinction survives on the *programmatic* `dispose()` path (D_close_operation_dispatch), not the display-yanked path.
- *Drop `@PreserveOnRefresh` and hand-teleport the Swing peer tree to the fresh F5 UI ourselves* (to make prompt last-tab shutdown fall out for free — without the annotation Flow eagerly closes the old UI on the unload beacon, so a real close orphans promptly with no beacon-capture handler needed). Rejected — it moves Flow's most delicate internal operation into our code: the guarded cross-`StateTree` `StateNode` move (reproduce `removeFromTree(false)`'s id-reset/marker step or `doSetTree` throws "can't move a node from one state tree to another") *including UI-level overlay transfer* — `SWindow`/dialog/notification peers are UI children moved by Flow's *separate* `moveElementsFrom` path, not route-subtree children, so a naive route-root teleport strands every open dialog and breaks parked-VT `Registration`s — on the exact seam Flow itself is buggiest on (flow #8286/#14609/#18390), with risk concentrated on precisely our `Dialog`-backed and Quill/Grid peers. High work, high risk, for a latency-only soft-requirement payoff, and it *still* doesn't make the last tab prompt on its own (the tab-scope reap needs a further init/detach regardless). Flow exposes **no supported public API** for cross-UI tree transfer — `@PreserveOnRefresh` is the only one ([vaadin/flow#25019](https://github.com/vaadin/flow/issues/25019); #5316 was a 2019 spike closed without an API) — so tab-scope#3 handles the preserve case directly instead (beacon starts the grace clock *without* closing the UI, letting Flow still re-adopt the tree on a real F5).

**Accepted limitations.**
- *Best-effort delivery.* `WINDOW_CLOSING` runs on an explicit `session.close()` (tab-scope teardown hook or in-app logout) and on a normal session teardown. The `vaadin-tab-scope` README pins the residual gap to a **JVM crash / `kill -9`, or a session deserialized-but-never-used before it expires** — cases where no session-destroy fires at all, so cleanup simply doesn't run. That is exactly the task-manager-kill case of the reframe; no framework can change it, and the migrator's `WindowListener` was never a durability guarantee. (Whether *our* Vaadin Boot setup fires session-destroy on a plain idle timeout is still worth confirming — [mvysny/vaadin-boot#39](https://github.com/mvysny/vaadin-boot/issues/39).)
- *`window.name` fragility — probed, non-issue on current browsers.* Tab-scope survival rests on the browser preserving `window.name` across a same-tab reload; a dropped name would read as a spurious close. The one historical offender was **Safari ≤18.3.1**, which dropped it on an address-bar / bookmark reload with Web Inspector closed. Confirmed cleared: the full 17-scenario matrix passes on current Chrome (Chromium 150), Firefox 152, and **Safari 26.5.2** — the name survives every reload/navigation path, and only genuinely-new-tab actions (duplicate, reopen, quit/crash-restore) get a fresh scope, which is exactly the behavior a close *should* produce. Chrome never dropped it. Matrix + per-scenario results in vaadin-tab-scope's `WINDOW-NAME-BROWSER-TESTS.md`; tracked upstream — [mvysny/vaadin-tab-scope#2](https://github.com/mvysny/vaadin-tab-scope/issues/2).
- *Transient false-curtain window.* Between a real tab-close and the grace-delayed `session.close()`, the session is briefly alive with the D_active_ui_pointer pointer aimed at the dead UI, so a new tab opened *inside that window* is falsely curtained (multi-tab limitation #2). Deferred to the multi-tab design pass — it's the curtain's own recovery story, not the shutdown path's.
- *Prompt-shutdown latency — single last tab.* **Precise claim:** the `WINDOW_CLOSING` *dispatch* (the migrator's cleanup hook) is prompt — it arrives within tab-scope's ~60 s reaper grace — for the fraction of closes the browser's unload beacon reports (~85–91 %; the rest fall to the session idle-timeout backstop, which always delivers, so correctness is unaffected). The underlying `VaadinSession`/HTTP teardown is **not** made prompt (still reclaimed at the container timeout); that's acceptable since `WINDOW_CLOSING` is best-effort and its job is to run the migrator's server-side cleanup, not to free the session object. Browser-confirmed 2026-07-22 (see Validation). Four pieces, all in place (upstream FR [mvysny/vaadin-tab-scope#3](https://github.com/mvysny/vaadin-tab-scope/issues/3), resolved; `:emulators` on tab-scope 0.2):
  1. tab-scope 0.2's **~60 s reaper thread** fires the orphan reap without needing another tab's activity (the "scheduled reap");
  2. since under `@PreserveOnRefresh` Flow ignores the unload beacon so the D_shutdown_lifecycle app UI (`MainWindowRoute`) never orphans on its own, the app installs tab-scope's **opt-in tab-close beacon handler** (`TabScope.installTabCloseBeacon`, wired in Sampler's `SamplerServlet`): it captures the beacon to start the orphan grace clock *without* closing the UI, so an F5 still re-adopts the same `window.name` and cancels the reap while a real close lets it fire;
  3. **`WINDOW_CLOSING` is dispatched directly from the tab-scope destroy listener**, not via `VaadinSession`-destroy — `AppTab.onTabClosed` calls `JFrame.dispatchShutdownFromTabClose(session)` before `session.close()`. Necessary because the reaper thread is request-less: `session.close()` there only sets state `CLOSING`, and `fireSessionDestroy` (hence the session-destroy backstop dispatch) runs only at `requestEnd`, so relying on it would defer `WINDOW_CLOSING` to the container timeout. The visibility/`shuttingDown` dedup keeps the eventual real session-destroy a no-op;
  4. firing `WINDOW_CLOSING` hides the frame → detaches the peer tree → each `Component`'s detach listener funnels `removeNotify` through `EHelper.callSwing`, which has no current UI on the reaper thread. Per the **R_callswing_envelope shutdown carve-out**, `callSwing` runs those inline when `isShuttingDown()` (the tab is gone; nothing to push to) instead of throwing — otherwise a real close dumped one `IllegalStateException` per detached component.
  
  Multi-tab was already prompt — a surviving/opening tab's activity drives the reap (confirmed in the 2026-07-21 run). The reliable *close-cleanup* path (distinct from promptness — the confirm-dialog problem below) stays a **migration transform**: port the main window's `WINDOW_CLOSING` handler to a dialog-free session-destroy hook ([M1D_mainwindow_split](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_mainwindow_split)), since a real close has no UI to host a confirm dialog anyway (a modal park on the shutdown path already throws the actionable "shutting down" `IllegalStateException`, `Dialog.parkUntilClose`).

**Validation.** Karibu (`JFrameShutdownTest`): dispatch fires `WINDOW_CLOSING` on a visible registered `@MainWindow` frame and marks `shuttingDown`; the visibility-dedup skips it after a self-`dispose()`; a no-registered-window session is a no-op; a throwing listener routes to the `ErrorHandler`; real session-destroy (teardown-driven) invokes the registered dispatch; an F5 detach/re-attach does *not* fire it; the prompt tab-close dispatch (`dispatchShutdownFromTabClose`) fires `WINDOW_CLOSING` once and dedups the session-destroy backstop; the R_callswing_envelope shutdown carve-out runs `callSwing` inline with no current UI while `shuttingDown` (and still throws when not); and the three `shuttingDown` throws (modal park, `SwingWorker.get()`, `invokeAndWait`) each carry the shutdown message. The `vaadin-tab-scope` tab-close detector leg (`SwingBridgeEmulatorsBootstrap` → `AppTab.onTabClosed` → `session.close()`, guarded to the app tab) is browser-only, **inert under Karibu by default** but driven in `JFrameTabCloseTest` via `MockBrowser` (the trick vaadin-tab-scope tests itself with — `newTab`/`closeTab(beaconLost)`/`reapInactiveUIs` + a shrunk `CLEANUP_DURATION_MS`): app-tab close → session closes, curtained-tab close → session stays open, F5 → session stays open. **Real-browser confirmation done** (Playwright/Chromium, 2026-07-21): F5 preserves `window.name` (no spurious `WINDOW_CLOSING`), the second tab renders the D_active_ui_pointer curtain over a shared session, and closing the app tab drives the full chain to a real `WINDOW_CLOSING` — the dead app UI closes only once a *second* tab's heartbeats reach `VaadinService.closeInactiveUIs` (`heartbeat×3.1`), and the orphaned tab-scope is reaped only by a *further* tab init/detach, so the browser recipe needed two live tabs plus a reap-driving third-tab init. **A second real-browser run (Playwright/Chromium, 2026-07-22) confirmed the single-last-tab path end-to-end** on tab-scope 0.2 + the `SamplerServlet` beacon handler + the direct-dispatch fix: closing the sole tab captured the beacon (grace clock started without closing the UI), the reaper reaped the orphan at exactly 60 s, `AppTab.onTabClosed` fired `WINDOW_CLOSING` ~1 ms later, and the peer-tree detach (73 `removeNotify` callbacks) ran inline via the R_callswing_envelope carve-out with **zero** `callSwing`/`ErrorHandler` errors. **Safari `window.name` probed and cleared** (2026-07-22, Safari 26.5.2 / macOS Tahoe, Web Inspector closed — the exact config that dropped the name on 18.3.1): the full 17-scenario matrix passes, `window.name` survives address-bar and bookmark reload, so no spurious `WINDOW_CLOSING` on Safari either (see the `window.name` fragility limitation above and vaadin-tab-scope's `WINDOW-NAME-BROWSER-TESTS.md`). One residual stays un-probed in a real browser, low-value: the curtained-tab-close-leaves-app-alive non-event (already Karibu-covered — `JFrameTabCloseTest`). No standing real-browser harness.

---

<a id="D_jscrollpane"></a>
## D_jscrollpane. JScrollPane emulator — thin shell over `SJScrollPane`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, JViewport + JScrollBar as shadow JDK components, scrollbar-policy mapping, MainWindowRoute route-sizing model

**Decision.** Surfaced by the CRUD-testbed walkthrough. `vaadinx.swing.JScrollPane` lands as a thin delegating shell over the [SD_sjscrollpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjscrollpane) `SJScrollPane` surrogate. The slice spans **the emulator thin shell with R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down** (D_jscrollpane_thin_shell), **the scrollbar-policy ↔ ScrollDirection mapping table with auto-scroll-content guard** (D_scrollbar_policy_mapping), **`JViewport` + `JScrollBar` as emulator-only shadow JDK components** (D_viewport_scrollbar_shadows). The MainWindowRoute route-sizing model lands alongside as [D_inline_route_sizing](#D_jframe_as_route) (under D_jframe_as_route's existing scope, since it's a JFrame-sizing concern that's a pre-flight for JScrollPane consumers).

<a id="D_jscrollpane_thin_shell"></a>**D_jscrollpane_thin_shell — Emulator thin shell + R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `vaadinx.swing.JScrollPane extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent`. R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down: `javax.swing.JScrollPane` is a leaf in the public `javax.swing.*` hierarchy, so the protected `(Component peer)` ctor is omitted and all public ctors funnel through a private `(SJScrollPane peer)` ctor that hard-codes the surrogate. Public ctors mirror JDK: `JScrollPane()`, `JScrollPane(Component view)`, `JScrollPane(int vsbPolicy, int hsbPolicy)`, `JScrollPane(Component view, int vsbPolicy, int hsbPolicy)`. Same shape JComboBox / JCheckBox / JMenuBar / JTable / JOptionPane take per [D_menu_tree](#D_menu_tree) / [D_jtable](#D_jtable).

The full JDK constants surface (`VERTICAL_SCROLLBAR_AS_NEEDED = 20`, `VERTICAL_SCROLLBAR_NEVER = 21`, `VERTICAL_SCROLLBAR_ALWAYS = 22`, `HORIZONTAL_SCROLLBAR_AS_NEEDED = 30`, `HORIZONTAL_SCROLLBAR_NEVER = 31`, `HORIZONTAL_SCROLLBAR_ALWAYS = 32`) ports as `public static final int` constants verbatim — mechanical port, integer values match JDK exactly so `KeyStroke.getKeyStroke(int)`-shape APIs round-trip.

<a id="D_scrollbar_policy_mapping"></a>**D_scrollbar_policy_mapping — Scrollbar-policy mapping table; ALWAYS WARNs as R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a).** The emulator field-shadows the H/V policy ints (always — JDK round-trip, R_swing_is_truth store-then-drive). After every `setViewportView` / `setVerticalScrollBarPolicy` / `setHorizontalScrollBarPolicy` mutation, the emulator pushes the translated `ScrollDirection` to the surrogate via `pushPolicyToSurrogate()`, **except** when the current viewport content is auto-scrolling (Grid / TextArea / Scroller) — the surrogate's setContent override has already forced `NONE` per SD_sjscrollpane's auto-scroll guard, and the emulator's push would either re-confirm NONE or contradict it; the emulator skips the push so the field-shadowed JDK ints round-trip without driving a contradictory direction. Mapping cross-product:

| H \ V | `NEVER` (21) | `AS_NEEDED` (20, default) | `ALWAYS` (22) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `NEVER` (31) | `NONE` | `VERTICAL` | `VERTICAL` + WARN |
| `AS_NEEDED` (30, default) | `HORIZONTAL` | `BOTH` | `BOTH` + WARN |
| `ALWAYS` (32) | `HORIZONTAL` + WARN | `BOTH` + WARN | `BOTH` + WARN |

`ALWAYS` policy is R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a) — *blocked-upstream-shape*. Vaadin Scroller has no "always-show scrollbar" affordance per its `@Tag("vaadin-scroller")` web component; treating ALWAYS as AS_NEEDED is the closest Vaadin can render. Each ALWAYS push fires `EHelper.onUnimplemented("JScrollPane", "setVerticalScrollBarPolicy.ALWAYS", ...)` so migration logs surface the gap. Default policy ints are AS_NEEDED for both axes (JDK contract); fresh `new JScrollPane()` lands `BOTH` on the surrogate (Scroller's own default).

<a id="D_viewport_scrollbar_shadows"></a>**D_viewport_scrollbar_shadows — JViewport + JScrollBar as emulator-only shadow JDK components.** Two shadow ports under `vaadinx.swing.*`, no surrogate counterparts (per the [SD_no_sjoptionpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_no_sjoptionpane) precedent — first SD_no_sjoptionpane-shape carve-out was JOptionPane; this is the second). The "shadow JDK component" pattern: emulator-side full state-model bookkeeping with no DOM rendering, so user code that introspects via the JDK API gets a non-null object that round-trips its own state without NPE.

- **`vaadinx.swing.JViewport extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent`** — one-method facade over `Scroller.getContent()`. Eagerly constructed by the `JScrollPane` ctor and added to `JScrollPane`'s `Container.components` via `Container.addSlotChild` (see "Sub-decision D_shadow_children_tree_shape" below). Surface: `getView()` returns the emulator-side `vaadinx.awt.Component` whose peer is currently `Scroller.getContent()` (resolved via `EHelper.getEmulator(peer)`); `setView(Component)` delegates to the owner's `setViewportView(Component)`. Round-trip-only fields (`extentSize` / `viewPosition` / `viewSize` / `addChangeListener` / `scrollRectToVisible`) field-shadow but never drive the peer — Vaadin Scroller doesn't fire server-side scroll events without a custom DOM listener stack (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a) until a migration target asks). User code reads back what it set; visible behaviour is "no scroll-position events fire" (documented).
- **`vaadinx.swing.JScrollBar extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent implements Adjustable`** — full state-model bookkeeping for `BoundedRangeModel` (`getValue` / `setValue` / `getMinimum` / `setMinimum` / `getMaximum` / `setMaximum` / `getExtent` / `setExtent` / `getValueIsAdjusting` / `setValueIsAdjusting`), plus `setUnitIncrement` / `setBlockIncrement`, plus `addAdjustmentListener` / `removeAdjustmentListener` storing in a JDK `EventListenerList`. Listeners never fire (no Vaadin source for scroll position events; documented). `getOrientation()` returns the JDK int (HORIZONTAL=0, VERTICAL=1) set at construction. Eagerly constructed by the `JScrollPane` ctor (one per axis) and added to `JScrollPane`'s `Container.components` via `Container.addSlotChild`.
- **No DOM rendering for either.** JViewport's peer is an inert `Div` (constructed in its protected `JComponent(Component)` ctor); JScrollBar's peer is also an inert `Div`. The visual scrollbar (when ScrollDirection allows) is rendered by Vaadin Scroller's web component — the JDK `JScrollBar` instances don't reach the DOM. Migrators that do `scrollPane.getVerticalScrollBar().setUnitIncrement(16)` no longer NPE; the value round-trips through the shadow component without affecting the rendered scroll behaviour.

<a id="D_shadow_children_tree_shape"></a>**D_shadow_children_tree_shape — Shadow children populate `Container.components` for R_swing_is_truth tree-shape fidelity.** The shadow `JViewport` + two `JScrollBar`s are constructed eagerly in the `JScrollPane` ctor and added to `Container.components` via a new `Container.addSlotChild(Component, int)` seam, so `JScrollPane.getComponentCount()` returns 3 (matching JDK) and `getComponent(i)` resolves to viewport / verticalScrollBar / horizontalScrollBar in JDK order. The viewport view lives one level deeper — `setViewportView` attaches it as a child of the shadow `JViewport` via a package-private `JViewport.attachView` helper, mirroring JDK's `JScrollPane → JViewport → view` chain. `addSlotChild` and its sibling `removeSlotChild` populate `components` + reparent + fire `COMPONENT_ADDED` / `HIERARCHY_CHANGED` without touching the peer DOM and without notifying the layout manager — slot-based containers manage child DOM via their peer's own slot setters (Vaadin `Scroller.setContent`, `SplitLayout.setPrimary/setSecondary`), so the AWT-side bookkeeping and the Vaadin-side DOM stay on separate edges per R_swing_is_truth's "two parent edges, both maintained" model. `setViewport` / `setHorizontalScrollBar` / `setVerticalScrollBar` swaps detach the old shadow and re-insert the replacement at the JDK-faithful index; the view migrates across viewport replacement to stay parented under whichever JViewport is currently bound.

D_shadow_children_tree_shape corrects the original D_viewport_scrollbar_shadows stance, which cited R_layouts_close_enough to justify `getComponentCount() == 0` against JDK's count=3. That was a category error: R_layouts_close_enough's domain is *visual layout fidelity* (pixel positions, layout-manager arithmetic), not the *structural API contract* of `Container.getComponents()`. Walking the JComponent tree is how third-party frameworks introspect (accessibility, focus traversal, popup-menu propagation, custom paint dispatchers); silently returning the wrong list produces "works in desktop, mysteriously doesn't in browser" with no diagnostic breadcrumb. The earlier "single source of truth / avoid two parent edges" framing was also wrong — R_swing_is_truth explicitly maintains both AWT-side state and Vaadin-side state in lock-step; the AWT-side `components` and the Vaadin-side Scroller slot are *different edges*, both rightfully present. The `Container.addSlotChild` seam is the cleanest minimal landing for that R_swing_is_truth contract.

**Why "shadow JDK component" pattern matters here.** JDK JScrollPane's `getHorizontalScrollBar()` / `getVerticalScrollBar()` / `getViewport()` are non-null contract — common migrated patterns (`scrollPane.getVerticalScrollBar().setUnitIncrement(N)`, `scrollPane.getViewport().addChangeListener(l)`) NPE if we return null. WARN-and-return-null is technically R_match_swing_errors-compliant but produces user-visible regressions for trivial calls; full server-side bookkeeping with no DOM cost is the cleaner R_swing_is_truth read for objects with no Vaadin counterpart but real JDK identity. Same R_swing_is_truth stance the rest of the project takes for JDK fidelity (store fields, fire events) — extended one step further to "store everything, fire what we can, document what we can't." Future shadow JDK components (e.g. `JButtonGroup` model logic, hypothetical `JPopupMenu` server-side state) follow this template.

**Rationale.**

- **Vaadin `Scroller` peer at the surrogate, not custom Div + overflow CSS.** Vaadin 25's native scroll container ships `ScrollDirection` semantics that map directly onto JDK's two-axis policy, plus future scroll-position helpers (`scrollToTop` / `scrollToBottom`) we can lift through later. Custom Div + overflow:auto would re-implement what Scroller provides for no win.
- **R_swing_is_truth field-shadow + auto-scroll-content skip on emulator side.** The emulator's policy ints round-trip JDK-faithfully (R_swing_is_truth store) regardless of what the surrogate's actual ScrollDirection is. The push-to-surrogate skip when content auto-scrolls preserves the R_swing_is_truth contract without contradicting the surrogate's auto-scroll guard from SD_sjscrollpane. Migrators reading back via `getVerticalScrollBarPolicy()` see what they set, even when wrapping a Grid (where Vaadin's actual scroll behaviour is owned by the Grid itself).
- **ALWAYS policy WARNs but doesn't throw.** R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a) — Vaadin doesn't expose a force-show scrollbar API; we render the closest available (AS_NEEDED) and surface the gap in migration logs. Throwing would force migrators to rewrite ALWAYS-using code; field-shadow + WARN is non-destructive.
- **JViewport + JScrollBar as emulator-only ports, no surrogate.** Vaadin Scroller has no separate viewport object (`Scroller.getContent()` IS the viewport view); Vaadin doesn't ship a JScrollBar concept at all (the web component owns scrollbar rendering internally). Pure-surrogate users compose with Scroller's own `getContent` / `setScrollDirection` API; emulator-side JDK API on the shadow ports is for stage-2 import-swap migrators only. SD_no_sjoptionpane precedent — "no surrogate by design" carve-out under [D_surrogate_first](#D_surrogate_first), justified by the same per-component triage the JOptionPane case made.
- **No surrogate touch.** Two emulator-only ports + one ~100-line surrogate is the minimal slice. Adding surrogate-side JViewport / JScrollBar would duplicate Vaadin Scroller's internal model for no behavioural gain.

**Alternatives.**

- **Always-Scroller without auto-scroll guard.** Rejected per SD_sjscrollpane — produces stacked scrollbars or zero-height grids. Pre-flight design discussion with the user closed this.
- **WARN-and-return-null for `getHorizontalScrollBar` / `getVerticalScrollBar` / `getViewport`.** Considered briefly. Rejected — common migrated patterns NPE; the migration arc's "mostly-mechanical rewrite" value prop is broken. Shadow JDK components are the cleaner R_swing_is_truth read.
- **Surrogate-side JViewport / JScrollBar with full state-model bookkeeping.** Rejected — Vaadin has no counterpart, no UI behaviour to drive; pure-surrogate users have no use for them (they go through Scroller directly). Emulator-only minimises slice surface.
- **Conditional peer — Scroller for non-scrolling content, plain Div for already-scrolling content.** Rejected per SD_sjscrollpane — breaks 1:1 emulator↔peer invariant; Karibu locators that match `Scroller` would skip half the SJScrollPane instances.
- **Throw on ALWAYS policy.** Rejected — forces migrators to rewrite policy-setting code that's mostly migration-source-noise (default-AS_NEEDED is the dominant case). WARN-and-treat-as-AS_NEEDED is non-destructive.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **`ALWAYS` policy renders as `AS_NEEDED`.** Vaadin Scroller has no force-show; field round-trips, visible scrollbar behaviour is "as needed." R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a). Document in javadoc.
- **`getHorizontalScrollBar()` / `getVerticalScrollBar()` return shadow components with no DOM presence.** The shadows are full JDK-side objects (state-model bookkeeping, listener registration) whose inert `Div` peers stay out of the peer DOM — Vaadin Scroller's web component owns scrollbar rendering internally. Per D_shadow_children_tree_shape the shadows DO enter `Container.components` so `getComponents()` / `getComponentCount()` round-trip JDK's tree shape (count=3 post-ctor); the DOM-level absence is independent of the AWT-level presence.
- **`JViewport.addChangeListener` stores but never fires.** Vaadin Scroller has no server-side scroll-position event without custom DOM wiring; documented. Migrated code that depends on scroll-position events for paginated load triggers will need to rewrite (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a)). Same for `JScrollBar.addAdjustmentListener`.
- **`scrollRectToVisible` / `getViewPosition` / `setViewPosition`** WARN-and-skip the peer write. R_layouts_close_enough — no server-side coordinates; the browser owns scroll position. Field round-trips (so JDK code reading back values it set sees them) but no actual scroll happens.
- **No `JScrollPane.setColumnHeaderView` / `setRowHeaderView` / `setCorner` support.** All four corner / header slots WARN per R_vaadin_first (Vaadin Scroller is single-content-slot). Header components are visual-only, not lifecycle-critical; a migration target can revisit.
- **`getViewportBorder` / `setViewportBorder`** WARN — JScrollPane's separate viewport border slot doesn't map onto Scroller's single host element. Use `setBorder` on the JScrollPane itself instead.
- **`setLayout(LayoutManager)`** stores but doesn't dispatch — JScrollPane's `ScrollPaneLayout` orchestration isn't reproduced (no header/corner/viewport slot dance, single-content-slot only). Same accepted limitation SJPanel documents for unrecognised LayoutManagers.

**Validation.** `:emulators` test suite: `JScrollPaneTest` covers ctors (4 forms), `setViewportView` round-trip + emulator↔peer wiring, `getViewport().getView()` symmetry, scrollbar-policy mapping cross-product (9 cases asserted explicitly; ALWAYS branches WARN), `setViewportView(null)` clears, content swap re-pushes policy, auto-scroll content (Grid via SJTable, TextArea via SJTextArea) keeps emulator policy ints field-shadowed but doesn't drive Scroller direction. JViewport surface: `getView()` / `setView()` round-trip, listener storage round-trip, no listener fires. JScrollBar surface: full BoundedRangeModel round-trip, AdjustmentListener storage, no listener fires. R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down via reflection (no protected `(Component)` ctor exposed). D_shadow_children_tree_shape tree-shape: post-ctor `componentCount == 3` with `[viewport, verticalScrollBar, horizontalScrollBar]` in JDK order, view parented under the JViewport (not the JScrollPane directly), `setViewportView` swaps the JViewport child without touching JScrollPane children, `setViewport(other)` migrates the view across viewport replacement, `setHorizontalScrollBar` / `setVerticalScrollBar` reflect the swap at the JDK-faithful index. Sampler `ScrollPanesPanel` route + `ScrollPanesWarnInventoryTest` exit gate: three demos (JScrollPane around tall JPanel of labels, around JTextArea, around JTable) with the auto-scroll guard exercised in cases 2 and 3, plus the API-surface micro-driver covering ALWAYS-WARN, JViewport / JScrollBar shadow round-trip, header/corner WARN. The sampler route also validates D_inline_route_sizing's route-sizing model: the JTable case exercises BorderLayout.CENTER → JScrollPane → JTable height-chain that motivated the sizing fix.

<a id="D_box_family"></a>
## D_box_family. BoxLayout + Box + Box.Filler — emulator-only layout family, third built-in layout, Box.Filler as glue/strut/rigid-area component

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.BoxLayout` joins `vaadinx.awt.FlowLayout` / `vaadinx.awt.BorderLayout` as the third built-in `LayoutManager2` implementation. Lives in `vaadinx.swing` rather than `vaadinx.awt` because the JDK class is `javax.swing.BoxLayout`, not `java.awt.BoxLayout` — the import-swap rule pins the package. `LayoutCss.boxLayoutCss(int axis)` writes `display: flex; flex-direction: row|column` (X_AXIS / LINE_AXIS → row, Y_AXIS / PAGE_AXIS → column; LTR-pinned per R_layouts_close_enough, same shape as BorderLayout's LINE_START caveat). `BoxLayout` is bound to one container at construction — `invalidateLayout(Container)` and `layoutContainer(Container)` throw `AWTError("BoxLayout can't be shared")` on a foreign container, matching JDK's `checkContainer` per R_match_swing_errors. Invalid axis throws `AWTError` at construction, also per R_match_swing_errors.

`vaadinx.swing.Box extends JComponent` ships alongside as the canonical container for BoxLayout-shaped UIs, plus seven static factories matching JDK's: `createHorizontalBox` / `createVerticalBox` / `createGlue` / `createHorizontalGlue` / `createVerticalGlue` / `createHorizontalStrut(int)` / `createVerticalStrut(int)` / `createRigidArea(Dimension)`. Box's ctor pins peer at `Div` (R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down) and `super.setLayout`s a BoxLayout pointed at itself; the public `setLayout` always throws `AWTError("Illegal request")`, mirroring JDK's "the layout is fixed at construction" contract.

`Box.Filler extends JComponent` (R_leaf_peer_lockdown-locked-down, Div peer) is the invisible component the static factories return. Three CSS shapes determined by the (min, pref, max) triple at construction:
- **Glue** (`pref == (0,0)` with at least one max dim ≥ `Short.MAX_VALUE`): writes `flex-grow: 1`. Container's main axis decides growth direction — canonical pattern (matched-axis glue) renders correctly; cross-axis-glue (h-glue in a Y_AXIS Box) gets `flex-grow: 1` and grows along the cross axis rather than doing nothing (R_layouts_close_enough close-enough, documented).
- **Strut** (one pref dim non-zero, the other zero): writes the non-zero dim as a fixed `width: Npx` or `height: Npx`, plus `flex-shrink: 0` so the strut doesn't collapse under tight container pressure.
- **Rigid area** (both pref dims non-zero): both fixed dims, plus `flex-shrink: 0`.

`Box.Filler.changeShape(min, pref, max)` re-runs the CSS write; the prior shape's keys are cleared first so a strut→glue reshape doesn't leak stale dimensions. Min/pref/max getters return defensive clones (JDK no-arg-mutation contract).

<a id="D_peer_content_element_public"></a>**D_peer_content_element_public — `Container.peerContentElement()` bumped from `protected` to `public`.** Same-package layout managers (`vaadinx.awt.FlowLayout` / `vaadinx.awt.BorderLayout`) reached the dispatch element via package-private access. Cross-package `vaadinx.swing.BoxLayout` cannot. Bumping to `public` is the minimal change; the architecture's "stays protected" stance was based on the assumption that all layouts live in `vaadinx.awt`, which the JDK package straddle invalidates. Layout managers are internal infrastructure regardless of package; a public Element accessor is the natural seam (the raw `Element` is already exposed via `EHelper.applyContainerCss`'s public signature).

<a id="D_box_no_surrogate"></a>**D_box_no_surrogate — emulator-only family, no surrogates by SD_no_sjoptionpane carve-out.** Neither `BoxLayout` (a layout manager — no Vaadin component peer) nor `Box` / `Box.Filler` (composed-from-Div, no Vaadin counterpart) get surrogates. The SD_no_sjoptionpane "no surrogate by design" precedent applies: pure-surrogate-stage users have no use for Box — Vaadin's `VerticalLayout` / `HorizontalLayout` cover the same ground without the JDK ergonomic lift, and a layout manager can't be ported to a context where the LayoutManager type doesn't exist. Layout-manager dispatch already had no surrogate; this carve-out extends the same stance to the Box utility class. Third SD_no_sjoptionpane-shape carve-out (after JOptionPane and JViewport / JScrollBar).

<a id="D_box_align_self_deferred"></a>**D_box_align_self_deferred — per-child `align-self` writes deferred.** JDK BoxLayout reads each child's `getAlignmentX` / `getAlignmentY` to drive `align-self` per child. `JComponent.setAlignmentX/Y` is currently `onNoop` (Bucket B) and the getters always return `0.5f`, so any per-child write would be `align-self: center` — flex's default. Adds DOM noise with zero information today. Pre-flight: when a future migration target needs non-default alignment, lift `setAlignmentX/Y` from onNoop into a stored field first, then add the per-child write. Same R_infra_not_surface "build infrastructure properly when you touch it" cadence the rest of the project follows.

**Rationale.**

- **Path of least surprise.** BoxLayout in canonical Swing usage is "vertical row stack with struts" or "horizontal toolbar with glue pushing things to one side" — both patterns map cleanly onto CSS flex with the strut/glue components carrying spacing and expansion. Trying to reproduce JDK's exact min/pref/max distribution (which itself behaves surprisingly under tight containers) would be more code for less win; flex's defaults plus targeted per-Filler CSS gives migrators what they actually expect.
- **Box deferral was tempting but too costly.** Initial plan had Box as out-of-scope (deferred). Bringing it in is roughly +150 LOC for the utility-class plus tests; it eliminates the otherwise-pervasive workaround of `setBorder(EmptyBorder(8,0,0,0))` for spacing, and migrators reach for `Box.createVerticalStrut(8)` reflexively. Cheap relative to value.
- **Leaf lock-down at first landing.** Box and Box.Filler are JDK leaves with surrogate-by-design exemption per D_box_no_surrogate — no future surrogate will swap the peer choice, so R_leaf_peer_lockdown's "lock down at first landing" applies cleanly. Both omit the protected `(Component peer)` ctor; user-code subclasses inherit the locked Div peer.
- **`setLayout` throws to match JDK.** Box's `setLayout(LayoutManager)` always throws `AWTError`, matching JDK exactly (which uses `super.setLayout` in its own ctor to bypass). R_match_swing_errors — the throw is migrated-code-visible and changing it would make migrators write code that compiles under `vaadinx.swing` but fails under stock Swing.

**Alternatives.**

- **Defer Box.** Rejected. Migration ergonomics matter at the import-swap moment; deferring Box means migrators land in the WARN-on-getBorder-for-spacing pattern, which is exactly the "running-but-uglier" outcome we're trying to avoid.
- **Smarter glue rule that distinguishes h-glue vs v-glue vs omni-glue.** Considered. CSS `flex-grow: 1` on the wrong-axis glue does grow along the container's main axis instead of doing nothing — a small visual divergence under R_layouts_close_enough. The canonical pattern (matched-axis glue) is correct in all cases; the rare cross-axis case isn't worth a per-shape CSS dispatch. Documented as accepted divergence.
- **Per-child `align-self` writes via current `getAlignmentX/Y`.** Rejected per D_box_align_self_deferred — current getters always return 0.5f (CENTER), so every write would be `align-self: center` (flex default). Add the dispatch when alignmentX/Y becomes a stored property, not before.
- **Surrogate `SBox` extending Vaadin's `VerticalLayout` / `HorizontalLayout`.** Rejected per D_box_no_surrogate. Pure-surrogate users would just use Vaadin's layouts directly; an `SBox` would be a thin wrapper duplicating Vaadin API for stage-3 users who don't need it. SD_no_sjoptionpane-shape carve-out applies.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **RTL flipping out of scope.** JDK BoxLayout's `LINE_AXIS` flips to row-reverse under `ComponentOrientation.RIGHT_TO_LEFT`; we pin LTR (LINE_AXIS → row, PAGE_AXIS → column). R_layouts_close_enough close-enough; mirrors BorderLayout's LINE_START / LINE_END caveat. An RTL migration target can revisit.
- **Per-child sizing is flex defaults, not JDK's min/pref/max distribution.** Children get `flex: 0 0 auto` (intrinsic content size, no growth, no shrink unless flex-shrink:0 is overridden). Containers without struts/glue distribute remaining space differently than JDK would. Canonical patterns work; pathological mismatches will look different from JDK. R_layouts_close_enough.
- **Cross-axis glue grows.** Horizontal glue dropped into a Y_AXIS Box gets `flex-grow: 1` and grows vertically rather than doing nothing. Matched-axis usage is canonical and correct.
- **`Box.setLayout(LayoutManager)` always throws.** JDK contract; migrated code that tries to swap layouts on a Box gets the same `AWTError` it would under Swing. Use `Box.createVerticalBox()` etc. for fresh instances.
- **`getAccessibleContext()` returns null with WARN on Box and Box.Filler.** JPanel precedent — L&F-shaped accessibility context isn't wired.

**Validation.** `:emulators` test suite: `BoxLayoutTest` (14 cases) — per-axis CSS write, invalid axis AWTError, foreign-container invalidate AWTError, validate() pass writes CSS to JPanel content element, addLayoutComponent no-op, getAxis/getTarget round-trip, max/min/preferred sizes, non-Div peer guard. `BoxTest` (16 cases) — Box(axis) installs BoxLayout, setLayout AWTError for any layout type, all seven factories produce correct min/pref/max + correct CSS shape (glue / strut / rigid), defensive copy on Filler ctor, changeShape strut↔glue↔rigid-area transitions, getMinimumSize/getPreferredSize/getMaximumSize return clones, accessibility null-and-WARN. Sampler `LayoutsPanel` route demonstrates all three layouts plus glue/strut/rigid-area in Box. CRUD swing-source `EmployeePreviewPanel` adopts `Box.createVerticalStrut(4)` between rows in place of per-row `EmptyBorder(2,0,2,0)` — eight strut sites, one larger strut around the JSeparator. Sampler's `SamplerNav` column stacks its category headers and leaf buttons with `BoxLayout(Y_AXIS)` plus `createVerticalGlue` at the bottom, and each collapsible group is a nested `BoxLayout(Y_AXIS)` panel.

<a id="D_gridbaglayout"></a>
## D_gridbaglayout. GridBagLayout — emulator-only fourth built-in layout, GridBagConstraints stays JDK, RELATIVE/REMAINDER buckets 1+2 supported

**Decision.** `vaadinx.awt.GridBagLayout` joins `vaadinx.awt.FlowLayout` / `vaadinx.awt.BorderLayout` / `vaadinx.swing.BoxLayout` as the fourth built-in `LayoutManager2` implementation (the last of the CRUD-testbed-surfaced compile-time blockers). Lives in `vaadinx.awt` because the JDK class is `java.awt.GridBagLayout`. `LayoutCss.gridBagLayoutCss(double[] columnWeights, double[] rowWeights)` writes `display: grid; grid-template-columns: …; grid-template-rows: …` to the container's peer content element via `vaadinx.EHelper.applyContainerCss`, with per-track sizing derived from max-aggregated weight (non-zero → `minmax(0, Nfr)`, zero → `auto`). Per-child CSS (grid-column / grid-row / span / justify-self / align-self / margin / padding / min-width:0 / min-height:0) writes in `layoutContainer` after constraint resolution.

<a id="D_gridbagconstraints_stays_jdk"></a>**D_gridbagconstraints_stays_jdk — `GridBagConstraints` stays JDK; only `GridBagLayout` is ported.** Per [D_whitelist_porting](#D_whitelist_porting)'s data-types-stay-JDK rule. `GridBagConstraints` is a pure data carrier — no Component reference, no methods that touch the Component hierarchy; same shape as `Color` / `Font` / `Dimension` / `Insets`. User code's `GridBagConstraints.WEST` / `HORIZONTAL` / `REMAINDER` / etc. constants land from `java.awt.GridBagConstraints` unchanged across the import swap. The `Insets` field on `GridBagConstraints` is also JDK-reused (same data-carrier rule, doubly-applied since it's a field of an already-JDK-reused struct). The user-visible surface needs both classes available, but only `GridBagLayout` itself touches the Component hierarchy.

<a id="D_gridbag_no_surrogate"></a>**D_gridbag_no_surrogate — Emulator-only family, no surrogates by SD_no_sjoptionpane carve-out.** `GridBagLayout` is a layout manager; it has no Vaadin component peer and no UI behaviour to drive on the surrogate side. Pure-surrogate-stage users compose with Vaadin's `FormLayout` / `Grid`-flavoured layouts directly — they never reach for an emulated `GridBagLayout`. The SD_no_sjoptionpane "no surrogate by design" precedent applies; layout-manager dispatch already had no surrogate, and BoxLayout extended the same stance to its utility-class sibling per [D_box_no_surrogate](#D_box_family). Fourth SD_no_sjoptionpane-shape carve-out (after JOptionPane, JViewport / JScrollBar shadow components, BoxLayout / Box / Box.Filler).

<a id="D_gridbag_relative_remainder"></a>**D_gridbag_relative_remainder — RELATIVE / REMAINDER resolution: buckets 1+2 supported, bucket 3 deferred.** JDK `GridBagLayout`'s full placement engine is ~500 lines of cursor-and-cache machinery handling pathological corner cases (multi-row REMAINDER cursor reset, RELATIVE chains with mixed absolute components, RELATIVE-everything across the whole grid). The useful surface splits into three buckets:

- **Bucket 1 — canonical idioms (in scope).** `gridx = RELATIVE` ("next column in current row"), `gridy = RELATIVE` ("next row in current column"), `gridwidth = REMAINDER` ("end of row, advance row cursor"), `gridheight = REMAINDER` (column-major equivalent). Resolution: a `cursorX`/`cursorY` pair maintained on the GridBagLayout instance, advanced on every `addLayoutComponent`; RELATIVE for position fields resolves immediately against the cursor. The row-by-row idiom (`g.gridwidth = REMAINDER; add(field, g)`) is the most common GridBag form pattern in the wild and depends entirely on this bucket — without it, the migration arc's "mostly-mechanical rewrite" value prop breaks for any form not using absolute gridx/gridy.
- **Bucket 2 — RELATIVE on width/height (in scope).** `gridwidth = RELATIVE` ("next-to-last in row") needs the row's eventual end. Resolved at `layoutContainer` time by walking constraints to find peak track count, then computing `peakCols - 1 - gridx`. Symmetric for `gridheight`. Same one-pass shape as bucket 1's resolution; ~15 lines.
- **Bucket 3 — algorithmic faithfulness (deferred).** JDK's cursor-reset semantics on multi-row REMAINDER, RELATIVE chains across explicitly-positioned absolute components, RELATIVE-everything blocks where the cursor model can't pin a position. Constraints whose `gridx`/`gridy` is still RELATIVE at `layoutContainer` time fall here — drop-and-WARN per `EHelper.onUnimplemented`, the child is skipped from per-child CSS but doesn't crash the layout. Out of scope per R_best_effort_behaviour ("close enough to run a typical Swing app") and R_layouts_close_enough; the corner cases that need bug-for-bug parity are vanishingly rare in real-world forms. A later slice can revisit if a migration target hits one.

Bucket 3's drop-and-WARN classification: R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a)-shape — *blocked-by-policy*. Not a Vaadin gap; an explicit "we're not implementing JDK's full placement engine" decision pinned at R_best_effort_behaviour/R_layouts_close_enough. Visible-state divergence (RELATIVE child not laid out) is documented and surfaces in migration logs.

<a id="D_gridbag_weight_aggregation"></a>**D_gridbag_weight_aggregation — CSS Grid weight aggregation.** Per-track sizing follows JDK's "any non-zero `weightx` in a column makes that column absorb extra space" rule, with one refinement: weights are spread across spanned tracks (each track this child spans takes `max(currentTrackWeight, weight / span)`), matching JDK's behaviour for the common case (single-cell components carry the full weight; multi-cell spans share). Aggregation: per-column max `weightx`, per-row max `weighty`. CSS mapping: non-zero weight → `minmax(0, Nfr)` (the `minmax(0, …fr)` lets weighted tracks shrink below intrinsic content size when the grid container is bounded — same shape as `BorderLayout`'s CENTER track), zero weight → `auto`. The `Nfr` value preserves the relative-ratio contract user code expects (column-A-weight-1 + column-B-weight-2 → 1fr + 2fr → A gets 1/3, B gets 2/3 of slack space).

<a id="D_gridbag_anchor_fill"></a>**D_gridbag_anchor_fill — Anchor / fill mapping.** All 13 absolute anchor constants (CENTER + 8 cardinals/corners + 4 baseline variants × 3 leading/center/trailing) plus orientation-relative anchors (PAGE_START / LINE_END / FIRST_LINE_START / LAST_LINE_END / etc.) map to (justify-self, align-self) pairs. Orientation-relatives pin LTR per R_layouts_close_enough — same shape as BorderLayout's LINE_START / LINE_END caveat and BoxLayout's LINE_AXIS / PAGE_AXIS pinning. Baseline anchors (BASELINE / ABOVE_BASELINE / BELOW_BASELINE × leading/trailing) collapse vertical to top/center/bottom — CSS has no baseline-grid concept; R_layouts_close_enough close-enough. `fill` (NONE / HORIZONTAL / VERTICAL / BOTH) overrides anchor on whichever axis it stretches; NONE preserves the anchor mapping unchanged.

<a id="D_gridbag_insets_ipad"></a>**D_gridbag_insets_ipad — Insets and ipadx/ipady mapping.** `insets` (a JDK-reused `java.awt.Insets`) writes per-child `margin: top right bottom left` (CSS shorthand order, which differs from JDK's `Insets(top, left, bottom, right)` field order — the layout swizzles). `ipadx`/`ipady` writes per-child `padding: ipady ipadx` (vertical horizontal). Combined effect approximates JDK's pixel arithmetic to within R_layouts_close_enough; the exact "preferred-size adjustment before grid assignment" semantics don't translate to CSS Grid. `min-width: 0` / `min-height: 0` on every child (BorderLayout precedent) so cells respect their track when bounded.

**Rationale.**

- **Path of least surprise.** GridBag's canonical idioms (label + field rows with REMAINDER end-of-row, weighted second column for the field track) map cleanly onto CSS Grid. Trying to reproduce JDK's exact pixel arithmetic — which itself behaves surprisingly under tight containers and depends on Component preferredSize / minSize hints we don't compute — would be more code for less win; per-track weight aggregation plus the standard fr / auto template gives migrators what they actually expect.
- **GridBagConstraints stays JDK is non-negotiable under D_whitelist_porting.** No Component reference, pure data carrier with constants and field-sets only. Porting it would violate the data-types rule for no benefit (user code's existing `GridBagConstraints.WEST` constants work fine from the JDK class). Gives migrators a smaller import-swap delta.
- **Cursor model resolves the canonical idioms cheaply.** ~30 lines + ~15 lines for the two RELATIVE/REMAINDER buckets covers the row-by-row form pattern that's by far the dominant real-world use. Bucket 3's pathological corners aren't worth the ~500 lines to chase JDK's full algorithm — R_best_effort_behaviour ("close enough") and R_layouts_close_enough ("layouts are close-enough") apply.
- **Per-child CSS at `layoutContainer`, not `addLayoutComponent`.** Constraints are cloned at add-time (mirroring JDK's `Hashtable<Component, GridBagConstraints>` contract — user code's "mutate g, add, mutate g, add" pattern depends on this), but per-child CSS writes wait for `layoutContainer` because RELATIVE width/height needs the peak track count and weight aggregation needs the full child set. Two-pass at layout time, single source of truth. Container CSS and per-child CSS land together, no race between revalidate calls.

**Alternatives.**

- **Port `GridBagConstraints` to `vaadinx.awt.GridBagConstraints` for migrator-tooling tidiness.** Considered. Rejected — violates D_whitelist_porting's data-types rule for no functional benefit; the migrator's "rewrite java.awt.* → vaadinx.awt.*" rule already needs a stay-JDK list (Color, Font, Dimension, Insets, …), and GridBagConstraints joins that list cleanly. Lighter weight, fewer classes to maintain.
- **Implement bucket 3 (full algorithmic faithfulness).** Considered. Rejected — JDK's full `GetLayoutInfo` is ~500 lines covering corner cases (RELATIVE-everything, cursor reset on multi-row REMAINDER) that don't appear in real-world forms; effort doesn't pay back within R_best_effort_behaviour/R_layouts_close_enough.
- **Skip RELATIVE/REMAINDER entirely (absolute gridx/gridy only).** Rejected — the row-by-row REMAINDER idiom is one of the two dominant real-world GridBag patterns (alongside absolute coords). Skipping it would leave the layout looking half-finished and force migrators to rewrite forms.
- **Per-child CSS at `addLayoutComponent` time (BorderLayout-shape).** Rejected — RELATIVE width/height resolution and weight aggregation both need the full child set; adding a child can change earlier children's resolved widths or per-track weights. Layout-time write is the cleaner single-pass shape.
- **Field-cache `columnWeights[]` / `rowWeights[]` arrays as JDK exposes.** Considered. Rejected — JDK's public arrays are part of the post-layout introspection surface and aren't read by typical migrated code; keeping them computed-and-thrown-away inside `layoutContainer` is simpler. R_infra_not_surface — add the public surface when a migration target asks.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **Bucket 3 RELATIVE configurations drop-and-WARN.** Constraints whose gridx/gridy can't resolve via the cursor model fall through to `EHelper.onUnimplemented` and skip per-child CSS. Layout still completes; the affected child renders without grid placement. Migration logs surface the gap; revisit only if a real target hits it.
- **Pixel-accurate sizing is out of scope.** R_layouts_close_enough. Per-track sizing comes from CSS Grid's `fr` / `auto` distribution, not JDK's preferredSize-driven arithmetic. Forms with components that rely on JDK's exact pixel padding won't render bit-identically; the layout shape (which row, which column, which span) matches.
- **Baseline anchors collapse to top/center/bottom.** CSS has no baseline-grid concept; the 9 baseline-family anchors (BASELINE / ABOVE_BASELINE / BELOW_BASELINE × leading/center/trailing) map by combining vertical (top/center/bottom) with horizontal (start/center/end). R_layouts_close_enough.
- **RTL flipping pinned LTR.** Orientation-relative anchors (LINE_START / PAGE_START / FIRST_LINE_START / etc.) map to LTR positions. Same shape as BorderLayout's LINE_START / LINE_END caveat and BoxLayout's LINE_AXIS / PAGE_AXIS. An RTL migration target can revisit.
- **`columnWidths` / `rowHeights` / `columnWeights` / `rowWeights` JDK public arrays** are not exposed on the emulator (`getLayoutDimensions` / `getLayoutWeights` / `getLayoutOrigin` not ported). R_infra_not_surface — add when a migration target reads them.

**Validation.** `:emulators` test suite: `GridBagLayoutTest` (22 cases) — clone-on-add (mutating original after add doesn't bleed), non-GridBagConstraints constraint throws IllegalArgumentException, null constraint falls back to defaultConstraints, absolute gridx/gridy → grid-column / grid-row CSS shape (1-indexed), REMAINDER row-end resolution, REMAINDER cursor advance to next row, RELATIVE gridx (next-column cursor), RELATIVE gridwidth (next-to-last) resolution at layoutContainer, weightx → fr/auto template aggregation, anchor → justify-self/align-self mapping (cardinals + corners), fill HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL/BOTH overrides, insets → margin in CSS top-right-bottom-left order, ipadx/ipady → padding (vertical horizontal), min-width/min-height: 0 (BorderLayout precedent), LINE_START LTR pinning, removeLayoutComponent clears CSS, setConstraints + re-layout, end-to-end JPanel.setLayout(GridBagLayout) + validate, non-Div peer guard, max/min/preferred sizes. Sampler `LayoutsPanel` route grows a fourth demo cell exercising the canonical CRUD form shape (label + field rows with weighted second column); `NavigationSmokeTest` extends to cover the Layouts route (was previously omitted).

---

<a id="D_jformattedtextfield"></a>
## D_jformattedtextfield. JFormattedTextField — ctor-time formatter-driven peer dispatch via `FormattedFieldStrategy`

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.JFormattedTextField` extends `vaadinx.swing.JTextField` (JDK shape preserved) and at ctor time picks a `FormattedFieldStrategy` from the formatter argument's class. The strategy hard-codes the Vaadin peer family: `DatePicker` (DateFormatter), `IntegerField` / `LongField` / `NumberField` (NumberFormatter, dispatched by `getValueClass()`), or `TextField` (DefaultFormatter / MaskFormatter / no formatter). The chosen strategy is pinned for the instance's lifetime; `setFormatter` and `setFormatterFactory` calls that stay within the same family swap the formatter logic without rebuilding the peer; cross-family swaps WARN via `EHelper.onUnimplemented` and keep the original strategy.

Six sub-decisions land together because the strategy interface, the peer family, the D_framework_peer_selection carve-out, the swap rule, the JTextField ctor widening, and the R_leaf_peer_lockdown stance are co-determined — splitting them invites divergent assumptions.

<a id="D_formatted_strategy_interface"></a>**D_formatted_strategy_interface — Strategy interface.** Package-private `interface FormattedFieldStrategy` alongside `JFormattedTextField`. Methods (mirror the FrameStrategy shape, adapted for value-bearing peers):

```
interface FormattedFieldStrategy {
    Component createPeer();                                  // called from private ctor
    void install(JFormattedTextField, Component peer);       // peer-side commit listeners (focus-loss / value-change / Enter)
    void afterSetValue(JFormattedTextField, Object value);   // push value into peer + Document via formatter.valueToString
    void afterCommitFromPeer(JFormattedTextField);           // pull peer value, publish as JFormattedTextField.value
    boolean accepts(AbstractFormatter f);                    // family check for D_formatter_swap_rules swap rule
}
```

Implementations: `DateStrategy` (peer = `SJFormattedDatePicker`), `IntegerStrategy` (`SJFormattedIntegerField`), `LongStrategy` (`SJFormattedLongField`), `NumberStrategy` (`SJFormattedNumberField`), `MaskStrategy` (`SJFormattedTextField` + browser-side `pattern` attr), `DefaultStrategy` (`SJFormattedTextField`). All strategies are stateless singletons; per-instance state lives on `JFormattedTextField`.

Strategy resolution at ctor time via `private static FormattedFieldStrategy pickStrategy(AbstractFormatter f, Object initialValue, Class<?> valueClass)`:

1. `DateFormatter`, or `InternationalFormatter` wrapping a `DateFormat`, or value class assignable to `Date` / `Calendar` → `DateStrategy`.
2. `NumberFormatter`, dispatched by `formatter.getValueClass()` (or `initialValue.getClass()` fallback): `Integer.class` → `IntegerStrategy`; `Long.class` → `LongStrategy`; `Number` / `Double` / null → `NumberStrategy`.
3. `MaskFormatter` → `MaskStrategy`.
4. Otherwise → `DefaultStrategy`.

JLS forbids `getClass()` in `super(...)`, so the resolution runs in a static helper before chaining to the private peer ctor — same shape JFrame's `pickStrategyForCurrentInstance()` uses.

<a id="D_formatted_peer_family"></a>**D_formatted_peer_family — Peer family: one surrogate per Vaadin input type.** DatePicker, NumberField, IntegerField, LongField, and TextField are separate concrete classes in the Vaadin hierarchy with no common stateful supertype that exposes `setValue(Object)` polymorphically. A single `SJFormatted*` surrogate cannot extend all five. Family of five surrogates lives in `:surrogates` per [SD_sjformatted_family](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjformatted_family). The strategy interface in D_formatted_strategy_interface is what bridges across them on the emulator side.

<a id="D_formatter_is_framework_config"></a>**D_formatter_is_framework_config — Formatter argument is "framework-level configuration" for D_framework_peer_selection's purposes.** D_framework_peer_selection says the framework may select the peer based on framework-level configuration; "user code cannot influence the choice." The formatter is user code's argument. We extend D_framework_peer_selection's invariant rather than violate it: a `JFormattedTextField`'s formatter is *declarative type info* in the same spirit as `@MainWindow` — "this field is a date" / "this field is an integer" — pinned at ctor and unswappable at runtime across families. D_framework_peer_selection's spirit ("the peer is pinned and predictable; runtime cannot swap it underneath user code") is preserved, even though the trigger now reads from a ctor argument rather than an annotation. D_framework_peer_selection's wording extends to: *"The framework selects among multiple canonical peer types for a given emulator based on framework-level facts (annotation presence, formatter type at construction); user code cannot dynamically swap the peer at runtime."* User code that wants to swap from a date field to a number field in-place mid-life-cycle is constructing the wrong abstraction — the JDK contract for `JFormattedTextField` permits formatter swap, but Vaadin's component-per-input-type shape doesn't, and we'd rather throw away the round-trip than ship a phantom peer-swap that can't happen.

<a id="D_formatter_swap_rules"></a>**D_formatter_swap_rules — Formatter swap rules.** `setFormatter(AbstractFormatter)` and `setFormatterFactory(AbstractFormatterFactory)` accept the new formatter / factory. If `strategy.accepts(newFormatter)` returns true (same family — e.g. swapping one DateFormatter for another with a different pattern, or a NumberFormatter bound to `Integer.class` for another), the formatter logic re-runs: current value re-stringifies, current text re-parses, no peer rebuild. If `strategy.accepts` returns false (cross-family — DateFormatter → NumberFormatter), `EHelper.onUnimplemented` WARNs and the original strategy is kept; the formatter field is updated so `getFormatter()` round-trips, but the peer continues to render under the original strategy. AbstractFormatterFactory's focus-state-driven display/edit formatter swap typically uses two formatters in the same family (DateFormatter with two patterns); pathological cross-family factories WARN at each swap attempt and keep the original strategy.

<a id="D_jtextfield_ctor_widening"></a>**D_jtextfield_ctor_widening — JTextField protected ctor widening.** JTextField's `(Component peer)` ctor currently throws `IllegalStateException` on any peer that isn't `TextField` or `PasswordField` (a guard installed alongside Enter-as-submit wiring). JFormattedTextField legitimately passes non-TextFieldBase peers (DatePicker, NumberField, …) through this seam. The guard is split into two halves:

- Enter-as-submit wiring is gated on `peer instanceof TextField || peer instanceof PasswordField`; foreign peers skip wiring silently (no WARN — it's a legitimate non-applicability, not an incompleteness).
- JFormattedTextField uses a new `protected JTextField(Component peer, FormattedFieldStrategy strategy)` overload that bypasses Enter wiring entirely — the strategy installs its own commit semantic (focus-loss / Enter-on-DatePicker / value-change / explicit `commitEdit()`).

The previous "fail loud on TextArea misuse" stance is preserved by JTextArea's own ctor (which extends JTextComponent directly, not JTextField), so no defense is lost.

<a id="D_jformattedtextfield_lockdown"></a>**D_jformattedtextfield_lockdown — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `JFormattedTextField` is a leaf in the public Swing class hierarchy (no public class in `javax.swing.*` extends it). With D_formatter_swap_rules's swap-rule shape settled (factory-driven formatter pull lands the same-family swap; cross-family WARNs and keeps the original strategy), R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down applies: no protected `(Component peer)` ctor, no escape hatch for user-code subclasses to swap the peer. The class stays non-final per R_leaf_peer_lockdown — user-code subclasses for behavior (custom `commitEdit`, `fireActionPerformed` override, custom focus handling) inherit the strategy-dispatched peer and work fine. The package-private `(FormattedFieldStrategy)` ctor is the single dispatch funnel; user code cannot reach it from outside the `vaadinx.swing` package, so the framework-canonical peer choice per D_formatter_is_framework_config holds.

**Rationale.**

- **Strategy pattern, not branches in JFormattedTextField's body.** Same reasoning D_frame_strategy applies: every `setValue` / `getValue` / focus-loss / `commitEdit` site would otherwise need a peer-type branch; the body becomes unreadable, and adding a new formatter family later means revisiting every branch. Strategy keeps dispatch surface in one place per shape.
- **Pin at ctor, not on every commit.** Vaadin DatePicker / IntegerField / NumberField / TextField are different concrete classes with different DOM templates; swapping the rendered component live mid-life-cycle would force full peer reconstruction, lose any user-set Vaadin properties (helperText, placeholder, label), and break Karibu locator references held by user/test code. Pinning matches user expectations: "I declared this field as a date field; it stays a date field."
- **Cross-family swap WARN, not throw.** The JDK contract for `setFormatterFactory` permits cross-family swap (text-mode → date-mode is legal Swing). Throwing would crash code paths that pass a `DefaultFormatterFactory` whose display/edit formatters happen to differ in family. WARN-and-keep matches R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c) — no Vaadin counterpart for the JDK contract, drop with WARN, accept the lossy round-trip.
- **Surrogate family of five, not one fat surrogate.** Vaadin's input-component hierarchy is parallel-not-shared; one surrogate that "is-a" all five is impossible. SJPasswordField precedent (SD_sjpasswordfield — duplicates the JTextField surface because PasswordField is not a TextField subclass) is the correct shape; SJFormatted* siblings share a `SJFormattedFieldMixin` for the JFormattedTextField-specific surface (value, focusLostBehavior, commitEdit) per [SD_sjformattedfieldmixin](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjformattedfieldmixin).
- **Preserve JDK shape for the import-swap drop-in.** Real Swing's `JFormattedTextField extends JTextField`. Migrators who call `formattedField.setColumns(20)` or `formattedField.addActionListener(...)` get inherited JTextField behavior (columns is field-shadowed, ActionListener fires on commit) without code changes. Breaking the inheritance would force a rewrite.

**Alternatives.**

- **Single peer (always `TextField`), formatter logic inline.** Considered. Rejected: defeats the user-stated goal — a `JFormattedTextField` constructed with a `DateFormatter` should render as a Vaadin `DatePicker` in the browser. Falling back to plain text with format validation gives no migration value-add.
- **Multiple emulator subclasses (`JFormattedDateField`, `JFormattedNumberField`, …) instead of strategy dispatch.** Rejected — breaks JDK shape; the migrator's `import javax.swing.JFormattedTextField` rewrite would no longer compile.
- **Live peer swap on `setFormatter` cross-family.** Rejected — see Rationale.
- **Throw on cross-family swap.** Rejected — see Rationale; WARN-and-keep matches R_match_swing_errors (c).
- **Emulator-only (compose Vaadin DatePicker / NumberField / TextField directly without surrogates).** Rejected — violates D_surrogate_first's surrogate-first policy. JOptionPane's emulator-only carve-out (D_joptionpane, SD_no_sjoptionpane) is justified by being a factory class with no instance hierarchy; JFormattedTextField is a stateful JTextField subclass, so SD_no_sjoptionpane's logic doesn't transfer.
- **CustomField-composite single-surrogate (SJSpinner shape, SD_sjspinner).** Considered for the surrogate side. Rejected — extra DOM nesting + Karibu locator drilling, and the cross-family swap problem still surfaces (the inner peer would have to rebuild, breaking the same Vaadin-property invariants pinning is designed to preserve).

**Accepted limitations.**

- **Cross-family `setFormatterFactory` swap loses peer match.** A factory whose display formatter is `DateFormatter` and edit formatter is `NumberFormatter` keeps the original strategy (whichever was active at ctor); the mismatched-family formatter operates as a logical formatter only, with the rendered peer staying in the original family. R_match_swing_errors (c) drop-and-WARN.
- **`JFormattedTextField(Object value)` ctor's formatter inference is hardcoded.** JDK consults a registry to pick a formatter from value type. We mirror the typical mappings (Date / Calendar → DateStrategy; Integer / Long / Double / Number → corresponding numeric strategy; everything else → DefaultStrategy). Custom JDK formatter-registration hooks are not consulted.
- **DatePicker locale-aware parsing vs SimpleDateFormat strict matching.** A `DateFormatter(new SimpleDateFormat("yyyy-MM-dd"))` user expects strict pattern-driven parsing. Vaadin DatePicker uses its own locale-driven parser. The round-trip via `valueToString(getValue())` uses the formatter's pattern (correct shape); typed input parses through DatePicker's locale logic, not the formatter. R_best_effort_behaviour/R_layouts_close_enough close-enough — calendar popup is the dominant input path.
- **`MaskFormatter` browser-side regex coverage is partial.** Mask chars `#`, `'` (literal escape), `H` (hex), `L` (lowercase), `U` (uppercase), `?` (any letter), `*` (anything), `A` (alphanumeric) convert to regex equivalents. Unrecognised chars degrade to permissive validation per R_match_swing_errors (c). Overwrite mode is not modeled — typed input behaves as insert mode.
- **`JFormattedTextField.AbstractFormatter` (the inner class)** is reused from JDK per [D_whitelist_porting](#D_whitelist_porting) — it doesn't reference Component. Subclassing `AbstractFormatter` for custom formatters works unchanged across the import swap.
- **No `SJFormattedDateTimePicker` for time-bearing date formats.** A `DateFormatter` with a time component (e.g. `"yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"`) renders as `SJFormattedDatePicker` (date-only); the time portion is dropped silently. A later slice may add `SJFormattedDateTimePicker extends DateTimePicker` if a real migration target uses time-bearing date formats; deferred per R_infra_not_surface. Mirrors SJSpinner's existing limitation under SD_sjspinner.
- **R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down deferred (D_jformattedtextfield_lockdown).** Re-evaluate after D_formatter_swap_rules's implementation settles.

**Validation.**

- `:surrogates` test suites — `SJFormattedDatePickerTest`, `SJFormattedIntegerFieldTest`, `SJFormattedLongFieldTest`, `SJFormattedNumberFieldTest`, `SJFormattedTextFieldTest` — each cover ctor variants, `setValue` / `getValue` round-trip with the strategy's typed value class, formatter-driven displayed-text round-trip, focus-loss commit, peer-originated value change updating the surrogate's Object value, listener storage / fan-out for ActionListener and PropertyChangeEvent("value"), R_vaadin_first drop-and-WARN sweeps for absent JTextField surface (alignment, columns where peer has no width concept), L&F getUI / setUI WARN-and-drop.
- `:emulators` test suite — `JFormattedTextFieldTest` covers the strategy-dispatch table (each ctor → expected peer type), the swap rules (same-family swap re-runs formatter; cross-family WARN-and-keep), `commitEdit()` / `getValue()` / `setValue(Object)` round-trip per formatter family, focus-lost-behavior enum honoring, JTextField surface inheritance per peer type (DatePicker silent for setColumns, etc.).
- Sampler `FormattedFieldsPanel` route demonstrates each formatter family + a Karibu `FormattedFieldsWarnInventoryTest` exit gate (zero stub WARNs across user paths + per-strategy API drivers), per the [sampler exit-gate inventory](../sampler/description.md#exit-gate-inventory).
