<a id="D_jspinner_editor"></a>
## D_jspinner_editor. JSpinner editor surface — `DateEditor` port via synthetic `JFormattedTextField`; `setEditor(DateEditor)` plumbs date pattern through `DatePicker.setI18n`

The CRUD testbed's `EmployeeEditDialog` constructs `dobField.setEditor(new JSpinner.DateEditor(dobField, "yyyy-MM-dd"))` ([testapps/crud/swing/.../EmployeeEditDialog.java:53](../testapps/crud/swing/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/testapps/crud/swing/EmployeeEditDialog.java)); pre-D_jspinner_editor the editor classes were drop-and-WARN at `getEditor` / `setEditor` per the [D_emulator_surrogate_split](#D_emulator_surrogate_split) bare-minimum stance, so the migrator either fell back to year-only `SpinnerNumberModel` or shipped a date field with no format applied. D_jspinner_editor ports `JSpinner.DefaultEditor`, `JSpinner.DateEditor`, `JSpinner.NumberEditor`, `JSpinner.ListEditor` as nested classes on `vaadinx.swing.JSpinner` and routes `DateEditor`'s pattern through to the underlying Vaadin `DatePicker` via [SD_sjspinner](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjspinner)'s `SJSpinner.setDatePattern` (added in this slice).

**Decision.** Five concrete pieces:

1. **`SJSpinner.setDatePattern(String)` on the surrogate** ([surrogates/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/SJSpinner.java](../surrogates/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/SJSpinner.java)) — translates a JDK `SimpleDateFormat`-shaped pattern into a `DatePicker.DatePickerI18n` and applies it to the inner DatePicker. R_layouts_close_enough best-effort: pattern's date components (`yyyy / MM / dd / d / M / yy`) ride through unchanged; time components (e.g. `"yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm"`) are stripped (split on first space) and the time portion is dropped silently per [SD_maskformatter_regex](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_maskformatter_regex)'s "no SJFormattedDateTimePicker" precedent. Pattern is field-shadowed on the surrogate so a subsequent `setModel(SpinnerDateModel)` swap re-applies it to the freshly-built DatePicker (without the field shadow, model swap silently reverts to locale default). No-op when the inner field isn't a DatePicker (numeric / list / unknown-model paths) — pattern is still stored, takes effect if/when the model swaps to date-typed.

2. **`JSpinner.DefaultEditor` nested class on the emulator** — extends `vaadinx.swing.JPanel`, implements `ChangeListener` + `PropertyChangeListener` (matching JDK's interface set; `LayoutManager` skipped — the editor never renders, so layout responsibilities don't transfer). Holds a synthetic `vaadinx.swing.JFormattedTextField` accessible via `getTextField()` so migrated code that reaches through the editor (`editor.getTextField().setColumns(8)`, `setText`, `setEditable`, `getValue`) doesn't NPE. The synthetic field is **never attached to any container** — the spinner's underlying Vaadin peer (DatePicker / IntegerField / NumberField / Select) is what actually renders. JDK's `stateChanged` / `propertyChange` body is replaced with a no-op on the emulator side: peer↔model sync already runs through SJSpinner's value-change listener before the editor's PCE would fire, so the JDK shape is redundant.

3. **`JSpinner.DateEditor` nested class** — extends `DefaultEditor`. Public ctor `(JSpinner spinner, String pattern)` builds a pre-configured synthetic `JFormattedTextField(new DateFormatter(new SimpleDateFormat(pattern)))` and passes it through a package-private `DefaultEditor(JSpinner, JFormattedTextField)` ctor seam. Building the synthetic field with a `DateFormatter` from the start pins its strategy to [D_formatted_strategy_interface](#D_jformattedtextfield)'s `DateStrategy` — avoids the cross-family setFormatter swap WARN that JDK's "construct plain ftf, install DateFormatter via setFormatterFactory afterwards" shape would trigger against [D_formatter_swap_rules](#D_jformattedtextfield) (c). `getFormat()` returns the constructed `SimpleDateFormat` (round-trips the pattern). `getModel()` returns the spinner's `SpinnerDateModel`, with a R_match_swing_errors-shaped WARN if the model isn't date-typed (matches JDK's `ClassCastException` shape but degrades to a WARN + null since the editor exists at the JComponent type — losing the cast site).

4. **`JSpinner.NumberEditor` and `JSpinner.ListEditor` as drop-and-WARN nested classes** — exist at the type level so `new JSpinner.NumberEditor(spinner, "#0.00")` compiles. `setEditor(NumberEditor)` and `setEditor(ListEditor)` WARN via `EHelper.onUnimplemented` per R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c) and store the editor for `getEditor` round-trip. `NumberEditor.getFormat()` returns the constructed `DecimalFormat` so introspection round-trips; the format is **not** plumbed to IntegerField / NumberField (Vaadin's numeric fields don't accept `DecimalFormat` patterns). `ListEditor` is a near-no-op — `SpinnerListModel` already dispatches to Vaadin `Select<Object>` per [SD_sjspinner](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjspinner)'s `createInnerFieldFor`, so the JDK `ListEditor` chrome (combo-with-typing) adds nothing the peer doesn't already cover.

5. **`JSpinner.setEditor(JComponent)` dispatch** — type-checks the editor and routes:
   - `DateEditor` → extract pattern via package-private `getDateFormatPattern()`, call `spinner().setDatePattern(pattern)`, fire `"editor"` PCE.
   - `NumberEditor` / `ListEditor` / generic `JComponent` → WARN via `EHelper.onUnimplemented`, store editor for `getEditor` round-trip, fire `"editor"` PCE.

   Same-instance reassignment is a no-op (no PCE fire). Null editor throws `IllegalArgumentException` per JDK contract.

<a id="D_spinner_synthetic_field"></a>**D_spinner_synthetic_field — Synthetic `JFormattedTextField` is real, not null + WARN.** `editor.getTextField()` could return null and WARN. Rejected: JDK's typical migrator path goes `editor.getTextField().setColumns(8)` / `.setEditable(false)` / `.getValue()`, and a null return would NPE on the next dereference. Real (off-DOM) JFormattedTextField costs one extra surrogate allocation per editor construction (cheap — testbed has one DOB field per dialog) but eliminates the NPE class. The synthetic field's peer is never attached, so it consumes no DOM slot; its only observable effect is API readback for migrated code that introspects.

<a id="D_spinner_pattern_on_surrogate"></a>**D_spinner_pattern_on_surrogate — Pattern plumbing lives on the surrogate (`setDatePattern`), not the emulator reaching into the peer's inner field.** `SJSpinner.setDatePattern(String)` — package-public — is the single seam that knows how to translate a JDK pattern to `DatePickerI18n`. Alternative considered: emulator's `setEditor` reaches through `((SJSpinner) peer).getInnerField()` (would need to expose) and calls `setI18n` directly. Rejected because (a) the surrogate already owns the inner-field-class knowledge and the field-rebuild lifecycle (`ensureInnerFieldMatches` runs on every `setModel`); (b) cross-module reach-through would force `:surrogates` to expose the inner field as a public accessor, contradicting the `CustomField` composite shape's "inner is implementation detail" stance; (c) the surrogate-side seam survives a future surrogate-only consumer (pure-`:surrogates` user code that wants to set a date pattern without going through the emulator).

<a id="D_dateeditor_preconfigures"></a>**D_dateeditor_preconfigures — DateEditor pre-configures its synthetic field rather than mutating it post-`super()`.** JDK's DateEditor calls `super(spinner)` (which builds a plain `JFormattedTextField`) then mutates it via `setFormatterFactory(new DefaultFormatterFactory(new DateFormatter(...)))`. We can't replicate that mutation path because `JFormattedTextField.setFormatterFactory` → `setFormatter(DateFormatter)` against a plain (DefaultFormattedStrategy) field trips D_formatter_swap_rules (c)'s cross-family swap WARN at construction, polluting `WarnInventoryTest`. Resolution: package-private `DefaultEditor(JSpinner spinner, JFormattedTextField ftf)` ctor lets `DateEditor` inject a pre-configured field built directly with `new JFormattedTextField(new DateFormatter(...))` so the strategy pins to DateStrategy from the start. Slight JDK-shape divergence (the inherited `ftf` field is final and assigned via the seam ctor, not the `super(spinner)` body); accepted because the alternative is a noisy WARN at every DateEditor construction.

<a id="D_geteditor_null_until_set"></a>**D_geteditor_null_until_set — `getEditor()` returns null until `setEditor` is called; no lazy default-editor creation.** JDK's JSpinner lazily-creates a `DefaultEditor` on first `getEditor()` call so `editor.getTextField().setColumns(8)` works without an explicit `setEditor`. We skip this: the spinner's peer (DatePicker / IntegerField / Select / …) renders without any editor, so a default editor would be a phantom — its existence buys no functional behavior, only lifecycle complexity. Migrated code that reaches `getEditor()` before `setEditor` gets null and a clean NPE telling them to wire one. The CRUD testbed always calls `setEditor` explicitly; if a migration target depends on the lazy-default behavior, the carve-out is local (build a `DefaultEditor` and store it on first `getEditor`).

<a id="D_jspinner_lockdown"></a>**D_jspinner_lockdown — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down stays.** [R_leaf_peer_lockdown](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules)'s peer lock-down on `vaadinx.swing.JSpinner` predates D_jspinner_editor (the private `JSpinner(SJSpinner)` ctor closes the seam). D_jspinner_editor doesn't add new ctors that could leak the peer-swap seam — the editor classes are nested types operating on the spinner's existing peer, not new spinner construction paths. Lock-down holds.

**Rationale.**

- **Editor as API surface, not rendering host.** SJSpinner's per-model dispatch already chose the right Vaadin component for the spinner. Re-rendering the editor's contents on top would (a) double the DOM footprint, (b) require the editor's synthetic field to mirror the model's value (more sync code), (c) create two browser-side input affordances for the same value. The editor's role in the import-swap drop-in is the API surface migrators reach through (`getTextField`, `getFormat`), not the visual UI.
- **DateEditor pattern is the load-bearing case.** The CRUD testbed's pre-D_jspinner_editor fallback (year-only `SpinnerNumberModel`) is a worse migration outcome than a date picker with locale-default formatting. Plumbing the pattern through preserves the migrator's intent ("show this date as `yyyy-MM-dd`") without requiring a manual `DatePicker.setI18n` workaround that defeats the import-swap value prop.
- **NumberEditor / ListEditor as type-level drop-and-WARN, not whole-class WARN.** Migrators who pass a `NumberEditor` to a JSpinner whose peer doesn't accept `DecimalFormat` patterns deserve a one-line WARN at `setEditor` (so the gap surfaces in migration logs), not a noisy ctor WARN that fires even when the editor is constructed but never wired. The class itself exists (compilation-friendly); only the `setEditor` consumption path WARNs.
- **`getModel()` returns the typed model (or WARN+null on mismatch), not throws.** JDK's `DateEditor.getModel(): SpinnerDateModel` is implicitly typed via the editor's lifecycle invariant (DateEditor is built against a SpinnerDateModel-backed spinner). Our editor classes are nested type aliases attached at any spinner; if a migrator passes a non-SpinnerDateModel spinner to `DateEditor`'s ctor or swaps the model afterwards, we WARN + return null rather than throw. R_match_swing_errors-aligned: "do something silly beats crashing the host app" — the mismatch is recoverable (re-create the editor with the right model), throwing would force a `try/catch` around a rare misuse path.

**Alternatives.**

- **Render the synthetic JFormattedTextField inline (faithful JDK shape).** Rejected — see Rationale.
- **Plumb the pattern through a hidden parameter on `SJSpinner`'s ctor instead of a setter.** Rejected — the testbed wires the editor *after* spinner construction (`new JSpinner(model); spinner.setEditor(new DateEditor(spinner, "..."))`); a ctor-time pattern would force migrators to reorder their code or pre-stash the pattern in a temp variable.
- **Plumb the pattern through emulator-side `EHelper.applySpinnerDatePattern(spinner, pattern)` rather than a surrogate method.** Rejected — see D_spinner_pattern_on_surrogate. Surrogate-side ownership reduces the cross-module surface and makes pure-surrogate users first-class.
- **Auto-format `JSpinner` getValue's Date toString using the pattern.** Rejected — JDK doesn't reformat `getValue()` based on the editor's pattern (the model returns Date verbatim); imposing this would be a divergence we don't need. Migrator code that wants formatted-string display calls `editor.getFormat().format(spinner.getValue())` explicitly.
- **Throw `IllegalArgumentException` at `setEditor(NumberEditor)` instead of WARN.** Rejected — R_match_swing_errors's enumerated throw triggers don't include "wrong editor type"; migrators with mixed editor types (e.g. a settings dialog with one date and one number spinner sharing helper code) deserve a WARN per call site rather than a crash.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **Synthetic field allocation overhead.** Each `DateEditor` constructs a `vaadinx.swing.JFormattedTextField` + its `SJFormattedDatePicker` peer, including a value-change listener subscription. Off-DOM but not free. Acceptable — typical migrated code constructs editors once per dialog, not in tight loops.
- **NumberEditor pattern is silently ignored.** `getFormat()` round-trips the pattern, but the rendered IntegerField / NumberField doesn't honor it — Vaadin numeric fields display in locale default. R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c) drop-and-WARN; may revisit if a target depends on per-spinner DecimalFormat.
- **`stateChanged` / `propertyChange` are no-ops on `DefaultEditor`.** JDK uses these to keep the editor's text field synchronized with the spinner's model. Our peer drives the model directly via SJSpinner's value-change listener, so the JDK path is redundant. User code that overrides `DefaultEditor.stateChanged` for custom display behavior continues to receive the event but inherits a no-op base; documented in javadoc.
- **`createEditor(SpinnerModel)` is drop-and-WARN.** JDK builds a default editor matching the model type. We never call it internally (the peer renders without an editor). Migrators who override `createEditor` to plug in a custom editor see the WARN once — the override itself works; the WARN signals that we don't auto-call into it.
- **Time-component patterns drop the time silently.** `new DateEditor(spinner, "yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm")` renders as date-only — Vaadin DatePicker has no time concept. Mirrors the SJFormattedDatePicker stance per SD_maskformatter_regex. A later slice may add a `SJFormattedDateTimePicker` carve-out if a target needs it.

**Validation.**

- `:surrogates` test suite — `SJSpinnerTest`'s "Date pattern (D_jspinner_editor)" section covers `setDatePattern` applies DatePickerI18n to inner DatePicker; time-component pattern strips silently; pattern survives setModel rebuild; non-Date model stores pattern and applies on subsequent date-model swap; null pattern resets i18n.
- `:emulators` test suite — `JSpinnerTest`'s "Editor surface (D_jspinner_editor)" section covers DateEditor pattern → DatePicker.i18n round-trip, second `setEditor(DateEditor)` overrides the first, `getEditor` is null pre-`setEditor`, `"editor"` PCE fires once per swap, same-instance reassignment is a no-op.
- Sampler `InputsPanel` route hosts a `SpinnerDateModel + DateEditor("yyyy-MM-dd")` row alongside the existing JSlider / JSpinner demos; `InputsWarnInventoryTest`'s 5d bucket exercises the DateEditor surface end-to-end (construction, setEditor, introspection, peer-side i18n verification, setModel-rebuild pattern preservation) with zero stub WARNs across the path.

<a id="D_buttongroup"></a>
## D_buttongroup. ButtonGroup — `vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup` port; coordination on ported AbstractButton subclasses; ButtonModel-taking JDK methods drop-and-WARN

The CRUD testbed's `MainFrame` builds a View → density radio submenu via `densityGroup.add(dDefault); densityGroup.add(dCompact); densityGroup.add(dRoomy);` ([testapps/crud/swing/.../MainFrame.java:111](../testapps/crud/swing/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/testapps/crud/swing/MainFrame.java)). After import-swap, the migrator's `JRadioButtonMenuItem` instances are `vaadinx.swing.AbstractButton` — but JDK `ButtonGroup#add(javax.swing.AbstractButton)` won't accept them, so the testbed migrator dropped the coordination (multi-select chrome, no exclusion). D_buttongroup ports `ButtonGroup` to the `vaadinx.swing` package against the ported hierarchy and closes [SD_sjmenubar](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjmenubar)'s "JRadioButtonMenuItem multi-select gap" as a side effect.

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup` mirrors the JDK API surface (`add` / `remove` / `clearSelection` / `getElements` / `getButtonCount` / `getSelection` / `isSelected(ButtonModel)` / `setSelected(ButtonModel, boolean)`) with two divergences:

1. **`add(AbstractButton)` accepts `vaadinx.swing.AbstractButton`** — not `javax.swing.AbstractButton`. Same shape JDK takes, retargeted at the ported hierarchy. `getElements()` returns `Enumeration<vaadinx.swing.AbstractButton>` for the same reason. Cross-package `vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup#add(javax.swing.AbstractButton)` doesn't compile — but neither does the migrator's pre-import-swap code after `import javax.swing.JRadioButtonMenuItem;` rewrites to `import vaadinx.swing.JRadioButtonMenuItem;`, so the divergence is invisible at the migrator's seam.
2. **JDK `ButtonModel`-taking methods drop-and-WARN.** `getSelection() : ButtonModel` returns null + `EHelper.onUnimplemented`; `isSelected(ButtonModel)` returns false + WARN; `setSelected(ButtonModel, boolean)` is a WARN-and-noop. R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c) — :emulators flattened the ButtonModel surface (selection lives directly on AbstractButton subclass fields, no `DefaultButtonModel`), so there's no model to return or accept. Migrators iterating via `getElements()` + per-button `isSelected()` work without changes; chained `group.getSelection().isSelected()` patterns NPE — a later slice may add a synthetic ButtonModel proxy if a real migration target depends on the chain.

Internal coordination tracks `selectedButton : AbstractButton` (the ported counterpart of JDK's `selection : ButtonModel`). Coordination logic mirrors JDK `DefaultButtonModel.setSelected` exactly — at the top of every selection-bearing subclass's `setSelected(boolean)` and `makeOnClick`, the body calls a package-private `consultButtonGroup(boolean)` helper on AbstractButton that runs `group.setSelectedButton(this, b)` then re-reads `group.isSelectedButton(this)`, and replaces the proposed `b` with the verdict before any state mutation or peer write.

<a id="D_buttongroup_cross_package"></a>**D_buttongroup_cross_package — Cross-package compat resolution.** The two-package divergence (`vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup#add(vaadinx.swing.AbstractButton)` vs. JDK `javax.swing.ButtonGroup#add(javax.swing.AbstractButton)`) is the same shape `:emulators` already takes for every ported class — `vaadinx.swing.JButton`, `vaadinx.swing.AbstractButton`, etc. The migrator's `import javax.swing.ButtonGroup;` rewrites to `import vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup;` and the `g.add(menuItem)` call resolves against the ported overload after the rewrite. JDK ButtonGroup is the only "models stay JDK" carve-out the migration arc unwinds — it's not a pure model (it operates on `AbstractButton` instances), so the cross-package signature mismatch forces a port.

<a id="D_buttongroup_selection_storage"></a>**D_buttongroup_selection_storage — Selection storage.** `selectedButton : AbstractButton` instead of `selection : ButtonModel`. Reasons:

- :emulators flattened the ButtonModel surface — `DefaultButtonModel` doesn't exist on the emulator side; `AbstractButton.getModel()` is a drop-and-WARN. Storing a `ButtonModel` requires either a port (large surface — ~14 methods, ~5 listener types) or a synthetic proxy that fakes the shape. Neither benefit pays back now.
- Migrators almost never reach into `group.getSelection()` directly — the typical pattern is `getElements()` + per-button `isSelected()`. Drop-and-WARN at `getSelection()` is honest about the gap without forcing a model port.
- Storing the AbstractButton directly keeps the cascade logic trivial: `setSelectedButton(true)` swaps the slot and calls `oldSelection.setSelected(false)` — a method that already exists on the ported subclass, no model translation needed.

A later slice may revisit if a real migration target depends on `group.getSelection().isSelected()`; the resolution would be a thin synthetic ButtonModel that proxies through to `selectedButton.isSelected()`.

<a id="D_abstractbutton_group_hook"></a>**D_abstractbutton_group_hook — AbstractButton hook (lifted from `ButtonModel`).** Package-private `ButtonGroup buttonGroup` field on `vaadinx.swing.AbstractButton` plus `setButtonGroup(ButtonGroup) / getButtonGroup()` accessors. JDK stores group membership on `DefaultButtonModel.group`; we lift it to the button since :emulators flattened the model. Plain `JButton` inherits the field but its `setSelected` stays `EHelper.onNoop` (JButton has no selection state) — adding a JButton to a group is shape-only-legal but the button never becomes selected.

<a id="D_buttongroup_coordination"></a>**D_buttongroup_coordination — Coordination flow per `consultButtonGroup`.** Every selection-bearing subclass override (`JToggleButton.setSelected`, `JCheckBoxMenuItem.setSelected` + `makeOnClick`, `JRadioButtonMenuItem.setSelected` + `makeOnClick`) prepends:

```java
b = consultButtonGroup(b);  // group veto + cascade
```

`consultButtonGroup(b)` is package-private on AbstractButton:
- If `buttonGroup == null`, returns `b` unchanged.
- Otherwise calls `group.setSelectedButton(this, b)` (cascades `oldSelection.setSelected(false)` when applicable) then returns `group.isSelectedButton(this)` (the group's verdict).

The group's `setSelectedButton(req, b)` mirrors JDK exactly: when `b == true && req != selectedButton`, swap the slot and cascade deselect; otherwise no-op. The "no-op on `b == false`" case is what suppresses click-to-deselect-current — the requester's own `setSelected` then re-reads `isSelectedButton(this)` (still true if it was the lone selection) and proceeds with the verdict, keeping itself selected.

For `makeOnClick` (menu items), the consult takes `!selected` (the proposed flip). ActionEvent fires unconditionally on click, even when the group veto suppresses the selection mutation — matches JDK shape where `DefaultButtonModel` fires Action regardless of group decision.

<a id="D_buttongroup_browser_click"></a>**D_buttongroup_browser_click — Browser-click coordination on JToggleButton.** The `JToggleButton(Component peer)` ctor's SJToggleButton bridge wires `addItemListener` to mirror surrogate model pulses into emulator state. Pre-D_buttongroup the bridge was a straight `this.selected = newSelected; fireItemStateChanged(...)`. Post-D_buttongroup the bridge consults the group on the proposed `newSelected` and re-reads the verdict; when the verdict differs (group veto), the bridge pushes the verdict back to the surrogate via guarded `sjt.setSelected(verdict)` — the re-entry into the bridge sees a `preventGroupCoord` flag set, absorbs the corrected state into `this.selected`, and skips both the second consult and the user-facing ItemEvent (no event fires for a vetoed bridge entry, matching JDK semantics where the model's net state didn't change). Cascade-deselect of the prior selection flows through `oldSelection.setSelected(false)` from inside `group.setSelectedButton`, which lands in the sibling's setSelected, walks through its own SJToggleButton peer's setSelected pulse, fires DESELECTED on the sibling's bridge, and updates the sibling's `this.selected = false`.

The push-back path produces a brief surrogate-model flicker (model pulses to false then back to true on a vetoed click) — an `:surrogates`-stage user code that subscribed to the SJToggleButton's own ItemListener directly would observe both pulses. Accepted R_match_swing_errors (a) — surrogate-stage migrators should use a Vaadin-native coordination shape instead of round-tripping a Swing ButtonGroup; documented in javadoc.

<a id="D_buttongroup_class_shape"></a>**D_buttongroup_class_shape — Lock-down / class shape.** `vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup` is non-final, matching JDK shape (user-code subclasses are rare but legal — the JDK class is non-final too). R_leaf_peer_lockdown doesn't apply — ButtonGroup has no peer.

**Rationale.**

- **Port, don't proxy.** Two alternatives considered: (a) a JDK-reuse + reflection adapter that bridges JDK `add(javax.swing.AbstractButton)` calls to ported AbstractButtons — rejected because it requires migrators to keep `import javax.swing.ButtonGroup;` past the rewrite (breaks the "mechanical import-swap" promise) and runs into JDK's package-private `Vector<AbstractButton>` field with no public mutator; (b) keep ButtonGroup in `javax.swing` per the "models stay JDK" rule — rejected because the migrator can't add a `vaadinx.swing.JRadioButtonMenuItem` to it (compile error, the testbed's actual blocker).
- **Coordination via `consultButtonGroup` hook on AbstractButton.** Two alternatives considered: (a) push the group consult into `JToggleButton`-only — rejected because JCheckBoxMenuItem and JRadioButtonMenuItem extend JMenuItem, not JToggleButton, so the consult would have to live in three places anyway; (b) make the group itself walk callbacks into siblings via a per-button observer pattern — rejected because the cascade depth is bounded (1 sibling deselected per click) and the JDK shape (`group.setSelected(model, b)` returns void; the model re-reads `isSelected(model)`) is exactly the simple pattern this consultButtonGroup mirrors.
- **Drop ButtonModel-taking methods, don't synthesize.** A synthetic `ButtonModel` proxy that wraps `selectedButton.isSelected()` is achievable. Rejected because: (a) the testbed's actual usage is `add()` only — `getSelection()` chains aren't exercised; (b) ButtonModel has ~14 methods and ~5 listener types, none of which are individually testbed-driven; (c) a stub-with-WARN signals the limitation honestly while keeping the door open to ship a real proxy if a target needs it. R_match_swing_errors (c) drop-and-WARN is the project's standard answer for "no Vaadin counterpart, no internal fan-out."

**Alternatives.**

- **Defer browser-click coordination on JToggleButton-in-group.** Considered. Rejected — the bridge is the natural place to consult the group, and the `preventGroupCoord` re-entry guard is small and bounded. Closing the surface in this slice avoids splitting D_buttongroup across two slices and avoids a half-implemented coordination path that would complicate the standalone `JRadioButton` work.
- **Coordinate at the surrogate (push group ref into SJToggleButton's ToggleButtonModel).** Rejected — surrogate would have to know about a `vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup` type, breaking [SD_shelper_statics](../surrogates/decisions.md)'s "no cross-module reach into emulator code" rule. The R_swing_is_truth emulator-side state authority handles this cleanly; the surrogate model stays group-agnostic and the bridge does the bookkeeping.
- **Throw on `getSelection()` instead of WARN-and-null.** Rejected per R_match_swing_errors — `getSelection()` is a JDK method that compiles and is idiomatic to call; throwing would crash code paths that defensively check for null. WARN-and-null lets the migrator's defensive-null-check pattern keep working.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **`getSelection() : ButtonModel` returns null.** Migrator code chaining `group.getSelection().isSelected()` NPEs. Fix: read selection via `Collections.list(group.getElements()).stream().filter(AbstractButton::isSelected).findFirst()` or via per-button `isSelected()` queries. R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c).
- **`isSelected(ButtonModel)` and `setSelected(ButtonModel, boolean)` are WARN-and-noop.** No way to translate the JDK ButtonModel argument to a ported AbstractButton. Migrators using these directly are rare (the JDK pattern is `add()` + auto-coordination); the WARN signals the gap. R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c).
- **Browser-click on JToggleButton-in-group double-pulses the surrogate model on a vetoed click.** A pure-`:surrogates`-stage user that registered an ItemListener on the SJToggleButton directly observes a `false → true` pulse for a click that was supposed to do nothing. Emulator-side `JToggleButton.addItemListener` users see no extra event (the bridge absorbs the re-entry without firing). R_match_swing_errors (a) — surrogate-stage coordination is out of scope; documented.
- **`JButton` in a group is shape-only-legal.** `g.add(jButton)` works (no error), `g.getButtonCount()` increments, `g.getElements()` returns it — but `jButton.isSelected()` is `EHelper.onNoop` and always returns false, so it never becomes the group's selection. Matches JDK shape (DefaultButtonModel for a JButton has `selected = false` and never flips except by `setSelected(true)` which JButton doesn't expose meaningfully).

**Validation.**

- `:emulators` test suite — `ButtonGroupTest` (~14 tests) covers construction, add/remove/clearSelection, getElements ordering, selection cascading on setSelected, click-to-deselect-current suppression, ctor-time selected handling on add, remove tearing down membership, getSelection / isSelected(ButtonModel) / setSelected(ButtonModel, boolean) drop-and-WARN, JButton-in-group shape-only behaviour, mixed JCheckBoxMenuItem + JRadioButtonMenuItem coordination.
- `:emulators` test suite — `JRadioButtonMenuItemTest` extension covers ButtonGroup-coordinated setSelected exclusion, click-cascade-deselect-prior-selection, and click-on-selected-radio suppressing the deselect (with ActionEvent still firing).
- `:emulators` test suite — `JCheckBoxMenuItemTest` extension covers ButtonGroup-coordinated cascade-deselect-prior-selection on click.
- `:emulators` test suite — `JCheckBoxTest` extension covers ButtonGroup-coordinated setSelected, browser-click bridge cascade-deselect, and browser-click bridge veto-of-click-to-deselect-current.
- Sampler `MenusPanel` route wraps Light/Dark JRadioButtonMenuItems in a ButtonGroup; `MenusWarnInventoryTest` user-path test asserts post-clickEveryLeaf that Light is deselected and Dark is selected (the cascade landed) with zero stub WARNs across the full path.

**Forward pointer.** D_buttongroup_coordination's peer-dispatch (the `instanceof com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJToggleButton` narrowing in JToggleButton's Item-bridge / setSelected / doClick) was generalised to `instanceof AbstractButtonMixin` per [D_jradiobutton](#D_jradiobutton) so SJRadioButton (and any future toggle-shaped surrogate) slots into the same toggle pipeline without per-peer branching. The mixed JCheckBox + JRadioButton ButtonGroup coordination case D_jradiobutton unlocks is the proof.

<a id="D_jradiobutton"></a>
## D_jradiobutton. JRadioButton emulator — thin shell over `SJRadioButton`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, JToggleButton peer-dispatch generalised to `AbstractButtonMixin` + `HasLabel`

JLawyer's properties-dialog priority selector + similar group-of-N radio surfaces (31 files in JLawyer) drive the lift; the surrogate [`SJRadioButton`](../surrogates/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/SJRadioButton.java) landed first per [D_surrogate_first](#D_surrogate_first), and this entry covers the emulator wrapping it.

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.JRadioButton extends vaadinx.swing.JToggleButton implements javax.accessibility.Accessible`. Eight JDK constructors all funnel through the root `JRadioButton(String, Icon, boolean)` which calls `super(new com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJRadioButton())`. All toggle behaviour (selection state, ItemEvent/ChangeEvent/ActionEvent fan-out, ButtonGroup veto via `consultButtonGroup`, doClick pulse, peer round-trip) inherits from JToggleButton — no JRadioButton-specific override surface beyond `getUIClassID()` returning `"RadioButtonUI"`, an empty `paramString()` chain (matches JDK), and the `getAccessibleContext` stub. The class isn't doing much itself; the work is in the peer ([SJRadioButton](../surrogates/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/SJRadioButton.java)) and in the D_abstractbutton_mixin_dispatch generalisation below.

<a id="D_abstractbutton_mixin_dispatch"></a>**D_abstractbutton_mixin_dispatch — JToggleButton peer-dispatch generalised to mixin interfaces.** Pre-D_jradiobutton the JToggleButton emulator narrowed on a concrete surrogate type in four spots:

- AbstractButton's ctor: `else if (peer instanceof com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJToggleButton sjt) { … Action + Change bridge … }`
- JToggleButton's ctor Item-bridge: `if (peer instanceof com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJToggleButton sjt) { … Item bridge with group coord … }`
- `JToggleButton.setSelected`: `if (peer instanceof com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJToggleButton sjt) { sjt.setSelected(b); }`
- `JToggleButton.doClick`: `if (peer instanceof com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJToggleButton sjt) { sjt.doClick(pressTime); }`
- `JToggleButton.setText`: `if (peer instanceof com.vaadin.flow.component.checkbox.Checkbox cb) { cb.setLabel(…); }`

SJRadioButton extends [`VaadinRadioButton`](../surrogates/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/VaadinRadioButton.java) (the public re-host of Vaadin's package-private `RadioButton` Java wrapper), **not** Vaadin `Checkbox`. None of the narrowed branches above would match an SJRadioButton peer, so JRadioButton's toggle pipeline would silently fall into the legacy non-surrogate fallback paths — broken (no Item bridge, setText writes nothing, setSelected goes through the legacy ValueChangeListener instead of the mixin's model pulse).

**Resolution.** Refactor the narrowing to dispatch on shared interfaces both surrogates already implement:

- `instanceof com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.swing.AbstractButtonMixin abm` — covers SJButton, SJToggleButton, SJCheckBox, SJRadioButton, and any future surrogate that adopts the mixin. The mixin's `addActionListener` / `addChangeListener` / `addItemListener` / `setSelected` / `doClick` defaults supply identical behaviour to the previous per-peer branches.
- `instanceof com.vaadin.flow.component.HasLabel hl` (in `JToggleButton.setText`) — covers Vaadin Checkbox AND VaadinRadioButton, both of which use a label-slot rather than HasText. SJButton's peer (Vaadin Button) is HasText, so AbstractButton's `instanceof HasText` branch handles it unchanged.

The legacy non-surrogate fallbacks (`instanceof ClickNotifier`, `instanceof Checkbox cb`) stay intact — protected-ctor users passing custom Vaadin components don't pay the mixin requirement.

**Headline coverage unlock.** Mixed-type ButtonGroups (JCheckBox + JRadioButton in one group, or JToggleButton + JRadioButton, etc.) coordinate correctly post-D_jradiobutton — pre-D_jradiobutton the JCheckBox sibling's bridge would install (matches SJToggleButton) but the JRadioButton sibling's bridge would silently skip (no match), so the group's mutex would be invisible to half its members. The `mixed JCheckBox plus JRadioButton in one ButtonGroup coordinate via D_jradiobutton mixin path` test under [`JRadioButtonTest`](../emulators/src/test/java/vaadinx/swing/JRadioButtonTest.java) pins this.

<a id="D_jradiobutton_lockdown"></a>**D_jradiobutton_lockdown — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** JRadioButton is a public Swing leaf — `javax.swing.JRadioButton` is final-shape (no public subclass in `javax.swing.*` ignoring `javax.swing.plaf.*` per R_leaf_peer_lockdown's L&F-exempt clause), and SJRadioButton is the settled canonical peer (landed in its surrogate slice). R_leaf_peer_lockdown stance applies: omit the protected `(Component peer)` ctor, root public ctor calls `super(new SJRadioButton())` directly, hard-coding the peer. User-code subclassing for behaviour (composite button rows, app-specific click wiring, ...) inherits the locked peer and works fine; user-code subclassing for custom rendering (`paintComponent` override, pluggable `BasicRadioButtonUI`) is permanently out of scope per R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b) — so the lock-down doesn't close any door that was open.

<a id="D_vaadin_radiobutton_rehost"></a>**D_vaadin_radiobutton_rehost — `VaadinRadioButton` re-host (peer scaffolding).** Vaadin ships `vaadin-radio-button` as a public web component but the Java wrapper `com.vaadin.flow.component.radiobutton.RadioButton` is **package-private** inside `vaadin-radio-button-flow.jar` (intended exclusively as `RadioButtonGroup`'s internal item class — its ctor, `setChecked`, and `setDisabled` are all package-scoped). We can't extend it. `:surrogates` re-hosts the web component as a public Java component [`VaadinRadioButton`](../surrogates/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/VaadinRadioButton.java) — `extends AbstractSinglePropertyField<…, Boolean>` bound to the `checked` property (mirrors how Vaadin's own private `RadioButton` uses `@Synchronize("checked-changed")`), plus a label-slot manager via `NativeLabel` in the `label` slot. Same precedent [`LongField`](../surrogates/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/LongField.java) follows for Vaadin's missing `long`-typed numeric field. General-purpose: any Vaadin code can use VaadinRadioButton standalone (no Group required) — SJRadioButton just happens to be the first consumer.

**Why the lift to mixin interfaces is honest, not over-abstracting.** The mixin generalisation isn't "design for future flexibility we don't need" (which CLAUDE.md's "no premature abstractions" guidance rejects); it's "the existing concrete narrowing is the artefact, not the principle." JToggleButton's Item-bridge / setSelected / doClick logic doesn't *care* what concrete class the peer is — it calls four methods (`addItemListener`, `setSelected`, `doClick`, and via setText `setLabel`), all of which are already on AbstractButtonMixin or HasLabel by design. The pre-D_jradiobutton `instanceof SJToggleButton` narrowing was just the easiest thing to write when SJToggleButton was the only mixin-shaped peer in existence. Now there's a second one, and the abstraction the code actually wanted lights up — costing zero new code (the mixin and HasLabel interfaces existed already) and saving the per-peer branch explosion that adding SJRadioButton-specific branches would have required.

**R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down implications for the test suite.** No tests need the `(Component peer)` ctor — Karibu locators find `_get<VaadinRadioButton>()` / `_get<SJRadioButton>()` against the locked-in peer directly. User-code attempting `new JRadioButton(customPeer)` wouldn't compile; the migration checklist already enumerates the no-protected-ctor leaves so migrators don't reach for it.

**Verifications.**

- `:surrogates` test suite — [`SJRadioButtonTest`](../surrogates/src/test/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/SJRadioButtonTest.java) (38 tests) covers the peer-side: ctors, default model = JToggleButton.ToggleButtonModel, programmatic setSelected (Item/Change fire, no Action, feedback-loop safety), doClick pulse (Item before Action), peer-originated toggle, model swap (push-wire teardown + reinstall), Action wiring, layout drop-and-WARN, R_match_swing_errors IAE on bad axis, icon WARN-and-drop, setEnabled PCE, happy-path zero-WARN.
- `:emulators` test suite — `JRadioButtonTest` (22 tests) covers the emulator-side: peer type (SJRadioButton + VaadinRadioButton), text routing via HasLabel, setSelected mirror-into-peer + peer-into-emulator, ItemEvent / ChangeEvent / ActionEvent fan-out at the emulator level, doClick canonical ordering (`item:SELECTED, action:toggle`), getSelectedObjects ItemSelectable contract, end-to-end user-click via hosted frame, UIClassID = "RadioButtonUI", four ButtonGroup integration scenarios (setSelected mutex, deselect-cascade fires DESELECTED on prior, browser-click bridge cascade, browser-click bridge veto), and the **mixed JCheckBox + JRadioButton ButtonGroup** test pinning D_abstractbutton_mixin_dispatch.
- `:emulators` test suite — existing JCheckBoxTest / JButtonTest / AbstractButtonTest / ButtonGroupTest / JCheckBoxMenuItemTest / JRadioButtonMenuItemTest all pass post-refactor — D_abstractbutton_mixin_dispatch's `instanceof AbstractButtonMixin` swap preserves the original SJButton / SJToggleButton / SJCheckBox behaviour exactly (mixin defaults call the same surrogate methods the per-peer narrowing did).

<a id="D_jeditorpane"></a>
## D_jeditorpane. JEditorPane emulator — over `SJEditorPane` (RTE), owns its content type and page, R_leaf_peer_lockdown keeps the protected peer ctor (JTextPane is a JDK subclass)

Editable HTML via a single `RichTextEditor` peer (Shape S) — surrogate-side decision [SD_sjeditorpane_rte](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjeditorpane_rte), emulator side D_jeditorpane_editable below. Editable by default like the JDK class; `setEditable(false)` puts the RTE in read-only mode. The former read-only-only `Div` peer (SD_sjeditorpane_div) is deleted.

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.JEditorPane extends vaadinx.swing.text.JTextComponent`. Four JDK ctors — `()`, `(String type, String text)`, `(URL)`, `(String url)` — all funnel through the protected `(Component peer)` seam with `new com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJEditorPane()` as the peer. `setText` overrides JTextComponent's base to push the markup into the peer's RTE `htmlValue` on top of the inherited Document write; `setEditable` forwards to the peer's `setReadOnly(!b)`. The content type and the page are the emulator's own, per D_setpage_fetch: no getter reads the peer ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). `addHyperlinkListener / removeHyperlinkListener` forward and drop-and-WARN (RTE has no clean anchor-activation hook — SD_sjeditorpane_rte). `setEditorKit / setEditorKitForContentType / createEditorKitForContentType` drop-and-WARN.

<a id="D_jeditorpane_keeps_peer_ctor"></a>**D_jeditorpane_keeps_peer_ctor — R_leaf_peer_lockdown status: non-leaf, keeps the protected `(Component peer)` ctor.** JDK [`javax.swing.JTextPane`](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/21/docs/api/java.desktop/javax/swing/JTextPane.html) extends `JEditorPane`, so JEditorPane is non-leaf in the *public* Swing hierarchy (ignoring `javax.swing.plaf.*` per R_leaf_peer_lockdown's L&F-exempt clause). Per R_leaf_peer_lockdown we keep the protected `(Component peer)` ctor open as the D_peer_ctor_injection seam for a future `JTextPane` emulator (or other subclass) to pass its own peer through. The class itself stays non-final to match JDK shape. If `JTextPane` lands later as its own slice, it picks its own surrogate and passes through this ctor.

<a id="D_document_rte_sync"></a>**D_document_rte_sync — two-way Document↔RTE sync (RTE is not a TextFieldBase).** The inherited `JTextComponent.setText` mutates the installed `Document` (PlainDocument by default). Its internal `docToPeer` sync narrows to `TextField`/`PasswordField`/`TextArea` peers — RTE is a `HasValue<String>` of HTML but **not** a `TextFieldBase`, so that base sync is a no-op here. JEditorPane wires both directions itself: `setText` calls `super.setText(t)` (user DocumentListeners fire) AND `peer.setText(t)` → RTE `htmlValue`, guarded by `preventPeerEvents` so the peer's own value-change listener doesn't re-mirror the write; the ctor subscribes `peer.addValueChangeListener` (EAGER, per R_swing_is_truth's "Document tracks typing") to mirror browser edits back into the Document under the same guard, wrapped in `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope). So `getText()` reflects user edits and DocumentListeners fire on them.

<a id="D_direct_document_mutation"></a>**D_direct_document_mutation — Direct Document mutation does NOT reach the peer.** A migrator calling `pane.getDocument().insertString(0, "foo", null)` mutates the inherited PlainDocument but the peer's `htmlValue` doesn't update — the `preventPeerEvents`-guarded push only fires from `setText` / the peer value-change bridge, not from arbitrary Document edits. JDK Swing handles this via an `HTMLEditorKit` + `HTMLDocument` pipeline that's permanently OOS per R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b) (an HTMLDocument's rendering is built around `View.paint(Graphics, ...)`). Setting text via `setText(String)` is the supported entry point. Documented in the JEditorPane class javadoc.

<a id="D_setpage_fetch"></a>**D_setpage_fetch — the content type is the installed kit's, the page is the document's, and `setPage` is the JDK's body.** The emulator holds what the JDK's kit and document hold. **Content type:** `setContentType` (final, as in the JDK) strips the parameter list, turns a `text/` type's `charset` parameter into the `"charset"` client property (which fires its PCE), and resolves the type against the four kits the JDK registers (`text/plain`, `text/html`, `text/rtf`, `application/rtf`; anything else — `"ADMIN"`, `"TEXT/HTML"` — gets a fresh plain kit). A different kit brings **its own new, empty document** — an `HTMLDocument` ([D_htmldocument](#D_htmldocument)), a `DefaultStyledDocument` for RTF, else a `PlainDocument` — so a `setText` before `setContentType` is lost, as on the desktop; the installed registered type again changes nothing, and an unregistered one swaps every time. `getContentType` answers the resolved type. `JTextPane` keeps its `StyledDocument` through a content-type change, since that document is what its peer renders ([D_jtextpane](#D_jtextpane)). **Page:** `getPage()` is the document's `StreamDescriptionProperty`, so a content-type change or `setDocument` clears it and `setText` does not. `setPage(URL)` throws `IOException("invalid url")` on null, skips the fetch when the URL is the same file as the loaded one (only scrolling to a reference), and otherwise opens the stream through the protected `getStream` hook — which, as in the JDK, sets the content type from the connection *before* the stream opens, so a missing file has already switched the type and emptied the document when its `FileNotFoundException` arrives — then reads into a new document of that kit carrying the connection's properties, and fires `"page"`. The JDK's reload idiom, clearing that property first, works; so the surrogate's always-re-fetch divergence ([SD_setpage_audit](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_setpage_audit)) no longer applies to stage 2. A URL with a reference calls `scrollToReference`, a WARN stub (no view geometry). `setPage(String)` throws `IOException("invalid url")` on null and `MalformedURLException` from `new URL(String)`. Decoding: the `"charset"` client property when set (a response's `charset` parameter arrives there through `setContentType`), else an HTML page's `<meta>` declaration, else UTF-8 — SD_setpage_audit's precedence; an unknown charset name throws the JDK's `UnsupportedEncodingException`. Links resolve against the emulator's own `getPage()`. All measured on JDK 25 and replayed by `JEditorPaneTest.contentTypeMatchesTheJdk` / `setPageMatchesTheJdk`.

**Accepted limitations.** The fetch runs on the server and synchronously; the JDK loads an HTML page on a `SwingWorker`, so its `"page"` event arrives after `setPage` returns, and here before. The JDK fires `"editorKit"` at every kit change; this pane has no kit objects to name, so it does not. `setEditorKit` still leaves the content type and the document alone (D_htmleditorkit). POST data (`PostDataProperty`) is not sent, and an HTML `<meta>` charset does not become the `"charset"` client property.

Three accepted divergences from JDK (mirrored on both layers):

- **Server-side fetch.** Vaadin server's network reach, not the browser's.
- **No async wiring.** Every fetch blocks the Vaadin request thread; migrators wrap in SwingWorker for non-blocking page loads.
- **No EditorKit dispatch.** Always renders as HTML regardless of `Content-Type`.

Full rationale and the "best-effort UTF-8 with header override" charset stance live in [SD_sjeditorpane_rte](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjeditorpane_rte) and the `SJEditorPane` class javadoc. The emulator-side carve-out is the Document mirror only.

<a id="D_jeditorpane_editable"></a>**D_jeditorpane_editable — editable mode via a single RTE peer (implemented).** `JEditorPane` peers over `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJEditorPane extends RichTextEditor` as its **single, unconditional** peer (surrogate-side [SD_sjeditorpane_rte](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjeditorpane_rte), which carries the full design + license experiment). RTE is read-only-capable via `setReadOnly(true)`, so one peer covers both `editable` states (including a runtime view↔edit toggle) and the mutable-`editable`-post-ctor wrinkle dissolves — the emulator's `setEditable` forwards to `peer.setReadOnly(!b)`. Rejected alternatives — *keep both peers dispatched by editable-intent* (breaks the view↔edit toggle, needs a fragile runtime peer-swap or an order-dependent lazy materialization, and the deleted Div's raw `innerHTML` was an XSS vector), opt-in `:emulators-richtext` + SPI, ctor try/catch fallback — are all recorded in SD_sjeditorpane_rte. `setText` pushes markup through the RTE `htmlValue` (lossy HTML subset per SD_sjeditorpane_rte — **tables/arbitrary CSS lost in display too**), and JDK `JTextPane` follows as a thin subclass (StyledDocument surface → R_match_swing_errors(c) WARN).

**API partition.**

- **Bucket A (R_swing_is_truth source-of-truth forwarding to peer).** `setText` (Document + RTE `htmlValue`), `setEditable` (→ `peer.setReadOnly(!b)`), `setContentType / getContentType` and `setPage(URL) / setPage(String) / getPage` (emulator-owned per D_setpage_fetch, the resolved type pushed to the peer and a loaded page pushed as markup), plus the peer→Document value-change bridge per D_document_rte_sync.
- **Bucket C (R_vaadin_first drop-and-WARN).** `addHyperlinkListener / removeHyperlinkListener` (forward to surrogate, which WARNs — no clean RTE anchor-activation hook, SD_sjeditorpane_rte); `setEditorKit / getEditorKit / setEditorKitForContentType / createEditorKitForContentType`. `setDocument / getDocument` are NOT in this bucket — they're inherited from JTextComponent and operate on the local PlainDocument (round-trip works).

**Accepted limitations.**

- **`createDefaultDocument` uses `PlainDocument`.** JDK JEditorPane picks an EditorKit-driven document per content type (`HTMLDocument` for `text/html`). Our `createDefaultDocument` delegates to `super.createDefaultDocument()` (`PlainDocument`). The Document isn't the rendering source (the peer's RTE `htmlValue` is); PlainDocument as backing store means `getText()` round-trips the markup as a plain string — which is what callers using `getText()` for read-back actually want.
- **Lossy HTML subset in display and edit (SD_sjeditorpane_rte).** The RTE peer renders/accepts only its Quill subset — no tables, no arbitrary CSS, base64-only images. The emulator's Document keeps the faithful markup so `getText()` is exact, but the *rendered* peer is lossy — a genuine regression from the deleted Div peer, accepted as consistent + immediately visible (R_best_effort_behaviour/R_layouts_close_enough).

**Verifications.**

- `:surrogates` test suite — [`SJEditorPaneTest`](../surrogates/src/test/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/SJEditorPaneTest.java) (16 tests) covers the RTE peer per SD_sjeditorpane_rte.
- `:emulators` test suite — `JEditorPaneTest` (18 tests) covers the emulator side: peer-type pin via `assertIs<SJEditorPane>`, all four ctors (URL forms synchronously fetch via setPage; unreachable URL propagates IOException), two-layer setText push verified through both `pane.text` (Document) and the peer's RTE `value`, the peer→Document edit sync (a value-change on the RTE mirrors into the Document + fires DocumentListeners), setEditable→readOnly + PCE, contentType forwarding, HyperlinkListener WARN, setPage / getPage round-trip via classpath HTML fixture, EditorKit WARN paths, R_leaf_peer_lockdown protected-ctor subclass with non-SJEditorPane peer.
- `:sampler` test suite — [`EditorPanesWarnInventoryTest`](../sampler/src/test/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/sampler/EditorPanesWarnInventoryTest.java) (2 tests) — user-path navigation + an editable value-change driving the peer→Document sync + API-surface micro-driver, both assert zero stub WARN end-to-end.

<a id="D_jtoolbar"></a>
## D_jtoolbar. JToolBar emulator — the JDK's fields and bodies over an `SJToolBar` peer; separators are `JToolBar.Separator` children

Surrogate-side decision: [SD_sjtoolbar](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjtoolbar).

**`vaadinx.swing.JToolBar extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent` implements `SwingConstants` + `Accessible`** — matches JDK shape. It holds the JDK's four fields under the JDK's names (`paintBorder`, `margin`, `floatable`, `orientation`) and keeps `rollover` in the client-property table, as the JDK does, so every getter answers without the peer ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). The `SJToolBar` peer is told the current orientation and margin after each change and is never read back.

**R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `javax.swing.JToolBar` is a leaf in the public Swing hierarchy — `JToolBar.Separator` extends `JSeparator`, not `JToolBar`; nothing else in `javax.swing.*` extends it. All four ctors funnel into `JToolBar(String, int)`, which calls `super(new SJToolBar(orientation))` after running the JDK's orientation check, then `setName(name)` unconditionally and `updateUI()` — the JDK's order, bar the check moving ahead of `setName` because `super` must come first.

**The bodies are the JDK's.** `setOrientation` checks before its change guard, so an invalid value throws even when nothing would change; `setMargin` is unguarded, so a repeated `null` fires; `getMargin()` answers a fresh zero `Insets` while none is set, never `null`; `getComponentAtIndex` answers `null` out of range rather than throwing; `addImpl` turns a `Separator` perpendicular to the toolbar and makes a `JButton` non-default-capable; `createActionComponent` hides an icon Action's text, places the text centred below the icon, and takes its Action listener from the protected `createActionChangeListener` hook; `paramString` appends `floatable`, `margin`, `orientation`, `paintBorder` in that order. `JToolBarTest.toolBarMatchesTheJdk` replays the measured sequence.

**Separators are `JToolBar.Separator` children, as in the JDK.** `addSeparator(size)` adds `new JToolBar.Separator(size)`, so separators occupy component indices, show up in `getComponents()`, and render through their own `SJSeparator` peer as the same thin bar a `JSeparator` draws. The size is stored and read back — a separator built without one gets the L&F's 10×10 as a plain `Dimension`, which is what the desktop's `BasicToolBarSeparatorUI` ends up installing — and not rendered (R_layouts_close_enough). `SJToolBar.addSeparator` stays the stage-3 API and is not used here.

**Orientation turns the separators, as the L&F does.** `setOrientation` runs `BasicToolBarUI`'s `"orientation"` listener — every `Separator` child turns perpendicular and a non-square size swaps its sides — ahead of the fire. On the desktop that listener is registered before any app listener, so the order an app's `PropertyChangeListener` observes is the same: the separators' events first, then the toolbar's. It belongs to the L&F, not to `JToolBar`, and is reproduced anyway because every desktop L&F inherits it and a vertical toolbar with vertical bars is a structural misrender (R_layouts_close_enough).

**floatable / borderPainted / rollover: the effect is declined, state and events kept** (R_decline_effect_only). None has a Vaadin counterpart — no detachable toolbars in a browser, no rollover toggle, no painted-border flag distinct from the CSS border — so `SJToolBar` does not declare them at all (SD_sjtoolbar), while the emulator stores, fires and revalidates exactly as the JDK does. JLawyer calls `setFloatable(false)` + `setRollover(true)` on every toolbar, which is why none of them WARNs.

**Not ported:** `DefaultToolBarLayout` and the `setLayout` override that unhooks it. `SJToolBar` pins its flex flow per orientation instead.

**API partition.**

- **Bucket A (real impl, pushed to the peer).** Orientation, margin; separators and child management through the inherited `Container.add(...)`.
- **Bucket A (real impl, emulator-only).** All four ctors, floatable / rollover / borderPainted, `add(Action)` + `createActionComponent` + `createActionChangeListener`, `addImpl`, `getComponentIndex` / `getComponentAtIndex`, `JToolBar.Separator`, `paramString`.
- **Bucket C (drop-and-WARN).** `getUI` / `setUI` (L&F surgery not modelled), `getAccessibleContext`.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **The Action listener is strong-ref.** Real Swing's default is a weak-ref `PropertyChangeListener`; `AbstractButton.createActionPropertyChangeListener` here holds the button strongly, bounded by the session's lifetime. Changes to the Action still reach the button.
- **`setLayout` on the emulator is a noop store.** `Container.setLayout` writes to `layoutMgr` and invalidates; the value has no visible effect on the toolbar's pinned-flex CSS (the surrogate's `setLayout` override would WARN on this, but the emulator's `Container.setLayout` doesn't reach the surrogate — it stores on the emulator side). Migrators calling `toolbar.setLayout(BoxLayout)` get a silent noop store; the visual output stays pinned-flex. R_layouts_close_enough close-enough — typical toolbar use doesn't customise the layout manager.

**Verifications.**

- `:surrogates` test suite — [`SJToolBarTest`](../surrogates/src/test/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/surrogates/SJToolBarTest.java) (22 tests) covers the peer-side per SD_sjtoolbar.
- `:emulators` test suite — [`JToolBarTest`](../emulators/src/test/java/vaadinx/swing/JToolBarTest.java) covers the emulator side, `toolBarMatchesTheJdk` replaying the measured JDK sequence (margin events, `defaultCapable`, separator children and their orientation flip); `EmulatorOwnedStateTest.jToolBarAndJSeparator` reads the getters off the UI thread.
- `:sampler` test suite — [`ToolBarsWarnInventoryTest`](../sampler/src/test/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/sampler/ToolBarsWarnInventoryTest.java) (2 tests) — user-path navigation across the 3-demo panel (horizontal / vertical / margin toolbars) + 4 button clicks including the `add(Action)`-wired button + API-surface micro-driver, both assert zero stub WARN end-to-end.

<a id="D_jsplitpane"></a>
## D_jsplitpane. JSplitPane emulator — thin shell over `SJSplitPane`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, field-shadow cluster for no-counterpart knobs, addImpl constraint dispatch

Surrogate-side decision: [SD_sjsplitpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjsplitpane).

**`vaadinx.swing.JSplitPane extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent`** — matches JDK shape. Thin delegating shell over `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJSplitPane` for everything that has a peer-side counterpart (orientation, slot setters, divider double-form, resetToPreferredSizes); emulator-only field shadows for the six JDK knobs whose round-trip lives only on this layer.

**R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `javax.swing.JSplitPane` is a leaf in the public Swing hierarchy. All five ctors call `super(new SJSplitPane(orientation))` directly — no protected `(Component peer)` ctor. User-code subclasses inherit the locked peer. Same shape as JToolBar / JEditorPane / JPanel.

**Ctor matrix — funnels through `JSplitPane(int orientation, boolean continuousLayout, Component left, Component right)`:**

| Emulator ctor | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `JSplitPane()` | `this(HORIZONTAL_SPLIT, false, null, null)` (JDK default) |
| `JSplitPane(int orientation)` | `this(orientation, false, null, null)` |
| `JSplitPane(int orientation, boolean continuousLayout)` | `this(orientation, continuousLayout, null, null)` |
| `JSplitPane(int orientation, Component left, Component right)` | `this(orientation, false, left, right)` |
| `JSplitPane(int orientation, boolean continuousLayout, Component left, Component right)` | `super(new SJSplitPane(orientation))` + `setContinuousLayout(continuousLayout)` + slot setters if non-null |

Orientation validation lives in `SJSplitPane`'s ctor (`IllegalArgumentException` matches JDK). Re-validating on the emulator side would double-throw without value.

**Field-shadow cluster — JDK knobs without a Vaadin counterpart, round-trip lives here.** Six fields ride the emulator: `dividerLocation` (int, -1 sentinel), `lastDividerLocation` (int, -1), `resizeWeight` (double, 0.0), `oneTouchExpandable` (boolean, false), `continuousLayout` (boolean, false — JDK default), `dividerSize` (int, 0 — JDK installs L&F-derived value, we use 0 since no L&F). Getters round-trip; setters update the field + fire the JDK-named PCE on actual change (`"dividerLocation"`, `"lastDividerLocation"`, `"resizeWeight"`, `"oneTouchExpandable"`, `"continuousLayout"`, `"dividerSize"`). No peer touch — Vaadin SplitLayout doesn't expose Java-side knobs for any of these.

Same shape SD_sjbutton/SD_toggle_checkbox_first_cut/D_jtoolbar take for state-conditional button surface (icons, borderPaintedFlat, floatable). The choice is deliberate per SD_sjsplitpane's "present-but-drops" partition: the surrogate also exposes the setters (logs and drops), so pure-surrogate code that calls them gets a WARN and the JDK default back; emulator round-trip closes the gap for stage-2 callers without re-surfacing the WARN.

**`setDividerLocation(int pixel)` — emulator round-trip, surrogate drops.** Per SD_sjsplitpane the surrogate-side `setDividerLocation(int)` is blocked-upstream drop-and-WARN (no faithful translation to Vaadin's percent without container width). The emulator does NOT forward to the peer — it just updates the field shadow and fires `"dividerLocation"` PCE. Testbed code `outerSplit.setDividerLocation(240)` records 240 as the field value but the splitter's visual position stays at Vaadin's default (50/50) until a `setDividerLocation(double)` or drag arrives.

**`setDividerLocation(double 0–1)` — forwards to peer.** Multiplies by 100 and calls `peer.setSplitterPosition`. Does NOT update the int field (different semantic — JDK's proportional form doesn't pre-compute a pixel value). No PCE fired here either — Vaadin gives us percent strings on drag-end which we can't translate to JDK's expected Integer pixels (drop-and-WARN drag-end PCE per SD_sjsplitpane).

**`resetToPreferredSizes()` — forwards + resets shadow.** Calls the surrogate's `resetToPreferredSizes()` (snaps splitter to 50/50) AND resets the emulator's `dividerLocation` field to `-1` + fires `"dividerLocation"` PCE if the prior value was non-(-1). Matches JDK's "snap back to compute-from-children" sentinel reset.

**`addImpl(Component, Object, int)` constraint dispatch.** Override of `Container.addImpl` recognises JDK's slot-constraint strings and routes to the slot setters:

- `JSplitPane.LEFT` (`"left"`) or `JSplitPane.TOP` (`"top"`) → `setLeftComponent(comp)`.
- `JSplitPane.RIGHT` (`"right"`) or `JSplitPane.BOTTOM` (`"bottom"`) → `setRightComponent(comp)`.
- `JSplitPane.DIVIDER` (`"divider"`) → drop-and-WARN (Vaadin owns its splitter glyph; SD_sjsplitpane §"No JSplitPane.Separator …").
- `null` constraint → first add lands as left, second as right, third+ drops-and-WARN (JDK throws IllegalArgumentException on overflow — we soften to WARN per R_match_swing_errors minor-gap policy since the testbed and JLawyer real code use explicit slot setters).

<a id="D_jsplitpane_slot_tree_shape"></a>**D_jsplitpane_slot_tree_shape — Slot setters maintain `Container.components` for R_swing_is_truth tree-shape fidelity** (sibling fix to [D_shadow_children_tree_shape](#D_jscrollpane)). `setLeftComponent` and `setRightComponent` use `Container.addSlotChild` / `removeSlotChild` to mirror the slot occupant into the components list, so `JSplitPane.getComponentCount()` returns 2 when both slots are filled (matching JDK) and the slot occupants report `getParent() == this`. The Vaadin DOM under the SplitLayout peer is unchanged — `SplitLayout.setPrimaryComponent` / `setSecondaryComponent` own the peer-side child slots; the AWT-side `components` list and the Vaadin-side slots are separate edges, both maintained per R_swing_is_truth. Replacement matches JDK's `super.addImpl`-after-`super.remove` ordering: replacing the left slot detaches the old occupant and appends the new one at the end, so a `right`-then-`new-left` sequence lands as `[right, newLeft]` rather than `[newLeft, right]`. `validateTree` retains the explicit `.validate()` recursion into the two slots (handles the non-Container-child edge case `super.validateTree` skips).

**API partition.**

- **Bucket A (real impl, forwards to peer).** `setOrientation` / `getOrientation`, `setLeftComponent` / `setRightComponent` / `setTopComponent` / `setBottomComponent` + getters, `setDividerLocation(double)`, `resetToPreferredSizes` (with shadow reset).
- **Bucket A (real impl, emulator-only).** All five ctors, six field-shadow setters/getters (`dividerLocation` int, `lastDividerLocation`, `resizeWeight`, `oneTouchExpandable`, `continuousLayout`, `dividerSize`), `addImpl` constraint dispatch, `paramString` tail.
- **Bucket C (drop-and-WARN).** `getMinimumDividerLocation()` / `getMaximumDividerLocation()` (no server-side coordinates — R_layouts_close_enough), `getUI` / `setUI` (L&F surgery not modelled), `getAccessibleContext`.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **`setDividerLocation(int)` produces no visible effect.** Field round-trips and PCE fires; splitter visual stays at Vaadin's default. Documented in javadoc + WARN on the surrogate side. Lifts if Vaadin grows a pixel-based splitter API or a real migration target needs it.
- **Drag-end doesn't fire `"dividerLocation"` PCE.** Vaadin gives us a percent string; JDK expects Integer pixels; no faithful translation. Migration code listening for the PCE doesn't get notified on user drags. Same blocked-upstream lift criterion as the int form.
- ~~`getComponentCount()` returns 0~~ — fixed in D_jsplitpane_slot_tree_shape. Slot occupants now enter `Container.components` via `Container.addSlotChild`; post-ctor count is 2 with both slots filled. (Pre-D_jsplitpane_slot_tree_shape limitation retained here as a one-line history marker per the project's "edit in place, preserve cross-refs" convention.)

**Verifications.**

- `:surrogates` test suite — `SJSplitPaneTest` covers the peer-side per SD_sjsplitpane.
- `:emulators` test suite — `JSplitPaneTest` covers the emulator-side: peer-type pin via `assertIs<SJSplitPane>`, all five ctors, orientation forwarding + IAE propagation, slot setters with replace semantics, six emulator-only field shadows with PCE round-trip and zero peer touch, `setDividerLocation(double)` percent translation, `resetToPreferredSizes` shadow reset + PCE on prior non-sentinel, `addImpl` LEFT/RIGHT/TOP/BOTTOM dispatch, DIVIDER drop-and-WARN, L&F surface, paramString chain. D_jsplitpane_slot_tree_shape tree-shape: slot setters populate `Container.components` in JDK order, ctor with both slots pre-populates, replace detaches old and appends new (`[right, newLeft]` ordering), `setLeftComponent(null)` detaches, `add(c, LEFT)` enters the components list.
- `:sampler` test suite — `SplitPanesWarnInventoryTest` (2 tests) — user-path navigation (3-demo panel: nested outer-horizontal/inner-vertical mirroring the JLawyer-shape testbed) + API-surface micro-driver, both assert zero stub WARN end-to-end across the WARN-free portion of the API. Expected-WARN paths (`setDividerLocation(int)`, six no-counterpart setters) covered in per-class unit tests.

---

<a id="D_jtabbedpane"></a>
## D_jtabbedpane. JTabbedPane emulator — owns its pages and selection model over `SJTabbedPane`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, the JDK's tab management and `add` overloads

Surrogate-side decision: [SD_sjtabbedpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjtabbedpane).

**`vaadinx.swing.JTabbedPane extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent`** — matches JDK shape. **The pane owns its state, as the JDK's does** ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)): a list of per-tab `TabPage`s (the JDK's private `Page` — title, icon, disabled icon, tooltip, colours, enabled, mnemonic, displayed mnemonic index, content, tab component), the protected `model` / `changeListener` / `changeEvent` / `tabPlacement` fields, and the private `tabLayoutPolicy` and visible component. `insertTab`, `removeTabAt`, `removeAll`, `setComponentAt`, `setTabComponentAt`, the selection methods, the index lookups and the per-tab setters and getters are the JDK's bodies over them, so no getter reads the peer. Each setter then pushes to `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJTabbedPane` through `withPeer`.

**The selection model is not shared with the surrogate**, unlike the pilot's shared models. `SJTabbedPane` is the stage-3 JTabbedPane, so its structural methods shift its own model the way the JDK's `insertTab` / `removeTabAt` do. Sharing one model would give it two writers, and the surrogate's writes would fire the emulator's listeners inside its hop. So the surrogate keeps a private model, and the emulator keeps a listener on its own model that pushes the selected index into it after every change, whoever made it (a worker's `getModel().setSelectedIndex` included). The listener is registered before `changeListener`, so it runs after it, where BasicTabbedPaneUI's repaint runs. An index the pane has no tab for, which the JDK lets a model hold, shows no tab. A browser tab click runs `setSelectedIndex` in a `callSwing` fiber, as BasicTabbedPaneUI's mouse handler does, only for a different, non-negative index. A listener that puts the selection back is flushed to the peer like any other change. `preventPeerEvents` keeps the `SelectedChangeEvent` echoes of the emulator's own peer writes out of that path. The model notifies on the mutating thread, so a worker's switch fires the pane's `ChangeListener`s on the worker (`JTabbedPaneBackgroundModelTest`).

**Measured on JDK 25 and pinned by `JTabbedPaneTest.tabManagementMatchesTheJdk`**, the bodies restore what delegation had lost:

- **Visibility.** `insertTab` hides a new tab's content, and `fireStateChanged` shows the selected tab's content and hides the one shown before, so `isVisible()` is `false` on every unselected tab's content and a `ComponentListener` hears `componentShown` / `componentHidden` — the lazy-load-on-first-show idiom. `removeTabAt` shows the removed content again. The JDK's focus hand-over to the new content is not reproduced.
- **Events.** Removing the selected tab in the middle fires a `ChangeEvent` from the pane without a model change. `removeAll` deselects first and fires once. `removeTabAt` sets the `__index_to_remove__` client property, and the next removal of a content component clears it, as BasicTabbedPaneUI's `ContainerListener` does before any migrator's listener. `setMnemonicAt` fires `"displayedMnemonicIndexAt"` before `"mnemonicAt"`, and `setTitleAt` fires it when the underlined character moves.
- **`Container.components` is in insertion order**, as the JDK's `insertTab` appends through `addImpl`. Tab indices and child indices differ after an insert, which is why `getComponentAt` / `indexOfComponent` read the pages. A tab without content has an index, and `indexOfComponent(null)` finds it.
- **Moves and errors.** Inserting a component already in the pane moves its tab. A `null` title reads back as `""`, and `indexOfTab(null)` finds it. `setTabComponentAt` throws the JDK's `IllegalArgumentException` for a tab's content and moves a header that is already another tab's. `getComponentAt` and the per-tab getters throw the JDK's `IndexOutOfBoundsException` instead of answering `null`. `setComponentAt(null)` leaves the tab without content, where it used to WARN.
- **Mnemonics are stored:** `getMnemonicAt` answers `-1` by default and the stored key after that, and `setDisplayedMnemonicIndexAt` throws the JDK's `IllegalArgumentException` for an index outside the title. The surrogate still declines the keyboard effect.

**The JDK's `add` overloads, not `addImpl`.** The JDK overrides all five `add(...)` overloads, and so does the emulator: a `String` constraint is the title, an `Icon` the icon, anything else (an `Integer` included) is ignored and the tab appended under the component's name; `add(component, index)` inserts. `remove(Component)` and `remove(int)` remove a tab — `remove(int)` takes a tab index, not a child index. A `javax.swing.plaf.UIResource` is added as a plain child, as in the JDK.

**R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `javax.swing.JTabbedPane` is a leaf in the public Swing hierarchy (`javax.swing.plaf.*` excluded). All three ctors validate placement and policy with the JDK's messages, then call `super(new SJTabbedPane(...))` — no protected `(Component peer)` ctor. The ctor then runs the JDK's `setTabPlacement` / `setTabLayoutPolicy` / `setModel(new DefaultSingleSelectionModel())`, so `createChangeListener()` (returning the ported protected `ModelListener`) is reached. The surrogate holds both values from its ctor, so construction pushes nothing and stays WARN-free.

**Custom tab headers are not children.** A `setTabComponentAt` component lives in its `TabPage` and never enters `Container.components`. The JDK's BasicTabbedPaneUI adds a tab-container child to hold them. That child is L&F, and it is not reproduced.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **Non-TOP placement is visual no-op.** `setTabPlacement(LEFT/RIGHT/BOTTOM)` stores the field and fires `"tabPlacement"`; the surrogate WARNs and renders on top — Vaadin TabSheet has no placement knob. R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a) blocked-upstream.
- **WRAP_TAB_LAYOUT not delivered.** Vaadin scrolls the strip on overflow and has no wrap mode, so `getTabRunCount()` answers 1 while there are tabs, where the JDK's L&F counts rows from the pixel layout. R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a).
- **A disabled tab cannot be shown selected.** The model may point at a disabled tab, as in the JDK; Vaadin TabSheet refuses to select it, so the peer shows the previous tab (or none after a removal). R_best_effort_behaviour.
- **`getDisabledIconAt` answers only what was set.** The JDK's L&F derives a greyed icon when none was; with no L&F there is none to derive.
- **`getBoundsAt` / `indexAtLocation` WARN and answer `null` / `-1`** — no server-side tab geometry (R_layouts_close_enough).
- **The model has one listener more than the JDK's** — the peer flush — so `getModel().getChangeListeners()` is one longer.
- **`fireStateChanged`'s focus hand-over is not ported** — the JDK moves focus into the newly selected tab's content when the old selection held it.

**Verifications.** `JTabbedPaneTest` (the replayed JDK script, the peer following every selection change, a browser click running `setSelectedIndex` in a UI fiber with a veto flushed back, shown / hidden events, the `add` / `remove` overloads); `JTabbedPaneBackgroundModelTest`; `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest.jTabbedPane`; `PropertyFanoutTest`'s `indexForTitle` / `indexForNullComponent` / `mnemonicAt` pins; `:sampler`'s `TabbedPanesWarnInventoryTest` (user path + API driver, zero stub WARNs).

<a id="D_jlist"></a>
## D_jlist. JList emulator — over `SJList`, owning its models, R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, ListSelection + Mouse re-source, JDK `ListCellRenderer` bridge

Surrogate-side decision: [SD_sjlist](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjlist).

**`vaadinx.swing.JList<E> extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent implements javax.swing.Scrollable, javax.accessibility.Accessible`** — matches JDK shape. **The list owns its state, as the JDK's does**: `dataModel` and `selectionModel` are emulator fields, the model, selection-model and selection methods are the JDK's bodies over them, and no getter reads the peer ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). `createSelectionModel()` is the JDK's constructor hook, and a subclass override is reached. Both model objects are shared with `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJList` and pushed to it through `withPeer`. The surrogate renders the model, mirrors the selection onto the Grid, writes a browser selection into the selection model, and shifts the selection when rows are inserted or removed. That shift is the JDK's `BasicListUI` behaviour, not `JList`'s, so it stays surrogate-side, inside its model hop. Measured on JDK 25 and pinned by `JListTest.selectionMatchesTheJdk`, the bodies reproduce what delegation had lost. `setSelectedIndex(-1)` does not clear (`DefaultListSelectionModel` ignores it), so neither does `setSelectedValue` with an absent value, and re-selecting the selected value does nothing. `setModel` fires `"model"` before the clearing `ListSelectionEvent`. `setListData` goes through `setModel`, so it fires `"model"` too, and a subclass's `setModel` override runs. Null arguments throw the JDK's `IllegalArgumentException`, not the surrogate's NPE. And `new JList()` holds the JDK's empty `AbstractListModel`, not a `DefaultListModel`, so a migrated `(DefaultListModel) list.getModel()` cast fails as it does on the desktop. `indexToLocation` / `getCellBounds` answer `null` without asking the peer (R_layouts_close_enough); `locationToIndex` still reads the surrogate's click stash.

**R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `javax.swing.JList` is a leaf in the public Swing hierarchy. All four public ctors funnel through a private `(SJList<E> peer)` ctor — no protected `(Component peer)` ctor.

**Two-layer re-source (JComboBox/JTable shape).** Two bridges installed in the ctor re-source surrogate events to the emulator's own `listenerList` with the source rebound to `this`:

1. **`ListSelectionListener`** — the JDK's `ListSelectionHandler` on the selection model fires `fireSelectionValueChanged`, so `list.addListSelectionListener(...)` sees `source == this JList`. As in the JDK it is registered by the first `addListSelectionListener`, which decides its place among the model's own listeners, and `setSelectionModel` moves it. It relays through `EHelper.relayModelEvent`, so a browser selection, which the surrogate writes from a peer listener with no UI fiber, reaches the listener in one (SD_background_model_hop).
2. **`SMouseListener`** — the surrogate's `MOUSE_CLICKED` (driven by Grid item-click / item-double-click, carrying the browser click count) re-sources to a `vaadinx.awt.event.MouseEvent` dispatched via the inherited `processMouseEvent`, so `list.addMouseListener(...)` + `e.getClickCount() == 2` + `locationToIndex(point)` (the double-click-to-open idiom) works as written. `locationToIndex` answers the clicked index, which the emulator reads off the surrogate's item click and holds for the whole dispatch of the mouse event it caused — the surrogate's own stash (SD_sjlist) is restored when its synchronous fan-out returns, which is the moment a handler parked on a modal dialog yields, so reading it had answered `-1` after every such park. The rest is `BasicListUI.locationToIndex`, which every desktop L&F inherits and which was measured on JDK 25: a null location throws, and the answer is the closest cell, so a list shrunk during the dispatch answers its last row and an empty one `-1`. `-1` outside a dispatch (R_layouts_close_enough).
