**Renderer bridge (D_event_port_policy + D_jcombobox + R_vaadin_first).** The JDK `ListCellRenderer` surface lives on the emulator (its `getListCellRendererComponent` returns `vaadinx.awt.Component`, clashing with `java.awt.Component`). A dynamic Vaadin `ComponentRenderer` installed once on the surrogate resolves the current `cellRenderer` per render call, invokes `getListCellRendererComponent(this, value, index, isSelected, false)` — **passing the JList instance as the `list` arg** (D_jcombobox's list-arg, `null` from the JComboBox bridge, is now non-null here; renderers that down-cast `(JList) list` work) — and snapshots the result via `JComboBox.snapshotRendererOutput` (mutate-and-return-self → fresh Vaadin component). Default renderer is `DefaultListCellRenderer`; `setCellRenderer` swaps the field + `refreshAll` (no re-install — the closure reads the field live) + fires `cellRenderer` PCE.

**No-counterpart knobs — emulator-only R_swing_is_truth field shadows.** `layoutOrientation`, `visibleRowCount`, `fixedCellWidth/Height`, `selectionForeground/Background`, `dragEnabled` have no peer property, so the emulator field-shadows them (JDK-faithful round-trip + PCE) rather than delegating to the surrogate, which drops them per R_vaadin_first (SD_sjlist). This is the asymmetric R_swing_is_truth-shadow split of SJToolBar (D_jtoolbar) / JSplitPane (D_jsplitpane) — the emulator is the JDK-API-faithful layer (R_swing_is_truth), the surrogate is Vaadin-first (R_vaadin_first). `setLayoutOrientation` wrap modes and `setDragEnabled(true)` still WARN (real feature gaps); the rest round-trip silently (R_layouts_close_enough sizing/chrome). The selection-mode int is read back from the JDK selection model (no shadow on either layer).

**Scrollable (R_layouts_close_enough close-enough).** `getPreferredScrollableViewportSize` computes from the emulator's own `visibleRowCount` × cell height (dummy 16 when unfixed); unit/block increments and `getScrollableTracksViewport*` return JDK-shaped best-effort. Vaadin Grid owns real layout.

**Accepted limitations.** A selection model in `SINGLE_SELECTION` mode installed through `createSelectionModel` or `setSelectionModel` does not switch the Grid to single select, because only `setSelectionMode` pushes the mode. `getSelectedValues()` (deprecated since 1.7, and common in older code) is absent. The selection shift on insert / remove is `BasicListUI`'s, so it stays surrogate-side and its `ListSelectionEvent` fires inside the surrogate's hop rather than on the mutating thread.

**Verifications.**

- `:surrogates` — `SJListTest` (26 tests) covers the peer-side per SD_sjlist.
- `:emulators` — `JListTest` (16 tests): peer-type pin via `assertIs<SJList>`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown reflection check, ctors + `setListData`, selection delegation, `setSelectionMode` PCE, two-layer `addListSelectionListener` source-rebound (incl. across `setSelectionModel` swap), default + custom `ListCellRenderer` rendering via Karibu `_getCellComponent` (snapshot bridge), double-click + single-click re-source with `clickCount` + `locationToIndex`, `locationToIndex` after a parked handler and `BasicListUI`'s clamp and NPE, layout/sizing PCE, Scrollable, `getUIClassID`.
- `:sampler` — `ListsWarnInventoryTest` (2 tests): user-path (add / select / double-click-to-open via `_doubleClickItem` / remove, with a custom `DefaultListCellRenderer` subclass + a `JScrollPane`-wrapped list exercising the auto-scroll guard) + JList API-surface micro-driver, both assert zero stub WARN. `NavigationSmokeTest` extended with the Lists route.

<a id="D_clipboard"></a>
## D_clipboard. Clipboard — emulator-only `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit` + `WebClipboard` subclass of `java.awt.datatransfer.Clipboard`, helper JS as servlet-served static resource, VT-park on the read leg, secure-context missing throws

**Decision.** Cross-cutting, slotted before JPopupMenu because the popup's "copy path" entry needs it. Clipboard support lands emulator-only, with **no `:surrogates` counterpart** — first cross-cutting capability where the "no surrogate by design" stance follows SD_no_sjoptionpane's precedent for a different reason: there is no Vaadin `Component` to extend (`navigator.clipboard` is a browser API surface, not a Vaadin component). `java.awt.datatransfer.*` (`DataFlavor`, `Transferable`, `StringSelection`, `ClipboardOwner`, `FlavorListener`) is reused unchanged from the JDK per [D_whitelist_porting](#D_whitelist_porting) — none reference Component, all sit comfortably outside the port surface. Two new types only:

1. **`vaadinx.awt.Toolkit`** — entry point with a single static `getSystemClipboard()` returning a per-UI `WebClipboard`. Mirrors `java.awt.Toolkit.getSystemClipboard()` as the import-swap target; the rest of `java.awt.Toolkit`'s surface is not ported (per [D_whitelist_porting](#D_whitelist_porting) — most of it references AWT internals we don't carry, and migrated apps reach for `Toolkit` almost exclusively for the clipboard accessor). *(Superseded by [D_toolkit_full_surface](#D_toolkit_full_surface): `Toolkit` is now a full-surface emulator, and `getSystemClipboard()` is a JDK-faithful **instance** method reached via the global `getDefaultToolkit()` singleton — not static.)*
2. **`vaadinx.awt.datatransfer.WebClipboard extends java.awt.datatransfer.Clipboard`** — overrides `setContents(Transferable, ClipboardOwner)` and `getContents(Object)` to round-trip through the browser via `Page.executeJs` to a small static-resource helper JS. Inherited `getAvailableDataFlavors` / `isDataFlavorAvailable` / `getData` work unchanged because they all funnel through `getContents`. `addFlavorListener` / `removeFlavorListener` overridden to WARN per R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (a) blocked-upstream — the browser has no `clipboardchange` event today (Clipboard API spec issue, open at W3C for years, no shipped browser implementation). One per-UI instance held via `ComponentUtil.setData(ui, WebClipboard.class, …)` (matches the per-UI lifecycle pattern of [D_single_ui_per_session](#D_single_ui_per_session)'s scope decision for static Swing registries).

The supporting `WebClipboardSnapshot implements Transferable` (package-private to `vaadinx.awt.datatransfer`) carries the deserialised payload from a single `getContents` call — JDK-faithful snapshot semantics, advertises only the flavors that actually had data in the read result, throws `UnsupportedFlavorException` from `getTransferData` for unsupported flavors per the JDK contract.

<a id="D_clipboard_vt_park"></a>**D_clipboard_vt_park — Both legs VT-park; both legs require a UI + a virtual-thread carrier.** Symmetric VT-park on `setContents` and `getContents`, both gated by `EHelper.callSwing`'s standard contract: `UI.getCurrent() != null` (R_callswing_envelope — `executeJs` needs a `Page` to dispatch through) and `Thread.currentThread().isVirtual()` (R_callswing_envelope — parking on a `PendingJavaScriptResult` future drains the carrier without dismounting on a platform thread; reading off-VT would block the request thread instead of cooperatively suspending it). The read leg fundamentally needs to park (browser `navigator.clipboard.read()` is async); the write leg parks for symmetry — the helper JS reports back whether the browser accepted the write or rejected for permission / secure-context reasons, and a synchronous result lets us throw on the secure-context case (D_clipboard_helper_js) and WARN on the others (D_clipboard_throw_warn_split) at the call site, instead of letting failures vanish into a fire-and-forget executeJs queue. Both calls are typically inside `EHelper.callSwing` already (clipboard ops in real apps run from button-click ActionListeners and menu handlers, both of which spawn a VT via `callSwing`), so the cost is bounded: one round-trip per call, settled before the next user action.

<a id="D_clipboard_future_bridge"></a>**D_clipboard_future_bridge — VT-park bridges through a plain `CompletableFuture`, not `PendingJavaScriptResult.toCompletableFuture(...).get()` directly.** The natural shape — `pending.toCompletableFuture(JsonNode.class).get()` — fails inside the loom carrier: Vaadin returns a `DeadlockDetectingCompletableFuture` whose `get()` calls `throwIfDeadlock()`, which throws `IllegalStateException` whenever `VaadinSession.hasLock()` returns true. Our `VirtualThreadAwareLock` deliberately makes `hasLock()` answer `true` on a VT carrier (so Vaadin's element-write path accepts mutations from inside a VT continuation, per [D_vt_aware_session_lock](#D_vt_aware_session_lock)). The deadlock detector's check is correct for platform-thread holders of the session lock but incorrect for VT-on-carrier — VTs can park cooperatively, dismounting the carrier and releasing the lock so the response RPC can deliver the result. We bridge through a plain `java.util.concurrent.CompletableFuture` via `PendingJavaScriptResult.then(Class, resultHandler, errorHandler)`; the plain future's `.get()` has no `hasLock()` check. Same shape the existing modal-park machinery uses for blocking dialogs (`CountDownLatch.await` in `vaadinx.awt.Dialog`).

A non-VT call from inside a UI context (e.g. `ui.access(() -> clipboard.getContents(null))` written by hand outside `callSwing`) throws `IllegalStateException` with a message pointing at `EHelper.callSwing` or `SwingUtilities.invokeLater` as the proper dispatcher. Mirror the existing R_callswing_envelope throw shape; same message format EHelper.callSwing uses for the no-UI case.

<a id="D_clipboard_throw_warn_split"></a>**D_clipboard_throw_warn_split — Throw / WARN split mirrors D_gap_severity_triage case-1's deployment-vs-runtime axis.** Two error classes:

1. **Deployment-fixable failures throw.** Missing secure context (`window.isSecureContext === false` — plain HTTP intranet deployment) and missing `navigator.clipboard` (ancient browser) both throw `IllegalStateException` with a "deploy over HTTPS (or use localhost) and upgrade browser to one with the Async Clipboard API" message. The migrator's affordance is to fix the deployment / require a modern browser; silently no-oping would hide a deployment bug behind a feature that mysteriously doesn't work. This is the **fourth throw site under [D_gap_severity_triage](#D_gap_severity_triage)**, in the spirit of case-1 but not literally a vaadin-loom rescue — generalises D_gap_severity_triage's pattern from "silent rescue of Swing-deadlock" to "silent rescue of deployment-fixable capability gap." D_gap_severity_triage's case enumeration acknowledges future additions land case-by-case; this entry adds the case. The check happens inside the helper JS (returns `{error: 'NO_SECURE_CONTEXT'}` or `{error: 'NO_CLIPBOARD_API'}`); the WebClipboard read leg translates these into the throw at the Java seam.

2. **Runtime / per-call browser failures WARN and degrade gracefully.** `NotAllowedError` (permission denied / no transient activation), `DOMException: Document is not focused`, decode failures (`ImageIO.read` returns null for unrecognised bytes), and any unexpected JS error: WARN via `EHelper.onUnimplemented("vaadinx.awt.datatransfer.WebClipboard", "getContents/setContents", reason)` and:
   - **Read**: return a `WebClipboardSnapshot` that advertises no flavors (`getTransferDataFlavors()` returns `new DataFlavor[0]`; `isDataFlavorAvailable` returns false for every flavor; `getTransferData` throws `UnsupportedFlavorException` per JDK contract). This matches Swing's "clipboard had no data" semantics — migrated code's `try / catch (UnsupportedFlavorException | IOException)` handlers work unchanged.
   - **Write**: fire-and-forget post-WARN. Nothing to return; the user's `setContents` returns normally, the browser silently denied the write. The WARN is the migrator's signal.

The split codifies the project's general policy: deployment misconfigurations deserve a loud throw the migrator can fix once; per-call browser flakiness deserves the WARN-and-continue R_match_swing_errors stance so apps don't crash mid-flow on Firefox / Safari permission quirks.

<a id="D_clipboard_helper_js"></a>**D_clipboard_helper_js — Helper JS as a servlet-served static resource under `META-INF/resources/emul/clipboard-helper.js`, injected programmatically via `Page.addJavaScript("context://emul/clipboard-helper.js")` from `Toolkit.getSystemClipboard()`'s per-UI lazy-init path.** Lives in `:emulators/src/main/resources/META-INF/resources/emul/clipboard-helper.js`. The `context://` URL scheme routes through Vaadin's static-resource handler, **does not go through Vite bundling**. The annotation-based shape (`@JavaScript("emul/clipboard-helper.js")` on `WebClipboard`) was tried first and removed: Vaadin's dependency scanner only picks up `@JavaScript` on `Component` classes reachable from a `@Route`; `WebClipboard` extends `java.awt.datatransfer.Clipboard`, not Vaadin `Component`, so the annotation alone never brings the file into the page. Programmatic `Page.addJavaScript` is idempotent per `Page`, and the per-UI cached `WebClipboard` instance means exactly one load per UI on first clipboard access — the right scope for a capability that's only needed when the migrated app actually touches the clipboard.

The helper exposes two functions on `window.emulClipboard`:
- `writeClipboard(text, imagePngBase64)`: builds a `ClipboardItem` with `text/plain` and/or `image/png` entries (whichever was passed non-null), calls `navigator.clipboard.write([item])`. Returns `{ok: true}` or `{error: <name>, message: <msg>}`.
- `readClipboard()`: walks `navigator.clipboard.read()`, picks the first `text/plain` blob and the first `image/*` blob; returns `{ok: true, text: string|null, imagePngBase64: string|null}` or `{error: <name>, message: <msg>}`. Image bytes are Base64-encoded; the Java side decodes via `ImageIO.read` which handles PNG/JPEG/GIF natively.

Both functions check `window.isSecureContext` and `navigator.clipboard` up front and return the canonical `NO_SECURE_CONTEXT` / `NO_CLIPBOARD_API` error envelope before attempting the real call. Inline-string alternative considered and rejected as too verbose once the image-blob marshalling enters scope; the static-resource shape keeps the helper readable and debuggable in browser DevTools.

<a id="D_clipboard_image_png"></a>**D_clipboard_image_png — Image support via PNG round-trip through `ImageIO`; canonical write encoding is always PNG, decode accepts whatever the browser produced.** The image flavor path uses `java.awt.image.BufferedImage` + `javax.imageio.ImageIO` — both publicly exported by `java.desktop`, no `--add-exports` needed (those `sun.awt.datatransfer.*` flags listed in the Vaadin SwingBridge docs are for the *system clipboard implementation* we're bypassing). Write: `Transferable.getTransferData(DataFlavor.imageFlavor)` → expect a `java.awt.Image` (typically `BufferedImage`); if it's a plain `Image`, draw it onto a freshly allocated `BufferedImage` of the right dimensions so `ImageIO.write(img, "png", baos)` can serialise it. Result Base64'd, passed to the helper. Any `DataFlavor` whose representation class is assignable from `java.awt.Image` rides the same path; user-defined `new DataFlavor("image/png", null)` works the same way. Read: `imagePngBase64` decoded → `ImageIO.read(ByteArrayInputStream)` produces a `BufferedImage` for any browser-supported format; `WebClipboardSnapshot` advertises `DataFlavor.imageFlavor` only when decode succeeds.

PNG is the canonical write format because it's the only image MIME type all major browsers' `ClipboardItem` API accepts reliably (Safari is fussy about everything else). Read tolerates whatever the browser returned in the first `image/*` blob — `ImageIO.read` handles PNG/JPEG/GIF/BMP transparently. Soft size WARN above ~50MB encoded (Base64 inflates ~33%, so a 10MB BufferedImage rounds to ~14MB on the wire) — no hard cap; R_best_effort_behaviour best-effort, document as accepted limitation.

File-list flavor (`DataFlavor.javaFileListFlavor`) explicitly deferred — File System Access API is Chrome-only, drag-source semantics differ enough from clipboard-source that it needs its own design pass, `java.io.File` round-trip via temp uploads is its own can of worms. Lands with drag-and-drop if a migration target needs it.

<a id="D_clipboard_test_mode"></a>**D_clipboard_test_mode — Test-injection seam via `setTestMode(boolean)` + an in-process Transferable held server-side.** Karibu has no real browser; `executeJs` queues calls that never run, and `.toCompletableFuture().get()` would block indefinitely. `WebClipboard.setTestMode(true)` flips a per-instance flag that bypasses executeJs entirely: `setContents` stores the Transferable in a server-side field, `getContents` returns it (cloned via `WebClipboardSnapshot` so test code can't accidentally mutate the live snapshot). The flag defaults to false in production. Tests opt in:

```kotlin
val cb = Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit().getSystemClipboard() as WebClipboard
cb.setTestMode(true)
cb.setContents(StringSelection("hello"), null)
assertEquals("hello", cb.getContents(null).getTransferData(stringFlavor))
```

The seam is intentionally a separate code path, not a "detect Karibu and route differently" auto-mock — explicit opt-in keeps the production code path unencumbered with mock-aware branches, and gives the test author a clear toggle. A real-browser e2e integration test (none yet — pending Sampler panel + real-browser harness in a follow-up slice) covers the `executeJs` round-trip; Karibu unit tests cover the Java seam.

**Rationale.**

- **No surrogate.** No Vaadin `Component` to extend — `navigator.clipboard` is a browser API surface, not a server-side component. SD_no_sjoptionpane's "no surrogate by design" precedent applies for a different reason than JOptionPane (JOptionPane skipped the surrogate because its UI behaviour is intrinsically blocking and surrogate-side can't park; clipboard skips because there's no Vaadin counterpart to host the surrogate on). Both share the trait that surrogating would buy nothing.
- **Reuse JDK datatransfer types.** Per [D_whitelist_porting](#D_whitelist_porting), classes that don't reference `Component` stay JDK. `DataFlavor`, `Transferable`, `StringSelection`, `ClipboardOwner`, `FlavorListener` all qualify. Migrators' custom `Transferable` impls compile and run unchanged; their `new StringSelection("foo")` is the canonical happy path. The ported surface stays minimal: `Toolkit` (entry point only) and `WebClipboard` (the JDK Clipboard subclass).
- **Subclass `java.awt.datatransfer.Clipboard` rather than implementing from scratch.** The JDK Clipboard class is a non-abstract concrete class with a name, owner/contents fields, and listener support. Subclassing lets us override only `setContents` / `getContents` while inheriting the rest of the surface (notably `getAvailableDataFlavors` / `isDataFlavorAvailable` / `getData` which all delegate through `getContents`). Less code to maintain, JDK-faithful by construction.
- **Helper JS as static resource, not inline.** The image-blob marshalling path (Base64 ↔ Blob ↔ ClipboardItem) is ~50 lines of JS; inline-string-in-Java would be unreadable and DevTools-undebuggable. Static-resource shape via `Page.addJavaScript("context://emul/clipboard-helper.js")` keeps the helper out of Vite's bundle and gives the browser source-map-friendly access. The annotation form on `WebClipboard` was a dead end (D_clipboard_helper_js) — `@JavaScript` on a non-`Component` class isn't honored by Vaadin's dependency scanner.
- **VT-park both legs.** Symmetric error handling, both calls already run inside `EHelper.callSwing`'s VT envelope in practice, and the secure-context throw is only meaningful if we wait for the result. The "fire-and-forget write" alternative considered briefly (saves one round-trip per write) was rejected as a false economy: the round-trip is bounded (~50ms typical) and the gained synchronous error visibility is worth it.
- **Image support yes; file-list no.** Image is well-bounded (PNG round-trip via ImageIO, ~50 lines of JS, no platform-specific shenanigans). File-list crosses into the File System Access API (Chrome-only) and intersects drag-source semantics, deserves its own design pass alongside DnD (queue #10).
- **`addFlavorListener` blocked-upstream.** Polling burns the read-permission UX every tick (Firefox always denies non-gestured `readText`), and no browser ships `clipboardchange` today. Classify as D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (a) so the WARN log carries the right migrator affordance (file the browser request; wait for the spec) and we revisit when (if) it lands.

**Alternatives considered.**

- **Fire-and-forget writes (no VT-park on the write leg).** Considered. Saves one round-trip per write. Rejected: the secure-context throw becomes asynchronous (we'd find out the deployment was misconfigured only on the next refresh), and uniform Java-side error handling is worth the bounded cost.
- **Inline JS in executeJs strings, no static resource.** Considered for slice-1-only minimalism. Rejected once image-blob marshalling joined the helper scope — readability + DevTools debugging tip the balance to the static resource, and we have a precedent (SD_sjtabbedpane) for the shape.
- **`@JavaScript("./clipboard-helper.js")` from `frontend/` instead of `META-INF/resources/`.** Rejected per user requirement: the `./`-prefix shape pulls the JS into Vite's bundle for production builds, adding to the dev-bundle rebuild cost. The static-resource shape stays out of the bundle entirely.
- **`@JavaScript("context://emul/clipboard-helper.js")` annotation on `WebClipboard`.** Tried first, removed. Vaadin's dependency scanner only honors `@JavaScript` on `Component` classes reachable from a `@Route`; `WebClipboard` extends `java.awt.datatransfer.Clipboard` (JDK), so the annotation was silently inert and `window.emulClipboard` was undefined when `setContents` / `getContents` ran the executeJs payload. Replaced with programmatic `Page.addJavaScript` from the `Toolkit` lazy-init seam — same per-UI scope, but the load actually happens.
- **`pending.toCompletableFuture(JsonNode.class).get()` for VT-park (the obvious shape).** Tried first, removed. Vaadin returns a `DeadlockDetectingCompletableFuture` whose `.get()` calls `throwIfDeadlock()` and throws `IllegalStateException` whenever `VaadinSession.hasLock()` is true. The runner-required `VirtualThreadAwareLock` makes `hasLock()` return true for VT carriers (necessary so element writes from inside a VT don't get rejected), which collides head-on with the deadlock detector — the detector can't tell platform-thread holders apart from VT-on-carrier, even though only the former actually deadlocks. Bridged through a plain `CompletableFuture` via `PendingJavaScriptResult.then(Class, …)` (D_clipboard_future_bridge). Same pattern the existing blocking-dialog modal-park uses (`CountDownLatch.await` in `vaadinx.awt.Dialog`).
- **Detect Karibu test mode automatically; route around executeJs without an explicit flag.** Considered. Rejected: implicit auto-mocking surprises test authors and couples production code to Karibu specifics. Explicit `setTestMode(true)` is the same shape `BrowserTimeZone.setZoneId` already uses for the same problem (browser-side capability that needs server-side simulation in tests).
- **Port `Toolkit`'s full surface for type-system completeness.** ~~Rejected per D_whitelist_porting's "minimum port surface" stance — `Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit()`, `Toolkit.getScreenSize()`, beep, font metrics, screen DPI, and the AWT event queue are all out of scope. Most migrators reach for `Toolkit` solely for clipboard; further additions land case-by-case if a migration target needs them.~~ **Superseded by [D_toolkit_full_surface](#D_toolkit_full_surface):** the JLawyer round showed this over-rejection left `Toolkit.getScreenSize()` etc. as a runtime `HeadlessException`, breaking the import-swap-compiles promise. D_toolkit_full_surface ports the full surface (delegate / browser-back / fabricate / throw / WARN by tier).
- **`ClipboardOwner.lostOwnership` polling-based emulation.** Considered briefly (we hold the last `(Transferable, owner)` pair; when a subsequent `setContents` arrives with a different `Transferable`, we fire `lostOwnership` on the previous owner). Rejected: browser-side clipboard mutations from another tab / another app don't notify us, so we'd fire `lostOwnership` only on our own subsequent writes — half-faithful semantics worse than dropping entirely with a WARN.
- **Re-implement `java.awt.datatransfer.Clipboard` instead of subclassing.** Rejected — the JDK class is concrete, public, and reuses cleanly. Re-implementation buys nothing and introduces drift risk if the JDK adds new methods.
- **Back `WebClipboard` with Vaadin's built-in `Clipboard` API (`com.vaadin.flow.component.…Clipboard`, since V25.2) instead of the hand-rolled `executeJs` + `clipboard-helper.js` bridge.** Evaluated June 2026 (the API postdates D_clipboard's original design); rejected as the emulation backend — it is the wrong *shape* for the seam, on three counts:
  1. **Gesture-bound/declarative vs. imperative-anywhere.** Vaadin's API is fluent and bound to a future browser gesture — `Clipboard.onClick(component).writeText(…)` attaches a clipboard action to a component's *client-side click*, and reads deliver to async callbacks. The import-swapped Swing seam is the opposite: `Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit().getSystemClipboard().setContents(new StringSelection(s), null)` is imperative, synchronous, and runs from inside a server-side `ActionListener` (already funneled through `EHelper.callSwing` per R_callswing_envelope) — at which point the originating gesture is consumed and there is no component to bind to. There is no `Clipboard.writeNow(text)`, and we cannot know at button-construction time that an arbitrary `ActionListener` will touch the clipboard, so the declarative binding can't be pre-wired. Adopting it would mean abandoning the import-swap promise.
  2. **Data model.** Vaadin exposes fixed `text/plain` + `text/html` + `image/png` slots (+ paste/file-paste listeners); the Swing seam is `Transferable` / `DataFlavor` (arbitrary MIME, custom flavors). For the flavors we actually support (string→text, image→png) the two reach parity and custom flavors drop on both sides — a wash, not a win.
  3. **No low-level handle to delegate to.** Vaadin only surfaces the high-level gesture-bound facade, not the underlying `navigator.clipboard` mechanism, so `WebClipboard` can't delegate its `setContents`/`getContents` down into it even where the model lines up. Our `clipboard-helper.js` therefore stays — it duplicates what Vaadin ships internally, but Vaadin gives us no seam to drop it onto.

  Vaadin's API exists partly to fix a fragility `WebClipboard` carries: our write does a server→client `executeJs` round-trip *before* calling `navigator.clipboard.write`, so a slow round-trip can let the browser's transient-activation window go stale → `NotAllowedError` (handled as D_clipboard_throw_warn_split WARN-and-degrade; usually benign inside Chrome's ~5s grace). Vaadin avoids this by executing client-side within the gesture — but **only for declaratively-bound clicks, which our imperative seam can't be**, so it can't rescue the emulator path. Vaadin's `Clipboard` *is* the natural choice for the stage-3 `:surrogates` layer, where a "Copy" button is an explicit, gesture-bound Vaadin component.

**Accepted limitations.**

- **Custom `DataFlavor`s beyond stringFlavor and imageFlavor drop-and-WARN.** A migrator's `Transferable` advertising `application/x-jlawyer-case-bundle` compiles and runs but the data never crosses the browser boundary. R_vaadin_first stance: revisit if a real migration target needs a specific custom flavor by adding a typed marshalling path; the helper JS already accepts arbitrary MIME types in `ClipboardItem` but encoder/decoder pairs need designing per-flavor.
- **File-list (`DataFlavor.javaFileListFlavor`) deferred to the DnD slice.**
- **`addFlavorListener` WARNs and never fires** — D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (a) blocked-upstream on browser `clipboardchange`.
- **Multi-tab clipboard race:** browser clipboard is global per OS user, so two tabs of the same Vaadin app share the OS clipboard correctly. Our per-UI `WebClipboard` instances are fine — they all delegate to the same `navigator.clipboard`.
- **`Toolkit.getSystemSelection()` (X11 middle-click clipboard) is not ported** — no browser counterpart at all.
- **Off-VT calls throw `IllegalStateException`.** A `Toolkit.getSystemClipboard().getContents(null)` called from a hand-rolled `Thread { ... }` outside Vaadin context throws. The error message points at `EHelper.callSwing` / `SwingUtilities.invokeLater` / `UI.access` as the proper dispatcher. This is a real divergence from Swing (where `Toolkit.getSystemClipboard()` works from any thread); bounded — the canonical case is a button-click ActionListener which is already callSwing'd. Closes alongside the entry-point design pass when a real migration target hits it.
- **Image size soft WARN at ~50MB encoded; no hard cap.** Vaadin RPC handles it, just slowly. The WARN is the migrator's signal that they're shipping a screenshot the size of a small video; not an enforcement.
- **Karibu tests cover only the server-side seam via `setTestMode(true)`.** The executeJs round-trip itself is not unit-testable without a real browser. A follow-up Sampler panel + real-browser e2e harness (deferred slice) closes the gap; for now, the asymmetry is documented and accepted.

**Validation.**

- `:emulators` — `WebClipboardTest` (22 tests under `vaadinx.awt.datatransfer`): test-mode round-trip for `StringSelection`, custom `Transferable` advertising stringFlavor + imageFlavor, image-only Transferable, `getAvailableDataFlavors` / `isDataFlavorAvailable` / `getData` delegating through, `WebClipboardSnapshot` flavors-array contract (only what's present), `getTransferData(UnsupportedFlavor)` throws `UnsupportedFlavorException`, `addFlavorListener` / `removeFlavorListener` WARN, `Toolkit.getSystemClipboard()` returns the same per-UI instance across calls. Distinct UIs (via tear-down + re-setup) get distinct `WebClipboard` instances. Off-VT call from the test thread throws `IllegalStateException`.
- `:sampler` — `ClipboardPanel` (nav target between Lists and Layouts) demos all four sub-surfaces: text round-trip via `JTextArea` + `JButton "Copy text" / "Paste text"`; image round-trip via inline `ImageTransferable` carrying a server-generated 32×32 PNG; combined text+image in a single `Transferable`; and probe (live `getAvailableDataFlavors` + JDK-faithful `UnsupportedFlavorException` on `javaFileListFlavor`). Production code uses the real browser clipboard via `executeJs`; the Karibu exit gate engages `WebClipboard.setTestMode(true)` and drives the same code path through the in-process Transferable seam.
- `:sampler` — `ClipboardWarnInventoryTest` (2 tests): `inventory_user_path` navigates to the Sampler shell, swaps to ClipboardPanel, enables test mode, then drives nine steps through the four demos (Copy text → assert clipboard payload; Paste text → assert target JTextArea reflects clipboard; Copy / Paste image → assert dimensions round-trip; Copy / Paste combined → assert both flavors present; Inspect → flavor enumeration; Probe → UnsupportedFlavorException caught). `inventory_clipboard_api_surface` micro-drives the WebClipboard surface (Toolkit per-UI singleton, text / image / combined round-trip via test mode, `getAvailableDataFlavors` / `isDataFlavorAvailable` / `getData`, empty-advertise snapshot, `getName`), then exercises the intentional-WARN paths (`addFlavorListener` / `removeFlavorListener`, asserting exactly one WARN each naming the blocked-upstream rationale per D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (a)), then disables test mode and asserts the off-VT guard throws (`IllegalStateException` for both `setContents` and `getContents`). Both layer warnHooks wired to a single sink. `NavigationSmokeTest` extended with the Clipboard nav entry — ctor-only WARN-free smoke check.
- **Real-browser e2e harness deferred.** The `executeJs` round-trip itself (helper JS preflight, `navigator.clipboard.write/read`, secure-context branch, browser permission denial) is not exercisable through Karibu — covered by manual real-browser use against the Sampler panel today; an automated e2e harness lands when the project picks up a real-browser test pattern.

<a id="D_jpopupmenu"></a>
## D_jpopupmenu. `JPopupMenu` emulator — thin shell over `SJPopupMenu`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, `setComponentPopupMenu` signature port + peer delegation

**Decision.** The emulator half (surrogate half is [SD_sjpopupmenu](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjpopupmenu)). `vaadinx.swing.JPopupMenu extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent`, holding the JDK menu-item tree and pushing a `MenuNode` snapshot to its `SJPopupMenu` peer — structurally a sibling of `JMenuBar` ([D_menu_tree](#D_menu_tree)) that renders into a `ContextMenu` instead of a `MenuBar`.

**R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `javax.swing.JPopupMenu` is a leaf in the *public* Swing hierarchy — its only subclass, `javax.swing.plaf.basic.BasicComboPopup`, is L&F (dropped per R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b)). So the protected `(Component peer)` ctor is omitted and the root no-arg ctor calls `super(new SJPopupMenu())` directly, hard-coding the peer (same shape `JMenuBar` / `JMenu` / `JSeparator` take).

**Children machinery mirrors `JMenu`.** `JPopupMenu` carries a `List<Object>` of `JMenuItem`s (incl. `JMenu` / `JCheckBoxMenuItem` / `JRadioButtonMenuItem`) and `JSeparator`s, with `add` / `insert` / `remove` / `removeAll` / `addSeparator` / `getComponentCount` / `getComponentIndex` / `getSubElements` — the same list shape `JMenu` already uses. A `pushTree()` walks it building the `List<MenuNode>` (reusing `JMenuItem.toMenuNode` / `JMenu.collectChildren`) and calls `peer.rebuildFromTree(snapshot)` — verbatim the `JMenuBar.pushTree()` shape. (Real Swing has `JMenu` *contain* a `JPopupMenu`; our emulator stores children directly on each, so the two carry parallel — not nested — child lists.)

**One fan-in edit on `JMenuItem`.** `JMenuItem.notifyTreeMutated()` walks the parent chain to the root and pushes. It previously recognized only `JMenuBar` as a root; it now also recognizes `JPopupMenu` (`if (p instanceof JPopupMenu pm) pm.notifyTreeMutated()`), so an item mutated inside a popup tree re-pushes correctly. Expected, bounded fan-in.

**`setComponentPopupMenu` — signature port + peer delegation.** The current `JComponent.setComponentPopupMenu(javax.swing.JPopupMenu)` was a generated stub referencing the JDK type because no emulator `JPopupMenu` existed. It now ports to the emulator type per the standard D_whitelist_porting porting rule:

```java
public void setComponentPopupMenu(vaadinx.swing.JPopupMenu popup) {
    this.componentPopup = popup;                               // emulator-side round-trip
    if (peer instanceof com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.swing.JComponentMixin m) {
        m.setComponentPopupMenu(popup == null ? null
                : (com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJPopupMenu) popup.getPeer());
    }
}
public vaadinx.swing.JPopupMenu getComponentPopupMenu() { return componentPopup; }
```

The emulator does **not** reach into `ContextMenu.setTarget` itself — it delegates through the surrogate's `JComponentMixin.setComponentPopupMenu(SJPopupMenu)` helper (SD_sjpopupmenu), so the actual `setTarget(peer)` binding lives in exactly one place and both layers share it. `peer` is always a surrogate (`instanceof JComponentMixin` holds for every emulator peer); the cast of `popup.getPeer()` to `SJPopupMenu` is safe because `JPopupMenu` is R_leaf_peer_lockdown-locked to that peer. The getter's emulator-type return (`vaadinx.swing.JPopupMenu`) vs the surrogate-type return (`SJPopupMenu`) is the standard stage-2/stage-3 divergence.

**`show` / `setVisible` — `setTarget` + WARN.** `show(invoker, x, y)` resolves the invoker's peer and calls the surrogate's `setTarget`, then `EHelper.onUnimplemented` for the synchronous programmatic open (no Vaadin `ContextMenu.open()`; R_layouts_close_enough + sub-bucket (a) per SD_sjpopupmenu). `setVisible(true)` follows the same WARN path. The right-click-triggered idiom works natively once the target is bound.

**Peer→Swing open sync — `OpenedChangeEvent` drives `PopupMenuListener` + the `"visible"` bound property (`Q_popupmenu_visible_sync`, closed 2026-08-31).** The browser opens and closes the `ContextMenu` on its own (right-click, Esc, click-outside, item selection), and originally nothing carried that back — `isVisible()` read the peer truthfully while `addPopupMenuListener` was drop-and-WARN citing R_vaadin_first, **a surrogate-only rule misapplied on the emulator layer**, where [R_decline_effect_only](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules) governs: state and notification are the emulator's to keep. Now `installOpenedSync()` (wired in the ctor) subscribes to the peer's `OpenedChangeEvent` through `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope) and fires the JDK `setVisible` body's notifications in the JDK's order — the `PopupMenuListener` event first, then `firePropertyChange("visible", …)` (`JPopupMenu` being the only class in `java.awt`+`javax.swing` that fires a `"visible"` bound property, per [D_window_fanout](#D_window_fanout)). Listener storage is the inherited `listenerList`; the three `firePopupMenu*` notifiers take the JDK's protected no-arg shape. No `preventPeerEvents` guard: nothing on the emulator writes the peer's open state (`setVisible` declines the programmatic open), so an echo cannot happen. The programmatic-path stance is unchanged — no event fires from the declined `setVisible`, since firing would announce a state `isVisible()` denies (D_owed_events). Two documented divergences: (1) the JDK fires `willBecomeVisible` *before* display, while here the popup is already open when the server learns — the standard peer→Swing skew; (2) **`popupMenuCanceled` never fires** — `OpenedChangeEvent` cannot distinguish an Esc/click-outside cancel from an item-selection close (both arrive as `opened=false`), and a heuristic would invent cancels the desktop never fired (R_no_silent_improvements), so `firePopupMenuCanceled()` is exposed-but-unreached and says so in its javadoc (sub-bucket (a): deliverable if the `vaadin-context-menu` web component ever reports a close *reason*). The companion sweep ("one one-directional seam usually means several") found no other: item clicks already travel peer→Swing via the `MenuTreeBuilder` ActionEvent wiring, and the programmatic open stays blocked upstream. Surrogate side needs nothing — a stage-3 user subscribes to Vaadin's `addOpenedChangeListener` directly per R_vaadin_first.

**Rationale.** `JPopupMenu` is the menu family pointed at a different peer; reusing D_menu_tree's emitter (`toMenuNode` / `collectChildren` / `pushTree`) keeps a single JDK-tree-walk implementation and lets SD_sjpopupmenu's shared `MenuTreeBuilder` do the Vaadin-side construction. Delegating `setComponentPopupMenu` through the peer (rather than driving `setTarget` from the emulator) keeps the cross-cutting binding in one method and dissolves the "fan-out across every surrogate" an earlier audit predicted.

**Accepted limitations.** Inherits SD_sjpopupmenu's: no programmatic open-at-coordinates, one live target per popup instance, O(n) rebuild per mutation. `getComponent()` / `MenuElement` placeholder surface matches `JMenuItem`'s D_menu_tree stance (the per-item peer is never separately attached).

**Validation.** `JPopupMenuTest` — peer type + R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down (no `(Component peer)` ctor), children add/insert/remove/removeAll + `getComponentCount`/`getComponentIndex`, separator node emission, `add(String)`, nested `JMenu`, `JCheckBoxMenuItem` checkable node, `setEnabled` cascade, detached-item-then-add, `pushTree` reaches the peer's `rebuildFromTree`, `setComponentPopupMenu` round-trip + peer `setTarget` binding + null-clear, `show(x,y)` binds target + WARNs, `getUIClassID == "PopupMenuUI"`; the open-sync tests drive the browser path by writing the element's `"opened"` property (the same seam `ContextMenuBase`'s own property-change listener fires from) and assert the JDK firing order plus listener-removal unsubscription. Sampler `PopupMenusPanel` route + `PopupMenusWarnInventoryTest` exit gate (shared with SD_sjpopupmenu); its listener bucket asserts add/get/remove WARN-free.

<a id="D_drag_and_drop"></a>
## D_drag_and_drop. Drag-and-drop — emulator-only `TransferHandler` bridge over Vaadin native DnD, same-UI in-app scope, Grid-row + generic paths, third "no surrogate by design"

**Status: landed.** The design pass set the shape (sub-decisions the D_drag_and_drop sub-decisions); the implementation matches, with two recorded refinements: the bridge lives in package `vaadinx.swing` (package-private `DndBridge` / `CurrentDrag`), **not** a `vaadinx.swing.dnd` sub-package, so it can reach `TransferHandler`'s protected `createTransferable` / `exportDone` the way the JDK keeps its own DnD machinery package-private to `javax.swing`; and the per-component teardown state is a peer-stored `Wiring` holder rather than a `DndStore` class (D_dnd_envelope_teardown).

**Decision.** DnD lands **emulator-only with no surrogate** — the third "no surrogate by design" outcome after JOptionPane ([SD_no_sjoptionpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_no_sjoptionpane)) and Clipboard ([D_clipboard](#D_clipboard)), on a *third distinct rationale*: the surrogate already supports drag-and-drop by virtue of being a Vaadin component (a stage-3 user calls Vaadin's native `DragSource.create()` / `Grid.setRowsDraggable()` directly), so the `javax.swing.TransferHandler` → Vaadin-DnD translation is purely a stage-2 (emulator) concern. The emulator drives DnD entirely through **inherited Grid API + static Vaadin DnD factories on the peer it already holds** — *zero new surrogate code, no new `JComponentMixin` method*. (Contrast: JOptionPane skipped a surrogate because its UI is intrinsically blocking; Clipboard because there is no Vaadin component to extend at all; DnD because the surrogate's Vaadin-native DnD already *is* the stage-3 answer.)

<a id="D_dnd_in_app_scope"></a>**D_dnd_in_app_scope — Same-UI, in-app scope only; no browser marshalling.** Vaadin's `DragSource.setDragData(Object)` keeps the dragged object **server-side**, handed back via `DropEvent.getDragData()` / `getDragSourceComponent()` only when the drop occurs in the same UI (browser window/tab) as the drag source. That is exactly the migration target's shape — the JLawyer-shape testbed (`DocumentTransferHandler`) and JLawyer's 11 real DnD files all "drag a domain object between in-app lists/trees." So we stash the live Swing `Transferable` (plus the source `JComponent`, source `TransferHandler`, and action) in a **per-UI `CurrentDrag` holder** (`ComponentUtil.setData(ui, CurrentDrag.class, …)`) at drag-start and read it back at drop — mirroring Vaadin's own cross-grid example, which captures a shared `draggedItem` field at `DragStart` and consumes it at `Drop`. **No browser `dataTransfer` marshalling is needed** for the in-app path. External / OS-boundary DnD (drag a file from the desktop *into* the app, drag content *out* to another application) needs the browser `DataTransfer` / File API and is **deferred — D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (a) blocked-on-design**, not blocked-upstream. We reuse Clipboard's `java.awt.datatransfer.*` *types* (`Transferable` / `DataFlavor` / `StringSelection`, reused-from-JDK per D_whitelist_porting) but **not** its PNG/string browser-marshalling helpers — those only matter for the deferred external path.

<a id="D_dnd_transferhandler_only"></a>**D_dnd_transferhandler_only — `TransferHandler` path only; low-level `java.awt.dnd.*` stays drop-and-WARN.** We port `vaadinx.swing.TransferHandler` + `TransferHandler.TransferSupport` + the `TransferHandler.DropLocation` base and the `JList.DropLocation` / `JTable.DropLocation` per-component subclasses (later `JTree.DropLocation`). These reference our `vaadinx.swing.JComponent` (user code subclasses `TransferHandler` and casts `support.getComponent()` to `vaadinx.swing.JList`), so D_whitelist_porting/D_event_port_policy *forces* the port — the JDK types would hand user code a `javax.swing.JComponent`. `javax.swing.DropMode` is a Component-free enum → **reused from the JDK unchanged** (D_whitelist_porting). The low-level `java.awt.dnd` surface (`Component.setDropTarget`, `DragSource`, `DragGestureListener`, `DropTargetListener`) stays the existing `EHelper.onUnimplemented` stub — modern Swing and the migration target use `TransferHandler`, and R_infra_not_surface forbids preemptively building the low-level path.

<a id="D_dnd_wiring_paths"></a>**D_dnd_wiring_paths — Two wiring paths selected by peer type.** Both land this slice (per the design-pass scope pick: Grid-row on JList **and** JTable, plus the generic path):
- **Grid-row path** (JList / JTable — `Grid<Integer>` peers per [D_jlist](#D_jlist) / [D_jtable](#D_jtable); later JTree's `TreeGrid`): the emulator calls inherited `peer.setRowsDraggable(true)`, `peer.setDropMode(GridDropMode.*)`, and subscribes `addDragStartListener` → `handler.getSourceActions` + `handler.createTransferable(src)` (stash in `CurrentDrag`), `addDropListener` → `handler.canImport` + `handler.importData`, `addDragEndListener` → `handler.exportDone` + clear `CurrentDrag`. `GridDropEvent.getDropTargetItem()` (an `Integer` Grid row index) + `getDropLocation()` (`ABOVE` / `BELOW` / `ON_TOP` / `EMPTY`) translate to a Swing `JList.DropLocation(index, isInsert)` / `JTable.DropLocation`; Grid-row-index ↔ model-index translation reuses the emulator's existing selection bridge.
- **Generic path** (any other `JComponent.setTransferHandler`): `DragSource.create(peer)` + `DropTarget.create(peer)` with the same listener bodies; `DropEvent.getDragData()` / `getDragSourceComponent()` recover the `CurrentDrag`. Whole-component drag/drop (no row index → `DropLocation` is the no-index form).

<a id="D_dnd_semantic_mappings"></a>**D_dnd_semantic_mappings — Semantic mappings, R_best_effort_behaviour best-effort.** `DropMode.INSERT → GridDropMode.BETWEEN`, `DropMode.ON → ON_TOP`, `DropMode.ON_OR_INSERT → ON_TOP_OR_BETWEEN`, legacy `USE_SELECTION → BETWEEN`. `TransferHandler.getSourceActions(c)` (`COPY` / `MOVE` / `COPY_OR_MOVE` / `LINK` / `NONE`) → Vaadin `EffectAllowed`. Vaadin `DropEffect` (driven by `effectAllowed` + browser modifier keys, per the Vaadin DnD contract) maps back to the Swing action passed to `importData` / `exportDone`; a successful `importData` returning `true` with action `MOVE` triggers `handler.exportDone(src, t, MOVE)` so the source half of a move can delete the moved item. Browser `dropEffect`/`effectAllowed` mismatch handling follows Vaadin's documented Chrome/Firefox-block vs Safari/Edge-allow split — we validate the effect in the drop handler regardless (R_best_effort_behaviour "close enough").

<a id="D_dnd_envelope_teardown"></a>**D_dnd_envelope_teardown — R_callswing_envelope envelope + per-component teardown state.** Every Vaadin DnD peer→Swing callback body (drag-start build, drop import, drag-end exportDone) wraps in `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope) — `importData` may pop a modal `JOptionPane` ("overwrite?") which must VT-park. The active `TransferHandler` is a field on the emulator `JComponent` (the `componentPopup`-field precedent); the Vaadin `Registration`s are tracked in a `Wiring` holder stored on the *peer* via `ComponentUtil.setData` (the [`ComponentPopupStore`](#D_jpopupmenu) lazy-data pattern, peer-side). `DndBridge.reconfigure(emu)` is the single (re)wire entry point that all of `setTransferHandler` / `setDragEnabled` / `setDropMode` funnel through: it tears down the prior `Wiring` (removes registrations, `setRowsDraggable(false)` + `setDropMode(null)` on a Grid peer, or `setDraggable(false)` + `setActive(false)` on a generic peer) before installing fresh wiring iff a handler is set — so a null handler or `setDragEnabled(false)` leaks no subscriptions and re-setting overrides cleanly.

<a id="D_dnd_graduations"></a>**D_dnd_graduations — Graduations from drop-and-WARN.** `JList.setDragEnabled` / `JTable.setDragEnabled` (currently field-shadow + WARN-on-true per their D_jlist/D_jtable stubs), their `setDropMode`, and `JComponent.setTransferHandler` / `getTransferHandler` (currently `onUnimplemented` on `JComponent`, `JFrame`, `JDialog`) graduate to wired. The `dragEnabled` field stays as the JDK-faithful round-trip getter; setting it now also (re)configures the peer when a handler is present. `JTextComponent.setDragEnabled` stays drop-and-WARN (text-drag is not in the target's surface; revisit if a migration target needs intra-text drag).

**Rationale.** The surrogate is untouched because Vaadin already gives stage-3 users first-class DnD; the bridge is the stage-2 translation layer and nothing more — the same "the surrogate IS the Vaadin answer" logic that made Clipboard emulator-only, applied to a capability that *does* have a Vaadin counterpart (unlike Clipboard). Same-UI scope is not a shortcut: it is the actual shape of the migration target, and Vaadin's server-side drag-data model fits it exactly with no marshalling. Routing through the ported `TransferHandler` (rather than exposing raw `DragSource`/`DropTarget` to migrated code) keeps user code Swing-shaped per R_swing_is_truth and confines the Vaadin wiring to one bridge.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **External / OS-boundary DnD deferred** (drag file in from desktop, drag content out to another app) — D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (a) blocked-on-design; needs browser `DataTransfer`/File-API marshalling, lands when a migration target requires it.
- **`DataFlavor.javaFileListFlavor`** (carried over from D_clipboard's deferral) lands here only for the in-app case; the OS-boundary file case rides the deferred external path.
- **Drag image / cursor customization** (`TransferHandler.getDragImage` / `getDragImageOffset`) drop-and-WARN — Vaadin exposes drag-image config but Swing's `Icon`-based API doesn't map cleanly; R_layouts_close_enough/R_vaadin_first.
- **Pixel drop coordinates** (`TransferSupport.getDropLocation().getDropPoint()`) — R_layouts_close_enough, no server-side coordinates; the Grid-row index + `ABOVE`/`BELOW` is the faithful drop position, the `Point` is a dummy.
- **Multi-item drag** beyond the dragged-row set Vaadin reports is best-effort; `getDraggedItems()` drives `createTransferable` on the lead selection per JDK.
- **`exportToClipboard`** (TransferHandler → clipboard) reuses D_clipboard's `WebClipboard`; cut/copy/paste keybinding auto-wiring (`TransferHandler.getCutAction()` et al.) is drop-and-WARN unless a target needs it.

**Validation.** `:emulators` — `TransferHandlerTest` (17 tests): ported-type surface (action constants, base-handler no-op export/import, property-ctor `COPY`, paste-shape `TransferSupport`, `JList`/`JTable.DropLocation` getters); peer config + teardown observed via `SJList.isRowsDraggable()` / `getDropMode()` (armed on handler+dragEnabled+dropMode, town down on null handler, order-independent); R_match_swing_errors drop-mode validation (`JList` rejects `INSERT_ROWS`, `JTable` accepts it); the headline same-UI move (drag row 0 of list A, drop above/below a row of list B → document moves, source loses it via `exportDone(MOVE)`); cancelled drag fires `exportDone(NONE)` and moves nothing; drop with no tracked drag is a no-op; `exportToClipboard` writes the transferable; generic-component round-trip. The Grid-row drag/drop path is driven through `DndBridge`'s package-private test seams (`simulateGridDragStartForTest` / `simulateGridDropForTest` / `simulateDragEndForTest`) — Vaadin's `GridDragStartEvent` / `GridDropEvent` can't be constructed browserless without coupling to the Grid key-mapper, and Karibu ships no Grid DnD helper, so the seams invoke the exact internal handlers the real Vaadin listeners call (the original "Karibu can fire the events" sketch was wrong). `:sampler` — `DragAndDropPanel` (two `JList`s wired for real browser DnD via a shared `TransferHandler`, MOVE semantics, plus a no-drag "Move selected" affordance) + `DragAndDropWarnInventoryTest` (2 tests: user-path asserting both peers armed + the move affordance, and a DnD API-surface micro-driver over the graduated `setDragEnabled` / `setDropMode` / `setTransferHandler` surface on JList / JTable / generic JPanel) + `NavigationSmokeTest` entry. Real-browser e2e for the actual HTML5 drag gesture is deferred to the same e2e harness D_clipboard defers.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Host DnD on the surrogate (new `JComponentMixin` DnD methods).** Rejected — stage-3 users already have Vaadin's native `DragSource`/`DropTarget`/`setRowsDraggable`; a Swing-flavoured surrogate DnD helper would be storage-for-storage's-sake (R_vaadin_first anti-pattern) and the surrogate can't reference `vaadinx.swing.TransferHandler` anyway (`:emulators` depends on `:surrogates`, not the reverse).
- **Browser-marshal the `Transferable` through the clipboard helper-JS infrastructure for all drops.** Rejected for the in-app path — Vaadin's server-side `setDragData` already hands the live Java object back for same-UI drops; marshalling would lose object identity and force per-`DataFlavor` encoders for zero benefit on the only shape the target uses. Kept in reserve for the deferred external path.
- **Implement the low-level `java.awt.dnd` `DropTarget`/`DragSource` surface directly.** Rejected per R_infra_not_surface — the target uses `TransferHandler`; building the low-level path preemptively is unrequested surface.
- **Generic `DragSource`/`DropTarget` for the Grid-peer components too (skip Grid-row DnD).** Rejected — Grid's built-in row DnD gives the row index and `ABOVE`/`BELOW` drop location for free, which is exactly Swing's `DropMode.INSERT` `DropLocation`; whole-component generic DnD on a Grid would lose the per-row drop position.

<a id="D_jtree"></a>
## D_jtree. JTree emulator — thin shell over `SJTree`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, two-layer TreeSelection + TreeExpansion + Mouse re-source, JDK `TreeCellRenderer` bridge, TreeGrid-row DnD per D_drag_and_drop, rename-in-place via TreeGrid.Editor (D_jtree_rename_in_place)

**Status: implemented.** Surrogate-side decision: [SD_sjtree](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjtree). The driving use is the left-pane case-folder hierarchy ([`CaseTreeView`](../testapps/jlawyer-shape/swing/src/main/java/com/vaadin/swingbridge/testapps/jlawyershape/swing/CaseTreeView.java)).

**`vaadinx.swing.JTree extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent implements javax.swing.Scrollable, javax.accessibility.Accessible`** — matches JDK shape. Rendered by `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJTree`, which carries the model-driven data provider and the selection-model bridge; expansion state and the row⇄path queries are the emulator's own (D_jtree_row_path_bridge), so no expansion or row getter reads the peer. The closest precedent is JList ([D_jlist](#D_jlist)) — same Grid-family re-source + renderer-bridge shape, with selection/expansion specialised to paths.

**R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `javax.swing.JTree` is a leaf in the public Swing hierarchy. All public ctors funnel through a private `(SJTree peer)` ctor — no protected `(Component peer)` ctor. The convenience ctors that don't take a `TreeModel` build a `DefaultTreeModel` internally exactly as the JDK does: `JTree()` → a demo model (the JDK `getDefaultTreeModel()` sample), `JTree(TreeNode root)` / `JTree(TreeNode, boolean asksAllowsChildren)` → `new DefaultTreeModel(root, asksAllowsChildren)`, `JTree(Object[])` / `JTree(Vector)` / `JTree(Hashtable)` → wrap the entries under a synthetic hidden `DefaultMutableTreeNode` root with `rootVisible=false` + the `showsRootHandles=true` shadow the JDK sets alongside (the JDK `createTreeModel` shape; D_jtree_field_shadows). `JTree(TreeModel)` is the direct path. All `tree.*` model/node/path/selection types are JDK-reused per [SD_sjtree](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjtree)'s port analysis (D_event_port_policy) — only `vaadinx.swing.tree.TreeCellRenderer` / `DefaultTreeCellRenderer` port.

<a id="D_jtree_two_layer_resource"></a>**D_jtree_two_layer_resource — two-layer re-source (JList/JComboBox shape).** Three bridges installed in the ctor re-source surrogate events to the emulator's own `listenerList` with the source rebound to `this JTree`:
1. **`TreeSelectionListener`** — a handler on the surrogate's `TreeSelectionModel` fires the emulator's `fireValueChanged(TreeSelectionEvent)` so `tree.addTreeSelectionListener(...)` sees `source == this JTree` (the `CaseTreeView.fireCaseSelected` path). `setSelectionModel` moves the handler from the old model to the new. The JDK-shaped `getSelectionModel(): TreeSelectionModel` lives **here on the emulator** (clash-free — the emulator isn't a Grid) and reads through the surrogate's `getTreeSelectionModel()`; on the surrogate the name is taken by the inherited `Grid.getSelectionModel(): GridSelectionModel`, the same clash SJTable hit (SD_sjtable/SD_sjtree_selection_bridge).
2. **Browser toggles** — not a re-source. TreeGrid's *client-originated* `ExpandEvent` / `CollapseEvent` (`isFromClient()`) runs the JDK's `expandPath` / `collapsePath` inside `callSwing`, so `TreeWillExpandListener` and `TreeExpansionListener` fire as for a click on a desktop toggle, with `source == this JTree`; server-side expands are the emulator's own pushes and are ignored (D_jtree_row_path_bridge).
3. **`SMouseListener`** — the surrogate's item-click → `MOUSE_PRESSED`/`MOUSE_RELEASED`/`MOUSE_CLICKED` (carrying the browser button so right-click → `isPopupTrigger()`) re-sources to a `vaadinx.awt.event.MouseEvent` dispatched via the inherited `processMouseEvent`, so `tree.addMouseListener(...)` + `e.isPopupTrigger()` + `getRowForLocation(e.getX(), e.getY())` (the `CaseTreeView.selectOnRightClick` idiom) works as written. `getRowForLocation` delegates to `peer.getRowForLocation`, which returns the surrogate-stashed clicked row — valid because the dispatch is synchronous through `callSwing` (SD_sjtree_row_api; the stash is a store field, surviving the vaadin-loom VT boundary).

<a id="D_jtree_renderer_registry"></a>**D_jtree_renderer_registry — JDK `TreeCellRenderer` registry + dynamic hierarchy-column renderer (D_event_port_policy + D_jcombobox + R_vaadin_first).** The JDK `TreeCellRenderer` surface lives on the emulator (its `getTreeCellRendererComponent` returns `vaadinx.awt.Component`, clashing with `java.awt.Component`). The emulator swaps the surrogate's hierarchy-column `componentProvider` function once (the SD_sjtree_hierarchy_render function-level seam — TreeGrid's expand/collapse toggle lives in `HierarchyColumnComponentRenderer`'s template, so a renderer re-install would drop it); the swapped-in closure resolves the current `cellRenderer` per render call, invokes `getTreeCellRendererComponent(this, node, isSelected, isExpanded, isLeaf, row, /*hasFocus*/ false)` — **passing the JTree instance as the `tree` arg** so renderers down-casting `(JTree) tree` work — and snapshots the result via `JComboBox.snapshotRendererOutput` (the shared JLabel-shape snapshot, including `ImageIcon` Path 1 per [D_icon_rendering](#D_icon_rendering)). Default renderer is `DefaultTreeCellRenderer`; `setCellRenderer` swaps the field + `refreshAll` (no re-install — the closure reads the field live) + fires `cellRenderer` PCE. `isExpanded`/`isLeaf`/`row` for the render call read the emulator's `expandedState` and row walk (D_jtree_row_path_bridge; the per-cell row walk is O(visible rows), bounded by TreeGrid's viewport paging). `convertValueToText(value, sel, expanded, leaf, row, hasFocus)` is the JDK-overridable hook the default renderer's text flows through; kept on the emulator so subclasses overriding it (common) take effect.

<a id="D_jtree_type_ports"></a>**D_jtree_type_ports — `vaadinx.swing.tree.*` port surface.** Two live classes — `TreeCellRenderer` (interface, returns `vaadinx.awt.Component`) and `DefaultTreeCellRenderer extends vaadinx.swing.JLabel implements TreeCellRenderer` (its peer is a real Vaadin component via `SJLabel`, exactly `DefaultTableCellRenderer`'s shape per [D_jtable](#D_jtable)a). `DefaultTreeCellRenderer`'s leaf/open/closed `Icon` setters ride the JLabel icon slot (Path 1); selection-colour setters (`setBackgroundSelectionColor` etc.) drop-and-WARN per R_vaadin_first (theme owns chrome). `TreeCellEditor` ports as a documentation stub — the *default* text rename lands (D_jtree_rename_in_place), but installing an *arbitrary* editor component (`setCellEditor`) is D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (b) (the `TableCellEditor` precedent: faithful in-cell swap permanently deferred). `JTree.TreeModelHandler` ports, since it keeps the emulator-owned `expandedState` in step with the model (D_jtree_row_path_bridge); `JTree.AccessibleJTree` does not (accessibility, sub-bucket (b)).

<a id="D_jtree_field_shadows"></a>**D_jtree_field_shadows — no-counterpart knobs: emulator-only R_swing_is_truth field shadows.** The asymmetric R_swing_is_truth-shadow split (SJToolBar D_jtoolbar / JSplitPane D_jsplitpane / JList D_jlist): `showsRootHandles`, `rowHeight`, `scrollsOnExpand`, `toggleClickCount`, `visibleRowCount`, `editable`, `dragEnabled`, `expandsSelectedPaths`, `invokesStopCellEditing` have no peer property, so the emulator field-shadows them (JDK-faithful round-trip + PCE) while the surrogate drops them per R_vaadin_first. `rootVisible` is the exception — it is **not** a shadow: it drives the surrogate's root-level data-provider reshaping (SD_sjtree_lazy_provider), so `setRootVisible` delegates to the peer. `editable` is the other load-bearing one: it arms the D_jtree_rename_in_place rename-in-place editor (no longer a WARN). `setDragEnabled(true)` graduates per D_jtree_row_dnd; the sizing/chrome shadows round-trip silently (R_layouts_close_enough). Vaadin TreeGrid owns real layout, so `Scrollable` getters are JDK-shaped best-effort (R_layouts_close_enough) and `getRowHeight`/`getRowBounds` read the shadow / return dummy bounds.

<a id="D_jtree_row_path_bridge"></a>**D_jtree_row_path_bridge — the emulator owns expansion; rows are a walk of the model under it.** The JDK keeps `Hashtable<TreePath, Boolean> expandedState` on `JTree` itself, and so does the emulator ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). `setExpandedState` (ancestors first, each vetoable by `TreeWillExpandListener` and announced to `TreeExpansionListener`, last to first; collapsing moves a descendant selection onto the collapsed node), `isExpanded` / `hasBeenExpanded` / `isVisible` / `makeVisible` / `getExpandedDescendants`, `clearToggledPaths` / `removeDescendantToggledPaths` and the `TreeModelHandler` subscribed through the JDK's `treeModelListener` field are the JDK bodies. The rows are what the L&F's layout cache would hold, which the emulator lacks: the root when shown, then depth first into every node the table has expanded, recomputed per call. So `getRowCount` / `getPathForRow` / `getRowForPath` / the `RowMapper` and every expansion getter answer on any thread without reaching the peer. After each change the table is flushed to the TreeGrid (`syncPeerExpansion`: a diff against the nodes last pushed, the root always, since the surrogate re-expands a shown root on its own). A browser toggle has already moved the peer when the emulator hears it; it runs the same JDK path, and a veto is undone by the flush. `scrollPathToVisible` is `makeVisible` then `scrollToItem`, only when the path is then visible (R_layouts_close_enough — no pixel scroll guarantee). The four location getters run the JDK's call graph (`getRowForLocation` → `getPathForLocation` → `getClosestPathForLocation` → `getPathBounds` → `getRowForPath`, measured on JDK 25) over the emulator's rows, and the pixel hit test at its bottom is a stash: the path the surrogate's item click reported, which the emulator holds for the whole dispatch of the mouse event it caused — so a handler parked on a modal dialog still reads it — and `null` outside one (R_layouts_close_enough; the surrogate keeps its own stash for stage 3, SD_sjtree_row_api). `getPathBounds` is called, since the JDK calls it, and its answer ignored, since it has no geometry to give. The replayed JDK 25 script in `JTreeTest.expansionMatchesTheJdk` pins the whole shape.

<a id="D_jtree_row_dnd"></a>**D_jtree_row_dnd — TreeGrid-row DnD per D_drag_and_drop (slot #11 graduation).** Per [D_drag_and_drop](#D_drag_and_drop)b/c ("later JTree's `TreeGrid`" / "later `JTree.DropLocation`"), this slice ports `vaadinx.swing.JTree.DropLocation` (carries a `TreePath` + child index) and extends `DndBridge`'s Grid-row path to the `TreeGrid` peer: `peer.setRowsDraggable(true)` + `setDropMode(GridDropMode.*)` + the drag-start/drop/drag-end listeners, with `TreeGrid`'s `getDropTargetItem()` (a node) + drop location translating to `JTree.DropLocation(pathOf(node), childIndex)` via the surrogate's `parentMap` path reconstruction. `DropMode.ON` → `GridDropMode.ON_TOP` is the natural tree shape (drop a node *onto* a folder — the Vaadin TreeGrid DnD example's `setManagerId` reparent). `setDragEnabled(true)` on JTree graduates from the D_jtree_field_shadows WARN to wired (the `dragEnabled` field stays the JDK-faithful getter and now also (re)configures the peer when a handler is present). Zero new surrogate code — `DndBridge` drives it through inherited TreeGrid API, the third "no surrogate by design" envelope (D_drag_and_drop).

<a id="D_jtree_rename_in_place"></a>**D_jtree_rename_in_place — rename-in-place over the inherited `TreeGrid.Editor` (the D_jtable_cell_editing JTable precedent).** The *default* `DefaultTreeCellEditor` text-rename behaviour lands emulator-side, mirroring [D_jtable](#D_jtable)f: the emulator drives the surrogate's inherited `TreeGrid.Editor` (`getEditor()` + the single hierarchy column's `setEditorComponent`) — the surrogate `SJTree` adds **zero** editing code, exactly the D_jtree_row_dnd/DnD "no surrogate by design" shape. A binding-less `Binder` satisfies Vaadin's editor requirement; `setBuffered(false)` so a blur closes-and-commits. `startEditingAtPath` seeds a Vaadin `TextField` from `convertValueToText` (the node value, **not** the renderer's decoration — Swing edits the model text), sets it as the hierarchy column's editor component, and opens the editor. Commit → `TreeModel.valueForPathChanged(path, text)`, which the surrogate already turns into a `treeNodesChanged` → `refreshItem` repaint (SD_sjtree_is_model_listener) — the same reason no surrogate change is needed. **Trigger:** a double-click, or programmatic `startEditingAtPath`, gated by `isEditable()` + `isPathEditable()`. Desktop Swing instead uses a select-then-slow-click timer; double-click is an accepted R_best_effort_behaviour divergence and is **collision-free** because Vaadin `TreeGrid` expands on the toggle arrow, not a row double-click (confirmed by a gate-b spike). **Commit/cancel keys** are wired per-open as grid-scoped `Shortcuts` (Enter → commit, Escape → cancel), then removed on cleanup — Vaadin's built-in editor keys don't fire for a programmatic single-column `setEditorComponent` (the JTable B9 finding). `isEditing` / `getEditingPath` / `stopEditing` (commit) / `cancelEditing` (discard) round-trip the lifecycle. **Only the default text editor lands** — an arbitrary `setCellEditor(TreeCellEditor)` stays D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (b) and still WARNs (D_jtree_type_ports). **Cosmetic limitation (R_layouts_close_enough):** while the editor is open the cell's hierarchy indent + toggle are absent (the editor component replaces the `HierarchyColumnComponentRenderer` cell); edit-only, close-enough.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Value-`equals` `TreeModel` node collision** (SD_sjtree_node_identity) — surfaces at the emulator as duplicate-node selection/render confusion; R_best_effort_behaviour, documented; identity-wrapper is the future fix.
- **Arbitrary in-cell editor** (`setCellEditor(TreeCellEditor)`) — D_gap_severity_triage sub-bucket (b), permanently deferred (JTable cell-editor precedent); WARNs. The *default* text rename lands per D_jtree_rename_in_place; while editing, the cell's indent/toggle chrome is absent (R_layouts_close_enough cosmetic, edit-only).
- **A vetoed browser toggle flickers.** The browser opens or closes the node before the server hears of it, so a `TreeWillExpandListener` veto is applied by re-collapsing or re-expanding it.
- **Pixel geometry** (`getRowBounds`, `getPathBounds`, `getRowForLocation`'s true hit-test) — R_layouts_close_enough, no server-side coordinates; the click-stash covers the live-dispatch case, dummy bounds otherwise.

**Validation.** `:emulators` — `JTreeTest` (35): peer-type pin via `assertIs<SJTree>`, R_leaf_peer_lockdown reflection check (no protected `(Component)` ctor), all ctors incl. `DefaultTreeModel`-building convenience forms, model delegation + `setModel` swap, two-layer `addTreeSelectionListener` source-rebound (incl. across `setSelectionModel` swap) — the `CaseTreeView` selection path, JDK-shaped `getSelectionModel(): TreeSelectionModel` reads through the surrogate's `getTreeSelectionModel()`, expansion, veto, collapse-moves-selection and model removal against a script replayed from JDK 25, browser toggles (including a vetoed one) through TreeGrid's user-originated expand, default + custom `TreeCellRenderer` render via Karibu (snapshot bridge) + `convertValueToText` override, right-click mouse re-source with `isPopupTrigger` + `getRowForLocation` stash (the `selectOnRightClick` path), `getPathForRow`/`getRowForPath`/`getRowCount` over a partially-collapsed tree, `setRootVisible(false)` delegates to peer, no-counterpart knobs PCE + `setDragEnabled(true)` WARN, the D_jtree_rename_in_place rename-in-place lifecycle (open via `startEditingAtPath` → commit through a recording `valueForPathChanged`, cancel + disarm no-writeback, `setCellEditor` still WARNs), `getUIClassID == "TreeUI"`, Scrollable, plus the D_jtree_row_dnd DnD path (drag-start selection sync, `DropMode` validation, ON_TOP→`childIndex == -1` and ABOVE/BELOW→parent-path+model-index drop-location mapping) through the `DndBridge` test seams. `:sampler` — `TreesPanel` (case-folder hierarchy: `DefaultTreeModel`, select / expand / right-click-to-select, rename-in-place via double-click / a Rename button, a custom `DefaultTreeCellRenderer` subclass distinguishing folders from documents via text glyphs — no icon assets in Sampler, the `ImageIcon` Path-1 slot stays covered by `:emulators` icon tests — and TreeGrid-row drag-to-reparent wiring) + `TreesWarnInventoryTest` (2 tests: user-path + JTree API-surface micro-driver incl. the D_jtree_rename_in_place rename lifecycle, with enumerated intentional-WARN paths) + `NavigationSmokeTest` entry.

<a id="D_file_dialogs"></a>
## D_file_dialogs. File dialogs — `FileDialog` (AWT) + `JFileChooser` (Swing) emulator-only, shared `BrowserFileTransfer`, `java.io.File` gap bridged via per-session temp uploads/downloads

**Status: landed** (the file-IO slice). Covers `vaadinx.awt.FileDialog`, `vaadinx.swing.JFileChooser`, the shared `vaadinx.BrowserFileTransfer` helper, `vaadinx.SaveOutputs` (D_save_binds_download's directory walk), and the per-UI `vaadinx.UiScheduler`. FileDialog was built first as the simpler vehicle; JFileChooser second on the same machinery. (This entry retroactively documents FileDialog, which landed WIP-in-code-only without a D-entry.)

**Decision.** Both file-pick hosts land **emulator-only**. `FileDialog` is-a `vaadinx.awt.Dialog`, so it parks via the inherited modal latch ([D_callswing_loom](#D_callswing_loom) loom machinery). `JFileChooser` is the **JOptionPane shape** ([SD_no_sjoptionpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_no_sjoptionpane) / [D_joptionpane](#D_joptionpane)): no surrogate (there is no Swing dir-tree to reproduce in a browser), peer is a vestigial `Div`, and the real UI is an **internal modal `JDialog` built at show\* time** whose `setVisible(true)` parks the calling VT. The two can't share by inheritance, so the browser-transfer mechanics live in `vaadinx.BrowserFileTransfer` (with D_save_binds_download's pure directory walk factored out into `vaadinx.SaveOutputs`) and each host keeps its own park + buttons + result shape. The core gap both bridge: `java.io.File` has no browser equivalent, so **LOAD** stages a Vaadin `Upload` into a per-session temp file ([`SessionTempFiles`](#)) the migrated code reads back as an ordinary `File`, and **SAVE** hands back a per-session temp *target* the app writes to, then offers a synthetic download.

<a id="D_file_load_path"></a>**D_file_load_path — LOAD: upload → temp `File`, filter enforced server-side.** `BrowserFileTransfer.wireUpload` builds the `Upload` + a rejection-notice `Span` into the host's peer dialog and returns the synchronized list each accepted upload stages. It uses the modern streams `UploadHandler.toFile` — the deferred per-file success callback (under the session lock, after bytes are on disk), **not** `AllFinishedEvent` (fires earlier), is the "file ready" signal. The real filter runs against the real staged file: matches stage + enable the approve button, non-matches are deleted with a notice. We can't avoid the transfer (the browser uploads on selection) but refuse to hand the app a rejected file — faithful in *outcome* to the desktop "can't pick it" contract, not in mechanism. `multipleMode` / `multiSelectionEnabled` → `Upload.setMaxFiles`.

<a id="D_file_save_two_dialog"></a>**D_file_save_two_dialog — SAVE: two-dialog design; "block until written" would deadlock.** (1) The host's own modal dialog hosts a filename `TextField` + Save/Cancel and blocks **only for the name pick** — Save returns the name + a temp target, Cancel returns null. (2) Once Save returns, the app writes the file (sync or background); meanwhile a **separate non-modal "synthetic" Vaadin dialog** — invisible to the Swing app, like an a11y overlay — offers a real download link per file the app produced, clicked once their app has finished writing. The name picked in (1) seeds the target handed to the app but is **not** what the download is bound to: the app may write elsewhere in the directory, so the binding is to the directory (D_save_binds_download). We deliberately do **not** detect "fully written" (impossible in general — the write may be a background job): the human is the completion oracle. Blocking until written would **deadlock** — the write lives *after* `setVisible` returns, so a park there would wedge the very write the user is waiting on. The download dialog's size readout **auto-refreshes** on `UiScheduler` and pushes live (D_ui_scheduler); an early click that grabs a partial file is recoverable by waiting and re-clicking (the link streams current contents each click). Faithful divergence from desktop (R_best_effort_behaviour/R_vaadin_first): desktop saves silently to a chosen path; we make the user pull the file afterward.

<a id="D_ui_scheduler"></a>**D_ui_scheduler — `vaadinx.UiScheduler`: shared per-UI scheduled executor.** A single-thread daemon `ScheduledExecutorService` per UI (the lazy-attach + `shutdownNow()`-on-detach idiom of `Timer`'s old private `TimerScheduler` / `SwingWorker`'s `WorkerPool` / `EHelper`'s then per-UI callSwing executor), promoted to `vaadinx` and marked internal. `forUI(ui)` returns the executor directly. The scheduler thread does no user work — tasks hop to the UI thread via `ui.access`. **`Timer` was refactored onto it** (its private `TimerScheduler` deleted); the SAVE download watcher is its second client (`scheduleWithFixedDelay`, 500 ms, cancelled on the download dialog's `OpenedChangeListener` close, UI-detach `shutdownNow` as backstop) — it re-walks the transfer directory and reconciles the link rows, not just one file's size (D_save_binds_download). The watcher carries **no no-push fallback** — Push is mandatory (project-level invariant; emulator code may assume it). The earlier manual "Refresh size" button was removed when the auto-watch landed.

<a id="D_jfilechooser_park"></a>**D_jfilechooser_park — JFileChooser: internal-JDialog park + int return + filter adaptation.** `showOpenDialog` drives the LOAD path; `showSaveDialog` the SAVE path; `showDialog(parent, approveText)` throws (D_showdialog_throws). Each builds an internal modal `JDialog` owned by `parent`'s window ancestor (the `JOptionPane.createDialog` walk), `DISPOSE_ON_CLOSE` so X/ESC unparks → `CANCEL_OPTION`. Approve/Cancel are raw Vaadin Buttons whose handlers funnel through `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope — `dispose()` fires the Swing-side `WINDOW_CLOSED`). Result maps to `APPROVE_OPTION` / `CANCEL_OPTION`; `getSelectedFile(s)` read the staged temp files (LOAD) or temp target (SAVE). The Swing `FileFilter` (`File → boolean`) adapts to `wireUpload`'s `(dir, name) → boolean`; a **`FileNameExtensionFilter`** additionally sets `Upload`'s accepted-types to pre-narrow the browser picker (opaque filters can't expose extensions, so they fall back to server-side enforcement only — the authoritative gate either way).

<a id="D_file_dialogs_lockdown"></a>**D_file_dialogs_lockdown — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `JFileChooser` is a leaf in the public Swing hierarchy — no protected `(Component peer)` ctor; every ctor funnels through the no-arg ctor's `super(new Div())`. It stays non-final (JDK shape); the vestigial Div peer is never user-swappable. `FileDialog` inherits its Vaadin `Dialog` peer through `vaadinx.awt.Dialog`'s ctor chain (it adds no peer seam of its own); nothing public extends `java.awt.FileDialog`.

<a id="D_showdialog_throws"></a>**D_showdialog_throws — `JFileChooser.showDialog` throws, unconditionally, and is `@Deprecated`: the migrator is the only party that can supply the direction.** *(Decided + landed 2026-08-24; the enumerated R_match_swing_errors throw trigger case (4). First of the three save-intent problems: this one is the undeclared direction; D_save_binds_download is the predicted download path; D_showsavedialog_return_ignored the ignored return value.)*

`showDialog(parent, approveText)` sets `CUSTOM_DIALOG`, which declares **no direction**. On the desktop that costs nothing: all three `show*` variants merely put up a picker and return a `File`, and the app does the I/O afterwards — the JDK never acts on `dialogType`. In a browser LOAD and SAVE are different machinery outright (D_file_load_path vs D_file_save_two_dialog) and the mechanism must be committed **before** the dialog opens. Mapping `CUSTOM_DIALOG` to LOAD is the correct reading of the JDK contract in the abstract, and it fails **silently** on the common idiom of using a custom-button chooser to *name an output*: the user gets an upload, the app writes a real file server-side, no download is ever attached, and nothing throws or WARNs. So `showDialog` throws `IllegalStateException` with a message that names both replacements, and carries `@Deprecated`.

- **Why the migrator, and no one else.** *Observation can serve SAVE but never LOAD.* You can notice after the fact that the app wrote something; you cannot retroactively upload a file the browser never sent. The direction is therefore undeterminable at show time from anything except the source, which collapses the decider list to one party: whoever ports the call site.
