The migrating agent reads `getSelectedFile()`'s next few lines — reads → `showOpenDialog`, writes → `showSaveDialog`, both keeping a custom label via `setApproveButtonText`; a runtime-conditional direction splits into two branches calling the matching variant.
- **Why throwing is R_match_swing_errors-consistent, not a category break.** The three prior triggers share the property that *no continuation is defensible*. Upload-for-a-pick is defensible in itself — but only for pick-shaped call sites, and SB-Emulators structurally cannot tell which it has, so from SB-Emulators' vantage point no continuation is defensible either. That is case (3)'s shape exactly (`Date↔LocalDate` without `BrowserTimeZone.fetch()`): a default that is right in some deployments, unknowable from inside, silently wrong forever when wrong, and a one-line mechanical fix at the call site. Swap "an hour off" for "unreachable bytes" and it is the same entry. Per R_match_swing_errors's fallback there is no equivalent Swing failure to mirror, hence `IllegalStateException` (`UnsupportedOperationException` reads better for "cannot be emulated" but R_match_swing_errors names ISE; the message carries the teaching).
- **`@Deprecated` is the completeness gate; the throw is the residue net.** A throw only fires on paths someone walks, so alone it would leave untriaged sites invisible until exercised. The deprecation warning names **every** call site at compile time, mechanically, including ones nobody exercises — annotation-only, so no signature divergence and no R_no_vaadin_in_api concern. Together they double-gate: an untriaged `showDialog` neither compiles clean nor runs. A migrator on `-Werror -Xlint:deprecation` gets a build break, which here is the feature. **`WarnInventoryTest`s are unaffected** — a throw is not a WARN, so the exit gates cannot catch an untriaged site; the compiler is what makes the sweep complete.
- **No opt-out**, no system property, no `SwingBridgeConfig` direction default: it would immediately become the shortcut that reinstates the silence, and nothing legitimately needs it (the conditional case branches).
- **Unconditional, including the null-label form.** The JDK flips to `CUSTOM_DIALOG` only when `approveButtonText != null`, so `showDialog(parent, null)` runs under whatever `dialogType` the app already declared — a genuinely unambiguous direction we could honour. We throw anyway: the case is vanishingly rare, and a rare honoured path is a rare *untested* path and a hole in the guarantee.
- **What stays faithful.** The throw is on the *show*, not on the type: `setDialogType(CUSTOM_DIALOG)` / `getDialogType()` keep round-tripping, and no state is mutated before the throw (no `dialogType` write, no `approveButtonText` write) — the call is a no-op plus an exception.
- **Migrator guidance shipped with it** (needed whatever SB-Emulators decides — no SB-Emulators-side change removes the need to tell migrators that a chooser used to name an output must become `showSaveDialog`, and that the browser has no directory to write into): a [`§7` hazard entry](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/spec.md) with a grep-complete `Detect:` (`\.showDialog\s*\(`, verified against the inventory testapp's two call sites and nothing else) plus the paired `hazard-scan.sh` line, and the triage rule as the guide's *"`JFileChooser.showDialog` — you must pick a direction"* section, which also carries the two fixes that belong at the same call sites (check the return value; don't derive a path from the name). Its local-LLM overlay tag is the point of the whole change — **judgment · secret-free**, and pointedly **not ⚠silent**: detection is now a compiler warning *and* a grep *and* a throw, so the hazard rides the stuck-signal instead of needing a review-gate. The judgment call did not disappear, it got **fenced** — bounded to named call sites with a fail-loud default when the model cannot resolve it, where before it was unbounded and fail-silent.

**Rejected alternatives (D_showdialog_throws).**
- **Dual-affordance `CUSTOM_DIALOG`** — one dialog carrying both an `Upload` and a "File name" field, letting the end user pick. Rejected: the desktop dialog does not *offer a choice*, a native file browser just happens to do pick-existing and name-new with one widget, so the directionlessness is invisible to the user. The browser has no such widget, and gluing two together asks the human to **guess what the app already decided** from a label its author wrote for a different widget. The guess is also asymmetric — uploading in a save is recoverable, naming in a load is a `FileNotFoundException` — so one branch of the offered choice is a hard break.
- **Approve-label heuristic** (`/save|export|write|output/i` → SAVE) — silent and locale-bound, and strictly dominated by an LLM that can read the surrounding code. A heuristic choosing the *mechanism* is precisely the silent wrongness being eliminated; even the weaker "use it only to order the affordances" form dies with the dual dialog.
- **Keep the upload and WARN** — a WARN on a genuine pick is a false positive, and false positives train migrators to ignore the inventory that other gates depend on.
- **Observation-only** (infer the direction from what the app did with the `File`) — the structural non-starter above: it cannot serve LOAD. It survives as the answer shape for problem 2, not problem 1.

<a id="D_save_binds_download"></a>**D_save_binds_download — SAVE binds the download to the transfer *directory*, not to the predicted file.** *(Decided + landed 2026-08-24; the walk factored out to `vaadinx.SaveOutputs`. Second of the three save-intent problems — see D_showdialog_throws. Fixes both hosts at once: the download dialog is shared, and `FileDialog`'s SAVE had the identical bug.)*

D_file_save_two_dialog allocated `<transfer-dir>/<typed-name>` and bound the download link to **that exact path**. Swing never promised the app writes there — on the desktop `getSelectedFile()` is a path the app is free to *derive* from, and deriving is routine: `getAbsolutePath() + ".xls"`, an extension swap, several files from one pick, a name computed elsewhere under `getCurrentDirectory()`, a library appending its own suffix. Every one of those writes a **sibling** of the file the link points at, so the user gets a dialog whose readout says "Not written yet" forever and whose link streams zero bytes, while the real output sits beside it, unreachable. The emulator was binding to a path it **predicted**, when the only thing it actually knows is the **directory it owns**.

So it binds to the directory. `SessionTempFiles.newTransferDir()` already hands each show a **fresh, empty, unique** directory under the per-session root, so everything found there afterwards is, by construction, the app's output — no heuristics, no cross-user collision, nothing to disambiguate. The `UiScheduler` watcher (D_ui_scheduler) already polls that window every 500 ms; it re-walks the directory instead of stat-ing one path, and reconciles a link row per discovered file.

The walk itself is **`vaadinx.SaveOutputs`, a separate class**, not a corner of `BrowserFileTransfer`. Two different jobs live either side of that seam: *which files did this save produce, and which one goes on top* is a pure question — a directory, a name, an ordering, no Vaadin and no session — while `BrowserFileTransfer` is dialogs, uploads, download handlers and a scheduler. Keeping them apart is what lets the interesting half be unit-tested directly (`SaveOutputsTest`, no Karibu) instead of through a modal park and a 500 ms poll. `SaveOutputs.discover(dir, promptedName)` returns the record `(files, truncated)`, and `MAX_VISITED_ENTRIES` lives with it.

- **Why observation is legitimate here and was not for problem 1.** The asymmetry is the whole design: *observation can serve SAVE but never LOAD*. A LOAD decision must precede the browser interaction (nothing can retroactively upload a file the browser never sent), which is why D_showdialog_throws hands it to the migrator; a SAVE binding is needed only *after* the app's write, which is a window SB-Emulators is already watching. D_file_save_two_dialog's deadlock argument is satisfied trivially — a directory can be bound before anything exists in it, so nothing parks on the write.
- **Breadth-first, capped on entries *visited*, no depth cap.** Subdirectories count: the directory starts empty, so an `out/` the app created is the app's. The walk is **breadth-first** so the cap is meaningful — you get the shallowest N, which are the likely outputs, where a depth-first walk could spend the whole budget inside the first subdirectory. The motivating shape: an app that builds a large tree and then zips it writes the *one file that matters* at the root, and BFS surfaces it first. The cap counts **every directory entry visited**, not files displayed — a tree of 10 000 empty directories contains no files, would never trip a file-based cap, and would be re-walked in full every 500 ms. Counting visits also makes a depth cap redundant rather than merely usually-redundant: the walk cannot descend past what the visit budget allows. Symlinked directories are **not followed** (a symlink loop would spin the walk, and there is no case where following one is what the migrator meant). Directories are traversal, not rows — only files get a link. When the cap trips the dialog says so, rather than silently showing a truncated list.
- **Ordering is deterministic, and stable under a growing file.** Rows reconcile rather than rebuild (below), so an ordering that shifts between ticks would move rows under the user's cursor: mtime-first and size-first are both rejected for exactly that, since they reorder while the app writes. Files sort by `(depth, parent path, in-folder order)` — depth first is what puts root files above nested ones; parent path keeps same-depth files from different directories from interleaving nondeterministically. **In-folder order** is: (1) how well the file matches the **name the user typed at the prompt** — whole name, then stem, then stem-prefix — which is the one importance signal available and is stable because it cannot change as bytes are written; it is what surfaces `untitled.xls` for a prompt of `untitled`, and the rank has to look past the stem because an app writing `report.log` / `report.tmp` / `report.xls` beside a prompt of `report.xls` ties all three on stem alone and the extension tiebreak then puts `.log` on top — the exact wrong-file-first outcome the rank exists to prevent; then (2) extension ascending, then file name ascending, both case-insensitive with a case-sensitive fallback so `README` and `readme` cannot swap places between ticks. Alphabetical alone carries no importance signal — for `report.log` / `report.tmp` / `report.xls` extension-ascending puts `.log` on top — which is why the prompted-name match precedes it; grouping (`page_1.png … page_20.png` beside a `manifest.txt`) is what it is actually good for.
- **Rows are keyed by relative path and reconciled, not rebuilt.** Rebuilding anchors each tick would flicker and reset the per-row "Downloaded ✓" mark. New paths add a row, vanished paths remove one, sizes update in place — which renders the `report.xls.tmp` → rename sequence exactly as watching the folder in a file manager does, which is the honest picture and matches D_file_save_two_dialog's human-is-the-oracle stance.
- **Display the relative path, download under the base name.** `out/report.xls` reads correctly in the dialog; the `Content-Disposition` hint must be the bare name regardless (browsers sanitise path separators). This also fixes a second, quieter bug in the old binding: even when the app wrote where we predicted, the suggested filename was the name the *user typed*, not the name the app *produced* — `untitled` for a file the app made as `untitled.xls`.
- **Nothing discovered → a stated dialog message, plus a WARN when the human closes it.** "No files available for download yet" is what the end user sees. The migrator-facing WARN fires on dialog close with zero files ever discovered — there is no "app is done" signal, so no earlier moment is honest, but the close *is* the human giving up, the same oracle used throughout D_file_dialogs. This is the case D_save_binds_download cannot fix (an app writing to an unrelated absolute path) becoming **detectable** rather than silent, which is worth more than it looks: today "the link streams nothing" is indistinguishable from "the user clicked early".
- **The name prompt stays, with its contract restated.** (1) still prompts and still pre-fills from `setSelectedFile`, and `getSelectedFile()` still returns that real writable `File` — migrated code calls `getAbsolutePath()` on it freely. What changes is the name's *role*: it seeds the target the app is handed, and is a suggestion the app may override, rather than the path the download is bound to.
- **No signature change.** `BrowserFileTransfer.openDownloadDialog(File target, String name)` keeps its shape and derives the directory as `target.getParentFile()` — which is the transfer dir for both hosts, since both allocate via `newSaveTarget`. The in-memory `openDownloadDialog(byte[], name)` variant is unaffected (no directory involved).

**Rejected alternative (D_save_binds_download).** *The migrating agent reports the real path back to the emulator* (a `SwingBridgeDownload.offer(file)`-shaped call inserted after the write). Rejected on three counts: it puts a **SB-Emulators-specific call with no Swing counterpart into migrated code**, so a stage-2 view stops compiling against real Swing and the migrator loses the ability to diff against their original — a different category of change from the import-swap stage 2 promises; the inference is **strictly harder and non-local** than D_showdialog_throws's (that one asks "does the next statement read or write this path", answerable in a line or two; this one asks what path the write *landed* on, which can mean following a library into its own code or a background thread); and it is **silent when wrong** — a misreported path reproduces the exact zero-byte link being eliminated, whereas observation either finds the bytes or reports finding none.

**Accepted limitations (D_save_binds_download).** An app that writes to an unrelated absolute path outside the directory it was handed is not covered — detectable (above) but not fixable. Transient files churn the row list while a library writes-then-renames; shown as-is deliberately. "No write-complete detection" is unchanged from D_file_save_two_dialog — the human remains the completion oracle.

<a id="D_showsavedialog_return_ignored"></a>**D_showsavedialog_return_ignored — the ignored `show*` return value is the app's own bug: SB-Emulators owes nothing, the guide states it, the testbed keeps it.** *(Decided 2026-08-25; no code change. Third of the three save-intent problems — see D_showdialog_throws. The only one of the three that turned out not to be an SB-Emulators defect at all; recorded because it was investigated as one, and because the *guide* had to change.)*

Migrated code routinely discards `show*`'s `int` and dereferences `getSelectedFile()` on the next line, so a cancel throws `NullPointerException`. **That is faithful, not broken.** The JDK's own `CancelSelectionAction` nulls the selection on cancel, and both emulator paths reproduce it: `doLoad` and `doSave` each set `selectedFile = null` / `selectedFiles = new File[0]` before returning `CANCEL_OPTION`. An emulator that returned something non-null to spare the caller would be diverging from Swing to paper over the caller's bug — R_swing_is_truth backwards.

- **What the browser changes is the hit rate, not the nature.** Desktop users rarely cancel a save dialog they deliberately opened; browser users cancel an unexpected upload widget or name prompt readily. A crash that fired once a year fires in ordinary use. That is a migrator-visible surprise worth documenting and *not* a reason to change behaviour — the alternative reading, "the browser makes this common so the emulator should soften it", is how faithful emulation erodes one sympathetic case at a time.
- **The symptom is worth stating, because it is not the desktop's.** The NPE escapes the `ActionListener` into Vaadin's `ErrorHandler` — logged server-side, no dialog, the button simply looks inert — where on the desktop it hit the EDT's uncaught handler and printed to stderr. In the canonical shape the app's own `catch` never fires either, because the throw is on the `getSelectedFile()` line, *before* the `try` around the write. A silently-inert export button is the signature.
- **Rejected: WARN when `getSelectedFile()` returns null after a cancel.** It would fire on every correct caller too — checking the return value and returning early is exactly the right code, and it reads the selection in neither branch, so the WARN could only be attached to the null read itself, which the correct caller never makes... except when it does (`if (f == null) return;` is an equally valid guard). A gate that cannot distinguish the bug from its own fix is noise, and it would pollute the `WarnInventoryTest` budget the other gates depend on.
- **The guide states it instead of prescribing the fix.** This is the one place the answer had to change something. The §7 recipe used to say "two things to fix while you are in there" and inlined the `!= APPROVE_OPTION` early-return into its worked example — folding an unrelated behaviour change into an edit D_showdialog_throws already *forces* the migrator to make. It now describes the behaviour, the hit rate, and the symptom, then tells the migrator to record the bug and fix it in a **separate** commit after the port verifies, with the guarded form supplied for that commit. The reasoning generalises past this call site: a port whose diff mixes required rewrites with silent behaviour changes cannot be reviewed, because a behavioural difference from the desktop app can no longer be attributed.
- **The inventory testapp keeps both NPEs on purpose.** `StockQueryPanel:138` / `ItemReturnPanel:326` are the sharpest fidelity probe in the corpus precisely *because* D_showdialog_throws forces the port to touch those exact lines: a tempting adjacent bug on the one line that cannot be avoided. Expected port swaps the direction and changes nothing else; reporting the NPE as a finding is fine, silently fixing it is the failure mode being measured. Registered in that app's `PROVENANCE.md` under "bugs included, because they are ported, not fixed", beside the `ResourceManager.getImage` null image kept for the same reason.

**Confirmed deferrals (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c) — WARN-drop, never throw).** `JFileChooser.setAccessory` / `getAccessory` (no embedded-panel slot in a browser dialog); `DIRECTORIES_ONLY` (no browser bare-directory-handle pick — stored for round-trip, WARN on set, the show\* path always behaves as a file pick); opaque-`FileFilter` browser pre-narrow (server-side enforce only); `FileDialog.setDirectory` (no server-side dir to start the picker in); `FileSystemView` (not exposed). `getCurrentDirectory` round-trips a non-null field (defaults to `user.home`) so the common `getCurrentDirectory().getAbsolutePath()` idiom doesn't NPE — no server FS browse behind it. `setAcceptAllFileFilterUsed` is accepted-and-stored silently (commonly called, no behavioural counterpart — a per-call WARN would be noise).

**Accepted limitations.**
- **No write-complete detection** (SAVE) — the human is the oracle; an early download of a partial file is recoverable by re-clicking (R_best_effort_behaviour).
- **No server-side filesystem browse** — LOAD is a browser upload, not a server dir tree; `currentDirectory` / `setDirectory` are cosmetic round-trips.
- **Browser picker can't be pre-narrowed for opaque filters** — only `FileNameExtensionFilter` exposes the extensions needed for the accept-attribute hint; everything else relies on the (authoritative) server-side `accept` (R_best_effort_behaviour, faithful in outcome).

**Validation.** `:emulators` — `FileDialogTest` (10: LOAD single/multi/cancel, OK-gated-on-upload, SAVE name-pick + directory-bound synthetic download (empty at open, then a derived sibling offered — D_save_binds_download is in the shared helper, so AWT SAVE inherits it) + cancel, `FilenameFilter` server-side enforce, non-VT park guard, `setDirectory` noop) + `SaveOutputsTest` (12 — D_save_binds_download's walk, pure, no Karibu: empty/null/missing dir, the `+ ".xls"` sibling, BFS root-before-nested, the zip-beside-a-tree case, prompted-name rank (whole name > stem > prefix) and its win over extension-ascending, case-insensitive extension/name order with a stable case-sensitive tiebreak, the cap counting directories, truncation keeping what was found, symlinks neither followed nor offered) + `JFileChooserTest` (19: non-VT park guard, approve-gated-on-upload, single/multi open, cancel→CANCEL_OPTION, the four D_showdialog_throws `showDialog` tests (throws with both replacements + `setApproveButtonText` named in the message, throws for the null-label form and inside a VT envelope with no dialog built, mutates nothing before throwing, `setDialogType(CUSTOM_DIALOG)` still round-trips), SAVE target + download affordance + cancel, opaque-`FileFilter` enforce, `FileNameExtensionFilter` accept-type narrow, the D_save_binds_download SAVE trio (empty dialog at open then a link once the app writes, a derived `+ ".xls"` sibling offered under the name the app produced, several files root-before-nested), `currentDirectory` round-trip, `dialogType` validation, `DIRECTORIES_ONLY` WARN-store, accessory noop) + `TimerTest` (15, unchanged across the `UiScheduler` refactor). `:sampler` — `FileDialogsPanel` (FileDialog open/multi/save + JFileChooser open-with-extension-filter/save) + `FileDialogsWarnInventoryTest` (4 user paths: FileDialog LOAD + SAVE, JFileChooser open + save).

<a id="D_toolkit_full_surface"></a>
## D_toolkit_full_surface. `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit` is a full-surface emulator — `getDefaultToolkit()` singleton, browser-backed where faithful, WARN-default elsewhere; collapses the `Toolkit` migration rule to "always swap"

**Status: landed.** Surfaced by the JLawyer-shape migration round: the migrated app's `Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit().getSystemClipboard()` threw `java.awt.HeadlessException` at runtime because the migrator — following the guide's "`Toolkit` stays JDK" rule ([D_whitelist_porting](#D_whitelist_porting)) — left `import java.awt.Toolkit;`, reaching the server JVM's `sun.awt.HeadlessToolkit`. The follow-up docfix (point all `Toolkit` usage at `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit`) is done — the always-swap rule lives in `migration/1-swing-to-emulators/spec.md` §port table and `guides/1-swing-to-emulators/import-swap-reference.md` (the `Toolkit` watch-out), with the D_toolkit_screen_size viewport semantics noted alongside.

**Decision.** Promote `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit` from D_clipboard's clipboard-only minimal slice to a **full-surface emulator** like every other emulated class — the complete `java.awt.Toolkit` public method surface (hand-written from the `javap` signatures rather than generated; `java.awt.Toolkit` isn't in the [D_generated_stubs](#D_generated_stubs) generator whitelist and the per-method bodies are too custom for a skeleton to help). An import-swap recompiles **unchanged** and the migration rule collapses to one line — **`java.awt.Toolkit` → `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit`, always**, no carve-out, no shape change at the call site. The class stays **standalone** (does NOT extend the abstract `java.awt.Toolkit`): it's the import-swap surface, not a platform toolkit, so it exposes only the public API and drops every `protected` method (no one subclasses it — it's `final`).

This **reverses D_clipboard's "Port `Toolkit`'s full surface — Rejected" alternative** and **amends D_whitelist_porting's `Toolkit`-specific minimal-surface note**, on a correction to the reasoning behind both: a missing method on an *in-scope emulator class* is an **emulator bug, not a signal**. Emulators are the import-swap drop-in ([D_import_swap_target](#D_import_swap_target)) — user code must compile unchanged, and *behaviour* degrades via WARN ([R_match_swing_errors](#D_never_fail_on_gaps) / [D_gap_severity_triage](#D_gap_severity_triage)). Compile-failure-on-unsupported is the **surrogate** tool ([R_vaadin_first](../surrogates/decisions.md), which fails on inputs the Vaadin peer can't represent), not the emulator tool. D_clipboard correctly rejected *delegating* the full surface to the JDK toolkit; it over-rejected by also dropping the *surface*, which left `java.awt.Toolkit`'s non-clipboard methods reachable only as the JDK headless toolkit — a runtime `HeadlessException` instead of a triageable WARN. (`Toolkit` is now firmly in scope — clipboard landed in D_clipboard — so the D_whitelist_porting "minimum port surface" stance no longer applies to it; D_whitelist_porting still governs whether *other* unported AWT classes enter scope.)

<a id="D_toolkit_singleton"></a>**D_toolkit_singleton — `getDefaultToolkit()` returns a global stateless singleton; `getSystemClipboard()` becomes a JDK-faithful instance method.** `java.awt.Toolkit`'s accessors are *instance* methods reached via the static `getDefaultToolkit()` factory; D_clipboard's `static getSystemClipboard()` was a shape divergence that wouldn't round-trip a mechanical swap. D_toolkit_full_surface restores the JDK shape. The singleton is **global, not per-UI** — the toolkit object is stateless; all per-UI state lives elsewhere (`WebClipboard` per UI, `BrowserToolkitInfo` per UI), resolved at call time via `UI.getCurrent()`. So obtaining the toolkit needs no UI (it works at frame-construction time, off any VT); only the browser-touching calls do. `getSystemClipboard()` is now an **instance method** doing the per-UI `WebClipboard` lazy-init. Java cannot declare a same-named static *and* instance method, so the D_clipboard `static getSystemClipboard()` was **removed** (not kept as a deprecated convenience — that's impossible alongside the instance form), and the ~30 internal `:emulators`/`:sampler` call sites moved to `getDefaultToolkit().getSystemClipboard()`. No app code regresses: the JDK only ever had the instance form, so no migrated app wrote a static `Toolkit.getSystemClipboard()`.

<a id="D_gettoolkit_returns_emulator"></a>**D_gettoolkit_returns_emulator — `Component.getToolkit()` / `Window.getToolkit()` return `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit`, not `java.awt.Toolkit`.** `component.getToolkit().getScreenSize()` is the *same* `HeadlessException` trap as the bare `Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit()` path — `java.awt.Component.getToolkit()` returned the headless JDK toolkit. Both `getToolkit()` overrides now return the `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit` global singleton, and `Component.getFontMetrics` routes through `getToolkit().getFontMetrics()` (one source of truth). After an import-swap, `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit tk = component.getToolkit();` compiles and `tk.getScreenSize()` works.

<a id="D_toolkit_five_tiers"></a>**D_toolkit_five_tiers — five-tier bodies, grounded in an empirical headless probe.** Running each `java.awt.Toolkit` method under `-Djava.awt.headless=true` split the surface cleanly into what a server JVM computes correctly vs. what throws `HeadlessException`. The governing principle: **delegate to the headless JDK toolkit where the value is client-independent and the JVM is authoritative; browser-back genuinely client-specific values; fabricate a faithful constant where headless throws but the value is client-independent; throw where the JDK itself throws; WARN-and-ignore only where there's no web counterpart at all.**
1. **Delegate to the headless JDK toolkit** (verified to return real values headless): `getFontMetrics` (real `FontDesignMetrics` — `stringWidth`/`height` are correct), `getFontList`, `getSystemEventQueue`, `getDesktopProperty`, `isAlwaysOnTopSupported`, the `PropertyChangeListener` plumbing, and the static `getProperty`. No WARN — these are real, faithful values.
2. **Browser-backed** (client-specific; the JDK toolkit throws `HeadlessException`) — implemented **now** via `BrowserToolkitInfo` (D_toolkit_from_client_details): `getScreenSize` (the browser *viewport*, live-resize-tracked, per D_toolkit_screen_size), `getScreenResolution` (`96 × devicePixelRatio`), `getMenuShortcutKeyMaskEx`/`getMenuShortcutKeyMask` (`META` on macOS/iOS, else `CTRL`). `getScreenInsets` is browser-conceptually-empty → `Insets(0,0,0,0)` (no round-trip).
3. **Throw, faithful to the JDK contract (R_match_swing_errors)**: `getLockingKeyState`/`setLockingKeyState` → `UnsupportedOperationException`, exactly what a real toolkit throws on a host that can't toggle locking keys.
4. **Fabricate a faithful constant** (headless-throwing, client-independent) — no WARN: `getColorModel` → `ColorModel.getRGBdefault()`; `getMaximumCursorColors` → 0 / `getBestCursorSize` → `(0,0)` ("custom cursors unsupported"); `getSystemSelection` → null; `isModalityTypeSupported` → **true** (modal dialogs park a UI fiber); `isFrameStateSupported`/`isModalExclusionTypeSupported`/`isDynamicLayoutActive` → false; `areExtraMouseButtonsEnabled` → true.
5. **WARN + ignore** via `EHelper.onUnimplemented` — no web counterpart: `beep` (web pages do not beep at users — no-op), `setDynamicLayout`, `addAWTEventListener`/`removeAWTEventListener` (empty getters), `mapInputMethodHighlight` → null, `createCustomCursor` → default cursor, `createDragGestureRecognizer` → null (DnD is the [D_drag_and_drop](#D_drag_and_drop) `TransferHandler` path), `getPrintJob` → null (printing deferred), `createImage(ImageProducer)` → null (producer pipeline is paint-scope). Image loaders (`getImage`/`createImage` from `byte[]`/`URL`/`String`) are **implemented via `ImageIO`** (headless-capable), returning null on failure (debug-logged); `prepareImage` → true / `checkImage` → `ALLBITS` (ImageIO images are fully realised); `sync` → silent no-op.

The clipboard accessor keeps D_clipboard's throw contracts (no-UI / off-VT / secure-context — D_clipboard_vt_park/D_clipboard_throw_warn_split/D_clipboard_helper_js). Decision-3 (rewrite ported param types so app code compiles) falls out for free: `getPrintJob(Frame,…)` / `createDragGestureRecognizer(…,Component,…)` reference `vaadinx.awt.Frame`/`vaadinx.awt.Component`.

<a id="D_toolkit_surface_and_bodies"></a>**D_toolkit_surface_and_bodies — full surface AND browser bodies both land now.** The proposed entry deferred the browser round-trip bodies per R_infra_not_surface ("surface now, bodies on demand"). Reversed during implementation: with the project now committed to building a full Swing emulator layer, there is no speculation to avoid — the screen accessors are implemented browser-backed in this slice, not stubbed-until-demanded.

<a id="D_toolkit_from_client_details"></a>**D_toolkit_from_client_details — `BrowserToolkitInfo` sources from Vaadin's `ExtendedClientDetails`, NOT a bespoke `executeJs`, NOT fetch-at-init+cache.** Two reversals from the proposed entry:
- *Not fetch-at-init.* The proposed entry leaned on the [SD_browser_timezone](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_browser_timezone) `BrowserTimeZone.fetch()`-at-init pattern; reversed because that risks caching Vaadin's `screenWidth == -1` placeholder if the init listener runs before the browser responds — the app then reads garbage forever.
- *Not a custom `executeJs`.* The first implementation used a bespoke `executeJs` returning `{screenW, screenH, dpr, platform}`; reversed because Vaadin's `ExtendedClientDetails` already carries `getScreenWidth/Height`, `getDevicePixelRatio`, and `getNavigatorPlatform()` (read for iOS/iPadOS the way Vaadin's `isIOS()`, deprecated in 25.3, did) — the same channel `BrowserTimeZone` uses. Duplicating it was needless.

So `vaadinx.awt.BrowserToolkitInfo.get()` reads `Page.getExtendedClientDetails()`: when it is **already populated** (which it is in any app that wired `BrowserTimeZone.fetch()` at init — the guide requires it for dates), it derives the snapshot **synchronously on any thread**, so the screen accessors work even at frame-construction time on the request thread (an advantage the custom-`executeJs` version lacked — `executeJs` always needs a VT carrier). When not yet populated, it parks the calling VT on `ExtendedClientDetails.refresh(callback)` via a plain `CompletableFuture` (the [D_clipboard_future_bridge](#D_clipboard) bridge that dodges Vaadin's `DeadlockDetectingCompletableFuture` under the runner's `VirtualThreadAwareLock`). **Cache only real values:** a populated/fetched (or `setTestInfo`-injected) snapshot is cached per-UI via `ComponentUtil.setData`; the fallback is never cached, so a later call upgrades. **Quiet fallback:** when details are neither populated nor fetchable (no UI, or off a VT carrier with the browser not yet reported), `get()` returns `DEFAULT` (1920×1080, DPR 1.0, non-Mac → `CTRL`) and logs at **debug** — deliberately *not* `EHelper.onUnimplemented`, because screen metrics *are* implemented (graceful not-yet-known degrade, R_best_effort_behaviour/R_layouts_close_enough), and a WARN on a construction-time `getScreenSize()` / menu-accelerator path would trip the zero-stub-WARN exit gates. **macOS detection is iOS/iPadOS-only:** `ExtendedClientDetails` has no desktop-macOS flag, so desktop Mac falls to `CTRL` for the menu modifier — accepted (R_best_effort_behaviour/R_layouts_close_enough; the modifier is cosmetic, a bespoke `navigator.platform` probe isn't worth it). `setTestInfo` is the unit-test seam (the live `refresh` round-trip needs a browser — deferred e2e, as with WebClipboard). **No new migration-guide init step** — reads on demand.

<a id="D_toolkit_screen_size"></a>**D_toolkit_screen_size — `getScreenSize()` reports the browser *viewport* (`window.innerWidth/Height`), with live resize tracking.** Landed after the JWindow slice (SD_sjwindow) surfaced the placement gap: our windows position in viewport coordinates (`Window.setLocation/setBounds` → the SWindow Dialog overlay's top/left), while D_toolkit_full_surface's original `getScreenSize()` returned `ExtendedClientDetails.getScreenWidth/Height` — the physical monitor. Migrated edge-anchoring math (`screen.width - w - 20`, the classic toast/centering idiom) then computed positions far outside the visible page whenever the browser window was smaller than the monitor. In a browser, the "screen" a window lives on IS the viewport — the physical monitor size has no placement use — so `BrowserToolkitInfo`'s record now carries `viewportWidth/viewportHeight` sourced from `ExtendedClientDetails.getWindowInnerWidth()/getWindowInnerHeight()` (same D_toolkit_from_client_details channel; `screen.*` fallback only if the payload carried no inner size), and every migrated screen-math idiom (centering, edge anchoring, size-to-fraction-of-screen) lands on the page. Because the viewport — unlike the monitor — changes when the user resizes the browser window, the first per-UI cache also registers a `Page.addBrowserWindowResizeListener` (idempotent via a per-UI marker; the registration dies with the UI): each resize event replaces the cached snapshot's viewport, carrying dpr/mac over, through the package-private `onBrowserResize(UI, w, h)` seam — which is also the Karibu test hook, since MockVaadin has no browser to fire real resize events. `setTestInfo` injections deliberately do NOT install the listener (deterministic tests). **Bounded staleness, accepted:** resizes between page load and the first `get()` aren't tracked (no listener yet; Vaadin doesn't auto-refresh `ExtendedClientDetails`), so the first read reports load-time values and self-heals from then on — the alternative (an init-time registration) would reintroduce the init step D_toolkit_from_client_details deliberately avoided. **Non-goals:** re-anchoring already-shown windows on resize (Swing doesn't re-anchor on desktop-resolution changes either), firing any Swing-side event from browser resizes, and `java.awt.GraphicsEnvironment` / `getMaximumWindowBounds()` emulation (separate un-ported class; lands when a migration target needs it, R_infra_not_surface).

**Rationale.**
- **Emulators must compile; that's the whole drop-in proposition.** The import-swap value prop ([D_import_swap_target](#D_import_swap_target)) is "rewrite imports, recompile, run." A missing method breaks recompile. Once `Toolkit` is in scope, withholding part of its surface isn't minimalism — it's a hole in the drop-in.
- **The runtime trap is worse than any cost of the surface.** Today's gap fails *loud but late and in the wrong place*: `HeadlessException` from the server toolkit at click time, routed to the `ErrorHandler`. A WARN-default stub fails *soft and observable* — the migrator sees the WARN in the log triage pass (Phase 6) and decides. That's the R_match_swing_errors contract working as designed.
- **Delegate by *authority*, not blanket.** The refined rule (D_toolkit_five_tiers): delegate to the headless JDK toolkit only where the value is **client-independent** and the JVM computes it correctly (font metrics, font list, color model facts) — there the server is authoritative. Browser-back the **client-specific** values (screen size, menu-shortcut modifier) — there delegating returns the *servlet machine's* answer, the server-vs-browser divergence `BrowserTimeZone`/`WebClipboard` exist to avoid. The empirical headless probe is what draws the line: methods that throw `HeadlessException` are almost exactly the client-specific ones, so "delegate where it works headless" and "delegate where the server is authoritative" largely coincide.
- **One migration rule.** "`Toolkit` → `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit`, always" replaces "stays JDK except clipboard, and the clipboard call changes shape" — strictly simpler for the guide and the migrator, and the simplification is the user-facing point.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Keep the clipboard-only minimal `Toolkit`; document the call-shape change in the guide.** Rejected. Leaves every non-clipboard `Toolkit` method as a runtime `HeadlessException` and breaks the import-swap-compiles promise; the guide would have to enumerate which `Toolkit` methods are safe, which is exactly the per-method carve-out this entry removes.
- **Delegate unported methods to `java.awt.Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit()` (the headless JDK toolkit).** Rejected. Most throw `HeadlessException` anyway; the ones that don't return the server's answer, not the browser's (server-vs-browser trap). Browser-backed-or-WARN is the only faithful shape.
- **Make unported methods a compile error as a "loud, early signal."** Rejected — that's the surrogate stance ([R_vaadin_first](../surrogates/decisions.md)), which is correct for `:surrogates` (fail on what the peer can't represent) but wrong for an emulator import-swap target. (`Toolkit` has no surrogate — no Vaadin `Component` to extend, per D_clipboard — so the surrogate compile-fail tool isn't even available here.)
- **Extend `java.awt.Toolkit` so `Component.getToolkit()` could return our instance directly.** Rejected. Extending the abstract JDK class forces the `@Override` signatures to match JDK exactly (`getPrintJob(java.awt.Frame,…)`), which collides with decision-3's param-type rewrite to `vaadinx.awt.Frame`, and forces implementing the abstract `protected getSystemEventQueueImpl()` and friends. Standalone + changing `Component.getToolkit()`'s *return type* to `vaadinx.awt.Toolkit` (D_gettoolkit_returns_emulator) achieves the same `component.getToolkit().getScreenSize()` reachability without either cost.
- **Keep the D_clipboard `static getSystemClipboard()` as a deprecated convenience.** Rejected — impossible: Java forbids a same-named static and instance method, and the JDK-faithful form is the instance method. Internal call sites moved to `getDefaultToolkit().getSystemClipboard()` instead (D_toolkit_singleton).
- **`BrowserToolkitInfo` fetch-at-init + cache (the proposed D_toolkit_from_client_details).** Rejected during implementation — caches Vaadin's `screenWidth == -1` placeholder if the init listener beats the browser response. On-demand VT-park (D_toolkit_from_client_details) reads live and caches only real values.
- **Fetch-fallback via `EHelper.onUnimplemented` WARN (the proposed "WARN + default").** Rejected — a WARN on a construction-time `getScreenSize()` / menu-accelerator path trips the zero-stub-WARN exit gates, and screen metrics aren't a stub (they're implemented, browser-backed). The not-yet-fetched fallback logs at debug instead.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Screen metrics are best-effort (R_layouts_close_enough).** Sourced from `ExtendedClientDetails`; `getScreenSize` deliberately reports the browser *viewport*, not the monitor (D_toolkit_screen_size) — code that wanted the physical display size gets the viewport instead, the right answer for placement and the honest one for "how much room do I have." CSS pixels modulated by `devicePixelRatio` mean a faithful physical-pixel / DPI answer isn't always recoverable anyway. When details aren't yet populated and the caller is off a VT carrier, the accessors return `DEFAULT` (debug-logged, not WARN); pre-first-read browser resizes aren't tracked (D_toolkit_screen_size bounded staleness).
- **Menu-shortcut modifier is `META` for iOS/iPadOS only.** `ExtendedClientDetails` has no desktop-macOS flag, so desktop Mac clients get `CTRL`. Cosmetic (R_best_effort_behaviour/R_layouts_close_enough); revisit if a target needs Cmd accelerators on desktop Mac.
- **`getSystemSelection` → null; `getMaximumCursorColors`/`getBestCursorSize` → 0/(0,0)** — faithful "unsupported", no WARN.
- **AWT event queue listeners, `mapInputMethodHighlight`, `createCustomCursor`, `createDragGestureRecognizer`, `getPrintJob`, `createImage(ImageProducer)`, `beep`, `setDynamicLayout`** — WARN + ignore (no web counterpart; `beep` is a no-op because web pages do not beep at users).
- **`getPrintJob` defers to the printing slice** — WARN-drop (null) until printing lands.
- **`getLockingKeyState`/`setLockingKeyState` throw `UnsupportedOperationException`** — faithful to the JDK's unsupported-host contract; a real divergence from a desktop that supports locking keys, bounded (rarely called).
- **Clipboard contracts unchanged** — D_clipboard's no-UI / off-VT / secure-context throws (D_clipboard_vt_park / D_clipboard_throw_warn_split / D_clipboard_helper_js) still apply to the clipboard accessor.

**Validation.** `:emulators` — `ToolkitTest` (23): `getDefaultToolkit()` is a global singleton across calls and across a UI teardown/re-setup; `getSystemClipboard()` instance reaches the per-UI `WebClipboard` (and throws with no UI); `Component.getToolkit()` returns the singleton; `getFontMetrics` real metrics (no WARN); tier-1 delegated + tier-4 fabricated faithful constants (no WARN); tier-3 `getLockingKeyState`/`setLockingKeyState` throw; browser-backed `getScreenSize`/`getScreenResolution`/`getMenuShortcutKeyMaskEx` via `BrowserToolkitInfo.setTestInfo` (Mac → `META`, Win → `CTRL`) + uncached-off-VT `DEFAULT` with no WARN; `ImageIO` image decode (real PNG + garbage→null), `prepareImage`/`checkImage`; tier-5 WARN paths (`beep`/`getPrintJob`/`createCustomCursor`/`mapInputMethodHighlight`/`createImage(ImageProducer)`/`addAWTEventListener`) each emit a WARN, `sync` does not. `WebClipboardTest`, `ComponentGraphicsTest` (getToolkit now asserts the vaadinx singleton), `WindowTest` updated. `:sampler` — `ClipboardPanel` + `ClipboardWarnInventoryTest` moved to `getDefaultToolkit().getSystemClipboard()`; zero-stub-WARN gate stays green. Full `:emulators` and `:sampler` suites pass.

---

<a id="D_jcolorchooser"></a>
## D_jcolorchooser. JColorChooser — R_leaf_peer_lockdown-locked, owns its state over SJColorChooser; emulator-only `showDialog`/`createDialog` park via the JDialog modal machinery

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.JColorChooser extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent`, rendered by the [SD_sjcolorchooser](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjcolorchooser) `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJColorChooser` peer, owns its state as the JDK's does: `selectionModel`, `chooserPanels`, `previewPanel` and `dragEnabled` are its fields under the JDK's names, every accessor is the JDK's body over them, and no getter reads the peer ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). **The model is not shared with the surrogate**, which keeps a private one only this class writes — the JTabbedPane shape ([D_jtabbedpane](#D_jtabbedpane)), because the surrogate writes its model on a browser pick through its inline `SHelper.callSwing`, outside any UI fiber. Swing → peer is a flush: a listener on the chooser's model (the JDK L&F's `previewListener`, moved by `setSelectionModel` before the event fires, as that L&F's first-registered property listener does) pushes the current color. Browser → Swing is the model write a desktop chooser panel makes — `getSelectionModel().setSelectedColor(c)`, from the peer's value-change inside `EHelper.callSwing` — so a listener on the model runs in a UI fiber and may open a modal dialog. **There is no `ChangeListener` on the chooser itself**: the JDK has none (listeners go on `getSelectionModel()`), and the emulator's `addChangeListener` / `removeChangeListener` / `getChangeListeners` / `fireStateChanged` were invented surface, removed. Measured on JDK 25 and replayed by `JColorChooserTest.stateMatchesTheJdk`, the bodies reproduce what delegation had lost: `new JColorChooser((Color) null)` holds a null color (not white); a null model — at construction or in `setSelectionModel` — throws the L&F's NPE, the latter after storing it and before the event; the chooser starts with the five default panels (Swatches, HSV, HSL, RGB, CMYK, `ColorChooserComponentFactory.getDefaultChooserPanels()`, as `BasicColorChooserUI.installUI` installs them), so `removeChooserPanel(getChooserPanels()[0])` works where it threw `ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException`; `removeChooserPanel` of an absent or null panel throws `IllegalArgumentException("chooser panel not in this chooser")`; `setChooserPanels` copies its argument and throws on a null array or element; `setPreviewPanel` of the current panel does nothing; `setColor(int)` drops alpha; and `paramString` is the JDK's. Sub-decisions:

- <a id="D_jcolorchooser_lockdown"></a>**D_jcolorchooser_lockdown — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `javax.swing.JColorChooser` is a leaf in the public `javax.swing.*` hierarchy (nothing public extends it; `javax.swing.plaf.*` dropped per [R_match_swing_errors](../CLAUDE.md) sub-bucket (b)). Peer hard-coded to `SJColorChooser`; the `(SJColorChooser peer)` ctor is private + typed-narrow, no protected `(Component peer)` seam. Same shape JProgressBar / JSlider / JComboBox take.
- <a id="D_colorchooser_model_reused"></a>**D_colorchooser_model_reused — model reused from the JDK.** `javax.swing.colorchooser.ColorSelectionModel` + `DefaultColorSelectionModel` reference only `java.awt.Color` / `ChangeEvent` / `ChangeListener` / `EventListenerList` — no `java.awt.Component` — so they're reused unchanged per [D_whitelist_porting](#D_whitelist_porting)/[D_event_port_policy](#D_event_port_policy), exactly like `BoundedRangeModel` for JSlider. No port.
- <a id="D_colorchooser_blocking_statics"></a>**D_colorchooser_blocking_statics — emulator-only blocking statics.** `showDialog(parent,title,initial)` (+ the 4-arg `colorTransparencySelectionEnabled` form) and `createDialog(...)` live on the emulator only — the surrogate never parks ([SD_sframe](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sframe)). They build an internal modal `JDialog` (owner-walk helper copied from [D_file_dialogs](#D_file_dialogs)'s `JFileChooser.createJDialog`), embed a fresh `JColorChooser`'s peer, add OK/Cancel/Reset Vaadin Buttons whose click handlers funnel through `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope), and `dialog.setVisible(true)` parks the calling VT. `showDialog` returns `pane.getColor()` on OK, `null` on Cancel/X/ESC (JDK contract); Reset restores the initial color without disposing. `createDialog` returns a non-blocking JDialog wired to the caller's OK/Cancel `ActionListener`s.
- <a id="D_colorchooser_parent_narrowed"></a>**D_colorchooser_parent_narrowed — `parent` narrowed to `vaadinx.awt.Component`.** The JDK statics take `java.awt.Component parent`; we narrow to `vaadinx.awt.Component` per the JFileChooser convention (`java.awt.Component` isn't ported as a supertype).
- <a id="D_colorchooser_panels_dropped"></a>**D_colorchooser_panels_dropped — preview panel + chooser panels keep their state and events; rendering is declined.** The `AbstractColorChooserPanel` tabs and the preview panel are pure custom paint (sub-bucket (b)) — the native `<input type="color">` *is* the chooser UI. Per R_decline_effect_only the fields, the copies, the exceptions and the `chooserPanels` / `previewPanel` events are the JDK's, and `setChooserPanels` (which `addChooserPanel` / `removeChooserPanel` route through, as in the JDK) and `setPreviewPanel` WARN for the rendering. A panel's `installChooserPanel` hook is not called: it takes a `javax.swing.JColorChooser`. `dragEnabled` is a silent field; the JDK's headless `HeadlessException` is not thrown, since a browser is not headless. L&F (`getUI`/`setUI`/`updateUI`/`getUIClassID`="ColorChooserUI") stubs.

**Rationale.** Same drop-in shape as every other leaf component — the value is `javax.swing.JColorChooser` → `vaadinx.swing.JColorChooser` recompiles and runs. The blocking `showDialog` is the dominant real-world usage; reusing the JDialog modal-park machinery (already proven for JOptionPane / JFileChooser / modal JDialog) means zero new blocking infrastructure. The chooser-panel API is the part with no web counterpart, and the browser color input replaces it entirely; what a migrator can observe of it — the panel list, its exceptions, its events — is kept.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Port the `AbstractColorChooserPanel` tabs (swatches/HSV/RGB).** Rejected — pure custom paint, out of scope per R_match_swing_errors (b); the native input is a complete substitute.
- **Static `showDialog` on the surrogate.** Impossible — the surrogate's `SHelper.callSwing` never parks (SD_sframe). Blocking lives at the emulator layer by design.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Alpha dropped** — the peer is opaque `#rrggbb` (see SD_sjcolorchooser); a model color with `alpha<255` round-trips to opaque RGB on a browser edit. The model retains the last programmatically-set alpha until a browser edit overwrites it.
- **`showDialog` from a non-VT context throws `IllegalStateException`** — the modal park requires the `EHelper.callSwing` VT envelope (R_callswing_envelope), same as JOptionPane / JFileChooser.
- **`getPreviewPanel()` is `null` until one is set** — the JDK's L&F installs a `DefaultPreviewPanel`, a `javax.swing` component the `vaadinx.swing.JComponent`-typed getter cannot hold.

**Validation.** `:emulators` — `JColorChooserTest` (16): R_leaf_peer_lockdown no-protected-ctor + peer-is-SJColorChooser, ctor colors, `setColor` reaching the rendered input over an unshared model, the replayed JDK script, a browser pick writing the model inside a UI fiber, reaching a migrator-installed model and parking a model listener on a modal dialog, PCE on model swap, `showDialog` OK-returns-chosen / reflects-browser-pick / Cancel-returns-null / non-VT-throws (VT-park harness), `createDialog` invokes the OK listener, `getUIClassID`. `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest.jColorChooser` reads the getters on a bare thread without reaching the peer. `:surrogates` — `SJColorChooserTest` (19). `:sampler` — `ColorChoosersPanel` + `ColorChoosersWarnInventoryTest` (2: embedded-pick + showDialog user path, API-surface micro-driver) at zero stub WARN.

<a id="D_preferences"></a>
## D_preferences. `java.util.prefs.Preferences` — localStorage-backed, plugged in under the JDK `PreferencesFactory` SPI (no import swap), warm-once/read-synchronously per-UI cache with a VT-park first read

**Decision.** Preferences support is delivered under the JDK's own extension point, not as a `vaadinx.*` import-swap class. `vaadinx.util.prefs.VaadinPreferences extends java.util.prefs.AbstractPreferences` is the node type; `vaadinx.util.prefs.VaadinPreferencesFactory implements java.util.prefs.PreferencesFactory` is selected JVM-wide via `META-INF/services/java.util.prefs.PreferencesFactory`. Migrated code keeps calling `Preferences.userNodeForPackage(...)` / `userRoot()` **byte-for-byte unchanged** — `java.util.prefs` is not `javax.swing`, so there is no import to rewrite and nothing for the user to touch. The user tree is backed by the browser's `localStorage`; a per-UI `PrefsCache` (held via `ComponentUtil.setData`, the same per-UI storage Clipboard/DnD use) warms the whole tree once and then serves the synchronous `Preferences` API from memory. Emulator-only, **no surrogate** (fourth "no surrogate by design" after JOptionPane/SD_no_sjoptionpane, Clipboard/D_clipboard, DnD/D_drag_and_drop — there is no Vaadin component to extend). Sub-decisions:

- <a id="D_prefs_spi"></a>**D_prefs_spi — transparent SPI, `-D`-overridable.** The `META-INF/services` entry makes the JDK pick `VaadinPreferencesFactory` with zero host config (true drop-in). The JDK consults the `-Djava.util.prefs.PreferencesFactory` system property *before* the ServiceLoader, so a deployment that shares its JVM with non-UI code using `Preferences` for real persistence can override us for free. The SPI selects our factory JVM-wide, so background/non-UI `Preferences` users get routed here too — **classified and handled per D_prefs_scope_split** (the license checker that RTE brought into the tree is exactly such a user), not a `-D`-only caveat.
- <a id="D_prefs_localstorage"></a>**D_prefs_localstorage — `localStorage`, hard-coded.** The faithful web analog of Swing's machine-local store (Windows registry / `~/.java/.userPrefs/` / macOS plist) is the browser. No pluggable backend, no roaming, no auth-principal keying: an emulator reproduces Swing, it does not grow Swing a feature nobody expects. If a Swing app with login already has per-user settings, it uses its own mechanism — making prefs roam would be *enriching* Swing, out of charter. The per-UI cache is a legitimate sync-mirror of the browser store (Vaadin has no synchronous localStorage accessor), not a `Store`-style shadow the R_vaadin_first anti-pattern warns against — it exists to bridge sync-over-async, and every value in it round-trips to `localStorage`.
- <a id="D_prefs_warm_once"></a>**D_prefs_warm_once — sync API over async store, via warm-once/read-synchronously.** `Preferences.getInt(...)` is synchronous; reading `localStorage` from the server is an async `executeJs` round-trip. Resolution: on first access `PrefsCache.ensureLoaded()` pulls the *entire* `emul.prefs:*` tree in one `executeJs("return window.emulPrefs.readAll()")`, parking the calling virtual thread on a plain `CompletableFuture` — the exact `WebClipboard.awaitJs` bridge (sidesteps Vaadin's `DeadlockDetectingCompletableFuture` `hasLock()` refusal on VT carriers; see D_callswing_loom). After that every read is synchronous off the cache; writes update the cache and fire a fire-and-forget `writeNode`/`removeNode`. `flushSpi`/`syncSpi` are no-ops (writes are eager). Storage layout: one `localStorage` entry per node keyed `emul.prefs:<absolutePath>`, value a JSON `{key:value}` blob — one-blob-per-node sidesteps separator ambiguity (Swing keys may contain `/`; node paths never do). Helper JS ships as a servlet-served static resource (`META-INF/resources/emul/prefs-helper.js`, `addJavaScript("context://emul/prefs-helper.js")`), same shape as `clipboard-helper.js` (D_clipboard_helper_js).
- <a id="D_prefs_first_read_context"></a>**D_prefs_first_read_context — first-read EDT-context contract; twin of [SD_browser_timezone](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_browser_timezone).** The warm-up parks, so it must run on a virtual thread with a live UI — i.e. inside `SwingUtilities.invokeLater` (the load-bearing wrapper the migrated `mainUI()` already uses, [D_jframe_as_route](#D_jframe_as_route)) or any peer event listener under `EHelper.callSwing`. **Scoped to app-scoped access (D_prefs_scope_split):** the loud `IllegalStateException` fires when an `EmulatorContext` *is* active (so we know it's app code that wants localStorage) but no live UI is reachable — a pref read from a `static{}` block, `main()` before `VaadinBoot.run()`, or a `SwingWorker` body that reads prefs off the UI thread. The message points at the fix — the **exact same cases** the migration guide lists for `BrowserTimeZone.get()`, so this adds **no new migration rule**. (A caller with *no* `EmulatorContext` at all isn't app code and never reaches this throw — it falls through to the JVM-local store per D_prefs_scope_split.) Why this works without a new boot paradigm: SB-Emulators already boots deferred — window construction runs on a loom VT that can park exactly as a modal `JOptionPane` does. One honest asymmetry with SD_browser_timezone: `ExtendedClientDetails` is smuggled into Vaadin's handshake so timezone's first read is synchronous, whereas `localStorage` has no handshake channel, so the *first* pref read pays a one-time round-trip park. An optional non-blocking prefetch from a `UIInitListener` (kick off `readAll()` without awaiting) could warm the cache ahead of the first read; **not wired** — negligible payoff on real usage and it would add a prefs-access side effect to every UI init, so the lazy park stands as the shipped behaviour.
- <a id="D_prefs_abstract_tree"></a>**D_prefs_abstract_tree — `AbstractPreferences` gives the tree + listeners for free.** Extending it means `keys()`/`childrenNames()`/`node(path)`/`removeNode()` and the `PreferenceChangeListener`/`NodeChangeListener` fan-out are the JDK's; we implement only the nine backing `*Spi` methods against `PrefsCache`. Change listeners fire for local (this-UI) mutations via `AbstractPreferences`' own daemon dispatch thread; a mutation in another tab does not fire here (multi-tab gap, below).
- <a id="D_prefs_systemroot_deferred"></a>**D_prefs_systemroot_deferred — `systemRoot()` deferred (R_match_swing_errors minor gap, sub-bucket (a)/(c)).** `localStorage` is per-browser and structurally cannot represent "shared across all users of the deployment", so `systemRoot()`/`systemNodeForPackage()` return an inert `SystemPreferences` node — writes WARN via `EHelper.onUnimplemented`, reads return empty. `userRoot()`/`userNodeForPackage()` — the case real apps use — is fully backed. A server-side shared store is real scope for a surface almost no app touches; pulled in only if a target needs it. `SystemPreferences` is inert (no round-trip) and so needs no UI — a JVM-global singleton, and it never throws off-UI.
- <a id="D_prefs_scope_split"></a>**D_prefs_scope_split — app-scoped vs. JVM-scoped `userRoot()`, keyed on the session lock.** Because the SPI is JVM-wide (D_prefs_spi), the factory fields `Preferences` calls that aren't migrated-app code at all. The load-bearing case: adding RTE to the tree ([SD_sjeditorpane_rte](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjeditorpane_rte)) pulls in Vaadin's commercial-component **license checker**, whose `com.vaadin.pro.licensechecker.History` reads *and writes* `Preferences.userNodeForPackage(OnlineKeyValidator.class)` when an RTE-backed `JEditorPane` renders in dev mode. Instrumenting `userRoot()` pinned its exact thread state: a **Jetty request-pool thread** with the `VaadinSession` current, **`UI.getCurrent()` null**, and **the session lock not held**. Two first cuts each tripped on that: "no UI → throw" gave a bare `IllegalStateException`; then keying on `EmulatorContext.getOrNull() != null` was worse — `getOrNull()` *itself* reads `BrowserTimeZone` off the session, so merely evaluating the discriminator threw Vaadin's *"Cannot access state in VaadinSession or UI without locking the session"* (the checker swallows the stack trace, so it surfaced as a bare component failure). **The discriminator therefore has to be "can we safely serve localStorage right now" = do we hold the lock** — read via `session.hasLock()`, which needs no lock — and the session-present branch must **not** touch the context or any session/UI state:
    - **current session + lock held** (real UI thread / `EHelper.callSwing` continuation) ⇒ app-scoped ⇒ `localStorage`-backed `PrefsCache`;
    - **current session, lock *not* held** (license checker, other library on a session-associated but unlocked thread) ⇒ JVM-scoped ⇒ in-memory `JvmLocalPreferences`;
    - **no current session but a propagated `EmulatorContext`** (a `SwingWorker.doInBackground`) ⇒ app-scoped ⇒ a `BridgedPreferences` that reaches localStorage through the session's live UI (see D_prefs_swingworker_bridge);
    - **nothing** (JVM init, a library off any Vaadin thread) ⇒ JVM-scoped ⇒ `JvmLocalPreferences`.
  *Why in-memory, not the JDK file store:* the fallback is deliberately ephemeral so a **misclassified** app write — migrated code on a raw `Thread` that never propagated its `EmulatorContext` (the same discipline timezone already requires) — is lost to a process-local heap rather than silently persisted to the **server's** shared `~/.java/.userPrefs` (wrong machine, cross-user on a deployed server). The license checker only *caches* check timestamps there, so ephemeral just means it re-validates per boot in dev — correct, merely unthrottled. `systemRoot()` is unchanged (inert, D_prefs_systemroot_deferred). Accepted residual: the raw-background-thread misclassification is silent (no throw, no WARN — a WARN would fire on every license check); it folds into the existing "propagate `EmulatorContext` to your own threads" migration rule.
- <a id="D_prefs_lock_safe_getters"></a>**D_prefs_lock_safe_getters — `BrowserTimeZone.getOrNull()` / `EmulatorContext.getOrNull()` are lock-safe.** Evaluating the discriminator (and any background zone read) must never throw the "cannot access state without locking" error. `BrowserTimeZone.getOrNull()` reads the `ZoneId` session attribute directly when it holds the lock, else **briefly `lock()`/read/`unlock()`** (reentrant fast-path) — honoring its never-throw contract and returning the real zone instead of a `null` fallback. `EmulatorContext.getOrNull()` snapshots a present session's context via that lock-safe read; with no session it returns any propagated context.
- <a id="D_prefs_swingworker_bridge"></a>**D_prefs_swingworker_bridge — `SwingWorker` reads/writes localStorage prefs through a live-UI bridge.** A worker's `doInBackground` runs on a parkable VT with no current UI/lock but the session held via its propagated `EmulatorContext`. `userRoot()` returns a `vaadinx.util.prefs.BridgedPreferences` whose nine `*Spi` ops each run their `PrefsCache` body inside a new `EHelper.callOnLiveUISync(session, body)` — the synchronous, result-returning sibling of `onSessionLiveUI` (which is fire-and-forget). It queues via `session.access`, resolves `singleLiveUI`, runs the body under `accessSynchronously` + `callSwing` (so the first read parks on the `executeJs` localStorage round-trip via the loom carrier, lock released during the park), and latches the value back to the worker; the access queue drains via `@Push` (the mandatory-Push contract) / `MockVaadin.runUIQueue` in tests — the same drain `SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait` relies on. So a migrator's ordinary synchronous `Preferences.userRoot()…get(...)` in `doInBackground` just works, and warm-once amortizes the round-trip across the worker's reads. **Fails loud (user decision):** no single live UI reachable (tab/session gone), the multi-tab `singleLiveUI` throw, a body failure, or a 30s timeout backstop all surface as a thrown exception → the worker's `ExecutionException`, never a silent stale value or a hang (`callOnLiveUISync` always completes its latch, unlike `onSessionLiveUI` which silently drops).

**Rationale.** This is a *cleaner* drop-in than the component emulators: plugging in under `PreferencesFactory` means user code is genuinely untouched (no import rewrite), because prefs were never a `javax.swing` type. The sync/async gap — the one real obstacle — dissolves against SB-Emulators' already-deferred boot: the entry window's constructor, where "restore window bounds" lives, already runs on a parkable VT, so the WebClipboard VT-park pattern applies verbatim and the prefs contract becomes a mechanical twin of the timezone one migrators already follow.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Cookie-keyed server-side store (or cookies as the store).** Rejected as the backend: 4 KB/cookie vs Preferences' 8 KB/value, plus a bandwidth tax on every request. `localStorage` is the same "this browser = this machine" scope with room to breathe.
- **Cookie as a *sync-delivery transport*** (localStorage stays source-of-truth; a cookie mirror rides the first HTTP request so the server has prefs synchronously at bootstrap, preserving an eager-boot model). Genuinely considered — it would avoid even the first-read park. Rejected as unnecessary: the boot is already deferred (D_prefs_first_read_context), so there is no eager-construction model to preserve, and the cookie mirror re-adds size limits + per-request bandwidth for a one-round-trip saving.
- **Return-the-default until the async load lands.** Rejected — silently serves stale/empty values on first read (window opens at the wrong size, "recent files" empty), the subtle-wrongness SD_browser_timezone rejects; the loud EDT-context throw + VT-park is both faithful and correct.
- **Block first render behind a splash until preloaded.** Rejected — invasive (makes navigation await a browser round-trip) and unnecessary given the parkable-VT boot.
- **Roaming / auth-principal-keyed prefs.** Rejected — enriches Swing beyond what its API promises (machine-local, not roaming). Out of charter.
- **Pluggable storage backend.** Rejected — YAGNI; `localStorage` hard-coded keeps the surface narrow.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **First pref read pays a one-time round-trip park** (asymmetry with SD_browser_timezone, which rides the handshake). Transparent to correctly-placed code; optionally erasable via a prefetch (not wired).
- **Multi-tab:** each UI warms its own cache from the one shared `localStorage` → last-flush-wins; a write in tab A is invisible to tab B's already-warm cache, and cross-tab changes don't fire `PreferenceChangeListener`. Folds into the project's existing "multi-tab unsupported" gap; the fix, if ever tackled, is a `storage`-event bridge — recorded here so it isn't rediscovered.
- **`systemRoot` is inert** (WARN + empty) — see D_prefs_systemroot_deferred.
- **SPI selection is JVM-wide** — see D_prefs_spi; `-D` override is the escape hatch.
- **`localStorage` ~5–10 MB/origin** comfortably exceeds Preferences' 8 KB/value and typical usage — no practical ceiling.

**Validation.** `:emulators` — `VaadinPreferencesTest` (factory selection returns a `VaadinPreferences`; put/get round-trip; default for absent key; typed accessors + malformed-value fallback; `userNodeForPackage`; `keys`; child-node hierarchy + `childrenNames`; `remove`; `removeNode`; `PreferenceChangeListener` fires on put via the daemon dispatch; `systemRoot` WARNs + reads empty) run in `VaadinPreferencesFactory.setTestMode(true)`, the in-memory seam mirroring `WebClipboard.setTestMode` (incl. D_prefs_scope_split the unlocked-session → `JvmLocalPreferences` route) + `VaadinPreferencesOffUiTest` (D_prefs_scope_split: no `EmulatorContext` → `userRoot()` routes to the in-memory `JvmLocalPreferences` and round-trips the license-checker's `userNodeForPackage(...).putLong/getLong` shape without throwing or parking; inert `systemRoot()` stays usable with no UI) + `BrowserTimeZoneTest` / `EmulatorContextTest` (D_prefs_lock_safe_getters: `getOrNull()` never throws on an unlocked session, lock-and-reads the real zone) + `SwingWorkerTest` (D_prefs_swingworker_bridge: `doInBackground` reads+writes localStorage prefs through the `BridgedPreferences`/`callOnLiveUISync` bridge, and a body failure surfaces loud as the worker's `ExecutionException`). `:sampler` — `PreferencesPanel` (display-name + show-tips + persist-across-reload visit counter, Save/Reset) + `PreferencesWarnInventoryTest` (2: user path through panel build/Save/Reset + userRoot API-surface micro-driver) at zero stub WARN. Full build green.
