<a id="D_printing"></a>
## D_printing. Printing — virtual PDF printer in optional `:emulators-printing`; import-swap of exactly one class (`vaadinx.awt.print.PrinterJob`); Graphics2D→PDF via PDFBox; component printing stays out

**Decision.** Printing splits into two cases with opposite verdicts. *Printing components* (painting the widget tree onto the printer — `component.printAll(g)` inside a `Printable`, `JTable.print()`, `JTextComponent.print()`) stays permanently out: emulated components have no paint, unchanged R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b). *Printing hand-crafted graphics* (a `Printable.print(Graphics)` that draws shapes/text/images directly) is **supported** via a **virtual printer**: `vaadinx.awt.print.PrinterJob extends java.awt.print.PrinterJob` renders every page server-side into a PDF (Graphics2D→PDF bridge) and offers the document in a modeless Vaadin download dialog (`BrowserFileTransfer.openDownloadDialog(byte[], name)`); the user prints the PDF with their local viewer, on their own printer. One printer, always present; no OS print subsystem is ever touched — the server's printers are the wrong machine's printers. Emulator-only, **no surrogate** (fifth "no surrogate by design" after JOptionPane/SD_no_sjoptionpane, Clipboard/D_clipboard, DnD/D_drag_and_drop, Preferences/D_preferences — nothing Component-shaped to extend). Sub-decisions:

- <a id="D_printerjob_single_swap"></a>**D_printerjob_single_swap — injection seam is import-swap of exactly one class.** The historical `-Djava.awt.printerjob` SPI is dead upstream: JDK 25's `PrinterJob.getPrinterJob()` hard-wires `sun.print.PSPrinterJob` via `PlatformPrinterJobProxy`, no property lookup survives — so no D_preferences-style zero-swap drop-in exists. The consolation is that `java.awt.print` is tiny and self-contained: `Printable` imports only `java.awt.Graphics`, `PageFormat`/`Paper` only geom, `Book`/`Pageable` nothing relevant — all stay JDK, and only `PrinterJob` swaps. Extending the JDK class keeps `java.awt.print.PrinterJob`-typed variables compiling and inherits the concrete defaults (`printDialog(attributes)` delegates to `printDialog()`, `print(attributes)` to `print()`). Statics are shadowed: `getPrinterJob()` returns the virtual job; `lookupPrintServices()` returns empty (the inherited JDK static would have enumerated the *server's* printers). Wildcard-import code (`import java.awt.print.*;`) needs only an *added* explicit import — explicit beats wildcard per JLS.
- <a id="D_handcrafted_graphics_carveout"></a>**D_handcrafted_graphics_carveout — why hand-crafted graphics escape the paint-out rule-out.** The Graphics2D-port rule-out (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b)) was motivated by *component* painting: per-frame re-render cost, and no way to tell a pure-drawing component from L&F chrome. A `Printable` is neither — it is **static one-shot vector rendering** with an explicit page protocol, the moral equivalent of a Vaadin app hand-crafting a JasperReports template. Neither objection applies, so the narrow carve-out is principled, not a crack in the rule-out: `paintComponent`, custom-painted components, and L&F remain out; a `Printable` that calls `component.printAll(g)` gets a blank region plus the component stub's WARN.
- <a id="D_printing_optional_module"></a>**D_printing_optional_module — separate optional Maven module (`:emulators-printing`).** The PDF engine (~3.9 MB / 5 jars) would have been `:emulators`' first third-party functional dependency, against the D_pure_java_artifact consumer-classpath-minimal stance. The module `api`-depends on `:emulators`; migrators whose app prints add one dependency, everyone else stays PDF-free. Emulator-layer by naming and dependency, but a stage-3 view that keeps its `PrinterJob` code still works (the class touches no components, only needs a UI for the download dialog) — printing doesn't block stage progression.
- <a id="D_pdf_engine"></a>**D_pdf_engine — PDF engine: PDFBox 3 + `de.rototor.pdfbox:graphics2d`, behind a seam.** Apache-2.0 throughout (linkable from a GPLv2+CE work via the Classpath Exception, per D_gplv2_ce_relicense), pure Java, zero native libs; `graphics2d` declares no transitive deps by design, so we pin `pdfbox` explicitly in the version catalog. The library is isolated behind package-private `PdfPrinterGraphicsFactory` with a begin/commit/discard page protocol mirroring the print loop's "ask first, commit after" shape (`NO_SUCH_PAGE` discards an already-drawn page cleanly — the orphaned form object never reaches the saved PDF). Swapping engines later means rewriting one class. Text renders as vector glyph outlines: always looks and prints right, not selectable/searchable; font embedding is a known follow-up, not v1. Unit match makes the geometry trivial: `PageFormat` speaks 1/72" points, PDF's native unit, and `getWidth()/getHeight()` are already orientation-adjusted, so LANDSCAPE just yields a landscape-sized page.
- <a id="D_print_job_ui_capture"></a>**D_print_job_ui_capture — UI captured at job creation; print() may run on any thread.** The classic Swing pattern prints off the EDT to keep the UI live. The ctor captures `UI.getCurrent()`; `print()` falls back to the calling thread's UI; both null → `IllegalStateException` with a pointer at the fix (R_callswing_envelope-spirit programming error — a print with no session to deliver to). Delivery is `ui.access(...)` — inline when the caller already holds the session lock (an `EHelper.callSwing` continuation), queued for `@Push` delivery from a background thread.
- <a id="D_printing_divergences"></a>**D_printing_divergences — faithful divergences.** `printDialog()` returns true with no dialog — a single always-present virtual printer has no options, and the terminal download dialog is itself the cancelable moment (close without downloading). `pageDialog(pf)` echoes its argument; the format to print with goes to `setPrintable(p, pf)`. `defaultPage()` is A4 portrait with 1" margins where the JDK is locale-dependent — the *server's* locale says nothing about the user's paper, and A4-vs-Letter is absorbed by the PDF viewer's fit-to-page. Copies are stored but ignored at render (`EHelper.onUnimplemented` WARN when `> 1`) — a PDF download is inherently one copy. One `Printable.print` call per page — banded repeat-calls not emulated (the contract only promises *at least* one call; exactly one is always legal). Cancel follows `RasterPrinterJob` semantics verbatim: effective only mid-print, checked between pages, `PrinterAbortException`. `NO_SUCH_PAGE` at index 0 spools nothing silently (a zero-page PDF would be broken; Swing also prints nothing). User exceptions wrap in `PrinterException` with `initCause` (the JDK type has no cause ctor); a `PrinterException` thrown by the app propagates as-is.

**The server-print trap (migration-doc material, not code).** Unswapped `java.awt.print` code *compiles cleanly* after the import-swap (the package isn't `javax.swing`) and then either throws `PrinterException` (headless server, no service) or — worse — silently prints to the **server's** print queue. `javax.print.*` has the same shape and stays untouched JDK. This is the project's only known gap that bypasses the `EHelper.onUnimplemented` WARN funnel — there is no `vaadinx` class in the path to WARN from — so detection is a hazard-scan pattern rather than a runtime guard (grep `java.awt.print` / `javax.print` / component-`print()` calls), not a runtime guard.

**Rationale.** Faithful `PrinterJob` emulation is impossible in principle — browsers expose no printer enumeration, no silent print, no print-to-device API; the only primitives are `window.print()` and "serve a file". Within that boundary, the virtual printer preserves the migrated app's *printing feature* wherever the app's own code draws the pages: the render loop is exactly the JDK's contract driven against a PDF-backed `Graphics2D`, and the delivery rides machinery that already existed (`BrowserFileTransfer`'s download dialog from the JFileChooser SAVE flow). The Vaadin-idiomatic endgame — generate a PDF server-side, let the user download/print it — is exactly what the virtual printer does; the app's hand-crafted `Printable` *is* the report template.

**Alternatives considered.**
- **Browser `window.print()` of the current DOM.** Rejected: it prints the app's UI, not the document — a `Printable` has no DOM to print, and the use cases (reports, invoices) are precisely not screenshots of the app.
- **General `Graphics2D`-to-SVG port** (a third candidate). Rejected for printing: even a perfect SVG of each page ends at `window.print()` fidelity, below the PDF route, for far more work; and it would re-open the component-paint scope D_handcrafted_graphics_carveout keeps closed.
- **WARN-and-noop the whole surface.** Structurally impossible — `PrinterJob`/`javax.print` are the JDK's classes; there is no `vaadinx` code in the path to WARN from. Only the component-owned conveniences (`JTable.print()`, …) can WARN, and they already do.
- **`-Djava.awt.printerjob` SPI registration** (the D_preferences-shaped zero-swap dream). Dead upstream — see D_printerjob_single_swap.
- **Ship inside `:emulators`.** Rejected per D_pure_java_artifact — see D_printing_optional_module.
- **OpenPDF as the engine.** Rejected: requires `brotli4j` (JNI native lib — alpine/musl/GraalVM operational risk in a server library) and carries the noisier LGPL-2.1/MPL-2.0 dual license; PDFBox+graphics2d is pure-Java Apache-2.0.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Component printing renders blank + WARN** (D_handcrafted_graphics_carveout) — the rewrite verdict for `JTable.print()` / `JTextComponent.print()` / `printAll`-based Printables stands (server-side PDF report).
- **PDF text is vector outlines** — not selectable/searchable; font embedding is a possible follow-up on real demand.
- **Print attributes, page ranges, collation, copies** — ignored; the browser PDF viewer's own print dialog provides them at physical-print time.
- **`java.awt.print.PrinterGraphics` not implemented** on the bridge `Graphics2D` — apps sniffing `g instanceof PrinterGraphics` to branch print-vs-screen see false; add-on-demand.
- **`print()` runs synchronously on the calling thread** — same as the JDK; long documents belong on a SwingWorker, as on the desktop.

**Validation.** `:emulators-printing` — `PrinterJobTest` (22 tests): end-to-end under Karibu — `print()` → download dialog → `_download()` the Anchor → parse the bytes back with PDFBox asserting page count and per-page sizes; landscape `PageFormat`; `Book` mixed formats through the Pageable path; `UNKNOWN_NUMBER_OF_PAGES`; background-thread `print()` delivering via the captured UI; cancel mid-print aborts with `PrinterAbortException` and no dialog; cancel outside print is a no-op; `RuntimeException` wraps with cause, `PrinterException` propagates as-is; no-Printable and no-UI programming errors; `NO_SUCH_PAGE`-at-0 silence; jobName→filename; zero-stub-WARN happy path; `copies > 1` WARNs once; the trivial surface (defaultPage A4 geometry, validatePage clone, pageDialog echo, lookupPrintServices empty, getUserName). `:sampler` — `PrintingPanel` (hand-drawn two-page document through the canonical getPrinterJob → setPrintable → printDialog → print flow) + `PrintingWarnInventoryTest` (user path to the download dialog + PrinterJob API-surface micro-driver, zero WARN) + `NavigationSmokeTest` entry. `:emulators` — `BrowserFileTransfer.openDownloadDialog(byte[], String)` overload reusing the dialog/Anchor/safeName shell. Full build green.

<a id="D_jwindow"></a>
## D_jwindow. JWindow — R_leaf_peer_lockdown-locked thin shell over SJWindow; Window geometry retires the WARN stubs; setUndecorated becomes real on Frame / Dialog

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.JWindow extends vaadinx.awt.Window implements Accessible` mirrors JDialog's emulator shape *minus* the sections JDK JWindow doesn't have: no title, no `defaultCloseOperation` (JWindow doesn't implement `WindowConstants` — no chrome, no user close), no menubar slot. What remains is the RootPaneContainer subset — `windowInit()`, own contentPane + lazy `JRootPane` holder (shared with the peer's `SJRootPane` per the JFrame/JDialog idiom), `rootPaneCheckingEnabled` redirect for add/remove/setLayout — plus `setTransferHandler` drop-and-WARN per D_drag_and_drop scope. Surrogate side in [SD_sjwindow](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjwindow). Sub-decisions:

- <a id="D_jwindow_lockdown"></a>**D_jwindow_lockdown — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down + owner-aware Window seam.** `javax.swing.JWindow` is a public-hierarchy leaf; all five JDK ctors (no-arg / `GraphicsConfiguration` / `Frame` owner / `Window` owner / `Window`+gc) hardcode `new SJWindow(...)` as the peer, no protected `(Component peer)` ctor. `vaadinx.awt.Window` gains a protected `Window(Component peer, Window owner)` ctor mirroring `Dialog(peer, owner)` — the peer-injection seam that also registers the owner link, since the public owner-taking Window ctors hardcode `SWindow` as the peer.
- <a id="D_no_shared_owner_frame"></a>**D_no_shared_owner_frame — no shared-owner-frame substitution.** JDK's no-arg JWindow parents to `SwingUtilities.getSharedOwnerFrame()` and calls `setFocusableWindowState(false)`. We keep `owner = null` and skip the focus call: the shared frame exists to satisfy the native windowing system's parenting requirement (a browser has none), nothing observable depends on it without focus modeling (R_infra_not_surface), and replicating the focus call would WARN on every construction. Documented divergence in the ctor comment.
- <a id="D_window_geometry"></a>**D_window_geometry — Window-level geometry, R_swing_is_truth shape.** `setLocation` / `setSize` / `setBounds` / `reshape` (1.0 alias) retire their WARN stubs on `vaadinx.awt.Window`: store R_swing_is_truth shadows (`Point location` / `Dimension size`, null until user code writes), push to the `SWindow` peer's geometry channel (SD_swindow_geometry), fire `COMPONENT_MOVED` / `COMPONENT_RESIZED` on actual change. Getters (`getLocation` / `getSize` / `getBounds` / `getX`…`getHeight`, with the fill-or-allocate `(rv)` contracts) serve the shadows once set and fall back to Component's WARN stubs while unset — a read never preceded by a write keeps surfacing "we don't know browser geometry" instead of silently answering (0, 0). `setLocationRelativeTo(anything)` → peer `centerOnScreen()`, clears the location shadow, fires MOVED only if an explicit placement was in effect. Non-SWindow peers (JFrame InlineStrategy / SJPanel) skip the peer write — inline main windows keep the D_inline_route_sizing viewport-fill stance — while the field shadow + event still happen. *Window-level only*: general component bounds stay R_layouts_close_enough-out-of-scope; a top-level Window maps 1:1 onto the Dialog overlay's top/left/width/height with no layout manager involved.
- <a id="D_setundecorated_real"></a>**D_setundecorated_real — `Frame.setUndecorated` / `Dialog.setUndecorated` become real.** Both retire their WARN stubs: R_swing_is_truth field shadow + push `SWindow.setUndecoratedChrome` (the SD_undecorated_chrome `emul-undecorated` class), with JDK's displayable-time `IllegalComponentStateException` throw per R_match_swing_errors (messages verbatim: "The frame is displayable." / "The dialog is displayable."). JFrame/JDialog inherit. The typical migrated sequence — construct, `setUndecorated(true)`, `setVisible(true)` — works unchanged; toggling while shown throws exactly as on desktop Swing.
- <a id="D_window_scaffold_mirrored"></a>**D_window_scaffold_mirrored — emulator-side scaffolding stays mirror-copied.** JFrame / JDialog / JWindow each carry their own contentPane/rootPane redirect, matching the JDK, which also duplicates this per RootPaneContainer implementor (`java.awt.Window` has no root pane to hoist to). The dedup happened on the surrogate side instead, where JDK shape isn't the API surface — SD_rootpane_scaffold's `RootPaneScaffold`.

**Rationale.** The SWindow flip left the emulator `vaadinx.awt.Window` already peering over a fully functional `SWindow`; JWindow's genuine delta is the RootPaneContainer subset plus the two capability gaps undecorated windows expose (placement, chrome). Landing the geometry at Window level and the chrome at Frame/Dialog level means the slice pays for JWindow but JFrame / JDialog collect too (`dialog.setBounds(…)` is routine in migrated code).

**Accepted limitations.** Translucent / shaped splash windows stay sub-bucket (b) (`setOpacity` / `setShape` remain Window-level WARN stubs — pure paint). `getGraphics`-drawn splash art doesn't render (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b), user-authored paint). Geometry getters WARN-and-dummy until the first explicit setter call — AWT would report live window-manager geometry; we have no synchronous browser read.

**Validation.** `JWindowTest` (19) — R_leaf_peer_lockdown peer lock, peer-default wiring (undecorated / modeless / gestures), windowInit + content-pane redirect family, ctor owner links ×2, no-shared-owner divergence, geometry (store + peer push + event fire + no-change no-refire + round-trips), splash lifecycle smoke. Sampler `WindowsPanel` (splash + toast demos) + `WindowsWarnInventoryTest` (2) — user path end-to-end (Timer-stepped splash auto-dispose, toast at explicit bounds) and the API-surface micro-driver, both zero-WARN. `SFrameTest` / full `:surrogates` + `:emulators` + `:sampler` suites green.

<a id="D_glasspane_structural"></a>
## D_glasspane_structural. Glass pane goes structural (busy-curtain), layered pane stays a holder — supersedes D_rootpane_holder's glass/layered accepted-limitations

**Decision.** Split the two panes D_rootpane_holder kept as pure server-side holders and treat them differently:

- **Glass pane → structural.** `vaadinx.swing.JRootPane` keeps its AWT-typed `glassPane` holder (emulator users still read/write `vaadinx.awt.Component`), but `getGlassPane()` / `setGlassPane(...)` now push the pane's *peer* down to the `SJRootPane` surrogate, which (via [SD_glasspane_structural](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_glasspane_structural)) attaches it as a Dialog-direct child sibling of the content pane, tagged with the `emul-glasspane` overlay class. A *visible* glass pane fills the window body and — being the topmost element with `pointer-events: auto` — swallows all mouse input to the content beneath. `getGlassPane().setVisible(true/false)` is now a real busy-curtain, driven by the emulator's existing `Component.setVisible` → peer-visibility path (R_swing_is_truth). Same typed-holder split SJSlider / SD_sjframe use: AWT-typed convenience on the emulator, the one member with real browser wiring (here, structural attach) delegated to the surrogate.
- **Layered pane → stays a holder.** `getLayeredPane()` / `JLayeredPane.setLayer` / `moveToFront/Back` remain non-structural (unchanged from D_rootpane_holder). No consumer forces it: a structural layered pane demands the content-pane reparenting D_rootpane_holder/SD_sjframe explicitly rejected, and its real-world consumers — popups, drag layers, `JDesktopPane` — are already served by Vaadin's own overlay primitives (JDesktopPane deliberately renders each internal frame as a Vaadin `Dialog`, sidestepping this).

**Rationale.**
- **Only the busy-curtain use survives the project's scope, and it maps almost perfectly onto CSS.** Swing's glass pane has three canonical uses: (1) input blocking / busy overlay, (2) overlay *painting*, (3) event interception + redispatch. (2) is permanently out of scope (user-authored `Graphics` paint, R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b)); (3) needs an AWT mouse-event port we don't have. That leaves (1), and an absolutely-positioned overlay with `pointer-events: auto` blocks clicks for free — no custom hit-testing, no JS.
- **Blocking is tied to *visibility*, not to listener presence — matching Swing.** A *visible* Swing glass pane is the topmost hit target and swallows events even with no listener (redispatch is what lets them through, and we don't redispatch). So the default invisible pane is `display:none` (no paint, no block), and `setVisible(true)` is the whole switch. This is both faithful and simpler than a listener-triggered rule (which would break the canonical empty-`setVisible(true)` busy-curtain idiom).
- **Not Vaadin's modality curtain.** The modality curtain is conceptually the same input-blocker, but it isn't a public API (can change/break under us) and it isn't a component you can parent the pane's own content into. A plain Div we own is simpler and stable. Swing modal *dialogs* achieve modality through a window-level event mechanism, not the glass pane, so there's no coupling to model here anyway.
- **Layered pane has no forcing function.** A repo-wide sweep of sampler + testapps found zero visible-glass-pane or z-ordering consumers before this slice — every call site was `setDefaultButton` or a bare accessor in a WARN driver. Glass pane earns the structural port on the strength of the common busy-curtain idiom + Sampler-completeness; the layered pane doesn't, and paying D_rootpane_holder's rejected reparenting cost for no consumer is unjustified.

**Alternatives.**
- **Both panes structural.** Rejected — see layered-pane rationale; speculative churn with no consumer.
- **Ride Vaadin's modality curtain for blocking.** Rejected — non-public API + can't host the pane's own children. (See rationale.)
- **Listener-presence triggers blocking.** Rejected — diverges from Swing (a visible empty glass pane blocks) and would break the primary idiom.
- **Keep glass pane a holder too (status quo).** Rejected — the busy-curtain is a real, common Swing idiom and the one glass-pane use that survives our scope; leaving it a silent no-op is a visible gap.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Keyboard focus can still tab behind the curtain.** `pointer-events` blocks mouse only; a visible glass pane doesn't trap Tab focus into the content beneath. Real Swing has the identical gotcha unless the app also grabs focus on the glass pane — so this matches Swing, it isn't a regression. (Focus trapping would need a focus model we don't have.)
- **No overlay painting, no event redispatch.** Glass-pane uses (2) and (3) stay out (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b) / no mouse-event port). A `MouseListener` added to the glass pane is stored but never delivered events; blocking still works.
- ~~**Standalone panes stay non-structural.**~~ **Retired** by [SD_sjrootpane_structural](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjrootpane_structural): the glass pane now insets against the root pane, an ordinary light-DOM box, so a standalone `new JRootPane()` / `new SJRootPane()` renders one without needing a Dialog to overlay.
- **Layered pane unchanged.** Z-order round-trips, no rendering; `moveToFront/Back` no-ops (inherited from D_rootpane_holder).
- **The curtain blocks but does not *hide*.** A default glass pane is a `JPanel`, and per [SD_vaadin_first_binding](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_vaadin_first_binding) a fresh one writes no `background-color`, so it renders transparent: content beneath stays legible and a "Working…" label on the pane overlaps it rather than covering it. Real Swing paints an opaque control-grey. Found while browser-verifying the Sampler busy overlay; the geometry and the input blocking are right, so this is the R_vaadin_first opacity divergence surfacing visually rather than a glass-pane bug, and it belongs to whoever next touches opaque-background rendering.

**Validation.** Emulator `JRootPaneTest` (+2) — glass-pane peer structurally attached (`emul-glasspane` on the peer, `emul-has-glasspane` on the host), `setVisible` drives the peer, `setGlassPane` swaps the structural peer. Surrogate `SJRootPaneTest` (+3) — hosted structural attach + class wiring, swap re-tags + unplants the old pane, standalone stays a holder. Sampler `DialogsPanel` "Run task (busy overlay 2s)" demo + `DialogsWarnInventoryTest` glass-pane driver (get/set/setVisible), zero-WARN. Full `:surrogates` + `:emulators` + `:sampler` suites green.

<a id="D_internal_frames"></a>
## D_internal_frames. JDesktopPane + JInternalFrame — internal frames as decorated non-modal Dialog overlays; JDesktopPane an emulator-only holder on JLayeredPane; minimize is emulator-complete, browser-visual-only gap

**Context.** `JInternalFrame` is a MDI child window; `JDesktopPane` is the `JLayeredPane` subclass that hosts them. Both are public-hierarchy leaves. The runtime-emulation bet here: an internal frame maps onto a **non-modal Vaadin `Dialog` overlay** — the same primitive `SFrame` / `SJWindow` already peer over — so the whole window stack ([SD_sjwindow](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjwindow) geometry, `RootPaneScaffold`, opened↔`setVisible` sync) is reused, and the frame *keeps* the Dialog chrome (title, close-X, drag, resize) that `SJWindow` strips. Consequence, accepted per R_layouts_close_enough: frames **escape the desktop-pane's bounds and stack in Vaadin's overlay order** — which is exactly what lets this slice sidestep the deferred structural layered-pane port ([D_glasspane_structural](#D_glasspane_structural): layered pane stays a holder).

**Decision.**
- <a id="D_jinternalframe_shell"></a>**D_jinternalframe_shell — `JInternalFrame` R_leaf_peer_lockdown-locked thin shell over `SJInternalFrame`; a `JComponent` whose peer is an overlay.** JDK shape is `JInternalFrame extends JComponent implements RootPaneContainer` — *not* a `Window`. So the emulator extends `vaadinx.swing.JComponent` (import-swap fidelity) but hard-codes an `SJInternalFrame` (Dialog-backed overlay) peer via `super(new SJInternalFrame())`; no protected `(Component peer)` ctor (R_leaf_peer_lockdown leaf). `setVisible(true/false)` is overridden to drive the peer's `SWindow.setVisible` (overlay attach + open), since a bare `JComponent.setVisible` only toggles `display`. Default `visible=false` (a `JInternalFrame` is invisible until shown), matching JDK.
- <a id="D_internalframe_scaffold"></a>**D_internalframe_scaffold — contentPane / rootPane scaffolding mirror-copied (per [D_window_scaffold_mirrored](#D_jwindow)).** `JInternalFrame` is a `RootPaneContainer`: own `contentPane` (`vaadinx.awt.Container`) + lazy `JRootPane` (shared with the peer's `SJRootPane` via `createRootPane`, like `JDialog`) + `rootPaneCheckingEnabled` add/remove/setLayout redirect. Mirror-copied from `JDialog`, not pulled up — the JDK duplicates this per `RootPaneContainer` implementor; the dedup lives on the surrogate's `RootPaneScaffold`.
- <a id="D_internalframe_vetoable"></a>**D_internalframe_vetoable — vetoable constrained properties are real (R_swing_is_truth).** `setClosed` / `setMaximum` / `setIcon` / `setSelected` fire `fireVetoableChange` **before** mutating and propagate `PropertyVetoException` (`JComponent` already carries real `VetoableChangeSupport`); a vetoed change aborts with the field unchanged, exactly as JDK, then fires the bound `PropertyChangeEvent` on success. This is fidelity, not a gap.
- <a id="D_internalframe_close_listener"></a>**D_internalframe_close_listener — `setDefaultCloseOperation` mapping + `InternalFrameListener` bridge.** Default `DISPOSE_ON_CLOSE` (JDK's `JInternalFrame` default, unlike JFrame's `HIDE_ON_CLOSE`). The peer's close-X (SD_sjinternalframe) fires `SInternalFrameEvent` `INTERNAL_FRAME_CLOSING`; the emulator registers one `SInternalFrameListener` on the peer to relay all lifecycle fires (OPENED / CLOSING / CLOSED / ACTIVATED / DEACTIVATED) onto its own `listenerList` as `vaadinx.swing.event.InternalFrameEvent` with `source = this` (emulator), and applies the close-op on CLOSING (`DISPOSE_ON_CLOSE` → `setClosed(true)`; `HIDE_ON_CLOSE` → `setVisible(false)`; `DO_NOTHING_ON_CLOSE` → frame stays). `EXIT_ON_CLOSE` is not a `JInternalFrame` value.
- <a id="D_internalframe_maximize"></a>**D_internalframe_maximize — maximize → viewport-fill geometry (R_layouts_close_enough).** `setMaximum(true)` drives the peer's `SWindow` geometry ([SD_swindow_geometry](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_swindow_geometry)) to top/left `0` + `100%`/`100%`; `setMaximum(false)` clears it back to centered. Vaadin Dialog has no native maximize toggle, so this is surrogate-driven geometry — no listener event (`maximum` is a bound, not an `InternalFrameListener`, property).
- <a id="D_internalframe_minimize"></a>**D_internalframe_minimize — minimize is emulator-complete; only the desktop-icon *visual* is the gap.** Per the completeness ask, the emulator models the full iconify API: `setIcon(boolean)` (vetoable) / `isIcon`, fires `INTERNAL_FRAME_ICONIFIED` / `DEICONIFIED`, and `getDesktopIcon()` returns a real `JInternalFrame.JDesktopIcon` (ported as a minimal nested `JComponent`). The peer's **title-bar minimize button** (SD_internalframe_chrome) drives this same vetoable `setIcon(true)` (the ctor wires the header iconify/maximize handlers to the emulator's vetoable setters, gated by the `iconifiable`/`maximizable`/`closable` flags), so a header click behaves exactly like the programmatic call. The peer overlay is hidden while iconified (via `SWindow.setVisible(false)`, which does not reset the OPENED latch, so restore doesn't refire OPENED) and restored on deiconify. What the browser cannot render is the **clickable `JDesktopIcon` restore affordance** — a documented divergence (R_layouts_close_enough-shape), **not** an `onUnimplemented` WARN (the API *is* implemented, so WARNing would wrongly trip the Sampler exit gate); the migrator restores programmatically (`setIcon(false)` / desktop selection). This is the one place emulator and surrogate diverge on coverage by design (nothing on the surrogate; complete on the emulator).
- <a id="D_jdesktoppane_holder"></a>**D_jdesktoppane_holder — `JDesktopPane` emulator-only over `JLayeredPane`'s Div peer; add-routing intercepted.** `JDesktopPane extends JLayeredPane` (the existing minimal port, Div peer) — no surrogate (the component's whole job is bookkeeping + a background Div, both already covered; parallels [SD_no_sjoptionpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_no_sjoptionpane)'s "no surrogate by design"). Its frames escape to overlays, so **`add(JInternalFrame)` does not DOM-attach the frame** — it records the frame in a `List<JInternalFrame>` and lets the overlay open on `frame.setVisible(true)`; the one deliberate divergence from container add-routing. `getAllFrames` / `getAllFramesInLayer` / `getSelectedFrame` / `setSelectedFrame` read/drive that list. `DesktopManager` stored-but-inert; `setDragMode` WARNs (Vaadin drags natively). The Div peer styles as the desktop background. Layered-pane stance from D_glasspane_structural is undisturbed — `JDesktopPane` adds no z-order semantics.

**Rationale.**
- **Reusing the Dialog overlay is the whole win.** An internal frame is a movable, resizable, closable child window with a title bar — that is a Vaadin `Dialog` with `draggable`/`resizable`/`setHeaderTitle`, modeless. Everything `SFrame`/`SJWindow` built (geometry, RootPaneScaffold, opened-sync, close-X) transfers; the slice is mostly wiring plus the `InternalFrameListener` family.
- **Emulator-complete minimize, honest surrogate gap.** The migrator's code reads `isIcon()`, gets `INTERNAL_FRAME_ICONIFIED`, and can restore — the API contract holds. Only the *picture* of a desktop icon is missing, and hiding the overlay is the closest faithful visual. Splitting completeness (emulator) from the un-renderable visual (surrogate WARN) keeps both layers honest.
- **JDesktopPane as a holder, not a renderer.** Once frames are overlays, the desktop pane renders only a background; a surrogate would be an empty shell. Bookkeeping the frame list emulator-side is the JDK-API-faithful part; the Div background is the rest.

**Alternatives.**
- **`SJInternalFrame extends SFrame`.** Rejected — would inherit `defaultCloseOperation`+`WindowConstants`, `iconImages`, static `getFrames()`, window-state — none are `JInternalFrame` concepts. Same reasoning as [SD_rootpane_scaffold](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_rootpane_scaffold) (`SJWindow` chose `SWindow` over `SFrame`).
- **A structural `JDesktopPane` that nests frames as inline DOM children with CSS z-index.** Rejected — that is the layered-pane structural port D_glasspane_structural/D_rootpane_holder declined for want of a consumer, and it would forfeit Vaadin's overlay drag/resize/stack machinery we get for free.
- **`setIcon` → WARN-and-noop (the original proposal).** Superseded by the completeness ask — emulator now models the full state machine (D_internalframe_minimize).
- **A thin `SJDesktopPane extends SJPanel` for D_surrogate_first symmetry.** Rejected — empty shell; SD_no_sjoptionpane precedent covers the "no surrogate by design" carve-out.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Frames escape the desktop bounds; placement is viewport-relative.** Overlays anchor to the viewport, not the desktop pane (R_layouts_close_enough). `setLocation` on a frame is viewport pixels, not desktop-relative.
- **No desktop-icon restore visual** (D_internalframe_minimize) — iconified frames hide; restore is programmatic.
- **Precise z-order / `moveToFront` is Vaadin overlay order** (R_layouts_close_enough) — last-opened/focused on top; no pixel-exact stacking guarantee. `setSelected(true)` fires ACTIVATED and best-effort focuses.
- **`DesktopManager` / `setDragMode`** stored/WARN — no custom drag outline (Vaadin drags natively).
- **No new major-gap throws** — the enumerated set stays at three (all gaps here are under the WARN umbrella).

**Validation.** Emulator `JInternalFrameTest` — vetoable set{Closed,Maximum,Icon,Selected} (mutate + veto-abort + PCE), close-op mapping, minimize state+events+`getDesktopIcon`, maximize geometry; `JDesktopPaneTest` — add/remove frame bookkeeping, `getAllFrames`, selected-frame, add-routing doesn't DOM-attach. Surrogate `SJInternalFrameTest` — decorated non-modal Dialog, `InternalFrameListener` fires (opened/closing/closed/activated), maximize geometry. Sampler `DesktopPanel` route (desktop + internal frames: open, drag, resize, close, maximize, and minimize→"Restore" taskbar chip driven by the `INTERNAL_FRAME_ICONIFIED`/`DEICONIFIED` events — the emulator-only iconify path, demoed WARN-free) + `DesktopWarnInventoryTest` exit gate, zero-WARN on the user path (minimize/restore included). Full `:surrogates` + `:emulators` + `:sampler` suites green.

<a id="D_session_scoped_pools"></a>
## D_session_scoped_pools. Timer / SwingWorker survive the F5 `@PreserveOnRefresh` teleport — session-scoped scheduler/worker pools + lazy live-UI resolution at delivery; >1 live UI throws

**Decision.** Make the emulator's UI-scoped concurrency machinery **session-scoped** and resolve the delivery UI **lazily, at fire/delivery time**, instead of capturing a UI eagerly at construction:

- **`UiScheduler` and `SwingWorker.WorkerPool` are keyed on the `VaadinSession`**, stored as a session attribute, and disposed via a self-removing `SessionDestroyListener` (mirrors `SessionTempFiles`). They are no longer per-UI and no longer `shutdownNow()`'d on UI detach.
- **`Timer` / `SwingWorker` capture the `VaadinSession`, not the `UI`.** Their `final UI ui` fields became `final VaadinSession session`; the ctors throw if there is no current session (unchanged strictness, wider-but-correct scope).
- **Delivery routes through `EHelper.onSessionLiveUI(session, swingBody)`**: from the (lockless) scheduler/worker thread it does `session.access(...)` to take the lock, resolves the session's single live UI via `EHelper.singleLiveUI(session)`, then hops onto it with `UI.accessSynchronously(() -> callSwing(body))` so the R_callswing_envelope/loom VT envelope runs with `UI.getCurrent()` set.
- **`singleLiveUI` resolves the delivery UI purely through the [D_active_ui_pointer](#D_active_ui_pointer) `AppTab`** (set by `MainWindowRoute` at load + each F5 rebind): `AppTab.forSession(session)?.liveUI()`, or `null`. There is **no `getUIs()` fallback** — delivering to some arbitrary live UI could run app logic against the wrong (or a second-tab curtain) UI and produce unreproducible state, so a null resolve is the fail-loud signal (Timer/SwingWorker delivery **drops**; `callOnLiveUISync` **throws**). In production an `AppTab` is always recorded before any user `callSwing` (`MainWindowRoute` marks it before `bootstrap()`), so null means a genuine teardown, not a missing identity. It still **never throws** here — a genuine second tab is a D_active_ui_pointer curtain that never becomes the `AppTab`, so the one-app invariant is enforced at attach, not by guessing. A `callSwing` needs no `AppTab` at all: its UI fiber starts on the *invoking* UI, and a parked fiber resumes on whatever UI its anchor was last attached to ([D_callswing_loom](#D_callswing_loom)) — the reason it was never part of the orphan bug. The earlier `getUIs()` heuristic — the `ReplacedViaPreserveOnRefresh` private-class read, navigated-view disambiguation, a **>1-navigated `IllegalStateException`**, and finally the best-effort live-UI fallback — is **fully removed** (tab-scoped-app-identity Stages 0–2): the throw was the Blocker-3 curtain-vs-app confusion; the fallback was dead-in-production code (masking a future invariant break with a random UI). Identity is now the F5-stable browser tab, not the mortal UI.

**Rationale.**
- **The bug is present in F5 *today*, not latent.** On refresh Flow creates a fresh UI, teleports the preserved `@PreserveOnRefresh` component tree onto it (`AbstractNavigationStateRenderer` → `UIInternalUpdater.moveToNewUI`), and closes the old UI — which `shutdownNow()`'d the per-UI scheduler/pool, so a surviving `Timer` stopped firing and an in-flight `SwingWorker` delivered `done()`/`process()` to the dead UI. The scaffold *mandates* `@PreserveOnRefresh`, so every app with a clock / poller / background load hit this on any refresh. Proven end-to-end by `UiScopedFeaturesF5Test` (verified failing pre-fix).
- **Lazy resolution at delivery is immune to framework settle-ordering — but "one lock-holding request settles the whole refresh" was wrong, and that was a real production bug.** An earlier version of this entry claimed that by delivery time the session always holds exactly one live UI. Karibu upheld that on 2.7.0 (its `page.reload` was `closeCurrentUI` then `createUI`, so the old UI was already closing), which is why the round-trip test stayed green while **real Flow does not** behave that way — the reload-fidelity gap tracked at [karibu-testing#207](https://github.com/mvysny/karibu-testing/issues/207), now closed in karibu-testing 2.7.1 (PR #208): its `page.reload` reproduces the transient two-live-UI window, so this guard is now exercised faithfully in-test. On an F5 of a `@PreserveOnRefresh` view the old UI is deliberately *not* eager-closed (`ServerRpcHandler#handleUnloadBeaconRequest` skips the unload-beacon close for preserve views), the fresh UI is registered in the session (`BootstrapHandler#createAndInitUI` → `addUI`) *before* it navigates, and — unless the browser carried the window name on the init request — navigation defers a round-trip to fetch it (`AbstractNavigationStateRenderer#getPreservedChain` → `retrieveExtendedClientDetails`). For that window there are genuinely **two live, non-closing, unmarked UIs** in the session, and a Timer fire landing there threw `IllegalStateException` in production. The fix is the layered `singleLiveUI` above: the old (app-hosting) UI is the navigated one, the fresh peer has an empty router chain, so delivery goes to the app UI instead of throwing. The marker (Flow's own "superseded" signal, set in the later `disconnectElements` step) is the authoritative drop for the post-navigation window; the navigated-view check covers the pre-navigation window the marker doesn't reach yet.
- **Session scope is the correct lifetime, not a workaround.** One session runs one app; the app teleports between UIs across a refresh (and, under a future "re-run it here" multi-tab UX, non-active tabs are curtained, not running). So the scheduler/worker lifetime is the *session's*, and there is at most one live UI to deliver to at any instant.
- **`getUIs()` mandates the session lock** (`checkHasLock()`), so enumeration *must* happen inside `session.access` — the lockless scheduler thread cannot read it directly. `UI.accessSynchronously` re-enters the already-held lock and sets the current UI, giving `callSwing` the context it requires.

**Alternatives.**
- **Re-home machinery at old-UI-detach time** (enumerate/rebind when the old UI detaches). Rejected — depends on create/close ordering (Karibu vs Flow differ); lazy fire-time resolution sidesteps *when* the transition happens. (It does read Flow's internal `ReplacedViaPreserveOnRefresh` marker as one of its layers, but only as a best-effort drop that degrades gracefully — not as a load-bearing ordering assumption.)
- **Reparent via `moveToNewUI` ourselves.** Rejected — Flow already runs it for the element tree; our machinery isn't in the element tree, and its UI-scoped satellite state (VT carrier, captured `ui.access`) wouldn't ride along anyway. Rebuilding correct session-scoped machinery is simpler than salvaging orphaned bits.
- **Make delivery itself session-scoped (a UI-less `callSwing`).** Rejected — a deep re-plumb of the loom integration (D_callswing_loom) that owns modal-dialog parking; the one-line `singleLiveUI` resolver at the R_callswing_envelope boundary is far cheaper.
- **Accommodate >1 live UI (multi-tab) now.** Rejected — out of scope by policy (one app per session). The invariant is enforced at *attach* (the D_active_ui_pointer curtain: a second tab never becomes the `AppTab`), not by a delivery-time guess. An earlier version guessed among live UIs and threw on >1 *navigated* UI; that heuristic was the Blocker-3 curtain-vs-app confusion and is gone (see the `singleLiveUI` delivery bullet above and D_active_ui_pointer). The future multi-tab design replaces the `AppTab`-keyed resolver and nothing else.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Delivery is dropped (not re-homed) when zero UIs are live** — that only happens as the session is going down, when the pool is torn down anyway; the worker's terminal state (`isDone`/`get`) is already correct.
- **A file-download size watcher (`BrowserFileTransfer`) still targets its dialog's UI** — it doesn't re-home across F5 (the dialog-close listener is its authoritative cancel). Out of scope: transient, and the dialog teleports with the tree.
- **`Timer.start()` / `SwingWorker.execute()` must run under the session lock** (session-attribute access requires it) — always true on the UI/EDT thread they're called from; a raw background-thread call would need a `UI.access` wrapper, same as constructing them.

**Validation.** `UiScopedFeaturesF5Test` drives the real F5 path via Karibu `page.reload()` (verified against `MockPage.reload` bytecode): asserts `Timer` keeps firing on the post-reload UI, `SwingWorker.done()` is delivered on the *live* UI (checked by which UI it ran on, not a UI-agnostic counter), and `callSwing` self-heals — all three green, both orphan gates verified failing before the fix. Full `:emulators` (incl. `TimerTest`, `SwingWorkerTest`) + `:sampler` (`TimersAndWorkersWarnInventoryTest`) + all-module suites green.

<a id="D_active_ui_pointer"></a>
## D_active_ui_pointer. Active-UI pointer + multi-tab option 1 — one app per session, second tab shows a curtain; `singleLiveUI` resolves the pointer first

**Decision.** A migrated app is **active in exactly one UI per session**, tracked by the session-scoped [`vaadinx.AppTab`](../emulators/src/main/java/vaadinx/AppTab.java) identity (its live UI + the browser tab hosting it; stored under a `VaadinSession` attribute). `vaadinx.swing.app.MainWindowRoute.onAttach` maintains it via `AppTab.markAppUI(ui)`:

- **First load** (fresh route instance, no live app UI): bind this UI + its tab as the app, run `bootstrap()`.
- **F5 `@PreserveOnRefresh` rebind** (the preserved instance re-attaching, `bootstrapped == true`): re-bind the fresh UI to the same tab (idempotent — the `TabScope` survives F5), don't re-bootstrap — the app teleported here.
- **Second tab** (fresh route instance while the app is already live in another UI): don't run a second copy; render `onAppAlreadyActive()` (default: a "This application is already open in another browser tab." `Span`), leaving `bootstrapped == false` so this tab can claim the app on a later attach if the active tab goes away. This is **multi-tab option 1** (of three: (1) redirect-to-existing, (2) teleport-here, (3) restart-here) — the least code, forward-compatible with (2)/(3), which just enrich `onAppAlreadyActive` (e.g. a "take over here" action once the active tab is gone).

`EHelper.singleLiveUI` **resolves purely through the `AppTab`**: `AppTab.forSession(session)?.liveUI()` (the app UI if recorded and still live — in `getUIs()`, not `isClosing()`) or `null`. There is **no best-effort `getUIs()` fallback**: a null resolve is the fail-loud signal (background delivery drops; `callOnLiveUISync` throws) rather than a random-UI guess that could run app logic against the wrong tab. The `AppTab` is authoritative for `MainWindowRoute`-based apps (all production apps); a bare-route test provides one explicitly (`AbstractKaribuTest` marks the mock UI; the F5/dialog test views call `AppTab.markAppUI` in `onAttach`). A plain `callSwing` never needs it — its initial segment delivers to the invoking UI (D_session_scoped_pools bullet). (Evolution: the original fallback was a `getUIs()` heuristic that disambiguated the F5 window by rendered-view and **threw** on >1 navigated UI — Blocker 3, a curtain tab counts as "navigated" once the pointer clears — removed in Stage 0; the pointer/tab-marking sites were consolidated into `AppTab` in Stage 1; the residual best-effort fallback was eliminated in Stage 2 once `callSwing` was made UI-local. See the D_session_scoped_pools delivery bullet.)

**Rationale.**
- **Distinguishing F5 from a new tab needs a route-level signal, and `MainWindowRoute` already has it.** `@PreserveOnRefresh` re-attaches the *same* route instance for a refresh of the same tab (so `bootstrapped` is already set), whereas a new tab (different window name) gets a *fresh* instance. The once-per-instance `bootstrapped` flag (D_mainwindow_route) is exactly the F5-vs-new-tab discriminator — no window-name plumbing needed.
- **An explicit pointer beats inferring the app UI.** The [D_session_scoped_pools](#D_session_scoped_pools) heuristic (navigated-view detection, replaced-by-refresh marker) was reverse-engineering "which UI hosts the app" from Flow internals to survive the F5 window. With the pointer set at the teleport instant (the rebind's `onAttach`), that question has a direct answer, and it's the pointer Timer/SwingWorker delivery resolves through (blocking-dialog resume follows its anchor instead, [D_callswing_loom](#D_callswing_loom)), so they all follow the app across a refresh. **No fallback is kept**: a plain `callSwing` was the one caller that "must never resolve to null," and it no longer consults the resolver at all — it runs on the invoking UI. Everything left that resolves through `singleLiveUI` (background Timer/Worker delivery) genuinely wants the app's UI or nothing, so `null` → fail-loud (drop/throw) beats a random-UI guess.
- **Liveness = in `getUIs()` and not `isClosing()`.** A closed tab's UI is marked closing before it leaves `getUIs()`; treating closing as stale lets the *next* tab claim the app (self-heal). An F5 has already moved the pointer to the fresh UI by the time the old one closes (same locked request), so this never spuriously drops the app mid-refresh.

**Alternatives.**
- **Last-tab-wins (pointer overwritten on every attach).** Rejected — silently turns multi-tab into "the app jumps to whatever tab you opened last," which is surprising and not what option 1 asks for. The `active != null && active != ui` guard keeps the app in the first tab.
- **Track the pointer generally (UIInitListener), not in `MainWindowRoute`.** Rejected — a generic init hook can't tell F5 from new-tab without window-name correlation; `MainWindowRoute`'s preserved-instance flag gives it for free, and `MainWindowRoute` is already the universal app entry (both `@MainWindow` inline and frame-as-route bootstrap through it).
- **Delete the `singleLiveUI` heuristic now that the pointer exists.** Rejected — apps not using `MainWindowRoute` and the bare-route F5 tests have no pointer; the heuristic is their correct fallback.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **The curtain doesn't auto-recover.** A second tab shown the curtain stays curtained even if the active tab later closes — it only re-evaluates on its next attach (e.g. a manual refresh). Acceptable for option 1; option 2/3's "take over" upgrade (or a poll/push nudge) is the future fix, localised to `onAppAlreadyActive`.
- **New-tab detection needs a live, non-closing active pointer.** Under Karibu, an *unnavigated* mock UI reports `isClosing()==true`, so a second route added while the "active" UI is that mock would be treated as a first load; real (navigated) UIs aren't closing, so production and navigated-UI tests behave correctly. Covered by `ActiveUiPointerTest` (which navigates a landing route).

**Validation.** `ActiveUiPointerTest` — first attach becomes active + bootstraps; `singleLiveUI` returns the pointer with a second UI present; a second tab doesn't bootstrap and shows the curtain with the pointer unmoved; `activeUI` clears a stale (closed) pointer. Existing `JFrameMainWindowTest` bootstrap-gating tests (multiple routes on the *same* UI) stay green via the `active != ui` guard. Full all-module suite green.

---

<a id="D_gridlayout"></a>
## D_gridlayout. `GridLayout` — equal-cell CSS Grid, dimensions resolved from live child count at layout time

**Decision.** `java.awt.GridLayout` → `vaadinx.awt.GridLayout`, a hand-written plain `LayoutManager` (not `LayoutManager2` — GridLayout carries no per-child constraints) joining `FlowLayout` / `BorderLayout` / `BoxLayout` / `GridBagLayout` under the D_layout_css_on_content CSS mechanism. `layoutContainer` reads `Container.getComponentCount()`, resolves the grid the way JDK does — the fixed dimension wins and the other is `ceil(n / fixed)` (`rows > 0` ⇒ `cols = ceil(n/rows)`; `rows == 0` ⇒ `rows = ceil(n/cols)`) — and writes `display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(ncols, 1fr); grid-template-rows: repeat(nrows, 1fr); gap: vgap hgap; align/justify-items: stretch` via `LayoutCss.gridLayoutCss` → `EHelper.applyContainerCss`. Children auto-place row-major (CSS default), reproducing GridLayout's left-to-right/top-to-bottom fill with no per-child CSS. Ctor and `setRows`/`setColumns` throw `IllegalArgumentException` when both dimensions would be zero, matching JDK per R_match_swing_errors.

**Rationale.**
- **CSS Grid is the exact structural analogue.** GridLayout divides the container into equal rectangles and resizes every child to fill its cell — `repeat(N, 1fr)` + `*-items: stretch` is a one-to-one mapping, no per-child placement needed (unlike `GridBagLayout`, which needs per-child `grid-column`/`grid-row`).
- **Dimensions must resolve at layout time, not add time.** The derived dimension depends on the child count, which isn't known until `layoutContainer` — so, unlike the constraint-carrying `GridBagLayout` (which stores per-child state at `addLayoutComponent`), GridLayout reads the live count from the container inside `layoutContainer`, exactly as JDK's own implementation does.
- **Compile-blocker for real NetBeans-built Swing.** GridLayout appears across the JLawyer surface (and in the `CaseAccountEntryPanel`/`AddressPanel` slice alternatives); without `vaadinx.awt.GridLayout` the import-swap of any panel using it fails to compile. Built alongside `GroupLayout` ([D_grouplayout](#D_grouplayout)) as the two layout prerequisites the exit-gate slice forced.

**Accepted limitations (R_layouts_close_enough).**
- **No pixel arithmetic.** `preferredLayoutSize`/`minimumLayoutSize` return dummy 1×1 (FlowLayout precedent) rather than JDK's sum-of-max-child-size computation; the browser divides the container evenly. Pixel-accurate sizing is the deferred layout-library's job per R_layouts_close_enough.
- **Empty container clamps to `repeat(1, 1fr)`.** JDK lays out nothing for zero children; we clamp both dimensions to ≥1 so the emitted template is always valid CSS (and any leftover FlowLayout keys still get reset). Harmless — there's nothing to place.

**Validation.** `GridLayoutTest` — both-zero ctor / `setRows(0)` / `setColumns(0)` throw (R_match_swing_errors); rows-fixed derives columns; cols-fixed derives rows with ceiling; default ctor is one row; `hgap`/`vgap` → `gap` shorthand; cells stretch; empty container emits valid clamped grid; non-Div peer gets no CSS (D_layout_css_on_content `onUnsupportedPeerShape` guard).

---

<a id="D_grouplayout"></a>
## D_grouplayout. `GroupLayout` — full builder API + CSS-grid reconstruction from the two-axis group trees

**Decision.** `javax.swing.GroupLayout` → `vaadinx.swing.GroupLayout` (plus `javax.swing.LayoutStyle` → `vaadinx.swing.LayoutStyle` for the `ComponentPlacement` enum the gap calls reference), a `LayoutManager2` reproducing the layout manager **NetBeans' GUI builder emits in every generated `initComponents()`**. Two parts:

1. **Full builder API surface.** `GroupLayout(host)`, `setHorizontal/VerticalGroup`, `createSequentialGroup`/`createParallelGroup(±Alignment, ±resizable)`, the `Group` hierarchy (`SequentialGroup`, `ParallelGroup`) with covariant fluent returns matching JDK — `addComponent(±sizes, ±Alignment)`, `addGroup(±Alignment)`, `addGap`, `addContainerGap`, `addPreferredGap(ComponentPlacement ±sizes)` — the `Alignment` enum, and the `DEFAULT_SIZE`/`PREFERRED_SIZE` constants. This surface is what makes a NetBeans panel *compile* after the import-swap.
2. **Auto-add.** NetBeans code never calls `host.add(comp)` — GroupLayout adds referenced components to the host itself. `Group.addComponent` routes through `GroupLayout.autoAdd`, which adds each component to the host `Container` exactly once (idempotent via a managed-set, since every component is referenced in *both* axis trees).
3. **CSS-grid reconstruction (rendering).** GroupLayout positions each component independently on two axes (the horizontal and vertical group trees). `layoutContainer` flattens each tree into integer track intervals — a `SequentialGroup` concatenates slots, a `ParallelGroup` overlays children into one band (direct component children stretch to fill it) — and emits a CSS grid via `LayoutCss.groupLayoutCss`: each component gets `grid-column`/`grid-row` from its two bands and `justify-self`/`align-self` from the effective parallel-group alignment (per-component override winning; `BASELINE` → CSS `baseline`) — **except a component resizable on the axis gets `stretch`, so it fills its cell/band rather than sitting content-width at its leading edge.** A track is `minmax(0, 1fr)` (flexible, absorbs slack) when a **single-track** resizable component occupies it, or when it is a **spring** — a resizable gap (`max == Short.MAX_VALUE`) that claims its own spacer track; every other track is `auto` (content-sized). Resizability is read from the component's explicit max (`Short.MAX_VALUE` → resizable, `PREFERRED_SIZE` → fixed) or, for `DEFAULT_SIZE` (the 1-arg `addComponent`), its natural fill behaviour — scroll panes / text areas / editor panes both axes, single-line text fields + horizontal separators horizontally, everything else fixed — reproducing what JDK GroupLayout reads from `comp.getMaximumSize()`. Multi-track spanners (a component stretched across a parallel band, e.g. a full-width separator) fill via `stretch` and deliberately do **not** flex their sub-tracks: flexing all of them would collapse every column to one uniform width.

    **Row-stack right-alignment (horizontal axis).** A flat shared-column grid can't reproduce GroupLayout's *independent per-row* horizontal fill — sibling sequential rows under a parallel group don't share column boundaries in real GroupLayout, so pinning every row to one grid column strands a short row's trailing controls (a trash icon, up/down buttons) in a middle column with the far side empty. `assignRowStack` handles the dominant NetBeans idiom (a `ParallelGroup` whose children are sequential rows): each row's **leading** components align from the left, its **trailing** components (those after the row's slack absorber — a resizable component or a spring) align flush **right** in the band's rightmost columns, and the absorber **spans** the flexible middle column. Because absorbers *span* the middle rather than *flexing* the columns they cross, a narrow leading column in one row (a `"Menge:"` label) and a wide filling field in another no longer fight over a shared column, and the last trailing control of every row lands in the same rightmost column — so trash / up-down / total controls line up at the dialog's right edge, matching Swing. It falls back to the plain overlay (returns `-1`) when a child isn't a sequential row / component, or when no row has both an absorber and trailing content — so simple parallel groups render exactly as before. Vertical reconstruction never right-aligns.

**Rationale.**
- **Compile-blocker, not a nicety.** Unlike a runtime WARN, a missing `vaadinx.swing.GroupLayout` fails the import-swap at *compile* time — every NetBeans-built Swing panel is unmigratable without it. It's the layout prerequisite the first real JLawyer slice (`InvoicePositionEntryPanel`) forced, built with `GridLayout` ([D_gridlayout](#D_gridlayout)).
- **Grid reconstruction fits the dominant idiom.** NetBeans forms are a vertical sequence of rows, each row a parallel/baseline group of a few components that the horizontal tree groups into columns — exactly what the two-axis interval flattening turns into a clean grid with column alignment. The flattening is faithful for arbitrary nesting (sequential concatenate, parallel overlap-to-band); only gap sizing and independent-strip widths are approximated.
- **Filling is structural, not cosmetic.** The resizable-track + spring + `stretch` model exists because without it a grid narrower than its container packs entirely to the leading edge, leaving the far side empty — resizable fields never grow, springs never push trailing content to the far edge. That is the exact "half the dialog is empty / a field renders at preferred width instead of filling" failure [R_layouts_close_enough](../CLAUDE.md) does **not** license (only pixel/font fidelity is deferred). The remaining *proportion* gap — a field filling a shared flexible column that is narrower than Swing's independent per-row strip — is the R_layouts_close_enough-approximate part left to the pixel-accurate layout library.
- **Covariant fluent returns are mandatory, not stylistic.** NetBeans chains subtype-specific methods off `addComponent`/`addGroup` results (`createSequentialGroup().addComponent(x).addPreferredGap(...)`), so `SequentialGroup`/`ParallelGroup` must return their own type — the same covariant-return shape JDK uses.
- **`LayoutStyle` minimal.** Only the `ComponentPlacement` enum is load-bearing (GroupLayout maps `RELATED`/`UNRELATED` to fixed px gaps directly); the `getPreferredGap`/`getContainerGap` dispatch NetBeans never calls is an `onUnimplemented`-returning-default stub.

**Accepted limitations (R_layouts_close_enough).**
- **Fixed gaps consume no grid track; only springs do.** A *fixed* `addGap`/`addPreferredGap`/`addContainerGap` maps to the single uniform container `gap` (6px), not a per-gap track — exact inter-component spacing and container insets are R_layouts_close_enough-approximate. Keeping fixed gaps out of the track model is what keeps the reconstructed grid dense and column-aligned rather than exploding into gutter tracks that misalign across independent strips. The exception is a *resizable* gap (`max == Short.MAX_VALUE`, a spring/glue): it claims one flexible spacer track, because its whole purpose is to absorb slack and drive the following components to the far edge — dropping it is the structural failure above, not a spacing nicety.
- **Explicit preferred-pixel sizes not written as hard widths.** `addComponent(c, PREFERRED_SIZE, 120, PREFERRED_SIZE)` does not write `width: 120px` — that would fight the field surrogate's own columns-derived width. The `auto` track sizes to the surrogate's intrinsic width instead.
- **`setHonorsVisibility`/`linkSize`/`replace` are WARN stubs** — no clean Vaadin/CSS-grid counterpart (a hidden peer still occupies its cell; forced size-linking and live component replacement have no grid analog). R_vaadin_first drop-and-WARN.
- **Both axis groups required.** A GroupLayout with only one axis set can't place anything; `layoutContainer` WARNs and writes no CSS (R_match_swing_errors minor — real NetBeans code always sets both).

**Validation.** `GroupLayoutTest` (15) — null-host / null-group throw (R_match_swing_errors); auto-add is once-per-component across both trees; grid reconstruction places components by their two bands (incl. a direct parallel child spanning its band); parallel alignment → `justify-self`/`align-self` (incl. `BASELINE`); per-component alignment override wins; `Short.MAX_VALUE` max → flexible track, fixed-preferred → `auto`; fixed gaps consume no track; single-axis → no CSS. Resizable-fill coverage: a resizable gap (spring) claims a `1fr` spacer track and drives the edges apart; a naturally-resizable single-line `JTextField` added 1-arg gets a flexible column + `justify-self: stretch` while its row stays `auto` (no vertical stretch); a naturally-fixed plain component stays `auto` and non-stretch; a multi-track resizable spanner (`JSeparator` across a parallel band) fills via `stretch` without flexing every sub-track. Row-stack: a parallel group of two sequential rows with differing column counts right-aligns both rows' trailing components into the same rightmost column while the absorber spans the flexible middle. `LayoutStyle` covered incidentally via the gap calls.

---

<a id="D_default_font"></a>
## D_default_font. `getFont()` returns a non-null default (L&F stand-in); color getters stay null-returning

**Decision.** `vaadinx.awt.Component.getFont()` — and its surrogate twin `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.awt.ComponentMixin.getFont()` — return a shared non-null default (`com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SHelper.DEFAULT_FONT` = `Font("Dialog", PLAIN, 12)`) when no font is set locally and the parent-walk (emulator) / CSS reconstruction (surrogate) yields nothing, instead of returning `null`. `getForeground()` / `getBackground()` are **deliberately left null-returning** on both layers.

**Rationale.**
- **Real Swing's `getFont()` is non-null from construction.** A `JComponent` installs its L&F default font (`UIManager."TextField.font"` etc.) during `updateUI()` in its ctor, so `new JTextField().getFont()` is non-null before any `setFont` and before attach. We run no L&F, so nothing sets the field; returning `null` diverges from Swing.
- **The null return crashes GUI-builder code.** Every NetBeans/Matisse `initComponents()` emits `comp.setFont(comp.getFont().deriveFont(comp.getFont().getStyle() | BOLD, comp.getFont().getSize()-2))`. A null `getFont()` NPEs at form construction — this is exactly what blocked the first real JLawyer slice (`InvoicePositionEntryPanel`, 21 such call sites): the Invoice dialog crashed on open. `DEFAULT_FONT` makes the idiom survive. `Dialog` maps to CSS `sans-serif` (`EHelper.toCssFontFamily`), so a derived default pushed back through `setFont` yields a benign generic family, and `12`/plain matches `SHelper.fontFromCss`'s own fallbacks so a value read back is self-consistent whether it came from the constant or reconstructed CSS.
- **Shared constant, both layers.** Emulator (has-a peer) and surrogate (is-a peer) resolve the same `SHelper.DEFAULT_FONT`, so a stage-2→stage-3 migration sees the same default from `getFont()`.
- **`isFontSet()` unchanged.** The local-only "was a font explicitly set" question still reads the field (emulator) / the `font-*` CSS slots (surrogate) directly, so the non-null default doesn't lie about explicit sets.

**Why colors stay null (the asymmetry is intentional — do not "finish the job").** Real Swing's `getForeground()`/`getBackground()` are also non-null for a constructed component, but flipping ours would regress behaviour with no offsetting benefit: `JComponent.setOpaque(true)` reads `getBackground()` and, on `null`, *removes* the `background-color` CSS so the peer inherits the Vaadin theme; a non-null default would instead paint an opaque stand-in colour over every opaque component, fighting the theme (R_layouts_close_enough). No reported crash motivates the change either — the JLawyer slice chains `getFont()` 21× and the colour getters 0×. If a future migration target hits `getForeground().darker()`-style NPEs, revisit **together with** the `setOpaque` background-inheritance logic, not in isolation.

**Validation.** `ContainerTest` — `getFont` returns the non-null default on an unset/orphan component (with `isFontSet()` still false) and survives the NetBeans `deriveFont` idiom. `JTextFieldTest` — the exact reported crash idiom on `JTextField` no longer NPEs. `ComponentMixinTest` — surrogate `getFont` returns the default when no font CSS is set; the `setFont` PCE old-value is now the default rather than `null`.

<a id="D_date_emulators"></a>
## D_date_emulators. Date emulators — `vaadinx.text.SimpleDateFormat` + `vaadinx.util.Calendar`/`GregorianCalendar` are browser-zoned by import-swap; `vaadinx.EmulatorContext` propagates the browser zone to background threads

**Decision.** `java.text.SimpleDateFormat`, `java.util.Calendar`, and `java.util.GregorianCalendar` join the import-swap surface (`java.text.SimpleDateFormat` → `vaadinx.text.SimpleDateFormat`; `java.util.Calendar`/`java.util.GregorianCalendar` → `vaadinx.util.*`). Both default their time zone to the user's **browser** zone rather than the server JVM default, so the migrated `fmt.format(date)` / `cal.set(y,m,d); cal.getTime()` idioms produce the wall-date the user expects. A new `vaadinx.EmulatorContext` carries the browser zone onto background threads. All three are emulator-only (no Component, no surrogate — D_timer_swingworker siblings of `Timer`/`SwingWorker`) and `@Deprecated` (stage-3 code drops them for `java.time` / `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SHelper`).

- **`SimpleDateFormat` is a stateless facade.** The instance holds no live formatting state — safe to share JVM-wide as the ubiquitous `static final` field. It keeps a session-independent **config template** (a plain JDK `SimpleDateFormat`, prototype only); every `format`/`parse` operates on a per-session **backing** cloned from that template and pinned to the browser zone, reached only under the Vaadin session lock (so single-threaded per session). Config setters with no session write the template (the `static`-init window; the template **freezes** on first use — later background reconfiguration throws rather than silently corrupting every user); with a session they mutate that session's backing. The per-session registry uses a **weak-identity** map so a retained `static` formatter stays cached while loop-created throwaways are reclaimed (no session leak). Only overrides needed: the two non-final choke points `format(Date,StringBuffer,FieldPosition)` and `parse(String,ParsePosition)`, plus config setters/getters — everything funnels through them.

- **`Calendar`/`GregorianCalendar` is a thin zone-defaulting subclass, NOT a facade.** `vaadinx.util.Calendar` (abstract, hosts the `getInstance` factories) + `vaadinx.util.GregorianCalendar` (the ctors) set the browser zone at construction and inherit all of `GregorianCalendar`'s field math unchanged. The facade shape does **not** transfer from `SimpleDateFormat` for two reasons: (a) `Calendar`'s operational API is a stateful *sequential* mutation of *protected* fields (`fields[]`, `isSet[]`, `time`) that `GregorianCalendar`'s own `computeTime`/`computeFields` read directly — a facade can't fully intercept it, whereas `SimpleDateFormat`'s `format`/`parse` are atomic and its state is private; (b) `Calendar`s are short-lived locals created in profusion, so a per-instance session backing would leak unboundedly. Field ctors set the zone *before* the date fields so the lazily-computed instant is interpreted in it.

- **`EmulatorContext` closes the background-thread gap.** On the desktop one JVM serves one user, so `TimeZone.getDefault()` *is* the user's zone on every thread; on the server the user's zone is per-session and lives on the UI thread. `EmulatorContext.get()` snapshots `{session, browser zone}` on a UI thread; `ctx.run(Runnable)` / `ctx.call(Callable)` make the zone visible on a worker thread via a `ThreadLocal`, restored in a `finally`. It **never** calls `VaadinSession.setCurrent` — `getCurrent()` stays null in the body and only the zone is *exposed*. The captured session is a **handle, never a current session**: it is what lock-aware delivery (`SwingWorker.done()` through `EHelper.onSessionLiveUI`) and the off-UI-thread peer write (`vaadinx.awt.Component.withPeer` through `EHelper.runInUIThread`, [D_sync_ui_hop](#D_sync_ui_hop)) take the lock *with*, and it is never used for off-lock session-attribute access. It is therefore wrong to tell a migrator that "touching components still requires `UI.access(...)`" — that denies what [R_tolerate_off_ui_thread](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules) promises stage 2. `EmulatorContext.currentTimeZone()` is the single resolver both date emulators call: UI thread → browser zone (throws SD_browser_timezone if `BrowserTimeZone.fetch()` was never called); background thread carrying a context → the propagated zone; bare background thread → the server default, best-effort, with a once-per-thread WARN. `SwingWorker` captures an `EmulatorContext` at construction (superseding the bare-session capture noted in [D_session_scoped_pools](#D_session_scoped_pools)) and wraps `doInBackground` in `ctx.call(...)`, so worker date code formats in the user's zone automatically.

- <a id="D_emulator_context_wrap"></a>**D_emulator_context_wrap — `EmulatorContext.wrap(ExecutorService)` / `wrap(Executor)` apply the recipe once, at the executor.** The hand recipe above is a discipline the migrator must remember at *every* `submit`, and one miss is a silent server-zone date (and, as the emulator's off-UI-thread reach grows, a silently dropped peer write). `wrap` returns a view over the app's own executor — the delegate is not adopted, not shut down, and stays usable — so the change is one line where the pool is built and nothing at the call sites. **The context is captured per submit, on the submitting thread, never at wrap time**, which is why the signature is `wrap(executor)` and not `wrap(ctx, executor)`: a pool is typically built once at app startup, where there is no session, so a wrap-time snapshot would capture nothing for the pool's entire life. Per-submit capture also **chains** (a submit from a worker that already carries a context propagates that one) and lets a submit from a context-less thread **pass through unchanged** rather than borrow an unrelated user's session. No `wrap(Runnable)` / `wrap(Callable)` overloads: `ctx.run` / `ctx.call` already are that, and the pair would be ambiguous for a lambda anyway. A thread the app creates by hand still takes the long way — there is no construction to wrap, and **`CURRENT` stays a plain `ThreadLocal` rather than an `InheritableThreadLocal`** to serve it: inheritance looks free and is not, since a thread spawned on a request thread and living for the app's lifetime would pin that session — and a dead session pinned by a long-lived thread is exactly the leak a per-user handle must not cause. Revisit if the hand-rolled-`Thread` case bites in practice.

**Rationale.**
- **Import-swap beats a manual `SHelper` rewrite.** The prior guidance made every `SimpleDateFormat`/`Calendar` site a hand-rewrite to `SHelper.dateOf`/`formatAsISODate`. For an app with dozens of sites that is weeks of edits; a faithful import-swap emulator is a mechanical one-liner per import and preserves arbitrary `Calendar` math (`add`, `roll`, `getActualMaximum`) that `SHelper` can't express. `SHelper` stays the vocabulary for hand-written and stage-3 code, and for direct `Date`↔`LocalDate` conversions.
- **Why not throw on a bare background thread.** A shared `static SimpleDateFormat`/`Calendar` used from a background thread "worked" on the desktop (single-threaded luck); crashing the migrated app there violates R_match_swing_errors's spaghetti tolerance. Falling back to the server default matches what the original produced on that same thread (no browser context existed there either), and formatting is best-effort — so it degrades with a diagnostic WARN, never throws. The only date-side throws are the enumerated SD_browser_timezone case (a UI-thread wiring bug — forgot `fetch()`) and the frozen-template late-background-reconfiguration case (silent cross-user corruption otherwise).
- **Shared mutable `Calendar` is not rescued — it's flagged.** A `Calendar` stashed in a shared field and mutated across threads has no correct multi-user-server semantics (per-user zone, sequential cross-call state, and cross-thread sharing are mutually incompatible); it was already racy on the desktop. The migration answer is to *unshare* it (construct per use), a manual fix, not a silent (and false-confidence) emulation.
- **One zone arithmetic for every `Date`: `java.util.TimeZone`'s.** Both emulators zone via `TimeZone.getTimeZone(ZoneId)`, and the date pickers convert `Date`↔`LocalDate` with the same `GregorianCalendar` + `TimeZone` computation ([SD_browser_timezone](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_browser_timezone)), so a date picked in a `JSpinner` prints as the day picked, and a `Calendar`-built date shows its own day in the picker, in every browser zone and every year. That matters because the two vocabularies disagree before standard time: `TimeZone` applies today's raw offset to every pre-1900 instant, `ZoneId` the real local mean time, and midnight in one is the previous day in the other (Los Angeles 1867: `-08:00` vs `-07:52:58`; Berlin 1815: `+01:00` vs `+00:53:28`). What stays divergent is hand-written `java.time` over a pre-1900 `Date` (`date.toInstant().atZone(zoneId)`), the same gap desktop code mixing the two APIs had. `java.time` itself is **not** emulated — `LocalDate.now()` / `DateTimeFormatter.ofPattern(...)` still read the server zone and remain a manual `BrowserTimeZone.get()` fix.

**Validation.** `SimpleDateFormatTest` (frozen-template, zone matrix, freeze/throw, weak-identity leak guard, null-poison override-completeness), `EmulatorContextTest` (capture/propagate/nesting/fallback-WARN/UI-session-wins, plus D_emulator_context_wrap's seven — the load-bearing one being *"the context is captured per submit, not when the executor is wrapped"*, then the submitter's context reaching the task, a context-less submit passing through, a pooled thread left clean, `invokeAll`, `wrap(Executor)`, and lifecycle calls reaching the delegate), `CalendarTest` (getInstance browser zone, field ctor interpreted in the browser zone not the server zone, explicit-zone honored, inherited `add()` math, background propagation, bare-thread server-default no-throw), and `SwingWorkerTest` (`doInBackground` formats in the browser zone). Migrator-facing guidance in [`guides/1-swing-to-emulators/guide.md`](../guides/1-swing-to-emulators/guide.md) §"Date and time handling".

<a id="D_jseparator"></a>
## D_jseparator. `JSeparator` emulator — the JDK's orientation field and bodies over an `SJSeparator` peer

`vaadinx.swing.JSeparator extends vaadinx.swing.JComponent`, peered on `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SJSeparator` ([SD_sjseparator](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjseparator)).

**Decision.**
- **The peer seam stays closed.** `javax.swing.JSeparator` is not a leaf — `JToolBar.Separator` (shipped, [D_jtoolbar](#D_jtoolbar)) and `JPopupMenu.Separator` extend it — but neither wants a different peer, so there is no protected `(Component peer)` ctor and both ctors end in `super(new SJSeparator(orientation))`.
- **Orientation is the emulator's field; the bodies are the JDK's.** The constructor checks, stores, then calls `setFocusable(false)` and `updateUI()`, so a separator is not focusable. `setOrientation` returns early on an equal value *before* checking, stores, fires `"orientation"` on the emulator's own listener list, then pushes the current value to the peer, which is never read back ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). The IAE carries the JDK's message. `paramString` appends `orientation`. The surrogate keeps its own field and fires on its own list for stage-3 code.
- **Dual rendering path unchanged.** Inside a JMenu/JMenuBar the rebuild walk emits `MenuNode(separator=true)` and the `SJSeparator` peer never attaches (JMenu stores menu children in its own list, not via `Container.addImpl`); standalone (form rows, panels), the peer flows through `Container.addImpl` and lands as a painted flex child.

**Rationale.** Peering on `SJSeparator` rather than self-rendering on a bare `Div` gives stage-3 pure-surrogate users a `new SJSeparator()` to reach for, matching every other component. The "no surrogate by design" alternative was rejected — a divider has no VT/SPI/pipeline obstacle, only a lack of R_vaadin_first UI functionality, which is a weak reason to fight the D_surrogate_first default when the surrogate is ~15 lines and clean.

**Accepted limitations.** GridBag non-fill cosmetic gap + `getAccessibleContext` deferred WARN + null (both per SD_sjseparator).

**Validation.** `JSeparatorTest` — ctor wiring + peer install, orientation pushed to the peer, emulator-side `"orientation"` PCE (fires on change, no-op on equal), IAE leaving the state, focusability and `paramString`, L&F surface; `EmulatorOwnedStateTest.jToolBarAndJSeparator` reads the getter off the UI thread. Sampler `SeparatorsPanel` + `SeparatorsWarnInventoryTest` (2) + `NavigationSmokeTest` entry.

---

<a id="D_emulator_caret"></a>
## D_emulator_caret. The text caret is the emulator's own `DefaultCaret`; the browser reports its moves through `setDot` / `moveDot`

Every caret and selection method on `vaadinx.swing.text.JTextComponent` is the JDK's body over the installed `Caret`, and the installed caret is `vaadinx.swing.text.DefaultCaret` — a port of `javax.swing.text.DefaultCaret`'s model half. Before this, the emulator delegated the whole cluster to the surrogate's `PeerCaret` ([SD_caret_selection](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_caret_selection)), so every getter read the peer, and dot/mark were a write-only mirror the browser refreshed only while a caret listener was registered. The surrogate keeps that design for stage-3 code; the emulator no longer uses it.

**Decision.**
- **`DefaultCaret` is ported, public, and installed by the constructor through `setCaret`**, as the JDK's text UI installs its `BasicCaret` (blink rate 500, the Basic UI's). Public because the migrator's `(DefaultCaret) area.getCaret()` + `setUpdatePolicy(DefaultCaret.ALWAYS_UPDATE)` — the standard log-window idiom — is a `ClassCastException` against any other class once the import swap has rewritten the cast.
