It holds the JDK's fields under the JDK's names and runs its bodies: `setDot` / `moveDot` through the component's `NavigationFilter`, `handleSetDot`'s clamp, `moveDot`'s missing clamp (an offset past the end is stored, and `getSelectedText()` then throws the JDK's `IllegalArgumentException("Invalid location")`), the last-to-first change fan-out, `ensureValidPosition`, and the Document handler with its three update policies. So under the default `UPDATE_WHEN_ON_EDT` an edit on the UI thread moves the caret and an edit from a worker only clamps it — "the EDT" being `SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()`, a current UI.
- **`setCaret` installs a `DefaultCaret` fully** through a `vaadinx`-typed `install(JTextComponent)`, the JDK-faithful signature R_no_vaadin_in_api asks for. The `Caret` interface's JDK-typed `install` / `deinstall` WARN, and a hand-written `Caret` implementation is used but not installed, since there is still no `javax.swing.text.JTextComponent` to pass it ([D_owed_events](#D_owed_events)).
- **The caret registers no focus or mouse listener on its component.** Each would install a peer bridge costing a round trip per focus change or per click, and the browser already places the caret. So `focusGained` and the mouse callbacks run only when called, and `isSelectionVisible()` stays `false` — the unfocused JDK's answer, which is also the one the replayed script measures. The paint half (`paint`, `damage`, `adjustVisibility`, the blink timer, `positionCaret`, `moveCaret`) does nothing: those need view geometry only the browser has. `R12DeadHookTest` lists the four protected hooks this leaves unreached, with the reason.
- **Browser → Swing runs the caret's public methods** (rule 4 of [D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)): a click is `setDot`, a shift-extend is `moveDot`, a drag-select is both — with `CaretListener`s held back and fired once, as the JDK's `MutableCaretEvent` holds them between a mouse press and its release. A `NavigationFilter` therefore sees the user's moves, and a redirected move is rendered back.
- **The browser reports its selection two ways, through `JTextComponentMixin.addSelectionReportListener`** ([SD_caret_selection](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_caret_selection)). A *move* is held until the browser has been idle for a second; Flow's client sends a held event ahead of any DOM event without a synchronized property (`Debouncer.flushAll` in `SimpleElementBindingStrategy`), so a click, key or focus listener on the server sees the caret where the user left it, at no round trip of its own. Once anything listens for caret changes the moves are reported at once instead. A *pre-edit* report goes on every `beforeinput`, eagerly, and so reaches the server ahead of the value change that follows it: a Document filter reading `getCaret().getDot()` inside `insertString` — the inventory testapp's `NumberFormatDocument` — sees where the user typed, and the caret then follows the edit as the JDK's does.
- **Swing → browser is a flush of current state** (rule 5): every caret change schedules one `beforeClientResponse` render, which pushes `setSelectionRange` only if the selection differs from what the input shows. Setting an input's value puts its caret at the end, and the flush knows it — so a `setText` on the UI thread, whose caret also ends up at the end, pushes no selection at all. A render scheduled on a detached peer waits for attach.

**Rationale.** The caret was the one read the rollout could not remove by moving a field, because the browser, not the server, moves it; the question was where an emulator-owned caret gets its value from. Held reports answer it without the round trip SD_caret_selection refused to pay: the caret is exact at every server event the browser causes, and at most a second stale for code it did not cause. Porting `DefaultCaret` rather than hiding a private caret behind `JTextComponent` is what made the rest cheap — the update policy, the `NavigationFilter` hand-off and the listener order are the JDK's own bodies, and the port is also the only way the `ALWAYS_UPDATE` idiom compiles. `setText` is now the JDK's single `AbstractDocument.replace`, so a `DocumentFilter` sees a replace, and `replaceSelection` edits the emulator's Document directly rather than routing through the peer's.

**Accepted limitations.** A caret the user moved and no event followed — a Timer or a `SwingWorker` reading `getCaretPosition()` — can be a second stale. A focused JDK caret fires on a `setDot` that only collapses a selection; this one, never told of focus, does not. `JTextPane`'s selection-based styling still ignores the caret ([D_jtextpane](#D_jtextpane)), and the RTE behind `JEditorPane` reports no browser selection, so there the caret is server-side state only. A hand-written `Caret` is never installed.

**Validation.** `vaadinx.swing.text.JTextComponentCaretTest` (23 — two replays of a script measured on JDK 25, on the UI thread and off it, covering every caret and selection method, Document edits before, at and after the dot, the exception table and listener order; the `ALWAYS_UPDATE` idiom from a worker; the off-thread clamp; `setText` as one `replace`; the `NavigationFilter` on programmatic and browser moves; a browser click, extend and drag each reaching listeners as the JDK's gestures do; held vs immediate reports; the pre-edit report positioning the caret before a filter runs; one render per request with the final state; no render after `setText`; no echo of a browser report unless a filter changed it; a working caret on the RTE-peered `JEditorPane`; the zero-WARN happy path). `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest.jTextComponentCaret` reads the caret getters on a bare thread without reaching the peer. **Not browser-verified**: the client half — the held report, its flush ahead of a click, and the `beforeinput` report — runs only in a browser, and Karibu records the listeners without dispatching them.

---

<a id="D_jtextpane"></a>
## D_jtextpane. `JTextPane` emulator — thin subclass of `JEditorPane`; faithful `StyledDocument` surface via an HTML codec, emulator-only

`vaadinx.swing.JTextPane extends vaadinx.swing.JEditorPane` — reuses the `SJEditorPane` (RTE) peer for its editable surface and adds a faithful-within-the-RTE-subset styled-run model. No new surrogate: JTextPane reuses `SJEditorPane` unchanged (so no `SD*`). Foundation is the editable JEditorPane ([SD_sjeditorpane_rte](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjeditorpane_rte) / [D_jeditorpane](#D_jeditorpane)). The empirical RTE capture that pinned the mapping (driven against the live component) is folded into this entry and the `vaadinx.swing.text.RteHtmlCodec` javadoc.

**Substrate — one value format, HTML both ways (`RteHtmlCodec`).** Push and read use the same `RichTextEditor` HTML value; there is no second representation for the client to keep coherent:
- **Forward (doc → peer): RTE-subset HTML via the main `setValue` channel** (`RteHtmlCodec.toHtml` → `SJEditorPane.setText`), exactly the path JEditorPane uses. **Not** `asDelta().setValue` — the obvious "structure in, structure out" choice, and the one this design first took. `asDelta().setValue` internally does `getElement().setProperty("value", delta)` **then** `executeJs("return this.htmlValue").then(html → RichTextEditor.setValue(html))` — an async read-back that reconciles the main value. During construction (before attach) that JS read races Quill's render and returns empty, so it reconciles the whole editor to `""`: the content flashes in, then vanishes. The main HTML channel keeps the component's own value consistent and never self-clobbers. **Karibu can't reproduce this (browserless — no Quill, no `executeJs` round-trip), so it is silent under test**; the guard is the note on `toHtml` + this entry.
- **Reverse (browser edit → doc): the same HTML.** On the peer's value-change, read `editor.getValue()` — the *very property the change event fired on* — and parse it (`RteHtmlCodec.fromHtml`). The earlier design read `asDelta().getValue()` on the `htmlValue` change: a *different* property, which can lag the edit that woke the listener (both are serializations of one Quill model, propagated on possibly-different sync cycles). Reading the same property closes that cross-property staleness by construction, and collapses the codec to one format tracking one representation (the drift the two-codec split risked, untestable under Karibu). Verified structurally lossless in a real browser (see *Validation*).

Overridable seams (`wirePeerToDocument`, `pushTextToPeer`) were extracted on JEditorPane so JTextPane swaps in the HTML-read reverse wiring and suppresses the HTML text-push without a second, conflicting listener.

**Decision.**
- **Backing model = real `javax.swing.text.DefaultStyledDocument`** (reused per D_whitelist_porting — not in the `Component` hierarchy). Forced by `getStyledDocument()`'s non-null contract; also gives `getText()`/DocumentListeners/offset-based styling for free.
- **`getText()` returns plain visible text** — faithful `JTextPane` divergence from JEditorPane (whose `getText()` is HTML). Consequence: `setText("<b>hi</b>")` shows the *literal* string, matching a plain-StyledEditorKit JTextPane.
- **Codec mapping (empirically pinned against the live component).** Bidirectional + rendered: Bold/Italic/Underline/StrikeThrough ↔ bold/italic/underline/strike; Foreground/Background ↔ color/background (`Color`⇄`#rrggbb`); Super/Subscript ↔ script; paragraph Alignment ↔ inline `text-align` (incl. JUSTIFIED) on `<p>`/`<h1..3>`/`<blockquote>` — RTE persists it as inline style on exactly those three (browser-probed 2026-07-20), and it is **dropped + WARNed on `<pre>`/`<li>`** since `getSemanticHTML()` never serializes the align class there (blocked upstream, [D_gap_severity_triage](#D_gap_severity_triage) sub-bucket (a) — filed as [vaadin/web-components#12188](https://github.com/vaadin/web-components/issues/12188): the editor renders the alignment but `htmlValue`/`getValue()` drops it, so it can't round-trip); `ImageIcon` (`IconAttribute`) ↔ image embed op (`{insert:{image:dataURL}}`, base64 PNG). No `StyleConstants` home → carried opaquely on the AttributeSet (`RteHtmlCodec.HEADER`/`LIST`/`BLOCKQUOTE`/`CODE_BLOCK`/`LINK`) so a browser-originated heading/list/quote/code/link round-trips losslessly (the Swing setter API never produces them — matching a plain StyledEditorKit JTextPane). No RTE counterpart (font family, indents, line-spacing, `insertComponent`, non-`ImageIcon` icon) → **WARN per call + drop**. `HEADER` is clamped to 1..3 on write (RTE/jsoup whitelist only `<h1>`–`<h3>`).
- **`FontSize` ⇄ heading band (Idea A, graduated).** `StyleConstants` has no heading concept and RTE has no font-size control, so a *uniform-per-paragraph* `FontSize` is mapped to `<hN>` — the only lever that renders bigger text and survives the RTE round-trip (every inline/`ql-size` size form is stripped by the wrapper; browser-probed 2026-07-20). Bands from the browser-measured RTE render (h1 24px / h2 20px / h3 16px / normal 12px): write emits `<h1>` at `FontSize ≥ 22`, `<h2>` at 18–21, `<h3>` at 14–17; a sub-14 size still drops + WARNs. Uniformity skips neutral runs (whitespace-only — notably the trailing `\n` — and icon/component runs). The opaque `HEADER` key stays the **authoritative** heading carrier (browser-origin headings keep it; it wins over the band when both present); the band is the *set-from-Swing* entry point. A read `<hN>` sets `HEADER` **and** fabricates the band's representative `FontSize` (24/20/16) back onto the runs, so `StyleConstants` introspection shows a heading as large text and the round-trip is idempotent from the first cycle. Bold is **not** fabricated (the `<hN>` render is bold via RTE CSS; fabricating it would emit a redundant `<strong>` inside `<hN>`). Lists (`ol`/`ul`) have no `StyleConstants` analog and stay opaque-key/browser-only — a real `HTMLEditorKit`/`HTMLDocument` model would be their faithful home, but that supersede was spiked and rejected (see *Rejected: `HTMLEditorKit` supersede* below).
- **Write path.** A `DocumentListener` (incl. `changedUpdate`, which the base ignores) serializes the doc → HTML → the peer's main value on every mutation, under `preventPeerEvents`. So `getStyledDocument().insertString/setCharacterAttributes(...)` render. The main-value push fires the reverse value-change *synchronously*, so `preventPeerEvents` catches our own echo (unlike `asDelta().setValue`'s *async* self-fire, which the guard can't cover — another reason the forward push stays on the main channel).
- **Reverse path — parse back, rebuild-on-change.** A browser edit fires the peer's value-change; the handler reads `getValue()` (HTML) and `RteHtmlCodec.fromHtml` clears + re-inserts the whole document (firing document-level `DocumentEvent`s to user listeners, R_swing_is_truth), wrapped in `callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope). `fromHtml` parses the flat RTE HTML subset with **jsoup** (already Flow's transitive HTML parser), accumulating inline attributes regardless of tag-nesting order and reading colour from either a `<span style>` or a `style` on the inline element — the Quill read-back normalizations pinned by the browser probe.
- **Attach-handshake guard.** During attach the browser's RTE reports its transient *empty* init-state (`fromClient=true`, `<p></p>` / empty delta) **before** it renders our server-pushed value, then echoes the real content — mirroring that empty would momentarily wipe the Document (a visible flash + spurious `DocumentListener` churn). `JEditorPane.ignoreInitHandshake` drops `fromClient` empties until the peer has reported real content once; after that an empty IS a genuine clear-all. Only `fromClient` changes are gated (server pushes are `preventPeerEvents`-guarded). Latent in `JEditorPane` too — the JTextPane Element-dump demo surfaced it; the fix lives on `JEditorPane` and both share it. Found by running the Sampler and stack-tracing the empty value-change to `ServerRpcHandler` (a real client RPC) — **not reproducible in Karibu** (no Quill/RPC handshake).
- **Selection-based methods.** They ignore the caret: `setCharacterAttributes(attr,replace)` updates the pane's *input attributes* whatever is selected (the JDK's no-selection behaviour), and `setParagraphAttributes` targets the first paragraph (the JDK's empty-selection behaviour at offset 0, which renders). They predate the emulator-owned caret ([D_emulator_caret](#D_emulator_caret)), whose selection they could now read; the RTE still reports no browser selection into it. Programmatic styling that renders goes through the offset-based `getStyledDocument()` API. Named styles (`addStyle`/`getStyle`/`setLogicalStyle`) delegate to the document's `StyleContext`.
- **Faithful throws (R_match_swing_errors, verified against the JDK).** `setDocument(non-StyledDocument)` → `IllegalArgumentException`; `setEditorKit(non-StyledEditorKit)` → `IllegalArgumentException` (and is `final`, matching the JDK) — a valid `StyledEditorKit` is accepted but WARNs (we don't drive the kit pipeline, R_match_swing_errors(b)).
- **`insertIcon`/`insertComponent`.** `insertIcon(ImageIcon)` stores the JDK icon (`ImageIcon.asJdk()`) via `StyleConstants.setIcon` → renders as an image embed; a non-`ImageIcon` `Icon` and `insertComponent(Component)` drop-and-WARN.
- **R_leaf_peer_lockdown leaf lock-down.** JTextPane is a public-hierarchy leaf → omits the protected `(Component peer)` ctor; both public ctors funnel `super(new SJEditorPane())` through JEditorPane's D_peer_ctor_injection seam. Non-final (behaviour-subclassing).

**Rationale.** Emulator-only because the `StyleConstants`⇄RTE translation is pure Swing semantics; R_vaadin_first keeps the surrogate a Vaadin-first value-holder that knows nothing of `AttributeSet`. One value format both ways is the crux: push and read the same `htmlValue`, so there is no second client-side representation to keep coherent and no cross-property lag — the reverse reads the property whose change fired the event. The cost — an HTML→doc parser, the once-feared hard direction — is bounded because RTE's HTML subset is small and flat (no nested blocks) and jsoup does the tokenizing; the browser probe confirmed the round-trip is structurally lossless. Rejected: model-only storage (styling wouldn't render — fails the "faithful" goal); pure drop-and-WARN of the whole styled surface (strictly worse now that the editable foundation exists); Delta-both-ways (the first cut — clobbers via `asDelta().setValue`'s async reconcile); **push-HTML/read-Delta** (the prior design — reading `asDelta()` on the `htmlValue` change is a cross-property staleness seam, and two codecs tracking two Quill serializations is a drift risk, both Karibu-invisible; superseded by this single-format read after the browser gate passed).

**Accepted limitations.** Block structure (headings/lists/quote/code/link) is browser-only, not settable through the Swing styled API. `insertComponent`, non-`ImageIcon` icons, and non-RTE font attributes drop-and-WARN (per call — spam accepted for now per the design call; revisit by deduping on key if it bites). `Color` alpha is dropped (RTE has no alpha). Quill re-normalizes the pushed HTML (colour onto the format tag, inline-tag order, `rel`/`target`/`spellcheck` injection, a trailing `\n` in `<pre>`) — `fromHtml` absorbs all of it (verified in-browser), so a push→edit→read round-trip converges on the same document rather than byte-identical HTML.

**Rejected: `HTMLEditorKit` supersede** (spiked + prevalence-checked 2026-07-20). The recurring "why not replace the jsoup + opaque-key codec with the JDK's real `HTMLDocument`/`HTMLEditorKit` model, so headings/lists/quote become first-class `StyleConstants`-settable and `setEditorKit(new HTMLEditorKit())` apps run unmodified?" — rejected, don't re-spike. A headless JDK-25 spike of `kit.read()`/`kit.write()` found: (1) `read`/`write` are headless ✓ — the only point in its favour; (2) `write()` emits HTML-3.2 dialect (`<html>` wrapper, `align=` attrs, `<font color>`, `<s><strike>`, `<b>`/`<i>`, `<table>`, pretty-print whitespace) that clashes with RTE's subset on nearly every construct, so normalizing it needs **jsoup again** on top — the codec grows *larger and additive*, not smaller; (3) the headline payoff is **unreachable** — on an `HTMLDocument`, `StyleConstants.isBold()`/`isItalic()` return **false** for `<strong>`/`<em>` (stored as `HTML.Tag.*` keys, not `StyleConstants.*`; only colour + alignment resolve), and building a doc `StyleConstants`-first serializes to malformed HTML — the model is HTML-string-driven (`setInnerHTML`/`insertAfterEnd`/`getElement`), not `StyleConstants`-driven; (4) `HTMLEditorKit` is **not a sanitizer** — `read()`→`write()` passes `onclick`/`onerror`/`javascript:` through (only `<script>` bodies drop), so it would *remove* today's whitelist-emit XSS safety unless a sanitizer is bolted on. Prevalence check (GitHub code search + API contracts): `HTMLEditorKit` appears in ~5% as many Java files as `new JButton`, and its usage is overwhelmingly **read-only rendering** (about-boxes, help viewers, `setPage(url)`) — which push-only `toHtml` already covers — with interactive HTML authoring a known pain point serious apps route around (SHEF/FlyingSaucer/embedded-Chromium); it is not a staple of the typical-CRUD-app R_match_swing_errors baseline. Net: more code (jsoup + HTMLEditorKit + normalizer + sanitizer) for a payoff that's partly impossible and serves a niche-within-a-niche. If a concrete migrator app ever forces it, the only justified scope is read-only-first (`setText(html)`/`getText()` + hyperlink events + `getElement`/`setInnerHTML` element model on `JEditorPane("text/html")`, within the RTE subset) — **never** the `StyleConstants`-settable-heading story, which the spike proved dead.

**Validation.** `RteHtmlCodecTest` (toHtml serialize per attribute, alignment/heading blocks + alignment riding along on headings/blockquote + the `<pre>`/`<li>` alignment-drop WARN + `HEADER` clamp + FontSize→heading bands (uniform maps + consumes the size WARN-free, mixed/partially-sized stays `<p>`, trailing-newline neutrality) + sub-band FontSize drop-WARN, image/img, HTML escaping, unsupported-attr WARN; `fromHtml` parse of alignment (incl. merged onto headings/blockquote)/image/empty + heading FontSize fabrication + the Swing-authored FontSize-heading round-trip idempotency + the captured Quill-shape corpus; and the drift-eliminating **HTML round-trip** `fromHtml(toHtml(doc)) ≡ doc`, plain JUnit — the two codecs checked against each other) + `JTextPaneTest` (Karibu — peer/model wiring, plain-text getText, offset styling → peer **HTML**, browser-edit rebuild via the reverse entry point + DocumentListener fire, input attributes, ImageIcon embed, faithful throws, insertComponent/non-ImageIcon WARN, named styles). **Browser-only seams (Karibu-invisible, verified via Playwright + the Sampler EditorPanes route):** the `asDelta().setValue` construction-race clobber (why push stays on the main HTML channel), and the `push → read` idempotency gate — the Quill read-back normalizations are catalogued and baked into `fromHtml`; the composed server sanitizer (Flow's jsoup, both directions) is offline-reproducible. Sampler `EditorPanesPanel` Demo 3 (editable styled runs + live Element dump) + `EditorPanesWarnInventoryTest` (3 SJEditorPane peers, +JTextPane API micro-driver) at zero stub WARN. Full `:emulators` + `:sampler` build green.

<a id="D_htmleditorkit"></a>
## D_htmleditorkit. `HTMLEditorKit` + `StyleSheet` emulators — **extend** the JDK classes; `addRule` styles content via shadow-root CSS

**Status: implemented.** Slice 2 of the read-only-first HTML plan ([`ideas/html-document-model.md`](../ideas/html-document-model.md)). Closes the largest single gap the 2026-08-17 prevalence survey found: `getStyleSheet` / `addRule` appear in **56 / 49 of 127** surveyed files, making them the most-used members of the whole `javax.swing.text.html` surface — the A2 idiom of installing a kit purely to carry a stylesheet onto a pane nobody edits. Narrows `D_jtextpane`'s "Rejected: `HTMLEditorKit` supersede" rather than reversing it: the *rendering* pipeline stays rejected on the same four facts, and only the stylesheet carrier lands.

**Decision.** Two new classes in a new `vaadinx.swing.text.html` package, both **extending their JDK counterparts** rather than reimplementing them:

- `vaadinx.swing.text.html.HTMLEditorKit extends javax.swing.text.html.HTMLEditorKit` — overrides `getStyleSheet` (narrowed to our type) / `setStyleSheet`, plus `_bindTo(SJEditorPane)` for the emulator to hand it a peer. `insertHTML` drops-and-WARNs.
- `vaadinx.swing.text.html.StyleSheet extends javax.swing.text.html.StyleSheet` — overrides `addRule` to accumulate the rule text and push it at every bound peer.

`JEditorPane.setEditorKit` accepts our kit (binding its sheet to the peer, firing the `"editorKit"` PCE) and WARNs on any other kind; `getEditorKit` returns the installed kit, WARNing only when none was set. Peer-side injection is [SD_add_css_rule](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_add_css_rule).

**Why extend rather than port — the decision that shaped everything else.** The plan had assumed `HTMLEditorKit` "must be ported, not reused, because `EditorKit.install(JEditorPane)` references the Component hierarchy." That framed a false dichotomy: *reuse-unchanged* fails (a JDK kit has no route to our peer) but *extend* was never considered, and it wins on three counts, each of which a from-scratch port would have had to solve separately (all four claims below verified in a headless JDK-25 probe before any code was written):

1. **It is-a JDK `EditorKit`**, so `JEditorPane.setEditorKit(javax.swing.text.EditorKit)` keeps the JDK signature and migrated code needs no cast.
2. **The nested types come along by inheritance, and they *are* the JDK's types** — which dissolves the Mode-P collision the plan had flagged as slice 2's main risk. Code using this class as a headless HTML scraper (`ParserCallback` handed to `javax…parser.ParserDelegator`, no pane in sight — 13 corpus files, more than all DOM mutation combined) keeps compiling *and running* after the import swap, because a rewritten `vaadinx…HTMLEditorKit.ParserCallback` still resolves to, and is accepted as, the JDK callback. No shim types, no rewriter carve-out. Same mechanism makes the render-only custom-`ViewFactory` idiom (5 corpus apps) compile against the inherited nested `HTMLFactory`.
3. **Untouched surface degrades to JDK behaviour, not to a stub** — the safer default for a class whose rendering half we never drive.

**Deliberate divergence: the stylesheet is per-kit, not shared.** The JDK's `getStyleSheet()` returns a **static** sheet shared by every `HTMLEditorKit` in the JVM (verified: `new HTMLEditorKit().getStyleSheet() == new HTMLEditorKit().getStyleSheet()`), so one `addRule` silently restyles every HTML pane in the app. We give each kit its own. The sharing is a long-standing footgun rather than intent, per-pane styling is what the calling code means, and the injection is per-instance anyway (R_best_effort_behaviour best-effort tightening, same spirit as SD-era bounds validation). Sharing one kit across several panes still styles all of them.

**Order-independence is a requirement, not a nicety.** Rules land whether they precede or follow `setEditorKit`, because both orders are common in the field. Two levels of accumulation make that work: the `StyleSheet` holds rules until a peer is bound, and the peer holds them until it is attached to the DOM.

**Scope: the stylesheet, not the pipeline.** `setEditorKit` deliberately skips two JDK behaviours — it does not replace the document with `kit.createDefaultDocument()` (that would install an `HTMLDocument` whose element model nothing drives; the emulator's `PlainDocument` is what backs `getText`, per the plan's P1) and does not touch the content type. A custom `ViewFactory` is inert because Vaadin renders the HTML and the JDK path is `Graphics`-based (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b)). For the one factory idiom that actually appears — refusing `<img>` views so a report pane never hits the network — inertness costs nothing, since images outside base64 data-URLs are dropped regardless.

**Accepted limitations.** The JDK-side rule model is not populated: `getRule`, `getDeclaration` and the inherited `AttributeSet` views read empty, because the rule text goes to the peer instead of into a parsed shadow model (R_vaadin_first — no store just so a setter round-trips through its own getter); `StyleSheet.getRules()` exposes what was added for anyone who needs it. Appearance only — no rule restores structure Quill's model refuses (tables), which is dropped before styling could apply (SD_sjeditorpane_rte). At-rules are skipped with a WARN. Subclassing the nested `Parser` (as opposed to using `ParserDelegator`) is a corner the inheritance trick does not fully cover; `ParserDelegator` is the documented way in.

**Validation.** `HTMLEditorKitTest` (Karibu — both call orders, repeated install, one kit across two panes, PCE + `getEditorKit` round-trip, per-kit-vs-JDK-static sheet, `setStyleSheet` install + foreign-sheet WARN, `getRules` vs the empty JDK model, `insertHTML` / foreign-kit WARNs) + `RteCssRulesTest` (selector rewriting, plain JUnit) + `HTMLEditorKitJavaCompatTest` — **whose claim is inexpressible outside Java, deliberately** (R_java_karibu_tests' worked example): the nested-type guarantee is a property of *Java* source resolution, so the test has to be written in the language migrated code is written in, and a green suite in any other language would only exercise the bytecode surface. Sampler `EditorPanesPanel` Demo 1 carries the full A2 idiom; `EditorPanesWarnInventoryTest` asserts the translated rules reached the peer at zero stub WARN. **Browser-verified (Karibu-invisible):** the injected `<style>` renders — `h2` colour, `body`→content font and `li` colour all took effect, the sibling editable pane stayed untouched, and the whole stylesheet **survived an F5** via the attach re-push.

<a id="D_htmldocument"></a>
## D_htmldocument. `HTMLDocument` emulator — read-only element model, **extending** the JDK class; markup stays `getText`'s source of truth

**Status: implemented.** Slice 4 of the read-only-first HTML plan ([`ideas/html-document-model.md`](../ideas/html-document-model.md)) — the last read-only slice, and the one this project had priced as expensive. It is not: the JDK builds the element model for us. Serves `getElement` / `getDefaultRootElement` / `getIterator` (17 / 11 / 3 of the 127 surveyed files) and retires the runtime `ClassCastException` that `((HTMLDocument) pane.getDocument()).setBase(url)` used to throw. Narrows `D_direct_document_mutation` ("`HTMLEditorKit` + `HTMLDocument` are OOS") to the *rendering* half only; the write half stays out (below).

**Decision.** `vaadinx.swing.text.html.HTMLDocument extends javax.swing.text.html.HTMLDocument`, installed by `JEditorPane.setContentType("text/html")` (and by `setPage`, whose fetch forces that type). It is a **read-only projection of the pane's markup**: `_setMarkup` reparses through the JDK's own `HTMLEditorKit.read`, and the six HTML mutators (`setInnerHTML`, `setOuterHTML`, `insertAfterStart` / `insertBeforeEnd` / `insertBeforeStart` / `insertAfterEnd`) WARN and change nothing. A `text/plain` pane keeps its `PlainDocument`; a document the caller installed themselves is never replaced.

**Extending wins again, and for a second reason this time.** D_htmleditorkit's argument (the cast keeps compiling, nested types stay the JDK's) applies unchanged — migrated code casts to `javax.swing.text.html.HTMLDocument`, which stays JDK per the migration spec's §5 table, so only an is-a subclass can satisfy it. The new reason is bigger: **`kit.read()` is headless (spike fact 1), so the JDK's parser builds the whole element tree.** `getElement(id)`, `getDefaultRootElement()`, `getCharacterElement`, `getParagraphElement` and `getIterator` are then JDK code paths, not emulation. The idea doc's plan — parse into our own `Element` tree with jsoup — would have been the expensive way to obtain what inheritance hands over.

**The blocker SD_setpage_audit named is sidestepped, not accepted.** SD_setpage_audit deferred `setBase` because installing an `HTMLDocument` "would break `getText()`": a document's text is the *rendered* text (`Report one two`), where the pane must return markup. Resolution: the **markup is the source of truth** and the document is derived from it, so `JEditorPane.getText()` overrides the base's read-the-document implementation and returns the markup verbatim. Swing's own JEditorPane serializes via `kit.write()` instead — deliberately not copied, because fact 2's HTML-3.2 dialect (`<font>`, `<b>`, `align=`, `<html>` wrapper) would rewrite the caller's markup on every read. `setBase` / `getBase` now round-trip, though they redirect nothing (SD_hyperlink_listener resolves links against `getPage()`; RTE takes only base64 data-URL images).

**One document instance, refreshed in place — the non-obvious mechanism.** A second `kit.read()` into a document that still holds content throws `RuntimeException("Must insert new content into body element-")`, which invites the conclusion that each refresh needs a fresh instance — which would silently drop every user `DocumentListener` registration. Clearing first (`remove(0, getLength())`, exactly what Swing's own `setText` does) makes re-reads work on one stable instance, listeners intact and firing. Refresh is **eager** and short-circuits on unchanged markup: the model is never stale, and listeners fire at the change rather than at the next read. Measured warm parse: ~0.1 ms small, **1.9 ms for a 200-paragraph / 8.6 KB document** — cheap enough that a lazy dirty-flag variant stays a later optimization behind the same seam.

**Model selection follows the content type, not the kit.** The JDK installs `kit.createDefaultDocument()` from `setEditorKit`; here `setContentType` decides, so installing a kit never silently changes what `getDocument()` returns (D_htmleditorkit's stance, kept). `createDefaultDocument()` still answers `PlainDocument` — it runs from the base ctor, before any content type exists. Switching a pane back to `text/plain` retires the model, installing an empty `PlainDocument`, since a kit change brings a new document in the JDK ([D_setpage_fetch](#D_setpage_fetch)). `JTextPane` is insulated by its own `createDefaultDocument` override (a `DefaultStyledDocument`, which the swap deliberately leaves alone), so its `StyledDocument` surface and `RteHtmlCodec` push are untouched.

**Accepted limitations.**
- **`getElement(id)` serves server-authored markup only.** The editor does not carry `id` attributes back out, so once content has round-tripped through a browser edit the ids are gone and the lookup answers `null`. Same family as SD_hyperlink_listener's protocol-allowlist finding, and pinned by a test so an upstream change surfaces as a failure rather than as a migrator's silently-null lookup.
- **The write half is out.** Mutators WARN because reaching the peer would mean serializing the model back to RTE-subset HTML — `kit.write()`'s dialect through a second jsoup pass, the additive translation fact 2 warns about. C-append code (7 of the 9 mutating files in the survey) rewrites to `pane.setText(pane.getText() + html)`, which needs no element model at all.
- **`getIterator(HTML.Tag)` answers `null` for block tags** (`p`, `li`, `h2`) and iterates only leaf tags (`a`, `img`, `b`). That is the JDK's own contract, inherited verbatim — not a gap to close.
- **A document user code builds itself** (`new javax.swing.text.html.HTMLDocument()`, `kit.createDefaultDocument()`) is untouched JDK behaviour, mutators included. This class is only what a pane hands out.

**Validation.** `HTMLDocumentTest` (13 — id lookup, root walk, character/paragraph lookups, refresh-on-same-instance with stale ids gone, listener survival + fire, unchanged-markup no-op, markup-vs-rendered-text split, all six mutators WARN-and-noop, leaf-vs-block iterator, `setBase` round-trip, malformed markup degrading without losing `getText`, `text/plain` keeping `PlainDocument`) + `JEditorPaneTest` additions (model installed by content type and by `setPage`, retired on switch-back, browser edit refreshing it, ids not surviving the round trip, a caller-installed document replaced as in the JDK) + `JTextPaneTest` (its `StyledDocument` unaffected by `setContentType("text/html")`). Sampler `HtmlViewerPanel` Demo 4 walks the tree and looks up by id as migrated code does; `HtmlViewerWarnInventoryTest` gates both at zero stub WARN.

<a id="D_focus_managers"></a>
## D_focus_managers. `FocusManager` / `KeyboardFocusManager` — flattened two-class port over a per-UI focus pointer; tiers 1 + 2 real, key dispatch and cycle roots permanently out

**Status: implemented.** Reverses the old "AWT focus traversal is out of scope" ruling, which had no decision entry behind it and which [SD_api_three_buckets](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_api_three_buckets)'s bucket C had always contradicted (it lists "focus-traversal + `hasFocus` / `isFocusOwner` / `setFocusable`" as unimplemented *stubs*, i.e. work not yet done, not work refused). The surrogate half — the focus pointer itself — is [SD_focus_tracker](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_focus_tracker).

**Trigger.** The inventory testapp's `NumberFormatDocument`: from inside a `PlainDocument.insertString` override, ask the focus manager who owns focus, check it is the component this Document belongs to (a Document has no back-reference to its component — this is *the* way to write the check), and `transferFocus()`. The auto-advance data-entry idiom, and a file the import swap could not compile past: `javax.swing.FocusManager` had no `vaadinx` counterpart, `getFocusOwner()` had nothing tracking focus behind it, and `Component.transferFocus()` was `onUnimplemented`. Leaving the import at `javax.swing` is not a workaround — the JDK's `getFocusOwner()` returns a `java.awt.Component`, so the `instanceof vaadinx.swing.text.JTextComponent` below it can never match and the whole block becomes dead code.

**Corpus weight, which reordered the work.** GitHub file counts (`language:java`, upper bounds — JavaFX shares some names): `getCurrentKeyboardFocusManager` 21,440; `getFocusOwner` 18,592; `.transferFocus()` 5,792; `FocusManager.getCurrentManager` 866. Two conclusions: the *query* outweighs the *move* 3:1, so tier 1 carries more weight than tier 2 rather than less; and the load-bearing class is the **AWT** one, outnumbering the Swing static 25:1 — so `vaadinx.awt.KeyboardFocusManager` holds the surface and `vaadinx.swing.FocusManager` is its thin cap.

**Two classes, not four.** The JDK chain is `KeyboardFocusManager` → `DefaultKeyboardFocusManager` → `javax.swing.FocusManager` → `DefaultFocusManager`, and the two `Default*` classes exist almost entirely for the key-event machinery tier 3 drops. So: `vaadinx.awt.KeyboardFocusManager` is **concrete** (the JDK's is abstract) and carries everything; `vaadinx.swing.FocusManager extends` it and adds only the four statics plus `FOCUS_MANAGER_CLASS_PROPERTY`, also concrete so `getCurrentManager()` has something to return. **`DefaultKeyboardFocusManager` and `DefaultFocusManager` are deliberately not ported** — code naming them fails at compile time with the class name in the message, which beats a stub that silently does nothing. Cheap to revisit if a real app turns up subclassing a focus manager; that is a scenario worth seeing before building for it.

**The instance is a stateless facade; the state is per UI — the load-bearing decision.** `getCurrentManager()` is static and the JDK's manager is effectively per-JVM, but focus is inescapably per browser tab. Handing out per-UI instances would be correct until a migrated app writes `private static final FocusManager FM = FocusManager.getCurrentManager();` — a static field holding a UI-bound object, and one the migration guide's static-field sweep would **miss**, because a focus manager is not a `Component` and so slips past `MigrationGuardrails`' static-component gate. Instead every method resolves `UI.getCurrent()` at call time and reads SD_focus_tracker's per-UI pointer, so caching the facade anywhere is harmless. This converts a silent multi-tab bug into a non-issue.

**Tier 1 — the queries.** `getFocusOwner()` / `getPermanentFocusOwner()` read SD_focus_tracker's pointer and map the Vaadin component up to its emulator through the new `EHelper.emulatorFor` (a lenient, ancestor-walking `getEmulator`: focus landing on the inner field of a composite peer answers with the emulator owning the composite; focus on a Vaadin component the app added outside vaadinx answers `null` rather than tripping `getEmulator`'s invariant). `getPermanentFocusOwner()` is the same answer — the JDK's split exists for *temporary* focus loss, which the browser does not model. `getFocusedWindow()` walks the emulator parent chain to the first `vaadinx.awt.Window`, so a `JDialog` / `JWindow` / `JInternalFrame` overlay wins over the frame behind it. **The idea doc's `MAIN_WINDOW_KEY` fallback turned out to be unnecessary**: a `@MainWindow` frame peers on `SJPanel` (D_frame_strategy) and is therefore frameless, but it is still a `JFrame` and so still a `Window` emulator in the parent chain — the walk finds it like any other, and the session-scoped attribute (which can name the *other* tab's frame in D_session_scoped_pools's transient two-live-UI window) is never consulted. `getActiveWindow()` is the same answer again: a browser tab has one active window by construction.

**Tier 2 — single-step traversal, walking our tree rather than the browser's.** `Component.transferFocus()` / `transferFocusBackward()` / `nextFocus()` route to `focusNextComponent` / `focusPreviousComponent`, which build a depth-first pre-order ring from the top-level ancestor and focus the first eligible neighbour, wrapping at the end. Eligible means Swing's own gate (`isFocusable()` — now a real field with its `"focusable"` PCE, not a stub — plus visible and enabled) **plus** the one thing Swing takes for granted and we cannot: the peer must implement Vaadin's `Focusable`. The alternative was asking the browser for its next tabbable element, which agrees with Tab by construction; **the emulator-tree walk wins because the fidelity gap is narrower than the testability gap is wide** — the walk is synchronous and Karibu-testable, where the JS route is async, untestable browserless, and lands the focus-owner update a round trip later. The orders diverge only when DOM order or an explicit `tabindex` disagrees with our child order, which R_layouts_close_enough's close-enough licence covers.

**One non-obvious rule in the walk: the root is collected unconditionally, descendants only while visible.** A top-level `Window` is hidden until `setVisible(true)` (AWT's contract, which our `Window` ctor keeps), and a ctor-time `transferFocus` — the auto-advance idiom's own timing — runs inside exactly that window. Gating the root on visibility makes traversal silently no-op for every not-yet-shown frame. An invisible *container* still hides its whole subtree, which is the behaviour that was actually wanted.

**`requestFocus` moved down from `JComponent` to `Component`, and now moves the pointer.** The peer-`Focusable.focus()` route was `JComponent`-private; `vaadinx.awt.Component` now owns it (so `Frame` / `Window` / `Dialog` inherit it too) and updates SD_focus_tracker's pointer optimistically, which is what makes a `requestFocus` + same-round-trip `getFocusOwner()` agree. `JComponent` keeps its overrides and chains, per R_swing_is_truth's JDK-shape rule; `grabFocus` routes to `requestFocus` since the traversal-policy check it skips is tier-3 anyway.

**A second, separate mechanism: the AWT `FocusEvent` bridge.** `Component.addFocusListener` stored listeners that **never fired** — nothing subscribed to the peer. It now installs, lazily on the first listener, one subscription to the peer's `FocusNotifier` / `BlurNotifier` that fans out over `listenerList` through `processFocusEvent`, wrapped in `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope) so a listener that opens a modal dialog can park. One subscription drives the whole listener list (R_vaadin_first's shared wiring shape); a peer that can report neither WARNs, since a stored listener there would never fire. **Two mechanisms, two jobs, and the distinction is worth keeping straight**: this one delivers AWT events to a component's own listeners; SD_focus_tracker's UI-wide `focusin` answers "who has focus" for every component, including the ones on non-focusable peers this bridge cannot subscribe to. The bridge feeds the pointer as well, free on a round trip the peer was already making.

**Tier 3 — permanently deferred, R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b).** Key-event dispatch (`processKeyEvent`, `dispatchKeyEvent`, `postProcessKeyEvent`, `enqueue` / `dequeue` / `discardKeyEvents`, `redispatchEvent`), focus cycle roots (`getCurrentFocusCycleRoot`, `upFocusCycle`, `downFocusCycle`, `transferFocusUpCycle`), `FocusTraversalPolicy` as a pluggable object, the protected `setGlobal*` mutators, `setCurrentManager` / `setCurrentKeyboardFocusManager`, and the vetoable-listener registry: all WARN. (The *property*-listener registry is real, per [D_focus_property_registry](#D_focus_property_registry); the vetoable one stays refused for a reason that entry states.) The browser owns key routing and Tab order, and reimplementing them server-side buys nothing a migrated app can observe. `setCurrentManager(userSubclass)` is WARN-and-ignore specifically *because* tier 3 is: a subclass's only overridable hooks are the methods that WARN, so honouring the swap would advertise more working behaviour than exists. `KeyEventDispatcher` / `KeyEventPostProcessor` are **absent rather than WARNing** — both reference `java.awt.Component`, so D_whitelist_porting's interface rule would drag them into the port for methods that do nothing; code naming them gets a compile error that says so. `getDefaultFocusTraversalKeys` returns an empty set *without* WARNing, matching `Component.getFocusTraversalKeys`'s existing honest answer.

**One bonus past the agreed tiers: `clearFocusOwner()` is real.** It clears the pointer *and* blurs the browser's `activeElement`, so the two stay in agreement — the natural inverse of a pointer we now own, and three lines. `clearGlobalFocusOwner()` is the same call (the JDK's split is about which AppContext may clear whose owner, which a single browser tab has no analogue for).

**Accepted limitations.**
- **Traversal order is ours, not the browser's** (above). Tab in the browser still follows DOM order; only server-driven traversal follows the component tree.
- **`setFocusable(false)` is not pushed to the peer as a `tabindex` rewrite.** Server-side traversal skips the component; a user pressing Tab in the browser does not. Rewriting the browser's Tab order from the server is the tier-3 line.
- **`getDefaultFocusTraversalPolicy()` returns `null`** rather than a JDK `DefaultFocusTraversalPolicy` instance. Nobody can usefully chain off it — its methods take `java.awt.Container`, which migrated code cannot obtain — so a non-null stand-in would only look more capable than it is.
- **Listener registries drop their listeners.** Nothing here ever fires a property change, and a stored listener that never gets called is the listener flavour of R_vaadin_first's shadow-cache anti-pattern.

**Validation.** `FocusManagerTest` (24: both statics handing out one stateless facade, a cached facade still answering per UI, nothing-focused defaults, `requestFocus` moving the owner with `isFocusOwner` / `hasFocus` following, inner-peer resolution to the owning emulator, focus outside vaadinx answering `null`, `getFocusedWindow` walking to the nearest Window and preferring a dialog over the frame behind it, an unparented owner answering `null`, `clearFocusOwner`, forward and backward traversal, depth-first crossing of container boundaries, wrap-around, skipping disabled / invisible / opted-out / non-focusable-peer candidates, an invisible container hiding its subtree, the manager's no-arg traversal, a lone focusable component staying put without WARNing, `setFocusable`'s PCE, the `NumberFormatDocument` idiom end to end, the `FocusEvent` bridge in both directions with one subscription per component, the non-focusable-peer WARN, and eight tier-3 calls each WARNing exactly once) + `FocusTrackerTest` in `:surrogates` (SD_focus_tracker). Sampler's `Focus` route is the browser-facing demo — a phone field that auto-advances through the `NumberFormatDocument` idiom, a live focus-owner readout driven by AWT `FocusListener`s, and traversal buttons — gated by `FocusWarnInventoryTest`, whose user path also *asserts* the auto-advance hops rather than merely driving them (a silent guard miss would otherwise leave the WARN inventory clean while the demo did nothing).

<a id="D_awt_button"></a>
## D_awt_button. `vaadinx.awt.Button` emulator — the first plain AWT leaf widget; R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down over `SButton`

`vaadinx.awt.Button extends vaadinx.awt.Component` — a thin delegating shell over `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SButton` ([SD_sbutton](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sbutton)). **Not** `vaadinx.swing.JButton`: this is `java.awt.Button`, whose entire API is twelve methods with no `ButtonModel`, no `Action`, no icon, no mnemonic and no selected state. Why this slice exists and what the rest of the AWT widget family would cost: [ideas/awt-widgets.md](../ideas/awt-widgets.md).

**Decision.**
- **R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `java.awt.Button` has no public subclass in `java.awt`, so the protected `(Component peer)` ctor is omitted and both public ctors call `super(new SButton())` directly.
- **`label` keeps an emulator-side field shadow; `actionCommand` keeps one *and* pushes to the peer.** AWT's `getLabel()` returns null verbatim where the Vaadin-backed peer reads back `""` — the emulator is the only side where that null survives (R_swing_is_truth over SD_sbutton's accepted R_vaadin_first loss), the same split `AbstractButton.setText` already uses for `text`. `setActionCommand` additionally writes through to the peer, so the `ActionEvent` the surrogate synthesizes on a browser click already carries the right command and the bridge forwards `e.getActionCommand()` unchanged. (`AbstractButton.setActionCommand` stores emulator-side only — the peer's own fallback happens to agree in the common case, but writing through is the correct R_swing_is_truth shape and is what this class does.)
- **Peer→AWT bridge re-sources the event.** The surrogate already funnels browser clicks through `callSwing` into its own `ActionListener` fan-out; the emulator subscribes there and rebuilds the `ActionEvent` with `source == this` so migrated code casting `(Button) e.getSource()` sees the emulator. `callSwing` again per R_callswing_envelope — nested calls run inline (D_callswing_loom).
- **`processEvent` peels `ActionEvent` off before `super`**, matching the JDK, and `processActionEvent` is the single funnel both the bridge and hand-dispatched events reach the listeners through.
- **`getLabel()` null propagates into `getActionCommand()`.** AWT's fallback is "return the label", not "return the label or empty" — a null-labelled Button really does report a null actionCommand.

**Rationale.** AWT `Button` on its own buys little — no real app is Swing-plus-one-AWT-button. It earns the slice on two counts: it is the cheapest end-to-end proof that the `java.awt.*` → `vaadinx.awt.*` lane works (an emulator hanging directly off `vaadinx.awt.Component`, a surrogate on `ComponentMixin`, no `JComponent` anywhere in the chain), and **AWT residue in a Swing app is a migration blocker of exactly the same size as a missing `JButton`** — one `java.awt.Button` left in a 200-view app is a hard stage-2 compile error with no workaround short of rewriting the view. It is also the first concrete non-window, non-Swing class under `vaadinx.awt.Component`, so it exercises that base on the path it was designed for; the slice found no Swing-shaped assumption leaked into it.

**Accepted limitations.** `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null. `dispatchEvent` low-level dispatch stays stubbed on `vaadinx.awt.Component` (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b)); `enableEvents` is a no-op rather than a stub, per [D_frameinit_shape](#D_frameinit_shape) — unconditional dispatch grants what it asks for. The rest of the AWT widget set is unported — notably the `java.awt.MenuComponent` hierarchy (`MenuBar` / `Menu` / `MenuItem` / `PopupMenu`), a second unported root, and `Canvas` + `paint(Graphics)`, which is permanently out.

**Validation.** `vaadinx.awt.ButtonTest` (14 — the AWT `this("")` no-arg chain, the null-label field shadow, `setLabel` reaching the rendered caption, actionCommand fallback and the write-through-to-peer regression guard, peer click with `source == emulator`, listener round-trip and null no-ops, `getListeners` over Component's shared list, `processActionEvent` as the subclass funnel, `processEvent` routing, an AWT Button dropped into a Swing `JPanel` inside a `JFrame`, and the inherited Component surface with no `JComponent` in the chain). Sampler `AwtButtonPanel` + `AwtButtonWarnInventoryTest` (2) + `NavigationSmokeTest` entry.

<a id="D_awt_label"></a>
## D_awt_label. `vaadinx.awt.Label` emulator — AWT static text; R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down over `SLabel`

`vaadinx.awt.Label extends vaadinx.awt.Component` — holds the JDK's two fields itself, rendered by `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SLabel` ([SD_slabel](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_slabel)). **Not** `vaadinx.swing.JLabel`: this is `java.awt.Label`, whose entire API is text plus a three-value alignment, with no listeners of any kind. Second widget in the AWT lane after [D_awt_button](#D_awt_button); the design pass it was built from: [ideas/awt-widgets.md](../ideas/awt-widgets.md).

**Decision.**
- **R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `java.awt.Label` has no public subclass in `java.awt`, so the protected `(Component peer)` ctor is omitted and all three public ctors funnel into `super(new SLabel("", alignment))`.
- **The emulator owns the state, as the JDK's does.** `text` and `alignment` are the JDK's fields under its names and the bodies are its, so no getter reads the peer and a `SwingWorker` reading `getAlignment()` needs no UI ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). `getText()` returns null verbatim where the Vaadin-backed peer reads back `""`. The constructor is the JDK's too: it assigns the text and routes the alignment through the public `setAlignment`, so a subclass override of `setAlignment` runs during construction and one of `setText` does not, and an invalid alignment throws from that call, with the text already stored. `paramString` switches on the field, not on `getAlignment()`.
- **The peer is written after the monitor is released**, as in [D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice): both setters change the fields under `synchronized (this)` and then flush text and alignment together, reading the fields inside the `withPeer` body. `setAlignment` loses the JDK's `synchronized` modifier for that reason. `setText` keeps the JDK's change guard, so an equal text writes nothing.
- **No bridge back from the peer.** `java.awt.Label` has no listeners at all, so unlike D_awt_button there is nothing for a browser event to re-source — the R_callswing_envelope `callSwing` envelope has no seam to guard here. Static text is the whole component.

**Rationale.** Where D_awt_button proved the AWT lane works end-to-end, this slice proves the shape is *repeatable* at near-zero cost — and closes the same class of stage-2 blocker: one `java.awt.Label` in a 200-view app is a hard compile error with no workaround short of rewriting the view. The one trap worth naming is that **the alignment constants are AWT's own (0/1/2) and collide numerically with `SwingConstants`' LEFT/CENTER/RIGHT (2/0/4)**, so a value borrowed from the Swing set means something else here or throws — surfaced in the class javadoc and asserted in both test suites.

**Accepted limitations.** `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null. Alignment is invisible where the layout gives the label no width to align within (a `FlowLayout` row) — AWT behaves the same, since `FlowLayout` sizes to preferred. The JDK's `invalidateIfValid()` after a text change is not reproduced (R_layouts_close_enough).

**Validation.** `vaadinx.awt.LabelTest` (15 — a replay of a script measured on the JDK (which public methods each constructor reaches, the exception table, `paramString` reading fields), the AWT `this("", LEFT)` no-arg chain, all three ctors, the peer rendering what the ctor stored, the null-text field, `setText` reaching the rendered span, alignment with the CSS checked through the peer, ctor and setter IAE, the constant-collision trap, R_leaf_peer_lockdown peer type through a plain instance *and* a user-code subclass, an AWT Label dropped into a Swing `JPanel` inside a `JFrame`, the inherited Component surface with no `JComponent` in the chain, `paramString`, and the `getAccessibleContext` WARN). `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest.awtLabel` reads the getters on a bare thread without reaching the peer. Sampler `AwtLabelPanel` + `AwtLabelWarnInventoryTest` (2).

**Browser-verified** (2026-08-21, Chromium) together with SD_slabel — measurements in its entry; the emulator path is what the Sampler demo drives (`vaadinx.awt.Label` ctors, `setAlignment`, `setText`, and `setBackground` through the inherited Component surface).

<a id="D_r12_provenance"></a>
## D_r12_provenance. Emulator public API never exposes a Vaadin type (R_no_vaadin_in_api) — provenance, not name; `JTable.prepareRenderer` was the lone violation

An emulator's public surface belongs to the JDK, in **types** and in **reachability**. Where the JDK
says `java.awt.Component`, the emulator says `vaadinx.awt.Component`; and a JDK hook the emulator
exposes must be *called* by the path that calls it in the JDK. The rule is [R_no_vaadin_in_api](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules);
this entry is the survey it came from and the one violation that survey found.

**Why the rule needed writing down at all: it was already the practice.** A sweep of every public
`vaadinx.**` signature mentioning a `com.vaadin` type — ~20 methods — partitions cleanly:

| bucket | methods | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| peer accessors | `vaadinx.awt.Component.getPeer`, `Container.peerContentElement` | sanctioned — the has-a seam itself |
| SB-Emulators-invented types, no JDK counterpart | the eight `*Strategy.createPeer` ([D_jformattedtextfield](#D_jformattedtextfield)), `EHelper.toVaadinIconComponent` / `getDialogs`, `VaadinIconAdapter.getVaadinIcon` / `createComponent` | sanctioned — no JDK signature to be faithful to |
| JDK-shaped, already faithful | the ported renderer/editor interfaces (`TableCellRenderer`, `ListCellRenderer`, `TreeCellRenderer`, `TableCellEditor`, `DefaultCellEditor`), `KeyboardFocusManager.getFocusOwner`, `BorderLayout.getLayoutComponent`, `TransferHandler.getComponent` | correct as written |
| **violation** | **`JTable.prepareRenderer`** | wrong on both limbs |

One method out of twenty, and its own sibling twenty lines below it — `JTable.prepareEditor` — was
already right. So this was a slip, not a design position, which is the reason the fix is a rule plus
one edit rather than a migration.

**Decision — the exception boundary is provenance.** The question to ask of a method is *"does the JDK
define this signature?"* Rejected alternatives, both of which go stale silently:
- **By name** (`getPeer` / `createPeer` / `peerContentElement` may speak Vaadin). Describes today's
  spellings rather than a reason, so it cannot judge the next method anyone writes.
- **By package** (emulated packages pure, `vaadinx` + adapters as the seam). Fails immediately —
  `getPeer` lives on `vaadinx.awt.Component`, the most emulated class there is.

**Decision — the matching in-scope test for limb 2, from the Window/Frame/JFrame audit.** Limb 1 has
a provenance question; limb 2 needs its own, or "reproduce the JDK's call graph" reads as "port
`sun.awt`". The audit's answer, which held across all six of its fronts: **is the JDK method `public`
or `protected`, and does the JDK reach it from another `public` or `protected` method?** If yes, the
edge is in scope **even when the method's body is an `onNoop`** — an exposed hook that is never
called is the failure limb 2 names, and a no-op that *is* called is not. If the path is private, or
the call is an internal `ComponentPeer` one, it is out. That boundary is what keeps the audit finite:
it puts `pack() → addNotify()` in scope ([D_window_displayable](#D_window_displayable)) and leaves
`isModalBlocked` / `updateChildrenBlocking` / `getMostRecentFocusOwner` out.

**Decision — no lint, for now.** An ArchUnit rule ("no `com.vaadin.**` in a public `vaadinx.**`
signature, minus an allow-list") is cheap and the infrastructure exists. Deferred deliberately: this
is the *first* isolated instance, and the allow-list such a lint needs is exactly the **by-name**
framing rejected above — so the lint would encode the weaker rule and rot into a list nobody
re-derives. Revisit if a second violation lands; two makes it a pattern worth mechanizing, one makes
it a slip.

**Decision — `prepareRenderer` was broken twice, and both limbs are fixed.**
- **Return type** → `vaadinx.awt.Component`, and the body is now JDK-faithful and symmetric with
  `prepareEditor`: fetch the value + selection state at the view row, hand them to the renderer,
  return *its* component unsnapshotted.
- **The render path now calls it.** It previously called nothing — `renderCellViaEmulator` reached
  `getTableCellRendererComponent` directly, so a subclass override of `prepareRenderer` never ran even
  where it compiled. The cell render path goes through the hook now, converting model→view on the way
  in and accepting the round-trip back inside: **two sorter conversions per cell**, against
  [D_jtable_cell_editing](#D_jtable)'s avoid-the-double-convert preference. The hook being
  reachable is worth more than the conversions cost.

**How it was found, and what it cost in the wild.** `testapps/inventory`'s `BetterJTable:67` and
`BetterJTableNoSorting:52` override `prepareRenderer` for row striping and call `setForeground` /
`setBackground` on the result. Under the old signature that is a **hard stage-2 compile error in two
files** with no workaround but deleting the override — and had it compiled, the override would have
been dead code. This is the first gap found by an app nobody on this project wrote, and it is exactly
the class of gap a hand-built testbed cannot produce: we would never have written an override of a
hook we knew was unwired.

**Decided — the renderer snapshot carries `foreground` / `background`.** It previously carried text +
`ImageIcon` only, so the commonest Swing renderer idiom of all — colour the cell by its value — rendered
unstyled:

```java
class RedNegativeRenderer extends DefaultTableCellRenderer {
    @Override public Component getTableCellRendererComponent(JTable t, Object v,
            boolean sel, boolean focus, int row, int col) {
        super.getTableCellRendererComponent(t, v, sel, focus, row, col);
        setForeground(((Number) v).doubleValue() < 0 ? Color.RED : Color.BLACK);
        return this;
    }
}
```

`setForeground` writes `color` onto the *renderer's own* peer element (`vaadinx.awt.Component:573`),
and `snapshotRendererOutput` then builds a **different** element and copied only the text across — so
the red never reached the browser. `JComboBox.withRendererColors` now carries both onto the snapshot,
which fixes the same drop for `JTable`, `JList`, `JTree` and `JComboBox` at once (all four share the
snapshot).

- **Swing's own rule, not an unconditional copy:** text paints in `foreground` always, `background`
  only when the component is opaque. `DefaultTableCellRenderer` is opaque from its constructor; a bare
  `JLabel` renderer is not — so a plain JLabel's background is dropped here exactly as Swing drops it.
- **Extent is the accepted R_layouts_close_enough loss.** The colour lands on the snapshot element — the text's own box —
  not the full cell or list item Swing would flood.
- **One residual gap, by construction:** D_jtable_cell_editing's perf refactor renders columns whose resolved renderer
  is a *bare* `DefaultTableCellRenderer` (exact class) through a `TextRenderer`, with no snapshot in
  the path at all. A uniform colour set on such an instance (`r.setForeground(BLUE)`, no subclass) is
  therefore still dropped. Subclass renderers — which is what colour-by-value always is — keep the
  `ComponentRenderer` path and work.
- **Corroborating smell, now explained:** `table.DefaultTableCellRenderer` stores `unselectedForeground`
  / `unselectedBackground` and nothing reads them. They stay unread: the JDK consults them only in the
  selection flip, and selection theming belongs to Vaadin's Grid (R_layouts_close_enough).

**Done — the dead-hook sweep.** Every `protected` method and every public `prepare*` / `configure*` /
`create*` / `update*` / `install*` in `:emulators` was checked for an internal caller, discounting
`super.x()` chains from an override of `x` (which prove nothing about the framework reaching the hook).
The classification that matters is **not** "is it called" but *"does the feature work while bypassing
its hook"*:

| disposition | hooks | action |
|---|---|---|
| **Feature works, hook bypassed** | `prepareRenderer`, **`prepareEditor`** (`editCellAt` called `getTableCellEditorComponent` directly), **`createDefaultModel`** (JTextField / JTextArea), **`isRootPaneCheckingEnabled`** (JFrame / JDialog / JWindow / JInternalFrame read the *field*, not the getter) | **fixed** — all four now on their path |
| Feature is a stub; hook WARNs if called | `JComboBox.configureEditor` / `getEditor` / `setEditor`, `JOptionPane.createInternalFrame`, `AbstractButton.create{Action,Change,Item}Listener`, `JSpinner.createEditor` | consistent — the whole feature is a documented gap, so an uncalled hook is not a lie |
| Out of scope by policy (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b)) | painting (`paintChildren`, `printComponent`, `getComponentGraphics`, `isPaintingOrigin`, `createVolatileImage`, `prepareImage`), L&F (`updateUI` ×29, `update`, `revalidate`, `createToolTip`, `updateLabelUIs`), low-level AWT dispatch (`processEvent`, `coalesceEvents`, `processKeyBinding`, `processComponentKeyEvent`; `enableEvents` moved to a no-op per [D_frameinit_shape](#D_frameinit_shape)), focus tier 3 (`KeyboardFocusManager`'s `*Global*` and `*KeyEvents`), input-method composition (`saveComposedText`), `EventQueue.pop`, `createBufferStrategy` | dead is correct |
| Not a hook | `SwingWorker.setProgress` (user-called by design; it does fire the `progress` PCE), `GroupLayout.createSequentialGroup` (a factory for user code) | no action |

**`createDefaultModel` was the sweep's real prize, and it was a live crash.** `JTextComponent`'s ctor
called a **SB-Emulators-invented** `createDefaultDocument()` (the JDK has no such method on `JTextComponent`),
while the JDK's actual hooks — `JTextField.createDefaultModel()` / `JTextArea.createDefaultModel()`,
the only seam Swing offers for installing a filtering `Document` — merely chained back up and were
never called. `testapps/inventory`'s `NumberTextField` overrides `createDefaultModel` to return a
`NumberFormatDocument`, then casts `getDocument()` to that type in `setMaxLength` — so the migrated app
got a plain `PlainDocument` and a **`ClassCastException` on a real user path**, from a hook that looked
correctly wired. Fixed by routing: `JTextField` / `JTextArea` override `createDefaultDocument()` to
return `createDefaultModel()`, so the base ctor's virtual call lands on the JDK hook. The JDK's own
footgun comes along with its shape — the call happens during `JTextComponent`'s constructor, so an
override reading the subclass's own fields sees them uninitialized, exactly as in Swing.

**Not swept:** hooks the emulators don't declare at all (e.g. `JEditorPane.createDefaultEditorKit`,
present on `JTextPane` only). Absent is a smaller problem than present-but-unreachable — it fails at
compile time in the migrator's face rather than silently — and belongs to per-component scope, not here.

**Validation.** `JTableRendererHookTest` (5 — the `prepareRenderer` override reaching the render path,
view-row striping alternating, colour-by-value through a `DefaultTableCellRenderer` subclass, the
opaque/non-opaque background rule, and an uncoloured renderer leaving the cell unstyled) and
`JdkHookReachabilityTest` (6 — `createDefaultModel` on JTextField and JTextArea including the live
filtering `Document`, the un-overridden default staying a plain `PlainDocument`, `prepareEditor` on the
edit path, and `isRootPaneCheckingEnabled` diverting `add` both ways). Both suites assert a hook *ran*,
because that is the regression: an unreachable hook still compiles and still looks wired. Existing
JTable suites + Sampler `TablesWarnInventoryTest` cover the re-routed render and edit paths; full
reactor green.

---

<a id="D_document_last_word"></a>
## D_document_last_word. Peer→Document sync delivers the browser's *edit*, and the Document has the last word

`JTextComponent.syncDocumentFromPeer` reconstructs the single contiguous edit that turns the
Document's current text into the browser's new value and applies it as `remove` + `insertString` at
the right offset — then, if the Document does not end up holding what the browser sent, pushes the
Document's text back to the peer and restores the caret. Replaces a whole-value
`remove(0, getLength())` + `insertString(0, wholeValue, null)`.

**The problem was not a missing feature, it was a state divergence we caused.** A user-supplied
filtering `Document` is written against per-keystroke edits, and the old sync handed it the entire
field value:

- A length cap (`getLength() + str.length() <= limit`) tested against the whole value **refuses an
  edit it would have allowed**, so nothing is inserted — and since the refusal was swallowed to a
  WARN while `preventPeerEvents` blocked any push-back, the Document ended up **empty while the
  browser still showed the text**. `getText()` returned something that was never on screen.
- Single-character branches (`str.equals(",")`, `str.equals("-")` — sign toggles, separator
  swallowing) **can never fire**, because `str` is always the whole value.
- A *rewriting* filter (thousands separators: `1234` → `1,234`) mutated the Document under
  `preventPeerEvents`, so its output never reached the peer — Document and browser held different
  text indefinitely.

R_swing_is_truth makes that ours: the emulator is the source of truth and user code must see consistent Swing
state. This is not an R_match_swing_errors minor gap to WARN about, because the divergence is produced by our own sync
rather than by something Vaadin can't do.

**Decision.**
- **Deliver the edit, derived from the common prefix and suffix.** Every pair of strings yields
  exactly one contiguous edit, so there is no "unrecognised change" fallback to write. It need not be
  literally the keystroke pressed (an IME commit or autofill can collapse into one edit with the same
  effect) — what matters is that a filter sees an edit of the right *shape and size* instead of the
  whole field.
- **Remove then insert, as Swing's own replace does**, so a filter overriding only one of the two
  still sees its half. If `insertString` refuses after a `remove` succeeded, the removal stands and
  the push-back syncs the browser to that state — again what Swing does.
- **The Document is authoritative.** When `readDocument()` differs from the incoming value, write the
  Document's text to the peer and re-apply the caret dot (captured *before* the write, since a
  reformatting filter moves it deliberately and the peer write would otherwise strand it at the end).
  Swing gets this for free: there, the field renders the Document.
- **A rejection does not WARN.** A `BadLocationException` from a filter is ordinary refusal, not an
  incompleteness — and WARNing on it would pollute the per-route `WarnInventoryTest` exit gates with
  events that mean "the app's own validation worked".

**Cost, and why it is acceptable.** The push-back is a server→browser write mid-typing, the classic
source of cursor jump and input lag. It fires **only when the Document disagrees with the browser** —
for the overwhelming majority of keystrokes the filter concurs and nothing is written, so the return
leg happens exactly on the keystrokes where the filter intervened. No round-trips are added: the peer
already runs in `EAGER` mode and sends one per keystroke either way.

**Rejected alternatives.**
- **Accept-and-WARN (R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c)), advising migrators to reach for `setMaxLength` /
  `allowedCharPattern` / `JFormattedTextField`.** Rejected because it leaves a lie rather than a gap:
  `getText()` disagreeing with the visible field is worse than a filter that doesn't filter. Even
  under this option the push-back half was still needed, which is most of the work.
- **Translating known filter shapes to Vaadin constraints** (detect a length-capping `PlainDocument`
  → `setMaxLength`). Arbitrary user logic can't be introspected, and the magic breaks the moment a
  filter does anything else.

**Accepted limitations.** A reformatting filter's caret arithmetic lands approximately rather than
exactly (it recounts separators either side of the dot, and our dot is pushed to the browser rather
than read from it — [SD_caret_selection](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_caret_selection)).
A filter's all-or-nothing check still refuses a paste larger than its cap outright — faithful, not a
shortcoming. `JEditorPane` keeps its own `syncDocumentFromPeer` (whole-markup, RTE subset per D_jtextpane) and
is untouched.

**Found by** `testapps/inventory`, whose `NumberFormatDocument` (thousands separators, sign toggle,
caret management) and `JTextFieldLimit` (length cap) are one of each shape — and which reached this
code at all only after [D_r12_provenance](#D_r12_provenance)
fixed the `createDefaultModel` hook that installs them.

**Validation.** `DocumentFilterSyncTest` (9 — a cap seeing the keystroke rather than the whole value,
wholesale refusal of an over-cap paste, push-back on refusal, a mid-string delete arriving as one
`remove` at the right offset, a mid-string insert at the right offset, a rewriting filter's output
reaching the browser, a rejected character leaving both sides on the last accepted value, the
unfiltered path unchanged, and `JTextArea` on the same path).

<a id="D_awt_dead_hooks"></a>
## D_awt_dead_hooks. The AWT lane's own dead-hook sweep — `toString` bypassed `paramString`, the click bridge bypassed `processEvent`, and AWT listener order was Swing's

Four defects in landed `vaadinx.awt.*` code, found not by an app but by design-passing the rest of
the AWT widget set (`ideas/awt-widgets.md`): writing down what a *future* widget must do surfaced
what the two landed ones already got wrong. Two are [D_r12_provenance](#D_r12_provenance)
limb-2 violations — the same exposed-but-unreachable shape as `JTable.prepareRenderer`. Note which
limb: the ArchUnit lint D_r12_provenance deferred is a **signature** rule, and would not have caught any of these.
Limb 1 is still at one instance ever; the recurrence is entirely in limb 2 — what that means for
the lint is worked out in [D_r12_mechanized](#D_r12_mechanized).

**`Component.toString()` never called `paramString()`.** It built `SimpleName(peer)` directly, so all
~39 `paramString()` overrides across `vaadinx.awt.*` and `vaadinx.swing.*` were reachable only from
each other's `super.paramString()` chains — a tower with no root caller. A migrator's override
compiled and never ran. `toString()` is now `SimpleName[peer=…<paramString>]`; `Component.paramString()`
still returns `""`, so the chain's leading-comma convention produces tidy output and
`Container.paramString()`'s contract is unchanged. Retained deviation from AWT: the *simple* name, not
`getClass().getName()`, because `Container.list()`'s indented tree dumps are the only bulk consumer
and the FQN makes them unreadable.

**`vaadinx.awt.Button`'s click bridge entered at `processActionEvent`.** AWT routes a peer-posted
event `dispatchEvent` → `processEvent` → `processActionEvent`; entering at the second hop left the
class's *own* `processEvent` override — written, tested for direct calls, documented — unreachable
from a browser click. The bridge now enters at `processEvent`. The lesson generalises to every future
AWT widget with a peer bridge, and is recorded as such in the lane doc.

**AWT listener fan-out ran in Swing's order.** `javax.swing.event.EventListenerList.getListeners`
walks its backing array from the tail, i.e. last-registered-first — correct for Swing, which fires in
reverse-registration order. `AWTEventMulticaster.add(existing, new)` dispatches `a` (the existing
chain) before `b`, i.e. first-registered-first. Every AWT-lane fan-out and every
`getXListeners()` used the Swing order, silently reversing what `java.awt.*` guarantees.

Fixed with one seam, `Component.awtListeners(Class<T>)`, which reverses in place (`getListeners`
allocates fresh per call, so the snapshot semantics that make in-dispatch mutation safe survive) —
now used by all 20 sites in `Component`, 6 in `Window`, 2 in `Container` and 2 in `Button`, plus a
local equivalent in `SButton`. **The `vaadinx.swing.*` sites are deliberately untouched**, including
those over AWT listener types (`AbstractButton`'s `ActionListener`/`ItemListener`, `JTextField`,
`JComboBox`, `Timer`): real Swing stores those in `JComponent.listenerList` and fires them last-first,
so the Swing order is the faithful one there. The split is per-class-hierarchy, not per-listener-type,
which is why the helper is documented as AWT-only rather than as a general utility.

**`Container.addImpl` was missing a guard and diverged on two more.** Against the JDK:
- `checkNotAWindow` was **absent** — adding a `Window` to a container silently nested its peer
  element inline instead of throwing `IllegalArgumentException("adding a window to a container")`.
  Safe to add: SB-Emulators' "inline frame" ([D_frame_strategy](#D_jframe_as_route))
  means a `JFrame` rendering as a route's content, not an `add()`-nested one, and `JDesktopPane`'s
  children are `JInternalFrame`s, which are `JComponent`s.
- The self-add message was invented. AWT has no separate self-check: `checkAddToSelf` walks from
  `this` *upward*, so a self-add reports `"adding container's parent to itself"`. Ours said
  `"adding component to itself"`, which a migrator matching on the message would never find.
- Guard **order** was ours, not AWT's. The bounds check runs first in the JDK, so `add(this, 999)`
  reports the bad position, not the bad component.
- The post-detach index re-check **clamped where AWT throws**. Re-adding a container's own child at
  the old end (`parent.add(child, 1)` with one child) shrinks the list to 0; AWT re-checks and throws,
  we silently accepted the position (R_match_swing_errors).

**Why one test had to change rather than the guard.** `JComponentTest`'s `getTopLevelAncestor` case
built a two-`Window` containment chain to assert the walk stops at the *nearest* one. That fixture is
unconstructible in real Swing for exactly the reason `checkNotAWindow` exists, so the distinction it
asserted cannot arise in Swing or here; it now asserts depth below a single Window instead.

**Validation.** `ButtonTest` +2 (a browser click reaches a `processEvent` override; three listeners
fire 1-2-3), `ContainerTest` +4 (`toString` shows a subclass's `paramString`; the Window rejection;
the self-add message and the bounds check outranking it; throw-not-clamp on re-add past the shrunken
end). Full reactor green, all 16 modules.

<a id="D_r12_mechanized"></a>
## D_r12_mechanized. R_no_vaadin_in_api is mechanizable — limb 1 is a guard with no allow-list; limb 2 needs the JDK's call graph as its oracle

[D_r12_provenance](#D_r12_provenance)
deferred an ArchUnit lint for R_no_vaadin_in_api and set the trigger at "a second violation". That trigger has
**not** fired, and [D_awt_dead_hooks](#D_awt_dead_hooks)
briefly claimed otherwise: the deferred lint is a **signature** rule (limb 1), while every defect
since has been a **reachability** one (limb 2). Limb 1 stands at one instance ever. The two limbs
want different machinery, and only one of them is cheap.

**Limb 1 — built, and the deferral's premise was wrong.** D_r12_provenance declined the lint because the
allow-list it needs "is exactly the **by-name** framing rejected above — so the lint would encode the
weaker rule and rot into a list nobody re-derives." No list is needed: *provenance is computable*.
Map `vaadinx.awt.Foo` → `java.awt.Foo` and ask the JDK class whether it declares a member of that
name. Every exception D_r12_provenance enumerated by hand falls out for free — a class the JDK has no counterpart
for (`EHelper`, `AppTab`, the `*Strategy` family) is sanctioned because the lookup misses, and
`getPeer` is sanctioned because `java.awt.Component` has no such member.

`R12ProvenanceTest` implements it in ~150 lines with **no new dependency** — plain reflection beats
