ArchUnit here, because it reads *generic* types and so catches a Vaadin type hidden inside a
JDK-looking signature (`EHelper.getDialogs`'s `List<Dialog>`), which raw bytecode inspection misses.
Current state: **0 violations**, 64 members sanctioned by provenance (50 on classes with no JDK
counterpart, 14 on members the JDK class does not declare). Verified to fail, not merely to pass: an
injected `getAccessibleContext(int)` returning a Vaadin `Component` is caught and reported with the
JDK class that proves it is a shadowed signature.

Note the surface grew ~4× since D_r12_provenance surveyed it (~20 members → 80 mentioning a `com.vaadin` type)
while staying clean, which is the case for a guard rather than a cleanup.

**Constructors are out of scope** for the rule: the protected `(com.vaadin.flow.component.Component peer)`
ctor *is* [D_peer_ctor_injection](#D_peer_ctor_injection)'s peer seam, sanctioned by R_leaf_peer_lockdown as
how a subclass supplies its peer.

**Limb 2 — designed, not built, and it cannot be allow-list-free.** The oracle is the JDK's own call
graph: if the emulated JDK class calls a method from its own bytecode, something in `vaadinx.**` must
call it too. Probing the current tree found 261 protected methods with 63 uncalled names, splitting
into ~15 deliberate scope exclusions (paint, L&F, key dispatch, input method, the event queue), a
bucket the scan simply cannot see the callers of (the `AbstractPreferences` SPI, Vaadin's `onAttach`,
migrator-called `SwingWorker.publish`), and **~10 suspected real dead hooks** — `createActionListener`
/ `createItemListener`, `createChangeListener` ×3, `JSpinner.createEditor`, `setRootPane` ×4,
`JTextPane.getStyledEditorKit`, `TableColumn.createDefaultHeaderRenderer`.

So limb 2 ships with a suppression list where limb 1 needed none. That list is **not** the one D_r12_provenance
rejected: D_r12_provenance refused a catalogue of *naming spellings*, which encodes no reason; this is a list of
*mechanisms the project has decided not to implement*, each already carrying an R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b)
ruling and a `D*` entry — reviewable on its merits, and an entry going stale is itself a finding.

**Limb 2 is now built** — as `R12DeadHookTest`, over the *protected* surface only, with the
suppression list on the **caller** side rather than the target side. What the build changed about the
design above, including the two of its "~10 suspected dead hooks" that turned out not to be hooks at
all: [D_dead_hook_lint](#D_dead_hook_lint).


---

<a id="D_dead_hook_lint"></a>
## D_dead_hook_lint. R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2 is a gate on the *protected* surface, with the suppression list on the caller side

`emulators/src/test/java/vaadinx/R12DeadHookTest.java`. The oracle is
[D_r12_mechanized](#D_r12_mechanized)'s: import `jrt:/java.desktop`, and for each emulator method ask
whether the emulated JDK class's own ancestry calls a method of that name from its own bytecode. If it
does, the JDK has declared an override point, and something in `vaadinx.**` / `com.vaadin.swingbridge.**` must call it
too. Which JDK class is an emulator's counterpart is computed from the same package table
`R12ProvenanceTest` uses, so the two limbs cannot drift apart.

**The `jrt:/java.desktop` import was the load-bearing unknown and it works** — but only one of the
three plausible routes does. `importUrl(jrtPath.toUri().toURL())` imports 5605 classes;
`importPaths(jrtPath)` throws, because ArchUnit's `Location` demands a `file` scheme; and
`importClasses(JTable.class, …)` — the classloader route — *silently* returns a short call graph,
since a caller outside the imported set is invisible. Method references register as accesses on 1.4.2
(633 in SB-Emulators), which the gate asserts, because if they ever stopped every `this::foo` wiring would read
as a dead hook — **and they are counted on our side of the join as well as asserted**, since
`getCallsFromSelf()` alone omits them, so `addChangeListener(this::fireStateChanged)` would have read
as no wiring at all.

**Decision: the gate covers protected methods; the public surface gets a printed report and no
assertion.** The same rule over public methods reports ~289 names and cannot be made green — and the
reason is not noise to be filtered but a real difference in kind. SB-Emulators drives a Vaadin peer where the
JDK computes geometry, so "the JDK's `getColumnName` calls `convertColumnIndexToModel` and SB-Emulators' does
not" is a different implementation, not a stranded override. A protected method exists *only* to be
overridden, so an uncalled one is exactly limb 2's trap. `reportProtectedHookCoverage` prints the
triage view; the public tier's residue is a report to read, not a list to carry.

**Decision: `final` methods are out of scope by rule, not by list.** No override can be stranded on a
method that cannot be overridden, so `JTextPane.getStyledEditorKit` — one of D_r12_mechanized's
suspected dead hooks — is not a limb-2 finding at all. It is still dead code, and it hides a
*separate* finding: `createDefaultEditorKit` is non-final and reachable only from it, so a scan that
asks "does anything call this" sees a live call site inside a dead method.

**Decision: a call site only counts if it can run — chain collapse on the SB-Emulators side, and it found
exactly one hook.** *(2026-09-10, the refinement this entry left open.)* The gate walks our own
invocation graph from the units something outside SB-Emulators can start — a constructor or static
initializer, a **public** method (an entry point whether or not we call it, because the migrator
calls it), or an override of something a foreign supertype declares, which is what keeps Vaadin's
`onAttach` and `BridgedPreferences`' JDK-called `*Spi` family from reading as dead — and a call site
in an unreachable unit no longer excuses a hook. **Reachability is per unit, not per class, and
lambda bodies fold onto the method enclosing them** (`lambda$foo$0` runs exactly when `foo` runs, so
its call sites and its reachability are `foo`'s). 6342 of 6457 of our code units are reachable, and
the gate asserts that ratio stays above three quarters: edges that stopped resolving would mark
almost everything dead and flood the report with artefacts, and one clear failure beats fifty false
ones. The **class** axis stays loose on purpose (a call to `JLabel.paramString` still excuses
`JButton.paramString`) — this refinement tightens the *reachability* axis only.

The one finding was the one this entry predicted: `JTextPane.createDefaultEditorKit`, whose only
caller was the final-and-never-called `getStyledEditorKit`. **Fixed in the JDK's own idiom** — the
ctor builds the kit through the hook exactly where `javax.swing.JTextPane`'s ctor does, so a
migrator's override runs at construction; `getInputAttributes()` now reads the kit's attribute set
rather than a private field of its own, which is both where the JDK keeps it and what makes an
override that seeds attributes observable; `setCharacterAttributes` / `getCharacterAttributes` read
through `getInputAttributes()` as the JDK's bodies do; and `JTextPane(StyledDocument)` delegates to
`this()` as the JDK's does, so the kit is built on both paths. Two deliberate deviations from the
JDK's ctor: the kit is **not** handed on to `setEditorKit`, because that path WARNs that the kit
drives no pipeline here — worth saying about a kit the migrator installed, noise about a default they
never asked for, and it would redden every `WarnInventoryTest` route holding a JTextPane; and
`getStyledEditorKit()` casts the ctor-built kit instead of `getEditorKit()`, which here answers only
what the migrator installed (JEditorPane's documented divergence). The hook's return type widened
`StyledEditorKit` → `EditorKit` to match the JDK's declaration, which is the *other* half of the same
defect: an override written as the JDK declares it did not compile, so the migrator could not reach
the hook even by hand.

**Decision: the suppression list is caller-side, and that is a measurement rather than a taste.**
Noise clusters by *caller*: `updateUI` alone proves 19 rows, `setUIProperty` 10, `paramString` 10,
`setDropLocation` 11. One entry naming a mechanism retires all of its rows under one reason, where a
target-side list needs an entry per stranded method with no reason shared between them. It also
self-invalidates the way D_r12_mechanized wanted: if L&F comes into scope, SB-Emulators starts calling
`updateUI` and the entry visibly stops firing. Both lists — the 19 caller mechanisms and the 10
individually-declined hooks — are **asserted live**, so a stale entry fails the build. That assertion
earned its keep on the first run, catching a `paintChildren` entry that never fired.

Three caller classes are distinguished, and only the middle one is a reviewable list:
- **`plaf` callers never count**, per D_r12_mechanized. Without it the rule fires on every
  `BasicXxxUI`-driven hook in Swing, which is most of them.
- **`SUPPRESSED_CALLER`** — mechanisms SB-Emulators declined (painting, L&F, key dispatch, pixel geometry,
  AWT's native focus-request queue). Each carries its reason and its `R_`/`D_` ruling.
- **`NOT_A_PATH_HERE`** — `readObject` and its serialization siblings, which are not declined
  mechanisms but paths that do not exist here at all, so they carry no reason and no staleness
  assertion. Left unhandled this was the single largest noise source: `readObject` proves every AWT
  listener-adder is a hook.

**Three sanctions that are not lists**, each of which cost a false positive when it was missing:
- **An emulator that *extends* a JDK class has the JDK as its caller.** `vaadinx.awt.event.ComponentEvent
  extends java.awt.AWTEvent`, whose `toString()` genuinely dispatches to the `paramString()` override
  — 9 false positives, and the same sanction `R12ProvenanceTest.overridesJdkDeclared` applies on limb
  1. Interfaces must be walked as well as superclasses.
- **Overload delegation is not a hook.** `GroupLayout$SequentialGroup.addContainerGap(int)` calling
  `addContainerGap(int,int)` says nothing about override points.
- **"Dead" for a *caller* means unreachable, not un-called-by-com.vaadin.swingbridge.** A first cut at collapsing chains
  retired `createActionListener` as "downstream of a dead `setModel`" — but `setModel` is *public*,
  i.e. an entry point the migrator calls, so it is live and its failure to call the factory is the
  finding. Only a protected-and-uncalled method counts as a dead caller. With that fixed there are no
  chains on the protected tier, only roots.

**What it found, and what it retired.** 15 protected hook names unreached, against
D_r12_mechanized's predicted ~10 — and the oracle disagreed with that hand-list in both directions.
`TableColumn.createDefaultHeaderRenderer` has **zero** callers anywhere in `java.desktop`, so it is
not a hook and the suspicion was unfounded; `setRootPane` was predicted on four classes and holds on
one, `JInternalFrame`'s. In the other direction, `JTable.prepareRenderer` — the founding case — is
provable only via `JTable.getToolTipText`, since refinement 1 excludes its `plaf` callers: one caller
is the whole difference between the case that started this being catchable and not, which is worth
knowing before anyone adds `getToolTipText` to a mechanism entry.

**Three fixed, in the JDK's own idiom:**
- `JSlider` / `JProgressBar` subscribed an inline `e -> fireStateChanged()` lambda where the JDK's
  ctor subscribes `createChangeListener()`'s return value. Both emulators *had* a working
  `createChangeListener` that nothing called — `JSlider`'s javadoc even called it "the installed
  bridge". Now stored in a `protected ChangeListener changeListener` field named as the JDK's is and
  subscribed from there. `EventListenerList.add` ignores a null listener, so an override returning
  null degrades as the JDK's would.
- `JInternalFrame` wrote `rootPaneCheckingEnabled` directly in `frameInit` and around
  `setContentPane`'s re-parent, while *reading* it through `isRootPaneCheckingEnabled()` — an
  asymmetry, since the JDK's own `setRootPane` brackets its re-parent with both accessors. All three
  writes now route through `setRootPaneCheckingEnabled`.

**One declined for a reason worth recording.** `JInternalFrame.setRootPane` stays unreached: SB-Emulators
builds the pane lazily in `getRootPane()`, and routing that construction through the setter would fire
a `"rootPane"` PropertyChangeEvent on first access. The desktop fires that event too — but from the
constructor, where no listener can yet be registered. Firing it later is an *invented* event, which
[D_property_fanout_audit](#D_property_fanout_audit) and R_no_silent_improvements rule out, and the
alternative — building the pane eagerly to match — is a lifecycle change this gate is not the right
occasion for.

**One left open.** `AbstractButton`'s `createChangeListener` / `createActionListener` /
`createItemListener` are declined against `setModel`'s existing javadoc, which folds the JDK's
listener rewiring into the declined effect. That reading is worth revisiting: what those factories
produce is a `fireStateChanged` / `fireActionPerformed` / `fireItemStateChanged` bridge attached to the
user's `ButtonModel`, and both the attachment and the fan-out are pure Java —
[R_decline_effect_only](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules) says the *repaint* is the declined effect while state
and notification are owed. Not changed here, because it alters `ButtonModel` semantics for every
button and wants its own slice.

**Validation.** `R12DeadHookTest` (2 — the gate at 0 violations / 10 declined / 19 suppressed over a
call graph asserted 6342-of-6457 reachable, and the triage report, down to 10 unreached protected
names from 12 before chain collapse). `JTextPaneTest` (17, one new: a subclass override of the hook,
seeded and read back through both ctors — the gate proves the wiring structurally, that proves it is
observable) + `JEditorPaneTest` re-run over the kit change.
Full reactor green. Runtime ~13s, almost all of it the `java.desktop` import. The scanners, the
per-refinement measurements and the public tier's residue lived in a scratch notebook that was retired
once the gate was in place; its probe did **not** collapse chains on our side, so its public-tier rows
were the looser count.


---

<a id="D_awt_choice"></a>
## D_awt_choice. `vaadinx.awt.Choice` emulator — the AWT dropdown; R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down over `SChoice`, three JDK call directions run backwards on purpose

`vaadinx.awt.Choice extends vaadinx.awt.Component implements java.awt.ItemSelectable, Accessible` — holds the JDK's item vector and selection itself, rendered by `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SChoice` ([SD_schoice](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_schoice)). **Not** `vaadinx.swing.JComboBox`: this is `java.awt.Choice`, whose whole state is a `Vector<String>` and an `int`. Third widget in the AWT lane after [D_awt_button](#D_awt_button) / [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label); the design pass it was built from: `ideas/awt-choice.md` (graduated into this entry and SD_schoice).

**Decision.**
- **R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** `java.awt.Choice` has no public subclass in `java.awt`, so the protected `(Component peer)` ctor is omitted and the public ctor calls `super(new SChoice())` directly.
- **The emulator owns the state, as the JDK's does.** `pItems` (a `Vector<String>`) and `selectedIndex` are the JDK's fields under its names, and the mutators are its bodies, so no getter reads the peer and a `SwingWorker` reading `getSelectedItem()` needs no UI ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). **The peer is written after the monitor is released, never inside it** — the one departure from the JDK's shape, which pushes to its peer inside `synchronized (this)`. Here a push off the UI thread takes the session lock, and a request thread holding that lock can be waiting on this monitor (`getSelectedItem` is `synchronized`), so a worker filling a shown `Choice` would deadlock against a listener reading it. A structural change therefore flushes a snapshot of the whole list plus the selection through `SChoice.setItemsAndSelection` once the monitor is released (the surrogate rebuilds its whole item list on every change anyway, so the cost is unchanged), and `select(int)` flushes only the selection — unless it runs inside a structural change, whose flush carries it. `select(int)` and `select(String)` lose the JDK's `synchronized` modifier for the same reason: both would otherwise flush under the monitor.
- **Browser → AWT runs the public `select(int)` before posting**, as `XChoicePeer` and `LWChoicePeer` both do, so a migrator's `select(int)` override sees the user's picks. The bridge listens to the surrogate's value change (gated on `isFromClient()`), not to the surrogate's own `ItemListener` fan-out, which stays for stage-3 code.
- **The peer bridge enters at `processEvent`, not `processItemEvent`** — [D_awt_dead_hooks](#D_awt_dead_hooks)'s finding applied at construction rather than as a later fix. AWT routes a peer-posted event `dispatchEvent → processEvent → processItemEvent`; entering at the second hop would leave a migrator's `processEvent` override compiling, looking wired, and never running on a real selection.
- **Three JDK call directions are preserved even though they read backwards** (R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2). `getItemCount()` delegates to `countItems()`, and `add(String)` delegates to `addItem(String)` — in the JDK the *deprecated* member is the implementation and the modern name is the wrapper, so inverting them (the "obvious" reading) would leave a migrator's `countItems()` / `addItem()` override silently dead: the D_r12_provenance failure mode, invisible to both the compiler and the WARN inventory. `select(String)` routes through `this.select(int)` because the JDK calls the public overload, so a subclass override intercepts both. Two *non*-routings are equally deliberate: `add` does not go through `insert`, and `remove(String)` does not go through `remove(int)` — in the JDK both pairs reach a private helper, so neither override intercepts the other.
- **Validation and the selection-adjust rules run here**, in the JDK's bodies, and re-select through the public `select(int)` as the JDK does. `SChoice` keeps its own copy for stage-3 code; `setItemsAndSelection` applies none of it, so the two copies never both act on one change.

**Rationale.** The AWT lane's third slice, and the first with real state: the four selection-adjust quirks (insert at or before the selection re-selects index 0 despite the JDK's own "selection shifted up" comment; remove-selected re-selects 0; remove-below decrements; a non-empty `Choice` always has a selection) are observable and are reproduced verbatim or not at all. The load-bearing divergence from the Swing cousin is that **`select()` fires nothing** — an `ItemEvent` from a `Choice` always means "the user picked something", never "the program changed the selection" — which is exactly what a re-skin of `SJComboBox` would have destroyed.

**Accepted limitations.** `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null. The JDK's `invalidateIfValid()` after each structural change is not reproduced (R_layouts_close_enough).

**Validation.** `vaadinx.awt.ChoiceTest` (22 — a replay of a script measured on the JDK (which public methods each mutation reaches, including the re-selections through `select(int)` on insert and remove, the selection each leaves, the reads through `getItem`, the exception table, no `ItemEvent` throughout), a browser pick running `select(int)` before the listeners, the peer rendering what the emulator holds after every kind of change, the AWT item family under its own names, the R_leaf_peer_lockdown peer type, the three call directions each proven by overriding the callee in a test subclass, the two non-routings, the browser pick reaching a `processEvent` override, the event re-sourced to the emulator, `select` silence, AWT FIFO listener order, a non-`ItemEvent` falling through to `Component`'s routing, the R_match_swing_errors exception table, an AWT Choice inside a Swing `JPanel` in a `JFrame`, the inherited Component surface, `toString`, `addNotify`). `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest.awtChoice` reads every getter on a bare thread without reaching the peer. Sampler `AwtChoicePanel` + `AwtChoiceWarnInventoryTest` (2).

**Browser-verified** (2026-08-21, Firefox) together with SD_schoice — measurements in its entry; the emulator path is what the Sampler demo drives (`vaadinx.awt.Choice` ctor, `add` / `insert` / `remove` / `removeAll`, `select(int)`, and the `ItemListener` re-sourced to the emulator).

<a id="D_awt_checkbox"></a>
## D_awt_checkbox. `vaadinx.awt.Checkbox` + `CheckboxGroup` emulators — one peer, two glyphs, and a veto that lives where the group does

`vaadinx.awt.Checkbox extends vaadinx.awt.Component implements java.awt.ItemSelectable, Accessible` over `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.SCheckbox` ([SD_scheckbox](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_scheckbox)), plus `vaadinx.awt.CheckboxGroup implements Serializable`, which is not a `Component` at all. Fourth widget in the AWT lane after [D_awt_button](#D_awt_button) / [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label) / [D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice), and the first to carry a second ported class with two-way package-private hooks into the first. The design pass it was built from: `ideas/awt-checkbox.md` (graduated into this entry and SD_scheckbox).

**Decision — R_leaf_peer_lockdown applies in full, and the dual rendering does not force a peer seam.** `java.awt.Checkbox` renders as two different widgets depending on runtime state, which reads at first like an R_leaf_peer_lockdown violation and is not one. AWT derives the glyph from `group != null` **at paint time**, and `setCheckboxGroup` can flip it at any point after construction; so the honest model is one peer type with a live property, not two peer types. R_leaf_peer_lockdown holds in its strongest form: no protected `(Component peer)` ctor, `super(new SCheckbox())` from the single root ctor, no dispatch. The three rejected ways out are worth recording, because each is the shape someone will reach for next time a JDK class renders two ways:
- *Ctor-time peer dispatch on the group argument* ([D_jformattedtextfield](#D_jformattedtextfield)'s `FormattedFieldStrategy` shape — and note it is **not** covered by R_leaf_peer_lockdown's framework-selects carve-out, which requires that user code cannot influence the choice; a ctor argument does). It answers the wrong question: `setCheckboxGroup` on a constructed box then either lies or has to swap the peer.
- *Peer replacement inside `setCheckboxGroup`*. `peer` is `protected final`, and bounds, colours, font, enabled state, tooltip, the `ComponentMixin` stores, the Vaadin attachment, `FocusTracker`'s pointer and every `Registration` live on the old one. A swap is a rebuild with a dozen ways to drop state silently.
- *WARN when the glyph would need to change*. Wrong in the way R_match_swing_errors exists to prevent: the group **is** honoured behaviourally, so the WARN would report a failure that did not happen while the real divergence (a glyph) is cosmetic — and WARN noise on a working path breaks the exit gate for no gain.

**Decision — the deselect veto lives here, not on the surrogate.** Two clicks post no event at all, both because the group vetoes the state change: unchecking the box that is its group's current selection, and re-clicking that box (JDK bug 4039594's carve-out in `XCheckboxPeer.action`). `XCheckboxPeer` reads both the glyph and the veto off one `checkBoxGroup != null`, so putting both on the surrogate's `radioLook` flag was the design pass's proposal. Rejected: our surrogate is not AWT's peer — it sits beside the group rather than below it, and D_buttongroup_browser_click keeps `:surrogates` free of group awareness. So the bridge calls `setState(selected)` and compares: if the field did not move, the group vetoed, `setStateInternal` has already bounced the peer back to checked, and we post nothing. One `if`, and it puts the AWT rule in the one class that knows what a group is.

**Decision — `CheckboxGroup` is ported, into `vaadinx.awt`, in `:emulators`.** It is not a `Component`, so D_whitelist_porting's Component-hierarchy half does not reach it — but its entire API traffics in `java.awt.Checkbox`, which we cannot produce, so `setSelectedCheckbox(java.awt.Checkbox)` is unusable from migrated code by construction. Exactly what forced `javax.swing.ButtonGroup` → `vaadinx.swing.ButtonGroup` under [D_buttongroup](#D_buttongroup), with the same irreducible signature divergence (D_buttongroup_cross_package): `getSelectedCheckbox()` returns `vaadinx.awt.Checkbox`. Not `:surrogates`, per D_buttongroup_browser_click — there is nothing Vaadin-shaped for it to be, and a stage-3 user has Vaadin's own `RadioButtonGroup`. The deprecated `getCurrent` / `setCurrent` pair is kept **carrying the implementation**, as in the JDK, so a subclass override of `setCurrent` intercepts `setSelectedCheckbox` (R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2, the same trap D_awt_choice named for `countItems`).

**Decision — `setCurrent`'s asymmetric setter pair is reproduced exactly.** The pointer moves *first*; the outgoing box then goes through the **public** `setState(false)`, which re-enters the group check but finds the pointer already moved so the cannot-deselect veto stays quiet; the incoming box goes through the **package-private** `setStateInternal(true)`, bypassing group logic entirely. A port using the public setter for both directions recurses; one using the internal setter for both leaves a stale selection. `CheckboxGroup`'s own field is `private` where the JDK's is package-private — nothing outside needs it, and a package-private field of that name **shadows the `getSelectedCheckbox`/`setSelectedCheckbox` property pair for same-package Kotlin**, silently routing `group.selectedCheckbox = box` around `setCurrent`. Found by six test failures, not by reading.

**Decision — nothing in either class throws, and resisting the urge is the R_match_swing_errors work.** `java.awt.Checkbox` and `java.awt.CheckboxGroup` have no exception surface beyond the never-firing `HeadlessException` clauses: a null label is stored verbatim, a null listener is a silent no-op, `setState(false)` on a group's selection is silently upgraded to `true`, and a **foreign box handed to `setSelectedCheckbox` is a documented silent no-op** — the one most tempting to promote to `IllegalArgumentException`, and the one migrated code is most likely to rely on. Getting R_match_swing_errors right here means adding no throws at all.

**Rationale.** The load-bearing divergence from the Swing cousins is that **only the browser posts `ItemEvent`s**. `setState`, every ctor, `setCheckboxGroup` and every `CheckboxGroup` mutator are silent; a browser toggle posts exactly one event, on the clicked box, and the sibling a group cascade turns off gets nothing — where Swing's `ButtonGroup` (and our D_buttongroup port of it) *does* fire `DESELECTED` on the outgoing button. Three field shadows carry it: `label` (AWT returns it verbatim, null included, and it is also the `ItemEvent`'s `item` payload and `getSelectedObjects()`'s single element), `state` (the AWT-side truth the group's re-selection dance reads), and `group`. `paramString` omits the label clause when null — unlike `Button.paramString`, which appends it always.

**Accepted limitations.** `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null. The radio glyph is a CSS approximation on a `vaadin-checkbox`; if a future theme supports neither knob SD_scheckbox uses, a grouped box keeps the checkmark glyph with mutual exclusion unaffected — visual only, R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c), and deliberately **no WARN**, since nothing failed.

**Validation.** `vaadinx.awt.CheckboxTest` (34 — the ctor chain and both three-arg orders, two boxes constructed checked into one group, the null-label field shadow, the veto and the silent-`setState` rule in and out of a group, the browser toggle re-sourced to the emulator with a null `item` where AWT has one, one SELECTED and nothing on the sibling, the vetoed re-click bouncing the peer back, the R_no_vaadin_in_api-limb-2 guard that a browser toggle reaches a `processEvent` override, AWT FIFO listener order, `getSelectedObjects()` including the `Object[]{null}` case, `setCheckboxGroup` install / re-home / same-group / null with the glyph flip reaching the peer, the R_leaf_peer_lockdown peer type through a plain instance and a subclass, an AWT Checkbox inside a Swing `JPanel` in a `JFrame`, `paramString`, `addNotify`). `vaadinx.awt.CheckboxGroupTest` (10 — the cascade firing nothing, the foreign-box and ungrouped-box no-ops, `null` clearing, the deprecated pair proven to carry the implementation by overriding it, and the asymmetric setter pair asserted directly). Sampler `AwtCheckboxPanel` + `AwtCheckboxWarnInventoryTest` (2).

**Browser-verified** (2026-08-24, Firefox, Sampler `AWT › Checkbox`); the glyph half is measured in [SD_scheckbox](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_scheckbox). What the emulator path proves that Karibu cannot: clicking `imperial` turns `metric` off in the DOM and logs one SELECTED line with no partner; `setSelectedCheckbox(nautical)` moves the selection and repaints both peers while the ItemEvent readout stays *stale* at `imperial` — programmatic silence end-to-end, not merely under Karibu; re-clicking the selected `nautical` leaves the readout stale **and** bounces the peer back to checked, which is the veto's server→browser push actually reaching the DOM; `setCheckboxGroup` flips the fourth box from a square checkbox to a round radio live; and Demo 6's `setState(!state)` unchecks the box and flips `getSelectedObjects()` to null with the event readout unchanged. No `onUnimplemented` WARN in the server log across the route.

<a id="D_awt_panel"></a>
## D_awt_panel. `vaadinx.awt.Panel` emulator — four lines over `Container`, and the case for it staying four lines

`vaadinx.awt.Panel extends vaadinx.awt.Container implements Accessible` — AWT's generic on-screen container, peered on the plain Vaadin `Div` that `Container`'s no-arg ctor already creates. Fifth widget in the AWT lane after [D_awt_button](#D_awt_button) / [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label) / [D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice) / [D_awt_checkbox](#D_awt_checkbox), and the first that is a `Container` rather than a leaf. The design pass it was built from: `ideas/awt-panel.md` (graduated into this entry and [SD_no_spanel](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_no_spanel)).

**Decision — the class is four members, and the design work was refusing to add a fifth.** `javap java.awt.Panel` is two ctors, `addNotify()` and `getAccessibleContext()`; `src.zip` shows the whole implementation is `this(new FlowLayout())`, `setLayout(layout)`, and an `addNotify` that allocates the native peer. Everything a migrator touches — all five `add` overloads, `remove` / `removeAll`, `setLayout` / `getLayout`, `getComponent(int)` / `getComponents()` / `getComponentCount()`, `getInsets`, `validate` / `doLayout` / `invalidate`, `isAncestorOf`, Z-order, `ContainerListener` — is inherited `vaadinx.awt.Container`, which already ships concretely: `JRootPane`, `JFrame`, `JDialog`, `JWindow` and `JInternalFrame` all use a bare `Container` as their content pane. So `java.awt.Panel` contributes a default layout manager and an accessibility role, and nothing else. Note this makes Panel **not** the AWT lane's first `Container` in the tree — `vaadinx.awt.Window` (and `Frame` / `Dialog` / `FileDialog` under it) got there first as `JFrame`'s bases; Panel is the first *general-purpose* one.

**Decision — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, expressed as `super()` rather than the lane's `super(new SXxx())`.** `java.applet.Applet` is `java.awt.Panel`'s only JDK subclass (`ScrollPane` and `Window` extend `Container` directly), and applets are permanently out of scope per R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (b) — with the JDK classes **removed in Java 26 per [JEP 504](https://openjdk.org/jeps/504)**, so unlike `javax.swing.plaf` (which still exists and is merely ignored) this subclass cannot return as future non-leaf pressure. R_leaf_peer_lockdown therefore applies in full: no protected `(Component peer)` ctor, both public ctors funnel through `super()`, and every instance — through any ctor or any user-code subclass — peers over a `Div` with no type-system seam to swap it. The spelling differs from the lane's three predecessors because there is no surrogate to name; writing `super(new Div())` would be equivalent but reads as a peer choice being made *here* rather than inherited from `Container`'s documented default. A user-code subclass for *behaviour* (`class ToolbarPanel extends Panel`, the commonest AWT-era idiom there is) inherits the locked peer and works; one for *custom rendering* is out of scope per R_match_swing_errors (b) regardless.

**Decision — the `<div>` peer is a hard gate, not a preference.** `LayoutCss.applyContainerCss` refuses to write layout CSS when the target's tag is not `div`, logging `onUnsupportedPeerShape` instead. Every rejected alternative fails on that gate or on seeded CSS: `SJPanel` as the peer (the `JTextPane`-over-`SJEditorPane` shape of [D_jtextpane](#D_jtextpane)) puts a `JComponent`-level peer under an AWT-level emulator *and* its ctor eagerly writes `java.awt.FlowLayout` CSS the emulator's own `FlowLayout` then overwrites; Vaadin `FlexLayout` passes the tag gate but seeds `display: flex` that a `BorderLayout`'s `display: grid` must then fight; `VerticalLayout` / `Scroller` / any Vaadin-namespaced component fails the gate outright and silently ignores its `LayoutManager`.

**Decision — `Panel(null)` installs no manager, and `setLayout` is called virtually from the ctor.** The JDK stores a null layout verbatim and `getLayout()` returns null (probe-verified); substituting a `FlowLayout` would silently change how migrated `Panel(null)` code lays out, so we don't. And `Panel(LayoutManager)` calls `setLayout` virtually exactly as the JDK's does, so a user override runs during construction and sees its own fields uninitialized — the footgun is inherited along with the shape, the same stance [D_r12_provenance](#D_r12_provenance) took for `createDefaultModel`. The R_no_vaadin_in_api limb-2 guard is a test that asserts the ctor's `setLayout` call actually reaches an override.

**Decision — `peerContentElement()` is left un-overridden, and the seam's real precedent is recorded here.** Children land in the peer `Div` itself, which is also where the layout CSS lands — that co-location is the property that matters, and it is now browser-verified rather than assumed. Worth recording for the *next* AWT container: **nothing in the tree overrides `peerContentElement()`.** Its own javadoc names `JFrame` as the motivating case and `JFrame` does not do it (`SJPanel` is itself a `Div`, so the default serves). `JScrollPane` is the one class that hit the problem for real — its peer is `SJScrollPane extends Scroller`, tag `vaadin-scroller`, so `applyContainerCss` refuses every write — and it **declined the seam**, instead bypassing `addImpl` via `Scroller.setContent` (SD_sjscrollpane's one-content-slot), overriding `setLayout` to store-only, and overriding `validateTree` because the view never enters `components`. `java.awt.ScrollPane` cannot copy that verbatim: its single child arrives through the public `add()`, both `setLayout` (which throws `AWTError("ScrollPane controls layout")`) and `addImpl` are `final`, and a *lightweight* child gets wrapped in `new Panel()` with a `BorderLayout` by `addToPanel` — so **`java.awt.Panel` is a dependency of `java.awt.ScrollPane`'s own implementation**, which settles the lane's ordering and hands the wrapper Div back for free. That fork (intercept `addImpl` vs override `peerContentElement`) belongs to `ScrollPane`'s own pass, not here.

**Decision — the auto-generated name stays dropped.** `new java.awt.Panel().getName()` is `"panel0"`; `vaadinx.awt.Component.getName()` deliberately skips AWT's auto-naming hierarchy-wide. Adding it means a static counter per class plus a `constructComponentName()` override, which would also resurrect a hook [D_r12_mechanized](#D_r12_mechanized)'s limb-2 probe would then have to classify — for a value the design pass found no reader of. Decided no, not left open.

**Rationale.** `Panel` is the most likely AWT residue in a real Swing app after `Label` — an AWT-era view is `Panel`s all the way down — so it is plausibly the highest value-per-line item in the whole family, and the Sampler demo is where that value sits. Two pre-existing blockers the design pass flagged were already closed by [D_awt_dead_hooks](#D_awt_dead_hooks) and did not need re-doing here: the `paramString` chain is live (so `Container.paramString`'s `,layout=` tail is observable through `toString`), and `addImpl`'s `checkNotAWindow` / self-add message / guard order / throw-not-clamp divergences are fixed. What the slice *did* need was one `Container`-level fix, landed separately: `setLayout` now drops the outgoing manager's container CSS, because AWT's "no layout until `revalidate()`" quirk is faithfully kept but a browser makes the un-revalidated interval *visible* — stale `display:flex` over children already carrying the incoming `BorderLayout`'s `grid-area` renders scrambled, where a cleared container renders a coherent block flow.

**Accepted limitations.** `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null (R_match_swing_errors (b)). Inherited and unchanged from `Container`: pixel hit-testing (`getComponentAt` ×2 / `locate` / `findComponentAt` ×2, `getMousePosition`), the five focus-traversal setters (tier-3 focus permanently out per [D_focus_managers](#D_focus_managers)), cross-container `setComponentZOrder`, a hand-rolled pixel `LayoutManager`'s WARN + vertical-stack fallback ([M1D_custom_layoutmanager](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_custom_layoutmanager)), `getPreferredSize` reporting the manager's dummy `1×1` (no synchronous child measurement in a browser), and `FlowLayout.setAlignOnBaseline` as a field-only round-trip. `ContainerListener` is the one place this layer is *more* capable than the surrogate layer, which `onNoop`s it under SD_listeners_without_analog.

**Validation.** `vaadinx.awt.PanelTest` (16 — the default `FlowLayout` and the un-substituted null layout, the ctor's virtual `setLayout` proven by overriding it, the R_leaf_peer_lockdown peer type through a plain instance and a subclass, child/CSS co-location, default-FlowLayout CSS landing on attach and *not* landing for `Panel(null)`, `BorderLayout` region assignment, `ContainerListener` add/remove with the container in its post-mutation state, an all-AWT subtree with no `JComponent` in its chain, an AWT Panel inside a Swing `JPanel` in a `JFrame`, fresh-instance zero `Insets`, `toString`'s `layout=` tail, `addNotify` reaching an override and laying the subtree out, and a WARN-free happy path). Sampler `AwtPanelPanel` (3 demos) + `AwtPanelWarnInventoryTest` (2). The API-surface bucket is **deliberately not claimed exhaustive** — Panel's own four members are trivial, but the surface a migrator uses is all of `Container`, a documented chunk of which legitimately WARNs; the exclusions are listed on the method.

**Browser-verified** (2026-08-24, Chromium, Sampler `AWT › Panel`). Five measurements, chosen because a server-side assertion structurally cannot make them — it reads style off `peerContentElement()` whether or not that is the element the children are in, and Karibu never computes layout, resolves shadow DOM, or applies the theme:
- **Co-location**: on all five Panels in the route, every child's `parentElement` *is* the element carrying the computed layout CSS. This closes the "right tag, wrong div" hole the `<div>` gate cannot see, and since Panel is the simplest possible container the result retro-validates the mechanism for every other one.
- **The default `FlowLayout` really wraps**: six AWT Buttons on one row at 596px, **4 + 2 across two rows at 263px** (child `top` 71 → 104), `justify-content: center`, `gap: 5px`. Wrapping is invisible to a CSS-string assertion.
- **`BorderLayout` regions are structurally right**: NORTH / CENTER / SOUTH strictly ordered (`top` 69 / 88 / 107), NORTH and SOUTH the full 596px, CENTER 580px inside the 8px gaps.
- **CENTER absorbs the slack**: rows compute `15px 15px 15px` at natural height (53px = 45 content + 8 gap, i.e. *no slack exists*) and `15px 162px 15px` when handed 147px — NORTH and SOUTH holding at 15px. This is the half of R_layouts_close_enough that is promised rather than deferred, and it needed forcing: at natural height the claim is untestable.
- **`Panel(null)` vs `new Panel()`**: computed `display: block` versus `flex`, making the slice's one functional difference from `Container` observable.
- **`ContainerListener` on live add/remove**: add ×2 then remove leaves one child in the DOM and reads `componentRemoved(btn 2) — getComponentCount() = 1`.

No `onUnimplemented` / `onUnsupportedPeerShape` in the server log across the route.

<a id="D_awt_scrollbar"></a>
## D_awt_scrollbar. `vaadinx.awt.Scrollbar` emulator — a value model whose JDK call graph runs backwards, and an event source the peer cannot be

`vaadinx.awt.Scrollbar extends vaadinx.awt.Component implements java.awt.Adjustable, Accessible` — the AWT 1.0 scrollbar, holding the JDK's value model itself and rendered by [SD_sscrollbar](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sscrollbar)'s `SScrollbar`. Sixth widget in the AWT lane after [D_awt_button](#D_awt_button) / [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label) / [D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice) / [D_awt_checkbox](#D_awt_checkbox) / [D_awt_panel](#D_awt_panel), and the first that carries a value model. The design pass it was built from was `ideas/awt-scrollbar.md`, graduated into this entry and SD_sscrollbar.

**Decision — it is a value control, and that is why it gets a real peer.** AWT's scroll pane does not use this class (`ScrollPane` hands out the `final` `java.awt.ScrollPaneAdjustable`), so a `Scrollbar` exists only because migrated code constructed one — and AWT 1.0 having no slider means that code is using it as a zoom / volume / colour knob. Hence a rendering peer rather than `vaadinx.swing.JScrollBar`'s inert `Div`; the full argument, the peer choice, and the `writing-mode`-over-`transform` measurements are in SD_sscrollbar.

**Decision — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** Nothing in `java.awt` extends `Scrollbar` (`javax.swing.JScrollBar` descends from `JComponent`; `ScrollPaneAdjustable` is `final` and merely implements `Adjustable`), so there is no protected `(Component peer)` ctor and all three public ctors funnel into `super(new SScrollbar(orientation))`, then seed the model through this class's own `setValues`, as the JDK's constructor does — so a subclass's `setValues` override runs from the constructor. Both orientations ride one peer type, so unlike [D_frame_strategy](#D_jframe_as_route) there is no peer dispatch. The illegal-orientation `IllegalArgumentException` (`"illegal scrollbar orientation"`, AWT's own message) is thrown inside the surrogate ctor, so it comes out of `super(...)` and leaves no half-built `Scrollbar` — SD_slabel's shape.

**Decision — the emulator owns the state, under the JDK's field names.** `value`, `minimum`, `maximum`, `visibleAmount`, `orientation`, `lineIncrement`, `pageIncrement` and `isAdjusting` are fields here, the mutators are the JDK's bodies over them, and no getter reads the peer, so a `SwingWorker` reading `getValue()` needs no UI ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). Every write flushes the *current* fields on to the surrogate, read inside the push rather than passed as the call's arguments, so the monitor the JDK holds around the field writes is not held while a push off the UI thread takes the session lock, and two racing writers still leave the peer on the last state. The clamped value still has one source of truth: the emulator is it, and the surrogate's own copy of the funnel receives values already clamped and passes them through. Replacing the delegation removed two divergences the old shape hid, both measured on the JDK: the constructor did not run an overriding `setValues`, and the single setters passed getters rather than fields, so an overridden `getMinimum()` sat on `setValue`'s path.

**Decision — R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2 is the substantive work, and the JDK's call graph runs backwards.** Four funnels an independently-written emulator would silently break:
1. **`setValue` / `setMinimum` / `setMaximum` / `setVisibleAmount` each call this class's own `setValues`,** which clamps, stores and pushes. `setValues` is the JDK's single funnel and the natural override point for a migrator tightening clamping; four independent setters would compile against that override and never invoke it. `setMaximum` additionally runs AWT's two pre-steps (`MIN_VALUE` nudged up; a `minimum` that would meet or pass the new maximum rewritten first) **here** rather than on the peer, because delegating to the surrogate's own `setMaximum` skips this funnel — a defect the R_no_vaadin_in_api test caught during implementation, not a hypothetical. The rewritten `minimum` goes straight into the field, as in the JDK, so it holds even past a `setValues` override that does not call super.
2. **The deprecated AWT-1.0 names are the real implementations**: `setUnitIncrement` → `setLineIncrement`, `getUnitIncrement` → `getLineIncrement`, `setBlockIncrement` → `setPageIncrement`, `getBlockIncrement` → `getPageIncrement`, `getVisibleAmount` → `getVisible`. Backwards from every other deprecated pair in the tree, and exactly [D_r12_provenance](#D_r12_provenance)'s shape: implementing them the other way round leaves a migrator's `setLineIncrement` override compiling, looking wired, and never running.
3. **`processEvent` peels `AdjustmentEvent` off before `super.processEvent`, and `processAdjustmentEvent` is the single dispatch funnel** both the peer bridge and a user-code `processEvent` reach the listeners through. The bridge enters at `processEvent`, per [D_awt_dead_hooks](#D_awt_dead_hooks)'s finding. Null is a no-op (the JDK calls it "unspecified"; D_awt_button settled no-op).
4. **`getAdjustmentListeners()` routes through `getListeners(AdjustmentListener.class)`**, as the JDK does. No `getListeners` override is needed — `vaadinx.awt.Component.getListeners` is already type-keyed over the shared `listenerList`, so the JDK's `AdjustmentListener` special case is that method's general case (the call D_awt_button made for `ActionListener`).

**Decision — the bridge re-sources the event, and needs two hooks rather than one.** The value hook subscribes to the surrogate's `addValueChangeListener` and, inside `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope), does what the JDK's Windows peer does for a drag step (`WScrollbarPeer.postAdjustmentEvent`): `setValueIsAdjusting(adjusting)`, `setValue(value)`, then post `new AdjustmentEvent(this, ADJUSTMENT_VALUE_CHANGED, TRACK, value, isAdjusting)`, so a migrator's `setValue` override sees the user's traffic. (The platforms disagree: the lightweight macOS peer does the same, X11's calls only `setValue`, so `getValueIsAdjusting()` never goes true there. Windows' is the only one with a drag end, which is why it is the one ported.) The event is sourced at `this`, so `(Scrollbar) e.getAdjustable()` sees the emulator, the same re-sourcing `vaadinx.awt.Button` does for `ActionEvent`, and necessary because the surrogate cannot legally be an `Adjustable` at all (SD_sscrollbar). The **second** hook is a raw DOM `change` listener that fires the non-adjusting event, as `WScrollbarPeer.dragEnd`: `setValueIsAdjusting(false)` and post, with no `setValue`. The browser's `change` carries no new value, so it produces no Vaadin value-change event for the first hook to ride, and without it the "commit when `getValueIsAdjusting()` goes false" idiom — the property's entire purpose — would never fire. The design pass assumed one hook; the two-event cost it predicted only materializes with two. **No `preventPeerEvents` flag is needed:** AWT fires nothing for a programmatic write, which is exactly the `!isFromClient()` case, so there is no echo to suppress (the `SCheckbox` precedent, and the inverse of `vaadinx.swing.JScrollBar`, whose `BoundedRangeModel` fires on every write).

**Decision — R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 1.** `getOrientation()` returns `int`, never `RangeInput.Orientation`; `getAdjustmentListeners()` returns the JDK array; the Vaadin enum stays behind the private `surrogate()` accessor. The int-named accessors the surrogate exposes (`getIntValue` / `getAwtOrientation`) exist precisely so the JDK spellings stay free on this class.

**Accepted limitations.** `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null (R_match_swing_errors (b)). The four R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c) items are the surrogate's and listed in SD_sscrollbar: `visibleAmount` as thumb length, `blockIncrement`, `TRACK`-always, advisory `setValueIsAdjusting` — plus `unitIncrement` being stored-and-inert because `step` stays 1, and arrow keys reading backwards on a min-at-top vertical bar. `getListeners(String.class)` returns an empty array where AWT throws `ClassCastException`, and `getListeners(null)` returns null where AWT NPEs — pre-existing at `Component`, deliberately defensive there, not this slice's to change. The `throws HeadlessException` clauses are kept for signature fidelity and never thrown (the `vaadinx.awt.Frame` / D_awt_button / D_awt_label precedent).

**Validation.** `vaadinx.awt.ScrollbarTest` (30 — a replay of a script measured on the JDK (clamping at the int extremes, the constructor running an overriding `setValues`, setters passing fields rather than getters, `setMaximum`'s pre-step, the increment aliases, silence on every programmatic write), a browser drag running `setValueIsAdjusting` + `setValue` before the post and a drag end running only the former, the three ctors, the constants agreeing with `Adjustable`'s *and* `SwingConstants`' (no collision here, the inverse of SD_slabel's `Label` trap), R_leaf_peer_lockdown peer type, band clamping, all four R_no_vaadin_in_api funnels proven by overriding the funnel and counting calls, `TRACK` + emulator-sourced `getAdjustable()` on a from-client change, programmatic writes firing **nothing** across all five mutators, the drag-end non-adjusting event, `processEvent` → `processAdjustmentEvent` → listener hop order, null-tolerant listener add/remove/dispatch, registration-order `getAdjustmentListeners`, an AWT leaf with no `JComponent` in its chain inside a Swing hierarchy, `paramString`'s exact tail, and a WARN-free happy path). `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest.awtScrollbar` reads every getter on a bare thread without reaching the peer. Sampler `AwtScrollbarPanel` (3 demos) + `AwtScrollbarWarnInventoryTest` (2 buckets, both zero) — the API-surface bucket is exhaustive over the class minus `getAccessibleContext`, and drives both increments through *both* name pairs so the alias funnels are on the asserted path.

**Browser-verified** (2026-08-24, Chromium 151, Sampler `AWT › Scrollbar`). Four measurements a server-side assertion structurally cannot make, plus one defect it structurally could not catch:
- **Vertical renders vertical, with the right layout box**: the `BorderLayout.EAST` bar computes **20×156** with `writing-mode: vertical-lr` and `transform: none`, inside a **420px-wide** region — i.e. it does not claim a horizontal control's width. This is the measurement the whole peer choice rested on, now taken through Vaadin's own CSS rather than on a bare page.
- **Minimum is at the top**: at `value=0` the thumb renders at the *top* of the track, matching AWT (a slider's convention is the opposite, and `direction: rtl` is what would flip it).
- **The band reaches the DOM**: `max="245"` for a 0–255 bar with `visibleAmount=10`, `max="90"` for 0–100 — SD_sscrollbar's `maximum - visibleAmount` storage, observable.
- **`step="1"` on all three bars**, so the whole band stays reachable (the decision measured in SD_sscrollbar).
- **The event chain, end to end**: a synthesized drag (two `input`s then `change`) produced `getValue()=200, getAdjustmentType()=TRACK, getValueIsAdjusting()=false, getAdjustable() is the Scrollbar=true` and tinted the `java.awt.Label` swatch to `rgb(200,200,200)` — the re-sourcing, the `TRACK`-always rule, and the second DOM hook's drag-end event all confirmed live.

**The defect the browser caught, and the tests could not.** A value of 0 equals `RangeInput`'s own initial value, so Vaadin's `setValue` writes no property at all — and an `<input type=range>` carrying no value renders its thumb at the **midpoint of its range**. A fresh `new Scrollbar()` (value 0, AWT's default, on a 0–90 band) therefore rendered at 45 while the server correctly said 0. Karibu reads the server-side value and sees nothing wrong; only a real browser shows the thumb. `SScrollbar.setValues` now writes the element property explicitly after `setValue`, with a regression test asserting the DOM property is present for a zero value. Worth generalizing: **any surrogate whose peer has a meaningful "no value set" rendering needs its initial value forced onto the element**, because the server-side round-trip passes either way.

No `onUnimplemented` / `onUnsupportedPeerShape` in the server log across the route.

<a id="D_awt_list"></a>
## D_awt_list. `vaadinx.awt.List` emulator — nine JDK call directions that run backwards, and two shadows the peer cannot answer

`vaadinx.awt.List extends vaadinx.awt.Component implements java.awt.ItemSelectable, Accessible` — the AWT 1.0 scrolling list box, holding the JDK's items and selection itself and rendered by [SD_slist](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_slist)'s `SList`. Seventh widget in the AWT lane after [D_awt_button](#D_awt_button) / [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label) / [D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice) / [D_awt_checkbox](#D_awt_checkbox) / [D_awt_panel](#D_awt_panel) / [D_awt_scrollbar](#D_awt_scrollbar), and the largest of them: 47 public methods and two event types. The design pass it was built from was `ideas/awt-list.md`, graduated into this entry and SD_slist and deleted.

**Decision — the modern→deprecated delegation runs the JDK's way, in nine places.** D_awt_choice found three on `Choice`; `List` is where the pattern is at its worst. `getItemCount()` → `countItems()`; `add(String)` → `addItem(String)` → `addItem(String,int)` (*the* insert body); `removeAll()` → `clear()` (*the* clear body); `remove(int)` → `delItem(int)` → `delItems(int,int)` (*the* delete body); `isIndexSelected` → `isSelected`; `isMultipleMode` → `allowsMultipleSelections`; `setMultipleMode` → `setMultipleSelections` (which holds the `if (b != multipleMode)` guard); `getPreferredSize()` → `preferredSize()` → `preferredSize(int)`, and the same for `minimumSize`. Wiring any of them the intuitive way round leaves a migrator's override of the deprecated name silently dead — **R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2's exact failure mode**, and the one thing no WARN inventory can catch, since both directions compile. `ListTest` drives one name and asserts the other's effect, plus a subclass whose four deprecated overrides must all be reached from modern calls.

**Decision — `getSelectedItems()` is composed, not delegated.** The JDK's body loops `getItem(sel[i])` over `getSelectedIndexes()`, both public. Reading the peer's own array instead would be simpler and would take two overridable methods off the invoked path, so the composition is kept and pinned by a test that counts `getItem` calls. Same reasoning puts `isSelected(int)` on `getSelectedIndexes()` and `paramString()` on `getSelectedItem()`.

**Decision — the size chain must not call `super.preferredSize()`.** The JDK's `List.preferredSize()` is `(rows > 0) ? preferredSize(rows) : super.preferredSize()`, and `java.awt.Component.preferredSize()` reads a field. **Ours delegates the other way** — `vaadinx.awt.Component.preferredSize()` calls `getPreferredSize()` — so writing the JDK's line verbatim would recurse: `List.getPreferredSize()` → `List.preferredSize()` → `Component.preferredSize()` → virtual dispatch back to `List.getPreferredSize()`. The emulator calls `super.getPreferredSize()` instead, preserving the observable behaviour and the `rows > 0` guard. **The guard is not cosmetic:** `new List(-3)` is legal (quirk of the JDK's `(rows != 0) ? rows : 4` substitution, which validates nothing), so the branch that skips the `(int)` form is reachable and is tested. Generalizes to any emulator whose JDK counterpart chains through a deprecated alias our `Component` chains in the opposite direction.

**Decision — the emulator owns the state, under the JDK's field names.** `items`, `selected`, `multipleMode`, `rows` and `visibleIndex` are fields here and the mutators are the JDK's bodies, so no getter reads the peer ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). `rows` and `visibleIndex` could never have been read back anyway: SD_slist floors the emitted `size` at 2, so `new List(1).getRows()` needs the field (negatives survive verbatim too), and scrolling has no read-back, so an out-of-range `makeVisible` is recorded as AWT records it.

**Decision — the selection follows the JDK's two rule sets, chosen by `isDisplayable()`.** The JDK keeps a list's selection in two places: in its own `selected` array while the list has no peer, and in the platform peer once it is displayable, and the two follow different rules. Measured on JDK 25 by one script run twice, peerless and after `addNotify` on a real frame under Xvfb (both replayed verbatim by `ListTest`): **peerless**, `select` appends to the array, an insert or remove leaves the stored indexes alone (so they may name other rows, or none), a multiple-mode selection keeps insertion order, and a multi → single flip keeps every entry; **displayed**, the selection shifts with inserts and removes, stays sorted in multiple mode, drops a removed row, and a multi → single flip keeps only the row with the location cursor. Both run here over the one `selected` field, which is exactly what the JDK's own hand-over amounts to: the peer seeds itself from `selected` at `addNotify` and is copied back into it at `removeNotify`. The displayed rules are **`XListPeer`'s** (`selectItem` / `deselectItem` / `delItems` / `addItem` / `setMultipleSelections`, plus its `focusIndex`, which a programmatic `select` and a user's click both move, and which `addNotify` seeds on the last selected row). The platforms differ in detail — the Windows peer is a native list box — and X11's is the one whose source and behaviour were both read here. Both branches store an out-of-range `select`, so `getSelectedIndex()` can answer a row that does not exist; the JDK documents that as unspecified and the measured JDK does it. The browser → AWT bridge applies each row the surrogate reports by the peer's rules, as `XListPeer` updates its own state before posting, and moves the location cursor.

**Decision — the peer is written after the monitor is released.** The JDK pushes to its peer inside `synchronized (this)`; here a push off the UI thread takes the session lock, and a request thread holding that lock may be waiting on this monitor, so a worker filling a shown `List` would deadlock against a listener reading it. Each mutator runs its body under the monitor and the outermost one then flushes the current state through `SList.setItemsAndSelection` / `setSelectedIndexes`. That also covers the JDK's nesting (`replaceItem` → `remove` + `add`, `remove(String)` → `remove(int)`), which flushes once, and it flushes after a body that threw part-way, since `delItems(-1, …)` removes rows and then throws. The `synchronized` modifiers on the mutators go for the same reason; the getters keep theirs. The surrogate diffs the list by common prefix and suffix, so filling a long list one `add` at a time touches one `<option>` per call (SD_slist).

**Decision — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down.** No public class in `java.awt` extends `List` (`javax.swing.JList` descends from `JComponent`; `java.awt.peer.ListPeer` is not in the public hierarchy and L&F dispatch is out per R_match_swing_errors (b)), so there is no protected `(Component peer)` ctor and all three public ctors funnel into `super(new SList(...))`. The `rows != 0 ? rows : DEFAULT_VISIBLE_ROWS` substitution happens *before* the peer is built, so a half-built `List` with the wrong row count is never observable — D_awt_label's shape.

**Decision — the peer bridge enters at `processEvent`.** Both bridges re-source the surrogate's event to `this` and re-enter `EHelper.callSwing` (R_callswing_envelope; nested calls run inline per D_callswing_loom), then call `processEvent` — not `processItemEvent` / `processActionEvent`. AWT routes a peer-posted event `dispatchEvent` → `processEvent` → `process*Event`, and skipping the first hop is precisely the defect [D_awt_dead_hooks](#D_awt_dead_hooks) swept out of this lane. `processEvent` peels `ItemEvent` first, then `ActionEvent`, then delegates — the JDK's order, and a test asserts all four hops in sequence.

**The one hook knowingly left dead.** In the JDK, `getItemListeners()` *is* `return getListeners(ItemListener.class)`, and `getActionListeners()` likewise. Ours route to `Component.awtListeners(...)` instead, so a migrator's override of `getListeners(Class)` is not on the invoked path. This matches `Button`, `Choice` and `Checkbox` — the deviation is **lane-wide and deliberate**, since the surrogate cannot carry `getListeners` at all (SD_sbutton's erasure clash) and diverging here would leave one of four AWT widgets wired differently for nothing. Recorded rather than left implicit: an unnamed dead hook is how this lane earned D_awt_dead_hooks. If it is ever fixed, fix all four.

**Accepted limitations.** All of SD_slist's, which are where the substance is. Emulator-side additions: `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null (R_match_swing_errors (b)); the eight size forms answer from `Component`'s own dimension rather than font metrics, routed there instead of an `onUnimplemented` so a plain `new List(5)` keeps the exit gate clean (R_layouts_close_enough cosmetic); `removeNotify()` has nothing to snapshot, since the JDK's job there is to save the selection off a peer that is about to vanish and ours is eternal — the override is kept and calls super, per the standing keep-the-override rule.

**Faithful oddities reproduced rather than smoothed.** `delItems(-1, 2)` removes indices 2, 1, 0 and *then* throws, leaving the list three shorter — the JDK's loop runs downwards, and only a negative `start` reaches that state (an end-too-high range throws with nothing removed). `getSelectedIndex()` is `-1` whenever the count is not exactly one, so two selected rows report `-1` and `getSelectedItem()` reports null. `replaceItem` is literally `remove(index); add(newValue, index)`, so on a displayed list the replaced row loses its selection (a peerless one keeps the index, as it keeps every index). `getSelectedObjects()` returns an **empty array** where `Choice`'s and `Checkbox`'s return null. And `list.add(null)` is ambiguous at the call site against `Component.add(PopupMenu)` — on real `java.awt.List` too, so the cast a migrator needs is not something we introduced.

**Validation.** `ListTest` (28 — adding both replays of the measured JDK script, peerless and displayed, a browser click moving the model and the location cursor, and the peer rendering what the emulator holds) and `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest.awtList`, plus `AwtListWarnInventoryTest`'s two buckets. The Sampler pane's user path asserts the thing most likely to regress silently: it captures Demo 1's `ItemEvent` readout, clicks the `select(2)` button, and fails if the readout **moved** — so a regression that starts firing on programmatic selects breaks the build instead of passing quietly.

**Browser-verified 2026-08-25** (Firefox 153 against a running Sampler), which closed the last open risk. All three panes render as real list boxes (`size=5`/`4`/`4`, first `<option>` laid out at 23px inside a 121px/98px control). `addEventData`'s joined-index expression **round-trips**: picking "Earth" produced `ItemEvent: getItem() = 2 (Integer), stateChange=SELECTED`, and a two-row ctrl-select produced `getSelectedItems() = [Anchovy, Caper]` with `getSelectedIndex() = -1`. `dblclick` and the Enter `keydown` both reach the server (`getActionCommand() = Mars`, then `= Earth`), and a non-Enter key is filtered out client-side as intended. `makeVisible(4)` scrolled the element from 22 to 68 of a 69px range. The duplicate-item claim holds end to end: with the two "Apple" rows selected, the server reported `[Apple, Apple]`, and inserting at index 0 shifted the DOM selection {0,1}→{1,2} with the server still reading both. The mode flip left `multiple=false`, DOM selection `[0]`, and `getSelectedIndex() = 0`. Both coercions are visible on the page (an empty `<option>` from `add(null, 99)`, "New"→"Banana" from `replaceItem`). No `onUnimplemented` / `onUnsupportedPeerShape` / exception in the server log across the whole route. So the `@ClientCallable` shim is not needed and the `Grid<Integer>` abort path is not taken.

**The defects the browser caught, and the tests could not.** Two initial-render disagreements between the server and the DOM, both invisible to the whole green suite: the browser auto-selected row 0 on every fresh render (single-select HTML requires one selected option, and `multiple` was written as a *property*, landing after the `<option>` children), and Demo 3's readout was wired to its buttons but not to an `ItemListener`, so a browser selection left it displaying stale text. Diagnosis, both fixes and the three generalizations are in SD_slist — the short version is that a peer property the browser acts on *while children are inserted* must be an attribute, and a Sampler readout with two update paths must be asserted after the **browser** one.

<a id="D_awt_scrollpane"></a>
## D_awt_scrollpane. `vaadinx.awt.ScrollPane` + `ScrollPaneAdjustable` emulators — a value model that refuses to clamp, and a JDK fork deliberately not taken

`vaadinx.awt.ScrollPane extends vaadinx.awt.Container implements Accessible`, over [SD_sscrollpane](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sscrollpane)'s `SScrollPane`; plus `vaadinx.awt.ScrollPaneAdjustable`, emulator-only. Eighth widget in the AWT lane after [D_awt_button](#D_awt_button) / [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label) / [D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice) / [D_awt_checkbox](#D_awt_checkbox) / [D_awt_panel](#D_awt_panel) / [D_awt_scrollbar](#D_awt_scrollbar) / [D_awt_list](#D_awt_list), and the first whose design question was a channel rather than a widget.

**Decision — `ScrollPaneAdjustable` is ported rather than JDK-reused, and this is forced.** `java.awt.ScrollPaneAdjustable` is `public final` with a **package-private constructor**: we can neither instantiate it nor subclass it. The only alternatives are "port" or "return some other `Adjustable`", and the second breaks the migrator whose code says `((ScrollPaneAdjustable) pane.getVAdjustable()).getUnitIncrement()` — a cast that compiles today and would `ClassCastException` after the import swap. It references `ScrollPane` (a `Component`) in its ctor, so it sits inside the porting rule's spirit the way [D_event_port_policy](#D_event_port_policy)'s `Component`-referencing event classes do. Emulator-only, no surrogate: it is not a `Component`, has no DOM, and Vaadin ships no scrollbar-object concept at all. D_viewport_scrollbar_shadows's "shadow JDK component" pattern — except that, unlike `JScrollBar`, this one is **not inert**: its `setValue` really does scroll.

**Decision — the JDK's `addToPanel` fork is not reproduced, and `getComponent(0)` is the child you added.** `java.awt.ScrollPane.addImpl` ends `if (!SunToolkit.isLightweightOrUnknown(comp)) super.addImpl(...) else addToPanel(...)`, and `addToPanel` is `new Panel()` + `setLayout(new BorderLayout())` + `child.add(comp)` + `super.addImpl(child, …)`. So for any Swing child — essentially every child a migrated app adds — the JDK's `getComponent(0)` is a `Panel`, not what you handed it. Four reasons not to follow, in order of weight. (1) **There is no SB-Emulators analogue of `isLightweightOrUnknown`, and inventing one would be fiction**: in AWT the predicate is load-bearing because a heavyweight child has a native window the native scrolled-window can host and a lightweight one does not; in SB-Emulators every emulator is peered identically on a Vaadin component, so any predicate we wrote would be a coin-flip dressed as fidelity. (2) **The wrapper serves a native peer we do not have** — SD_sscrollpane's probe shows the peer's shadow root is a bare `<slot>` that accepts any element, and this class never touches `peerContentElement()` at all. (3) **Where it is observable, omitting it fails *softer* than the JDK**: the only visible difference is the identity of `getComponent(0)`, and code that casts it to the added type throws `ClassCastException` in real AWT, so no working migrated app contains that line. Being more permissive on a pure-bookkeeping difference is R_best_effort_behaviour best-effort, not an R_match_swing_errors case — nothing is being swallowed, because nothing failed. (4) R_infra_not_surface. **Flagged by `ideas/awt-widgets.md`**, whose Panel pass spotted the fork and predicted the wrapper would hand ScrollPane a `<div>` host its peer denies it. Real, but unneeded — which also leaves that doc's "the next container will have to override `peerContentElement`" prediction still unproven, as it itself flags. Pinned by a test asserting `getComponent(0) === child`.

**Decision — `setValue` does not clamp, the slice's one knowing divergence from JDK arithmetic.** The JDK's `setTypedValue` clamps to `[minimum, maximum - visibleAmount]`, and the span is written **only** by `setSpan`, which only `ScrollPane.layout()` calls. We never compute a pixel span (R_layouts_close_enough), so a faithful clamp is `min(max(v, 0), 0 - 0)` — **every `setValue` collapses to 0 and fires nothing, forever**, making `setScrollPosition` permanently dead on exactly the panes migrated code calls it on. So the value is stored verbatim and the browser clamps on arrival, which SD_sscrollpane's probe confirms is synchronous. One consequence, recorded rather than left latent: `getValue()` can exceed `getMaximum()` (200 against 0), impossible under the JDK's clamp — but a migrator computing `value / (double) maximum` would have got `0 / 0` under a faithful port, so no working idiom is lost. `getMaximum()` / `getVisibleAmount()` answer **0, not 1**: 1 is `setSpan`'s floor and is reachable only *after* a layout, so 0 is what an un-laid-out JDK pane actually answers.

**Decision — the `AdjustmentEvent` fan-out is fired inline and must *not* go through `EHelper.callSwing`.** This reverses the design pass, and the descope is why: with no browser→server channel, every event originates in user code calling a setter, already on a Swing-side thread inside whatever envelope brought us there. R_callswing_envelope is the *peer→Swing* thread envelope and no peer event is involved. Wrapping would be actively wrong, not merely redundant — `callSwing` throws when no UI is current, so it would blow up on a legitimate `setValue` made off a UI thread. Contrast [D_awt_scrollbar](#D_awt_scrollbar), where the fan-out *is* browser-sourced and *is* wrapped. If the read direction is revived, the browser-sourced fan-out — and only that one — takes the wrapper.

**Decision — the listener chain starts null and every fire site guards.** The JDK's `adjustmentListener` can never be null because its ctor adds the internal `PeerFixer` (the listener that scrolls by *moving the child* to a negative offset — that is how AWT scrolls). We have no `PeerFixer`; the `executeJs` push replaces it. So `setValue` and `setValueIsAdjusting` both null-guard, and a test drives both with an empty chain.

**Decision — geometry answers the JDK's own un-realized values, and none of it WARNs.** `getViewportSize()` returns `100×100` because the JDK ctor seeds `width = height = 100` and its insets here are zero; `getHScrollbarHeight()` / `getVScrollbarWidth()` return `0`, the JDK's own answer whenever `peer == null` or the policy is `SCROLLBARS_NEVER`. Computed directly rather than through `getWidth()`/`getInsets()`, which would WARN and answer 0 — a rare case where dummy geometry and JDK geometry agree exactly, so the whole paragraph is `onUnimplemented`-free. The descope *improved* this: the design pass wanted browser `clientWidth`/`clientHeight` when known and `100×100` before, i.e. two paths; there is now one, and it is the faithful one.

**Decision — R_leaf_peer_lockdown lock-down, with the policy validated inside the peer ctor.** Nothing in `java.awt` extends `ScrollPane` and `javax.swing.plaf` is out per R_match_swing_errors (b), so there is no protected `(Component peer)` ctor and both public ctors funnel into `super(new SScrollPane(policy))`. The three-arm switch lives in `SScrollPane`'s constructor so an invalid value throws out of `super(...)` and leaves no half-built `ScrollPane` — [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label)'s trick, the JDK validating before assigning being otherwise unreachable from a subclass whose `super` call must come first.

**R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2, hook by hook.** `addImpl` is reached (Container funnels all five `add` overloads) and is `final`. `doLayout()` is **overridden to call `layout()` directly**, as the JDK does: our `Container.doLayout()` dispatches to the LayoutManager and only falls through to `layout()` when there is none, which happens to always be true here since `setLayout` throws — so the hook was live *by accident*, and the override makes it live by construction. A counting-subclass test pins it. `addNotify` keeps its override and calls super (the JDK's bug-4124460 adjustable save/restore has no analogue — our peer is eternal). `processMouseWheelEvent` is kept: `Component.processEvent` genuinely routes `MouseWheelEvent` here, so it is an *absent source* rather than a dead hook. **`eventTypeEnabled(int)` is deliberately not exposed** — it only matters to `enableEvents`/`dispatchEvent`, neither of which reaches it (the first no-ops per [D_frameinit_shape](#D_frameinit_shape), the second is a stub), so exposing it would give a migrator an override that compiles, looks wired and never runs, which R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2 calls worse than absent.

**A gap found here, fixed in [D_event_consume](#D_event_consume).** The JDK's `processMouseWheelEvent` calls `e.consume()` on the enabled path, and this slice could not: `consume()` / `isConsumed()` are **public on `java.awt.event.InputEvent`** but were not ported onto `vaadinx.awt.event.InputEvent`, leaving only `AWTEvent`'s protected version, unreachable from a non-subclass. Unobservable here (nothing dispatches wheel events) but a real hole for any migrated `MouseListener` / `KeyListener`, whose `e.consume()` failed to *compile*. Ported as its own slice rather than smuggled into this one; the JDK line is now present verbatim.

**Faithful oddities reproduced rather than smoothed.** `add(c2, null, 1)` on a populated pane removes the existing child **and then** throws `IllegalArgumentException("position greater than 0")`, leaving the pane empty — the JDK's body order, and a test asserts the count is 0 afterwards. `getScrollPosition()` / `setScrollPosition(int,int)` throw `NullPointerException("child is null")` on an empty pane (AWT chose NPE with a message, not `IllegalStateException`), while `setScrollPosition(null)` NPEs from the `p.x` dereference *before* the child check. The three `Adjustable` range setters throw `java.awt.AWTError` — an `Error`, not an exception — with the message verbatim. And the constant collision: `SCROLLBARS_AS_NEEDED/ALWAYS/NEVER` are `0/1/2`, numerically identical to `Adjustable.HORIZONTAL/VERTICAL/NO_ORIENTATION`, so `new ScrollPane(Adjustable.VERTICAL)` compiles and silently means `SCROLLBARS_ALWAYS`. The safe direction is `javax.swing.ScrollPaneConstants` (20–22 / 30–32, disjoint, therefore loud). Both directions are in the class javadoc and in tests.

**`remove(int)` is overridden where the JDK does not override it.** Necessary because `Container.remove(int)` calls `removed.peer.getElement().removeFromParent()`, which would rip the element out while `Scroller.getContent()` still pointed at it; it is also how `addImpl`'s own `remove(0)` reaches the right code. Worth a rationale comment because it changes the call graph a subclass sees. Left open by the design pass and still open: whether D_jscrollpane's `JScrollPane` has the mirror-image problem (it routes removal through `setViewportView`/`JViewport.attachView` rather than overriding `remove`) — if it does, that is a finding for D_jscrollpane, not for this slice.

**Accepted limitations.** All of SD_sscrollpane's. Emulator-side: `getAccessibleContext` WARNs and returns null (R_match_swing_errors (b)); `printComponents` WARNs (user-authored `Graphics` paint, also (b)); `setWheelScrollingEnabled(false)` is R_match_swing_errors sub-bucket (c) drop-and-WARN — CSS cannot disable the wheel while keeping scrollbars draggable, and `true`, the default, is free because the browser wheel-scrolls the peer natively; `unitIncrement` / `blockIncrement` round-trip but are inert (the browser owns the deltas), and unlike the JDK the stored `blockIncrement` survives, since `setSpan`'s `0.9 × visible` overwrite never runs. **The substantive one is the descope**: user scrolls fire no `AdjustmentEvent` and `getScrollPosition()` does not track a gesture, which silently breaks four migrated idioms — save/restore of a scroll offset, two panes synchronised through an `AdjustmentListener`, "scroll to bottom only if already at bottom", and hand-rolled paging near `getMaximum()`. Nothing *renders* wrong, and a `Grid`/`VirtualList` inside the pane lazy-loads over its own channel regardless; only the fourth is "populates wrongly", and only for the migrator's own AWT-side paging.

**Validation.** `ScrollPaneTest` (20) and `ScrollPaneAdjustableTest` (11) plus `AwtScrollPaneWarnInventoryTest`'s two buckets, all zero-WARN. Highlights: R_leaf_peer_lockdown peer type through a user subclass, the remove-then-throw wart with the count asserted at 0, `getComponent(0)` identity against the JDK fork, `setScrollPosition` firing exactly one event on the axis that changed, the `doLayout()` → `layout()` counting-subclass guard, geometry asserted WARN-free, and the `SCROLLBARS_ALWAYS == Adjustable.VERTICAL` trap pinned.

**Browser-verified 2026-08-25** (Chromium via Playwright against a running Sampler); full results in SD_sscrollpane, including the one defect it caught that no browserless test could — a `Scroller` with no bounded height never overflows, so the panes were inert until the Sampler pane bounded them. Two emulator-side claims were confirmed end to end here. **The offset re-push after a child swap lands**: with the pane at `scrollTop = 200`, clicking Replace-child swapped the content (first row read `gen1 line 1`) and left `scrollTop` at 200, with `getComponentCount()` still 1 — so `addImpl`'s re-push works and the single-child rule holds. **And the descope behaves as documented**: a real trusted wheel to 333 left the server reading `(0,200)`, silent and stale, exactly as the class javadoc warns. Zero `Unimplemented` / `onUnsupportedPeerShape` / exceptions in the server log across the route.

<a id="D_event_consume"></a>
