Merging lifted the `## Not a doc gap` routing out of the inventory copy into the shared procedure, since `agent-prompt.md` asks every run for that section and the crud and jlawyer-shape docfixes had been ignoring it. **Renamed 2026-09-28 (maintainer):** `/kit-dryrun` → `/guide-migrateapp` and `/kit-docfix` → `/guide-docfix`, the pair together being **the guide loop** and one pass through it a **round** (this entry's slug followed, per [DECISION-ID-MAP.md](../DECISION-ID-MAP.md); the skill names above are today's, not the ones each dated step introduced). "Dryrun" had said the opposite of what the step does — it runs a real migration and keeps nothing only because the next round replaces it — and it collided with `import-swap --dry-run`, which is a dry run. The names lead with `guide-` because the guides are what the loop improves; the kit is only how they are delivered.
- <a id="D_kit_lsp_agent"></a>**D_kit_lsp_agent — the kit ships the `migrator` agent definition and names the Java LSP as a prerequisite; the skills spawn that agent, not a default one.** **Superseded in its mechanism by D_kit_lsp_preflight (2026-09-08): the agent type did not reach the tool.** A freshly spawned `migrator` received `Bash, Read, Write, Edit` and nothing else — `ToolSearch` and `LSP` named in its `tools:` frontmatter were silently dropped — so the definition *looked* wired and never was, the exact failure shape R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2 names. The agent file is deleted; the README prerequisite (`jdtls-lsp` over a `jdtls` on `PATH`) and the "say so first when the LSP is absent" rule in the kit brief stand. The original reasoning follows, for the record. The guide's Phase 0 is a hard gate — no resolving Java model, no migration — and in Claude Code the `LSP` tool is deferred *and* unreachable from a freshly spawned general-purpose subagent (measured 2026-09-04, recorded in the guide-loop skills' pre-flight). The kit's skills said "spawn a subagent" and the kit named no LSP anywhere: not in the README's prerequisites ("a JDK 24+, that is the whole list"), not in the brief, not in the prompt. So a customer's `/migrate-testapp` would spawn an agent that cannot reach the language server, and Phase 0 would route it onto the read-every-file fallback — or stop on a blocker the customer had never been warned about — deterministically, on every run. **Three changes, one file.** (1) `.claude/agents/migrator.md` ships in the kit, sourced from *this repository's own file* rather than a copy, so the guide-loop skills' pre-flight and the customer's skills spawn the same definition and cannot drift; its wording is customer-neutral for that reason. (2) Both kit skills say `subagent_type: migrator` and why, and tell the agent what a missing `migrator` type means (Claude Code was not opened at the kit root). (3) The README's prerequisites gain the language server — `jdtls-lsp` from the official plugin marketplace over a `jdtls` on `PATH`, with the hover-on-`String` check — and the kit brief tells the agent to say so first when it is absent. **The reversed premise:** "a customer's default agent type is not ours to name" was right about *preference* and wrong about *capability* — when exactly one agent type reaches the tool the gate requires, the agent type is part of the kit, the same way the launcher scripts are. **What this does not do:** it does not install `jdtls` for the customer (a JDK-sized external dependency the kit cannot carry), and it does not soften Phase 0 — the fallback stays the guide's, reached by the guide's own instruction.
- <a id="D_kit_your_app_slot"></a>**D_kit_your_app_slot — `your-app/swing/` is the slot for the customer's own app, and it reproduces the testapps' stage geometry.** The kit's first-run story stopped at the examples: `/migrate-swing-app <folder>` existed, but nothing in the kit said *where to put your app*, and the in-place model leant on the customer's own version control for safety. The slot answers both. The customer copies their app into `your-app/swing/`; **`/migrate-your-app`** copies it to `your-app/1-emulators/` and migrates the copy, so `swing/` stays the untouched baseline and the two folders diff into exactly the migration — the same `swing/` → `1-emulators/` layout `testapps/` uses and the guides describe as the arc's stages. `/migrate-swing-app <folder>` keeps the in-place behaviour, which remains the right shape for an app in its own checkout; the slot's `README.md` states the choice. (The slot began as `/migrate-swing-app` *with no argument*; it became its own command on 2026-09-08 — one skill per shape, per D_kit_lsp_preflight's closing note.) **Marked by a `README.md`, not a `.placeholder`**, deliberately: D_kit_placeholders' convention means "a slot *we* did not fill this release", and its one-of-the-pair rule in `KitLayoutIT` would fight a slot the *customer* fills — the artefact appearing beside the marker is the intended outcome here, not rot. The README is the marker, and it is harmless once the app is in place. Rejected: reusing `work/` (that is the testapp-copy scratch area and its name says nothing to a first-time reader) and `/migrate-testapp your-app` (the customer's app is not a testapp, and the skill's guardrails about shipped content do not apply to it). Everything else today's probe scope forbids — the kit's `CLAUDE.md`, its README, the other docs — becomes *allowed*, because the customer sees it. What this buys is that there is no longer a maintainer prompt and a customer prompt to keep from drifting: `guides/1-swing-to-emulators/agent-prompt.md` is the single source, the two skills are thin wrappers that substitute the two paths into it, and **any further delta between the residue and the customer's instructions is a finding against the kit rather than a rule to add to the skill.** `STUMBLES.md` survives the shift because it is migrator-facing on its own terms — the feedback a customer would want to send back — not because the probe needs it.
- <a id="D_kit_lsp_preflight"></a>**D_kit_lsp_preflight — the kit ships `/lsp-preflight`; the migrate skills run it before migrating; the rounds drive the kit from a session rooted at the kit.** **Retired by [M1D_lsp_recommended](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_lsp_recommended) (2026-09-09): the LSP is a recommendation, `/lsp-preflight` leaves the kit, and a round's kit is unpacked from the zip into a temp folder outside any git repository — the kit-rooted rounds' "check 3 red" was the Claude Code `LSP` tool dropping locations of gitignored files under `zip-distro/target/`, not a server failure. The five measurements below stand as history.** **The "spawn the migration as a `fork`" half is reversed by [D_kit_no_subagent](#D_kit_no_subagent) (2026-09-09); measurement (1) below stands, the spawn it was read as justifying is gone.** Decided 2026-09-08 from five measurements in one afternoon, each of which retired an assumption a shipped document rested on. (1) **No agent type reaches the `LSP` tool except a `fork`, and a fork only after its parent loaded the tool.** A fresh `migrator` had `Bash, Read, Write, Edit` only; `claude` (`Tools: *`) had `ToolSearch` but `select:LSP` answered *"No matching deferred tools found"*; a `fork` spawned after the parent's `ToolSearch select:LSP` had `LSP` in its list. So the parent's load is load-bearing, and the spawn must be a fork. (2) **Phase 0's check 2 on a JDK type proved nothing.** A `.java` file `jdtls` had imported into no project — its own diagnostic: *"non-project file, only syntax errors are reported"* — returned full document symbols *and* a perfect `JPanel` hover (`Source: Java 25.0.4 (module: java.desktop)`), and even resolved a sibling class in the same folder; the only tells were the hover's `Source:` line reading `jdt.ls-java-project` and the diagnostic. A dependency type (`JDateChooser` → `Source: jcalendar-1.4.jar`) is the discriminating subject; the guide's check 2 now says so, and says to re-check on a `vaadinx.swing` type after Phase 2 when the app has no dependency to hover. (3) **The rounds' pre-flight graded the wrong tree.** It probed `testapps/crud/swing` in the repository (imported, resolves) while the migration ran in `SWINGBRIDGE_HOME/work/crud` under `zip-distro/target/`, which from the repository's session is *"not on the classpath of project swingbridge-zip-distro"* — symbols yes, types no, fallback branch deterministically. (4) **`jdtls` scans for build files at start-up only.** A Maven project copied into place mid-session is a non-project file to it — in a session rooted at the kit, `work/crud2` copied after start resolved `JPanel` (default JRE) and not its own `Employee`, while `work/crud` present at start resolved both, `Source: com.vaadin.swingbridge.testapps-testapp-crud-swing`. The shipped `/migrate-testapp` copies mid-session, so as shipped it would have passed the old check 2 and run the `static` sweep on an unwired classpath. (5) **Two `clean install`s in a row failed in untouched code** (124 `NoClassDefFoundError`s in `:surrogates`, then `cannot access` in `:migration-tool`'s test compile) — a parallel Claude Code session building the same tree, the third stale mode CLAUDE.md § Building names; recorded in `/build-kit` so the next reader rebuilds before believing it. **Decisions.** *Kit:* a third skill, `/lsp-preflight <app folder>`, runs Phase 0's two checks from the session about to spawn — on the folder that will be migrated, with a dependency type as check 2's subject — and ends in one of three named outcomes (A pass → migrate, in that same session per D_kit_no_subagent; B not imported → restart Claude Code in the kit root, the copy is kept; C no server → stop, the fallback is the human's call, recorded at the top of `STUMBLES.md`); both migrate skills run it as their step 4; step 2's copy keeps an existing copy still identical to `swing/`, so the B-restart redoes nothing; the README's first-run path copies the example out *before* opening Claude Code and says why; `.claude/agents/migrator.md` and its `dist.xml` fileSet are gone. *Guides:* check 2 rewritten as above; `agent-prompt.md` gains the phase-batching rule and the `## Not a doc gap` categories, both migrator-facing content that had been living in a round's residue. *Repository:* the guide loop is layered `/build-kit` → `/guide-migrateapp <app>` → `/migrate-<app>-dryrun` (residue only); `/guide-migrateapp` stages the copy before the kit session starts and drives the kit from a second Claude Code opened *in* the kit, for two reasons that are one fact each — the server only imports projects under the folder it started in, and the session that runs the pre-flight is the session that migrates, so driving from the repository's session would put this repository's `CLAUDE.md`, the guide-loop skill and the probe framing in the context of an agent that is supposed to be a customer. **Rejected:** keeping `migrator` and adding the load step (the type still cannot receive a deferred tool; a definition that declares what it cannot get is the bug, not a fix); a `.claude/skills/preflight.md` loose file (skills are `<name>/SKILL.md`, and a skill directory gives the customer a standalone `/lsp-preflight` to check a fresh install with — the README's "hover over `String`" advice was measurement (2) in miniature); putting the pre-flight in `guides/` (it is Claude-Code-specific — `ToolSearch`, `subagent_type`, diagnostics blocks — while Phase 0 stays the tool-neutral gate it implements). **Accepted limitations.** The session that migrates is the one the maintainer types into, so everything said there is context the migrating agent has — the deny-list arrives for free, and so does anything else said in that session. A headless `claude -p` drive is out of scope (maintainer, 2026-09-08); a round is interactive. And `your-app/swing/` — the bring-your-own-app path — is exercised by no round now that inventory ships and runs `/migrate-testapp`; the inventory residue names the shape a future probe should take. *Same day:* the slot got its own command, `/migrate-your-app`, and `/migrate-swing-app` narrowed to the in-place shape — one skill per shape, so the customer picks a name rather than an argument count, and each skill's step 4 can name the one cause of a B outcome that fits its shape (a copy that postdates the server's scan; an app outside the folder Claude Code was opened in).
- <a id="D_kit_no_subagent"></a>**D_kit_no_subagent — the kit's migrate skills do the migration themselves; there is no subagent.** Decided 2026-09-09 (maintainer), reversing the spawn half of D_kit_lsp_preflight. All three migrate skills' step 5 becomes *follow `agent-prompt.md` in this session*, and `/lsp-preflight`'s outcome A clears the session to proceed instead of naming an agent type. **What was wrong was not the fork — it was that nobody had asked whether to spawn at all.** The decision decomposes into two independent questions, and D_kit_lsp_preflight answered only the second: *(a) subagent or inline?* and *(b) given a subagent, which type?* Measurement (1) — no agent type reaches a deferred tool, a `fork` only after its parent's load — is a constraint on (b) and says nothing about (a); the shipped skill nonetheless presented it under the heading "the agent type is not a preference" directly above "do the migration work through a subagent rather than inline", which reads as one argument and is two. The spawn itself was never argued because it was never chosen: `.claude/agents/migrator.md` already existed, so when the measurement killed that agent type, `fork` came in as its *repair* and inherited its unexamined premise. **Reasons against the spawn, once (a) is actually asked.** (1) The tool is loaded in the pre-flight session, so inline is the shape with no capability problem to solve — the migration runs where the tool already is. *(Moot since [M1D_lsp_recommended](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_lsp_recommended) the same day: there is no pre-flight and no tool to be local to, so reasons (2) and (3) carry this decision alone — which they do, being about what the user can watch and what the reporter saw rather than about capability.)* (2) The user cannot watch a subagent work; the maintainer's own reason for asking (2026-09-09) was wanting to see what the migration is doing, and for a round — whose entire product is doc gaps — where the agent hesitated is the finding. (3) The parent gets back a summary, so its step-6 report cannot quote `STUMBLES.md` detail it never saw. And a fork re-sends the parent conversation as its prefix, so it saves no input tokens; it only spares the parent the migration's *output*, which the parent had nothing else to spend on — its remaining job is the report. D_kit_lsp_preflight's own accepted-limitation booked the fork's context inheritance as a hazard rather than a benefit, which is the same fact pointing the other way. **Reason for it, weighed and declined:** a fork's parent survives a context exhaustion that would kill an inline run, leaving the retry to a session that still has room (`jlawyer-shape` is the app most likely to test that). Declined as speculative — no run has hit it — and cheap to revisit if one does, since step 2's kept-copy already makes a rerun redo nothing. **What this does not change:** every measurement in D_kit_lsp_preflight, including (1), which is now the reason *not* to spawn rather than the reason to spawn a fork; the pre-flight's existence and its three outcomes; `/guide-migrateapp`'s kit-rooted second session, whose two justifications survive intact — the language server's start-up scan, and keeping the repository's own context out of the migrating agent's, which no longer needs "a fork inherits the conversation" as its mechanism because that agent *is* the session the maintainer typed into.

**Accepted limitations.** The kit is not an offline bundle and is not planned to become one (see D_kit_what_ships) — though its *tools* are, since D_kit_tool_zip; building the migrated app is what still needs Maven and the network. A development kit is usable only on the machine that built it. One slot ships unfilled. And removing the testapps from the reactor means a plain `./mvnw -C clean install` no longer compiles or tests them: that coverage lives in `-Pkit` now, so a local emulator change that breaks a testapp is caught by CI rather than by the next local build.

<a id="D_gplv2_ce_relicense"></a>
## D_gplv2_ce_relicense — relicensed to GPLv2 + Classpath Exception

**Decided 2026-09-08** (maintainer + product owner).
Supersedes nothing — there was no licence decision entry before this one.
**Its "project-wide" limb is superseded by [D_licence_lanes](#D_licence_lanes)**, which moved two
modules to Apache-2.0 once the evidence for them existed; everything else in this entry — the
derivative-work finding, the not-clean-room constraint, the header specification, the per-file
Oracle blocks — stands unchanged and is what the GPL lane still rests on. Read the two together:
this one says why the emulator core cannot be anything but OpenJDK's licence, that one says why the
repository is not obliged to inherit it everywhere.

**Decision.** SwingBridge Emulators is accepted as a **derivative work of OpenJDK** and relicensed
from Apache-2.0 to **GPLv2 with the Classpath Exception — byte-for-byte the same licence as OpenJDK
itself** — **project-wide**, for every SB-Emulators-authored module. Oracle's copyright header is kept
**verbatim, per file** on every JDK-derived file with Vaadin's own notice alongside it; how the code
was made is recorded in a root [`PROVENANCE.md`](../PROVENANCE.md); and the rule that carries the
state forward is [R_gpl_provenance](../CLAUDE.md#R_gpl_provenance), gated by
`emulators/src/test/java/vaadinx/LicenseHeaderTest.java`. `third-party/` and `testapps/` keep their
own upstream licences exactly as before.

**The derivative-work finding.** `:emulators` reads OpenJDK's `javax.swing` / `java.awt` sources as
its behavioural specification **by written policy**, not incidentally: R_swing_is_truth ("replicate
its original behaviour as closely as possible"), [R_decline_effect_only](../CLAUDE.md#R_decline_effect_only)
("the JDK's method body is the specification, not a judgement about what seems reasonable"),
R_infra_not_surface ("copy code from Swing which calls it"). 160 source files are named after and
shaped on a JDK class, and the [similarity measurement of 2026-09-04](#D_gplv2_ce_measurement)
found roughly 14 of them to be OpenJDK source with lines deleted. Its numbers are recorded below and
nowhere else, so there is one copy to re-check.

**Therefore it is not clean-room and must never be described as clean-room.** That is the real
constraint this entry imposes, and it outlives the licence choice: R_gpl_provenance rule 1 forbids
the claim in docs, in commits and in anything attested to a third party, and COMPARISON.md § "Claims
this project does not make" carries the outward-facing version.

### Why project-wide, and not per-file or per-module

*(As decided in 2026-09. Points 2 and 4 are permanent and are what `D_licence_lanes` had to satisfy
to move anything; points 1 and 3 were the reasoning of the day, and point 3's premise — that
`:surrogates` could not be separated — is the one that measurement later overturned.)*

1. **The maintainer asked for it in those words** — "relicense this project to GPLv2+CE (exactly the
   same license as OpenJDK)" — after the per-file option had been on the table for four days.
   The product owner's standing preference ("Apache 2.0 should be our default", "not to spread GPL
   unnecessarily everywhere") is real and is why points 2–4 exist rather than a shrug.
2. **Per-file is not a boundary a consumer can see.** DEVELOPING.md already states the principle for
   `third-party/`: *a licence boundary that isn't a module boundary is not a boundary.* A jar whose
   pom says Apache-2.0 while 160 of its classes are GPLv2+CE is the "ship them silently under
   Apache" outcome the measurement ruled out — every consumer's licence scanner reads the pom, not
   the headers.
3. **Per-module would put the line inside `:emulators`, which cannot be split.** The 41
   counterpart-less files are `EHelper`, the `FormattedFieldStrategy` family, the app bootstrap and
   the `vaadinx.util.prefs` implementations — glue the 160 JDK-shaped files call on every line. The
   other modules are small (`:loom` 3 files, `:migration-*` 15) and `:surrogates` is `:emulators`'
   peer layer, imported by it. Splitting buys a permissive label on the helpers and nothing else.
4. **The Classpath Exception makes the migrator's position identical either way**, which is what
   defuses the competitive objection raised on 2026-08-19. A migrated app *links* SB-Emulators
   exactly as it links the JDK, and the exception permits linking "with independent modules … 
   regardless of the license terms of these independent modules". So the answer to a migrator's
   legal review is "the same terms your app already accepted by running on OpenJDK" — not
   "permissive versus copyleft". COMPARISON.md § "On licensing" states it that way and draws
   no copyleft line against other approaches, since that licence class is now our own.
5. **What project-wide does not mean.** `third-party/jgoodies-forms-1.2.1` stays BSD (upstream's
   terms, unchanged); `testapps/inventory` stays on its author's informal grant;
   `testapps/jlawyer-shape` is left alone rather than adjudicated. `third-party/jcalendar-1.4` was
   Vaadin-authored and *inherited* at the time of this entry; it has since taken upstream's
   **LGPL-2.1** instead, per
   [M1D_addon_upstream_licence](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_addon_upstream_licence)
   (2026-09-21) — so **neither** add-on is under this licence now, and "project-wide" means
   SB-Emulators' own modules only.
6. **Compatibility of what we link.** GPLv2 is famously incompatible with Apache-2.0 *code inside the
   same work*, but SB-Emulators only **links** Apache-2.0 (Vaadin Flow, PDFBox, ArchUnit), BSD (the
   JGoodies fork) and Vaadin-commercial (RichTextEditor, via `SJEditorPane`) modules — and the
   Classpath Exception exists precisely to permit that. OpenJDK links Apache-licensed code the same
   way. Code Vaadin *owns* may also be copied in, since a copyright holder may relicense its own
   work; third-party code may not, which is R_gpl_provenance rule 5.

### The headers, and the two shortcuts rejected

Two texts for this lane, both reproduced in [PROVENANCE.md § Headers](../PROVENANCE.md#headers),
which is the specification `LicenseHeaderTest` enforces. **`HDR_jdk_derived`** is the counterpart's
own Oracle block byte-for-byte, then a Vaadin block that serves as GPLv2 §2(a)'s prominent notice,
names what the file derives from, and *extends* the Classpath exception to Vaadin's modifications
using the words `LICENSE` itself supplies for that act. **`HDR_vaadin_gpl`** is the GNU Classpath
project's shape: Vaadin's copyright, GPLv2-only, exception text **inline** — inline because the
Classpath section of `LICENSE` reaches only files "where Oracle has expressly included" the
designation, so a Vaadin-authored file cannot lean on it. (The two were called Header A and Header B
until `D_licence_lanes` put the set on slugs; the texts are unchanged.)

- **JetBrains Runtime's shortcut is rejected.** JBR puts `Copyright 2025 JetBrains s.r.o.` above
  Oracle's boilerplate *unchanged*, including "Oracle designates this particular file as subject to
  the Classpath exception". Oracle designated nothing about a file Oracle did not write. A false
  attribution is the same class of error as a missing notice, just pointed the other way — hence
  `LicenseHeaderTest` rule 2 failing in **both** directions.
- **`vaadin/feature-pack-internal`'s shortcut is rejected**, and it is the weaker precedent than
  remembered: its 13 JDK-derived files carry Oracle's header with nothing of Vaadin's in it but an
  `@author` tag, and it stamped `Copyright (c) 1997, 2021` on all of them regardless of the real
  years (`java.awt.Dimension` is `1995, 2021`). Years must be copied per file — measured here as **42
  distinct pairs across the 160** — so `LicenseHeaderTest` rule 4 rejects a uniform stamp outright.
  Its pom block *is* reused: `<name>GPL2 w/ CPE</name>` plus the classpath-license URL is the Jakarta
  convention, so scanners already know the pair.

**Upstream reference is the tag `jdk-25-ga`, not a vendor build**, and that distinction earned itself
during implementation: JetBrains Runtime 25.0.4's `src.zip` differs from `jdk-25-ga` on 4 of the 160
files, **in both directions** (`java.awt.GraphicsEnvironment` is `1997, 2021` there against
`1997, 2024` at the tag; `javax.swing.border.LineBorder` is `1997, 2025` against `1997, 2023`). Every
committed Oracle block was fetched from the tag. The same measurement forced a change to the planned
gate: rule 4 cannot assert byte-equality against the *local* `src.zip`, because CI runs JDK 24 and 25
and the end year legitimately moves between builds (`java.awt.Component` is 2024 on 24, 2025 on 25).
It instead compares the notice with the copyright line masked, pins the **start** year (a file's
creation year, which does not move), and asserts the spread of year pairs — which is the property
that actually catches templating.

**Not shipped: `ADDITIONAL_LICENSE_INFO` and `ASSEMBLY_EXCEPTION`.** OpenJDK's other two licence
files are Oracle-specific — the first is Oracle's advisory prose about *its* distribution's mixed
licences, the second Oracle's grant for assembling a JDK from its "Designated Exception Modules". No
header of ours references either, and copying an Oracle-specific grant into a non-Oracle project
would misstate who grants what. Only `LICENSE` ships, and it ships inside every jar because the
per-file headers name it by reference.

**Snapshot, not tracking.** SB-Emulators does not merge upstream changes, so there is no
upstream-merge bookkeeping and §2(a) marking is the per-file Vaadin year rather than a changelog.

### Rejected alternatives

- **(a) Rewrite the ~14 high-overlap files clean-room and stay Apache-2.0.** Rejected because the
  *method* for the other 146 is identical — all of them were written against the JDK's source by
  written policy — so a clean-room claim over the result would be false whatever happened to those
  14. It would buy the label by rewriting the evidence, not the practice.
- **(b) Per-file GPL headers inside an Apache-2.0 jar.** Rejected per point 2: the pom is what a
  consumer's tooling reads, so this is the silent-Apache outcome with extra steps.
- **(c) Per-module split.** Rejected per point 3: the only honest line runs through the middle of
  `:emulators`.

<a id="D_gplv2_ce_measurement"></a>
### The similarity measurement behind the finding (2026-09-04)

Measured against the JDK 25 `src.zip` (JetBrains Runtime 25.0.4: `java.desktop`'s `javax.swing.*` +
`java.awt.*`, plus `java.util`, `java.util.prefs`, `java.text`), repo at `main@941652b`, by Claude
(Fable 5.1) at the maintainer's request. Not legal advice; the numbers are the deliverable.
`JdkSimilarityTest` ([D_similarity_gate](#D_similarity_gate)) is its successor as a gate, with a
different metric; the throwaway `sim.py` / `split.py` scripts were not kept.

**Method.** Comments and string-literal contents stripped; `vaadinx.swing` → `javax.swing`,
`vaadinx.awt` → `java.awt`, `vaadinx.util` → `java.util` mapped, so a port differing only by the
import swap still matches. Each emulator file paired with its JDK counterpart by path — 159 of 199
had one. Metrics: verbatim **code lines** (whitespace-normalised, ≥12 chars, trivial lines like `}`
excluded), token **8-grams**, and **doc lines** (comment lines ≥30 chars); matched code lines split
into signature / field / body. `:surrogates`, which ports nothing, served as the **noise floor** —
what idiomatic Swing-flavoured Java matches by accident.

**Volume.** `:emulators` was ~25,000 code lines: ~10% touching Vaadin (`peer`, `com.vaadin`,
`executeJs`, `callSwing`, `S*` types), ~2% `onUnimplemented` / `onNoop` stubs, ~14% in the 40
counterpart-less files — so **85–90% Swing-shaped code, 10–15% Vaadin peer control**.

| Metric (159 paired files, 17,405 non-trivial code lines) | vs own counterpart | vs whole corpus | `:surrogates` vs corpus (noise) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Method signature lines | 38.2% | 38.6% | 36.4% |
| Field / constant lines | 53.3% | 49.1% | 53.8% |
| **Method body lines** | **20.9%** (2,039 / 9,759) | 23.6% | **12.8%** |
| Code token 8-grams | 15.1% | 20.4% | 15.9% |
| Comment lines (≥30 chars) | 0.1% (9 / 13,679) | 0.1% | 0.0% |

Signatures and constants match at the noise rate — that is the API shape itself. Body lines ran 8–10
points above noise, so roughly **1,000 of ~10,000 body lines** reproduce specific JDK expression, much
of it thin (`this.modelIndex = modelIndex;`) but not all (`minWidth = Math.min(15, this.width);`).
Javadoc was effectively all original.

**Concentration.** Files with a counterpart and ≥20 code lines, by fraction of code lines verbatim in
the counterpart: **≥50%: 14 files** (960 of 1,253 lines); 25–50%: 47 (1,608 / 4,691); 10–25%: 42
(1,563 / 8,407); <10%: 7 (27 / 366). The fourteen:

| File | code lines | line% | 8-gram% |
|---|---|---|---|
| `awt/CheckboxGroup` | 20 | 95.0 | 84.1 |
| `swing/table/TableColumn` | 151 | 94.7 | 89.2 |
| `swing/DefaultCellEditor` | 89 | 93.3 | 69.0 |
| `awt/event/KeyEvent` | 253 | 87.0 | 83.6 |
| `swing/table/DefaultTableColumnModel` | 156 | 84.0 | 89.9 |
| `swing/table/JTableHeader` | 101 | 81.2 | 63.3 |
| `awt/GridLayout` | 56 | 69.6 | 51.8 |
| `awt/event/InputEvent` | 47 | 66.0 | 52.6 |
| `swing/table/DefaultTableCellRenderer` | 41 | 61.0 | 60.3 |
| `awt/FlowLayout` | 53 | 60.4 | 37.8 |
| `swing/border/TitledBorder` | 89 | 57.3 | 42.6 |
| `swing/TransferHandler` | 86 | 54.7 | 27.0 |
| `awt/event/FocusEvent` | 40 | 52.5 | 38.0 |
| `awt/event/MouseEvent` | 71 | 50.7 | 49.5 |

The pattern: **peer-less model and layout classes, where a faithful port had no Vaadin work to
dilute it, became copies.** A re-check on 2026-09-08 diffed the top ones whole: `TableColumn` is the
JDK file with `@BeanProperty` removed and one renderer body trimmed, `DefaultTableColumnModel`
differs in import order and brace placement, `CheckboxGroup` in five lines. `KeyEvent`'s matches are
almost all `VK_*` constants — API shape. The large peered classes match only in scattered one-liners
(`JTree`: 40% of its lines occur somewhere in the JDK file, longest contiguous run 16 lines; top
absolute body counts `TableColumn` 94, `JFileChooser` 92, `awt.Component` 88).

**Limits.** Line and 8-gram matching sees verbatim and near-verbatim reproduction, not a paraphrase
keeping the JDK's structure with renamed locals — the 25–50% bucket likely holds some. The
`:surrogates` noise floor is approximate and probably low for pure-Java model code, so the true body
excess may be a few points under 8–10.

### What was edited in place rather than added

`D_pdf_engine`'s parenthetical ("matching SB-Emulators' own Apache-2.0") now reads "linkable from a
GPLv2+CE work via the Classpath Exception" — the dependency is unchanged and still Apache-2.0; only
the reason it composes has a different name. `DECISION-ID-MAP.md` lists no licence-related legacy ID
and is untouched.

<a id="D_licence_lanes"></a>
## D_licence_lanes — the licence follows the derivation, per module: everything but `:emulators` and `:emulators-printing` is Apache-2.0

**Decided 2026-09-22** (maintainer), on Vaadin's proposal to move every module the company wholly
owns off GPLv2+CE; **`:loom` and `:sampler` joined the lane the same day**, on the measurements in
"Why these modules" below — `:sampler` after the composition rule below was rewritten, since the
rule as first written excluded it. **The remaining six followed on 2026-09-23**, each measured by
[D_similarity_gate](#D_similarity_gate) first. **Partially supersedes [D_gplv2_ce_relicense](#D_gplv2_ce_relicense)** — its
*"project-wide"* limb only. The licence *choice* for `:emulators`, the derivative-work finding and
the not-clean-room constraint are untouched and are not up for revisiting.

**Decision.** The repository has **lanes** rather than one licence, and
[`PROVENANCE.md` § Lanes](../PROVENANCE.md#lanes) is the authoritative and exhaustive map: a path's
licence is what that table says, a per-file header wins over the table, and anything the table does
not name is the residual, **Apache-2.0**. Every module but `:emulators` and `:emulators-printing` moves to
**Apache-2.0** — **`:surrogates`**, **`:emulators-spring`**, **`:sampler`**,
**`:migration-annotations`**, **`:migration-guardrails`**, **`:migration-tool`**, **`:zip-distro`**,
**`:generator`** and **`testapps/crud`** — shipping [`LICENSE-APACHE-2.0`](../LICENSE-APACHE-2.0) in
their `META-INF/` instead of `LICENSE` and carrying `HDR_vaadin_apache` on all 343 of their `.java`
files. The two add-ons keep their upstream's licence
([M1D_addon_upstream_licence](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_addon_upstream_licence)).

**Apache-2.0 is the parent pom's default** (2026-09-23), so those modules inherit their
`<licenses>` and `<resources>` blocks rather than overriding them; `:emulators`,
`:emulators-printing` and the two add-ons are the modules that override, since Maven replaces both
blocks rather than merging them. `LicenseHeaderTest` follows the pom: it names the GPL lane
(`GPL_LANE`) and treats every other tree we author as Apache, and `JdkSimilarityTest` measures
whatever that admits. **That is what makes a permissive default safe rather than merely
convenient**: a new module is Apache-2.0 in its pom, its required header and the similarity gate at
once, so a JDK body ported into one fails the build on day one, where a GPL default would have let
it sit unmeasured. With the list the other way round, a new module would inherit Apache-2.0 from
the pom while the header test still demanded the GPL line — two gates disagreeing about one tree.

**The map's residual is Apache-2.0 too, and the map is exhaustive** (2026-09-23). Every tracked
surface has a row — the docs, `guides/`, `migration/`, `ideas/`, `.claude/skills/`, `.github/`, the
poms, the Maven Wrapper copies (the ASF's, kept) and the two licence texts (their authors') — so the
residual is a net for a file nobody mapped, not a lane anything sits in on purpose. The order is the
point: flipping the residual *inverts* what a forgotten surface inherits, so it had to wait until
nothing was forgotten; before that, a GPLv2+CE residual erred toward claiming too much rather than
granting what nobody decided to grant. Two consequences of naming everything:

- **The GPL row is the two modules' `src/`, not their whole trees.** `emulators/decisions.md`,
  `emulators/architecture.md`, the module READMEs and both poms are docs and build files like any
  other, and they are Apache-2.0: none ships in the jar (its `META-INF/` carries only `LICENSE` and
  `PROVENANCE.md`), and none carries JDK expression of its own. A pom's `<licenses>` block states its
  *artifact's* licence, not the file's. The add-ons are the other way round and stay whole-tree,
  because their `MIGRATION.md` ships *inside* the jar.
- **Quoted text keeps its own terms**, and every decision log now says so at its head alongside
  `PROVENANCE.md`: the logs quote JDK source, javadoc and Oracle's notice, and an Apache-2.0 row
  relicenses none of it.

**One tree waives its terms instead: the host-app seeds are 0BSD** (2026-09-24, maintainer).
`guides/1-swing-to-emulators/seed/` ([M1D_bootstrap_choice](../migration/1-swing-to-emulators/decisions.md#M1D_bootstrap_choice))
is the one tree whose files are meant to leave SB-Emulators: a migrator copies a seed into their own
app and edits it there, so whatever terms its header states become terms on their code. Under
Apache-2.0 they would carry Vaadin's notice on files that are, by then, theirs, and they want to bring
their own licence. So the seeds carry `HDR_vaadin_0bsd` and a `seed/LICENSE` of the same text, a
grant with no conditions: use, modify, redistribute and relicense, with no notice to keep. The
alternatives, and why not:

- **No header at all** reads as a waiver and is the opposite of one: a file with no licence
  statement is all rights reserved, which leaves a customer's lawyer holding Vaadin-authored code
  in their app with no grant whatsoever — worse than Apache-2.0.
- **CC0-1.0** is the literal public-domain dedication, but it expressly *withholds* any patent
  licence. That is why OSI never approved it, and why Fedora stopped accepting CC0 for code in
  2022; a customer's intake policy may flag it for the same reason, which defeats the purpose.
- **MIT-0** is equivalent in effect (OSI-approved, no attribution). 0BSD was chosen for being the
  shorter text in a header the customer is likely to delete anyway.

Gated like the other lanes: `LicenseHeaderTest` rule 7 holds the tree to the 0BSD header and fails on
any Apache, GPL or Oracle text in it, as well as on a missing `seed/LICENSE`, and `JdkSimilarityTest`
measures it with the Apache lane (`inPermissiveLane`), since JDK expression under a waiver would be
GPL code under terms that do not carry it.

**A seed keeps its 0BSD when a migration carries it into a testapp** (2026-09-24, maintainer). The
first `/guide-migrateapp crud` after the switch copied `AppRoute`, `AppShell`, `AppErrorHandler` and
`SpringWiringTest` into `testapps/crud/1-emulators/` with their 0BSD headers — correctly, since that
is what a migrator's app gets — and turned `LicenseHeaderTest` red, because `testapps/crud/` is an
Apache-2.0 tree. Restoring Apache headers after every copy-back was rejected: it is a hand-edit in
migration output (`testapps/CLAUDE.md`), it makes the committed baseline differ from what a customer's
migrated app looks like, and it would be one more step in the round's residue. So the Apache lane
admits `HDR_vaadin_0bsd` per file in any stage under `testapps/<app>/` but `swing/`, and
`LicenseHeaderTest` holds such a file to the whole 0BSD header (`keepsSeedHeader`). `swing/` stays
strict: it is authored, and nothing from a seed belongs in it.

**Why these modules, and one by one.** The bar is evidence, not ownership, and each cleared it
differently:

- **`:surrogates`** — no Oracle notice on any file and `LicenseHeaderTest.DERIVED_WITHOUT_NAME`
  empty, which was not true until it was *made* true: eleven files carried `HDR_jdk_derived`, and
  all eleven left by having the carried-over expression removed rather than re-judged (the ten
  `S*Event` constant tables now emitted from the JDK's public runtime API by
  `DelegatedConstantsTest`, `SJTextArea`'s three text-mutation bodies rewritten as bounds checks
  over one splice). [`PROVENANCE.md` § "The exceptions"](../PROVENANCE.md#exceptions) is the
  per-file record with the before/after numbers, and
  [SD_event_port_stance](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_event_port_stance) is the generator rule that
  keeps a future event port from putting one back.
- **`:emulators-spring`** — Vaadin-authored from the start, four files, no Oracle notice on any of
  them. It subclasses only *Vaadin's* `SpringServlet` / `SpringVaadinServletService` and reaches
  `:emulators` through a single import of `SwingBridgeEmulatorsBootstrap`.
- **`:loom`** — on this lane until it was replaced by the vaadin-blocking-dialogs dependency, which
  is Apache-2.0 upstream ([D_blocking_dialogs_library](#D_blocking_dialogs_library)). Five files, no
  Oracle notice owed: virtual-thread plumbing has no Swing counterpart to reproduce.
- **`:sampler`** — 99 files, no Oracle notice on any of them, and the one module where the evidence
  had to be *measured* rather than read off the headers, because it is the repository's heaviest
  consumer of the emulator API and so the case the composition rule below was rewritten against.
  The line-overlap script that preceded [D_similarity_gate](#D_similarity_gate), against the `java.desktop` + `java.base` corpus (1,578 files), puts it at **5.30% matched
  code lines** and **0 matched comment lines out of 1,243** — inside the 4.5–8.4% noise floor, and
  *below* `:migration-tool`'s 7.66%, a module that ports nothing whatsoever. The percentage was not
  taken on trust: all **99 distinct matched lines were read**, and every one is either an interface
  signature an implementor must write verbatim (`actionPerformed`, `createTransferable`,
  `canImport`, `getValueAt`, `setValueAt`, …), universal Java boilerplate (`return true;`,
  `if (name == null) {`), or an artifact of the normaliser (`return wrap;` 25× is a local variable
  name; the `"", "", ""` rows are string literals with their contents stripped). That is the same
  call already made for `:surrogates`' 20 listener siblings — API shape, not carried-over
  expression — and the zero comment matches are the strongest part of it, since copied code drags
  its comments along. **One check could not be run and does not bear on the lane:** Sampler is a
  Swing demo, so Oracle's SwingSet2 and the Java Tutorial examples are the obvious source for demo
  panels to have been adapted from, and that corpus is not available locally (modern JDKs ship no
  `demo/`). It would not change the answer if it were — **OpenJDK's demo sources are BSD-licensed**,
  deliberately, so a resemblance there is a third-party attribution question and never a GPL-lane
  one. Sampler is not published (`maven.deploy.skip`), so its lane states terms to repo readers
  rather than to a consumer.
- **`:migration-annotations`, `:migration-guardrails`, `:migration-tool`, `:zip-distro`,
  `:generator`, `testapps/crud`** — 59 files, no Oracle notice on any, measured 2026-09-23 with
  [D_similarity_gate](#D_similarity_gate)'s own metrics before moving (gate limit 20): longest body
  runs 0 / 4 / 8 / 7 / 5 / 4, zero JDK comments and zero shared literals across all six. Every run
  is boilerplate — `for (int i = 0; i < args.length; i++)`, `catch (IOException e)` then
  `throw new UncheckedIOException(e)`, `Calendar cal = Calendar.getInstance()`. Three details
  shaped the move. `:migration-tool`'s dist zip ships the Apache text as its `LICENSE`, since both
  `swingbridge-*` jars in its `lib/` are now Apache (`DistZipIT` asserts it), and the zip also
  publishes on its own. `:generator` *emits* `HDR_jdk_derived` into new emulators, verbatim from
  `src.zip`; that header is the emulator lane's, and its pom says so. `testapps/crud`'s stage-2 pom
  is the template a migrator copies, so it carries no `<licenses>` block — that would leak our
  terms into their app — and in the kit the root `LICENSE` covers it instead.

**The gate is the jar, not the file**, which is the whole reason the sweep and the pom had to move
together. `D_gplv2_ce_relicense` point 2 already settled it in the other direction — *a jar whose
pom says Apache-2.0 while its classes are GPLv2+CE is not a boundary a consumer can see* — so an
Apache-2.0 pom over Oracle-noticed classes was never an option, and clearing all eleven files was a
precondition rather than a tidy-up. `LicenseHeaderTest` now fails from both sides: rule 2 on an
Oracle notice anywhere outside the emulator trees, new **rule 6** on a Classpath-exception line
anywhere inside the Apache lane.

**The same gate runs the other way: `:emulators` is GPLv2+CE as a whole jar** (maintainer,
2026-09-23), Vaadin-authored files included. The product owner's 2026-09-08 direction — *"GPLv2+CE
in the emulator files where there is derivative work … If there is Vaadin code in some files, let's
use Vaadin copyright"* — could be read per file, putting `EHelper`, the `app` package, the `Store`s
and the rest of the `HDR_vaadin_gpl` files on Apache-2.0 inside a GPL jar. Rejected: a consumer's
scanner reads one licence per jar, so a mixed jar states a boundary nobody can see; those files are
glue the JDK-shaped ones call on every line (`D_gplv2_ce_relicense` point 3 is still true *inside*
the module); and the Classpath exception leaves a migrator's position identical either way. The
direction's second sentence is about the **copyright holder**, not the licence, and `HDR_vaadin_gpl`
already satisfies it — those files carry Vaadin's copyright, under the jar's licence.

**It composes, and `:emulators-spring` is the direction that needed checking.** Apache-2.0 is
GPLv2-incompatible on the FSF's reading (patent-termination and indemnity as "further restrictions"
under §6), and after the split GPLv2+CE `:emulators` depends on Apache-2.0 `:surrogates` (and on
the Apache-2.0 vaadin-blocking-dialogs) while Apache-2.0 `:emulators-spring` depends on `:emulators`. Both hold, for two independent
reasons:

1. **The Classpath Exception is the point.** `:emulators` grants permission to link "with
   independent modules … regardless of the license terms of these independent modules".
   `:surrogates` and vaadin-blocking-dialogs are upstream of it and derive from nothing of ours; `:emulators-spring`
   is the first permissive module **downstream** of the GPL core, where the exception is
   load-bearing rather than merely available, and it qualifies because it *links* the library rather
   than containing any of it.

   **What makes a module independent is expression, not coupling** — and that limb is stated
   carefully because the first attempt at it was wrong. **`:surrogates` and
   `:emulators-spring` each carry none of the emulator core's code**, which is the property that
   matters, and it is decided by two questions: does the tree carry **JDK expression** (an Oracle
   notice owed — the test `:surrogates`' eleven files had to clear), and does it carry
   **SB-Emulators' own GPL expression** — emulator source copied in, forked, or shipped as a
   modified copy, which is ordinary GPLv2 §2 territory and the one genuine limb here. A module that
   answers no to both may be permissive, and **the dependency direction does not enter into it**,
   because linking in either direction is exactly what the exception permits.

   **The rule this replaced said "never subclass an emulator type", and it does not survive its own
   reductio.** If extending `vaadinx.swing.JPanel` made a work derived, then extending
   `javax.swing.JButton` would too, the Classpath Exception would grant essentially nothing, and
   OpenJDK would be unusable for proprietary software — the precise case the exception exists to
   permit. A subclass contains none of its superclass's expression; it contains a reference to it.
   The rule also contradicted [D_gplv2_ce_relicense](#D_gplv2_ce_relicense) point 4 in this same
   file, which is the product's load-bearing promise: a migrated app links SB-Emulators "exactly as
   it links the JDK", and migrated apps subclass `vaadinx.swing.JFrame` as a matter of course. No
   reading can hold for the migrator and fail for a module of ours.

   **Where the error came from is the part worth keeping**, because the shape recurs: the rule was
   generalised from a favourable measurement of `:emulators-spring` — *one import, extends only
   Vaadin's own types* — which is a fact about how **thin** the coupling is. Thinness is reassuring
   and it is not the copyright question, so promoting it to a rule made the reassurance
   load-bearing. `:sampler` is what exposed that: 433 `vaadinx` imports and 50 classes extending an
   emulator type (46 `vaadinx.swing.JPanel`, plus `JFrame`, the three `Default*CellRenderer`s,
   `SwingBridgeVaadinServlet`, `MainWindowRoute`), measured 2026-09-22 — the heaviest coupling in
   the repository, not one line of emulator expression carried, **and on the permissive lane**.
   **An argument from
   authorship history was tried and is also retracted**: that Sampler was written *against*
   `:emulators` while a migrated app pre-existed it. Chronology is not what makes a work derivative,
   and a demo written against a library contains no more of its expression than an app retargeted
   onto one.
2. **Vaadin holds every copyright involved**, so compatibility only ever bites downstream — and
   downstream is covered by (1).

One thing gets *easier*: `com.vaadin.swingbridge.surrogates.BrowserTimeZone`, a port of
karibu-tools' Apache-2.0 `BrowserTimeZone.kt`, now sits in an Apache-2.0 module, so it no longer
needs the same-author-may-license-twice argument to be there at all.

**The headers went to slugs in the same pass.** `HDR_jdk_derived` / `HDR_vaadin_gpl` /
`HDR_vaadin_apache` / `HDR_vaadin_lgpl` replace Headers A / B / (new) / D, and Header C retires
altogether into `PROVENANCE.md` § "Trees we do not touch" — it was never a header text but an
instruction not to write one. Three reasons the letters had to go rather than gain an "E": at five
entries the ordering was historical rather than logical; the axes are *who wrote the file* × *which
lane*, which `HDR_jdk_derived` states and a letter hides; and **the licence identifier cannot carry
the distinction that matters most**, since `HDR_jdk_derived` and `HDR_vaadin_gpl` have byte-identical
SPDX lines and what separates them is Oracle's block — the false-attribution direction. The prefix is
`HDR_` because `H_` belongs to the migration hazards; `DecisionIdTest` learned it, so an `HDR_` slug
is as typo-proof as a `D_` one, with `PROVENANCE.md` added to the files that may *define* one.

**`HDR_vaadin_apache` is `vaadin/flow`'s own block plus our SPDX line.** Measured rather than
recalled: all 826 files in `flow-server-25.2.8-sources.jar` carry one identical header and **not one
of them carries an SPDX line**, so "copy byte-for-byte from Flow" could not be taken literally —
`LicenseHeaderTest` rule 1 asserts an identifier on every authored file. Adding the line in the
house position under the copyright keeps rule 1 a single uniform assertion whose expected value
varies by lane, and keeps the annual year sweep one line in every lane.

**Verified release-shaped, 2026-09-23**: a clean reactor build, `-Prelease` packaging with signing
skipped, and the kit unpacked outside the repository. Every main and `-sources` jar of the ten
published modules carries exactly its lane's texts, byte-identical to the repository's, and no
Oracle notice or Classpath-exception line appears in any Apache-lane jar outside `PROVENANCE.md`,
which discusses both. The kit's root `LICENSE` is the Apache text and its
`tools/lib/swingbridge-emulators-LICENSE.txt` the GPL one. The one surprise was the `-javadoc`
jars' `legal/` folder, which the javadoc tool writes into every lane's jar and which
[`PROVENANCE.md` § Lanes](../PROVENANCE.md#lanes) now accounts for.

**What is still open** is contributor terms: [`ideas/contributor-terms.md`](../ideas/contributor-terms.md).
**The deadline is first publish, not a date**: nothing has been conveyed yet, so every licence in
the repository still binds nobody and can be changed at will; after `-Prelease` runs, changing one
needs the consent of everyone holding a copy.

**Accepted consequences.**

- **GitHub will keep reporting GPL-2.0 for the repository**, since its detector reads the root
  `LICENSE` and there is no multi-licence UI. `README.md` § License is where a reader gets the
  per-artifact answer; the file layout cannot fix it.
- **The kit carries more than one licence**: GPLv2+CE for the `swingbridge-emulators` jar in
  `tools/lib/`, Apache-2.0 for everything Vaadin wrote around it (the guides, skills, kit docs, the
  crud example, the tool jars), each add-on's upstream licence, and their own terms for the other
  two example apps. The kit README's "Licences" paragraph maps them.
- **The kit swaps the repository's two licence file names.** Its root `LICENSE` is the Apache text
  — the lane of everything Vaadin wrote that the kit ships, and where a reader looks first — and the
  GPL text travels beside the one jar it governs, as `tools/lib/swingbridge-emulators-LICENSE.txt`
  (the jar also carries it at `META-INF/LICENSE`). The repository cannot make that swap (next
  bullet), but the kit can: it ships no Oracle-noticed source that names its `LICENSE` file, and no
  shipped link reaches either text, so mirroring the repository's names would buy no link and would
  put GPL text at the kit root. `KitLayoutIT` asserts each file's content matches its location,
  since a descriptor edit that mirrored the names would otherwise swap them silently.
- **`PROVENANCE.md` would be Apache-2.0 even without the docs row**, because it travels inside every
  jar in every lane and cannot sit on a lane narrower than the widest artifact it ships into.
- **The root `LICENSE` cannot be renamed or removed**, whatever else moves: 160 byte-frozen Oracle
  blocks say "a copy is included in the LICENSE file that accompanied this code". The Apache text is
  therefore a *second* root file rather than a replacement.

**Rejected alternatives.** *(a) Keep project-wide GPLv2+CE* — rejected because it **over-claims**:
there is no derivation behind GPLv2+CE on a module that has never read a line of OpenJDK, and a
claim we could not defend is not the conservative option, merely the quiet one. *(b) Flip the whole
sheet at once* — rejected as sequencing, not principle: each module moved on its own measurement,
and the residual moved last. *(c) Keep the GPL modules' whole trees on the GPL row*, their decision
logs and poms included — rejected because nothing but location put those files there: they ship in
no jar and carry no JDK expression of their own, and what they *quote* keeps its own terms on any
row. A lane that followed the directory rather than the derivation would be the coupling argument
this entry retracts, applied to files instead of modules.

**The authority behind "API shape is not expression"**, for whoever next carries this to legal
review. The sheet-era framing leaned on *Google v. Oracle*, which decided on **fair use** and
expressly assumed *without deciding* that declaring code is copyrightable — so it is not a holding
that API declarations are unprotected, and fair use is a US doctrine with no EU counterpart. For a
Finnish rightsholder the stronger authority is **Software Directive 2009/24/EC Art. 1(2)** (ideas
and principles underlying any element of a program, *including those underlying its interfaces*,
are not protected) and **CJEU *SAS Institute v World Programming*, C-406/10** (functionality,
programming languages and data-file formats are not expression). It makes the case for the
permissive lane stronger, not weaker.

<a id="D_similarity_gate"></a>
## D_similarity_gate — the Apache lane is measured against the JDK on every build

**Decided 2026-09-21 (a gate), shaped 2026-09-23** (maintainer). `emulators/src/test/java/vaadinx/JdkSimilarityTest.java`
measures every `.java` file `LicenseHeaderTest.inApacheLane` admits — every tree we author outside
`GPL_LANE` — against the running JDK's own
`lib/src.zip` and fails the build on carried-over JDK expression. It is what keeps
[D_licence_lanes](#D_licence_lanes)' "no JDK expression" true *after* a module moves, and it is an
**output** check on purpose: an agent that reproduces a JDK body from memory is indistinguishable
from one that read `src.zip`, so no input rule ("don't open the JDK sources") can be enforced, and
claiming one would collide with `R_gpl_provenance` rule 1.

**Two gates, both absolute.** A percentage red-flags every small event class whose few lines are
plumbing (`SFocusEvent` once scored 11 of 26), so neither gate is one.

- **Body run < 20** — the longest run of consecutive method-body statements that also sits
  consecutively in *one* JDK file, weighted by identifier/number tokens. Parsed with javac's own
  Tree API, not regex (regex classification let multi-line constructor signatures leak in as
  "body"). API shape is excluded on both sides first: signatures, fields and constants,
  `this(…)`/`super(…)` delegation, `this.x = x;`, and one-statement bodies (accessors, the
  `listenerList.add/remove/getListeners` triplet).
- **Zero comments** of 30+ characters identical to a JDK comment — copied code drags its comments
  along, and independent code never matches one.

**Calibration, measured 2026-09-23 on JBR 25.0.4.** The lane peaks at **17** (`SScrollbar`'s
visible/value clamp, Swing's behaviour reproduced on purpose and already cleared by reading), then
`SJTextArea` 14 and scattered one-liners at 10–12; everything outside `:surrogates` scores 10 or
less. Twelve known `:emulators` ports score 20 or more, up to 381 (`DefaultTableColumnModel`).
The Apache lane has no comment hits; several emulator ports do. **A canary** asserts five of those
ports still score at or above the limit, and that they still share a comment with the JDK, so a
broken parser or an empty corpus fails instead of passing clean.

**Printed, not gated:** single-file concentration (body weight shared with the one best JDK file)
cannot separate — cleared surrogates (`SJTable` 127) sit in the same band as derived emulators —
and shared multi-word string literals (51 today), which `R_match_swing_errors` often *wants*
matched.

**Blind spots, stated where the output is read (the test's javadoc):** it catches copying, not
paraphrase; and string-literal contents are stripped before comparing, so copied message text
never scores.

**The corpus is the running JDK.** `setup-java`'s Temurin 24.0.2 and 25.0.4.1 both ship
`lib/src.zip` (probe run 35821843586, 2026-09-23). The corpus differs by a few files between builds,
which is why the limit carries margin rather than sitting on the lane's maximum. Without a
`src.zip` the test **fails when `CI` is set** and is skipped with a loud message locally (a distro
JDK installed without its `-source` package).

**Apache lane only, deliberately.** `:emulators` and `:emulators-printing` take OpenJDK's own
licence, so their convergence with the JDK is not a licence risk and is not measured — the canaries
read five of their files only to prove the instrument still works.

**Rejected:** *keeping `sim.py` in CI* — a Python lane in a Java-only repo, and a gate that would
only run in CI rather than in every `./mvnw install`; *a per-file allow-list of cleared scores* —
the calibrated limit passes today's tree without one, and an allow-list is exactly the escape hatch
an agent reaches for. A future false positive narrows the exclusions (with its reason in
`PROVENANCE.md` § "The exceptions") rather than raising the limit.

<a id="D_no_notice_file"></a>
## D_no_notice_file — no `NOTICE` file; third-party attribution travels as `THIRD-PARTY.md`

**Decided 2026-09-22** (maintainer). The question splits in two, and only one half was optional.

**SB-Emulators publishes no `NOTICE` file.** Apache-2.0 §4(d) binds only *if* the Work includes one,
and four things say not to opt in: **house precedent** — `flow-server-25.2.8.jar`'s `META-INF/`
holds no `NOTICE` (and no `LICENSE` either); **§4(d) propagates into derivative works**, and the
tree built to be copied is exactly the one that would carry it — a migrator `cp -r`s the whole
`guides/` step folder into their own app and ticks there, so a `NOTICE` would hand its
reproduce-our-attributions obligation to the person the permissive lane exists to unburden; **our
own attribution is already per-file**, via [`HDR_vaadin_apache`](../PROVENANCE.md#HDR_vaadin_apache),
which is what Apache's own appendix recommends in place of a `NOTICE`; and **there is nothing
inbound to forward** — `archunit-1.5.0.jar` and `karibu-tools-0.27.jar` carry `META-INF/MANIFEST.MF`
and nothing else.

**Tripwire — this is "we have nothing to put in one", not "we decline to have one".** If
SB-Emulators ever vendors an Apache-2.0 upstream whose *published artifact* carries a `NOTICE`, its
attributions must travel with every distribution, and a `NOTICE` of our own becomes the cleanest way
to carry them.

**The half that was owed regardless of any lane.** The `:migration-tool` dist zip redistributes
third-party jars verbatim (`lib/archunit-*.jar`, Apache-2.0; `lib/slf4j-api-*.jar`, MIT), publishes
to Central as the `dist` classifier, and is unpacked into the kit's `tools/`. Apache-2.0 §4(a) wants
a copy of the License with the redistribution; MIT wants its notice in all copies; neither jar
carries its own text. So the zip ships **`THIRD-PARTY.md` + `licenses/APACHE-2.0.txt`**, gated by
`DistZipIT` (every `lib/` jar not ours must be attributed) and re-checked in the kit by
`KitLayoutIT`. **The name is the point**: it discharges §4(a) and MIT's notice term without
inheriting §4(d)'s propagation semantics, which a file called `NOTICE` would. It extends the pattern
the add-ons set — a third-party tree ships its own licence text rather than being folded into ours.
`licenses/APACHE-2.0.txt` is byte-identical to the root `LICENSE-APACHE-2.0`, which is not
duplication to fix: one covers third-party work, the other ours.

<a id="D_uncaught_handler_chain"></a>
## D_uncaught_handler_chain — a thrown listener reaches the session `ErrorHandler`, and nothing else

**What Swing does, measured** (JetBrains Runtime 25.0.4, 2026-09-16; `EventDispatchThread.processException`
is stock there). A click's whole dispatch — the migrator's `ActionListener` body included — runs inside
one `try` in `EventDispatchThread.pumpOneEventForFilters`, whose `catch (Throwable)` calls
`processException`, which is one line: `getUncaughtExceptionHandler().uncaughtException(this, e)`.
Nothing sets a per-EDT handler by default, so it falls through the `ThreadGroup` to
`Thread.getDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler()` and, with none installed, prints to `System.err`. Three
properties follow, and all three are ours already: **never silent**; **the EDT survives** (the catch is
inside the pump loop, so the next event dispatches normally — the "EDT dies and is recreated" folklore
is pre-JDK-1.3); and **nothing is shown to the user**, which is also what Vaadin's `DefaultErrorHandler`
does.

**`EHelper.callSwing` already is `processException`, and the session `ErrorHandler` already is the EDT's
`UncaughtExceptionHandler`.** Five of our seams route there and are at parity — every peer listener,
`Timer`, `SwingWorker.done()` / `process()` / its `PropertyChangeListener` — all through the UI
fiber's own routing (`UIFibers` hands what a fiber throws to the session's `ErrorHandler`; only a dead
wait ends it quietly, [D_blocking_dialogs_library](#D_blocking_dialogs_library)). Two JDK seams deliberately do *not* reach the handler and we match
that: `SwingWorker.doInBackground()` (captured by the `FutureTask`, surfaced only from `get()`) and
`invokeAndWait` (rethrown to the caller). The `doInBackground` swallow is therefore **faithful and
stays** — reporting it would be an improvement on Swing, which [R_no_silent_improvements](../CLAUDE.md#R_no_silent_improvements)
forbids. The asymmetry argument ("on the desktop `new JLabel(icon)` cannot throw, so the swallow hides
*our* gaps") is correct and its remedy is to stop the emulator throwing where Swing doesn't, not to
unswallow.

**A ported handler behaves as it did on the desktop.** Measured under Karibu: the handler runs with
`SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()` true, `UI.getCurrent()` set and on a parkable virtual thread, so
it can open a modal `JOptionPane`; a throw after a nested modal closes still routes; and partial work
done before the throw stays applied on both the emulator and the peer. One caveat worth knowing:
`DefaultErrorHandler.error` is not a pure logger — it first tries
`ErrorHandlerUtil.handleErrorByRedirectingToErrorView`, which navigates and returns **without logging**
when the app has a `HasErrorParameter` route for exactly that exception class (Swing never navigates),
and it drops `SOCKET_EXCEPTIONS` via `shouldHandle`.

### The emulate / port split

Everything that is one of *our* seams is emulated; every mechanism that reaches outside `vaadinx` for
its wiring is the migrator's to port. Nothing is half-emulated.

| Swing mechanism | Verdict |
|---|---|
| No handler at all | **emulated.** Only divergence is the sink — slf4j ERROR, not `System.err` (R_best_effort_behaviour) |
| `done() { try { get(); } catch … }` | **emulated**, unchanged |
| A handler that opens a dialog / touches the UI | **emulated** — it gets a current UI on a parkable thread |
| `Thread.setDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler(h)` | **migrator ports, by splitting the handler** — below |
| A per-EDT `Thread.currentThread().setUncaughtExceptionHandler(h)` | **migrator ports.** No stable EDT thread here, and `java.lang.Thread` is not ours to hook; today it silently does nothing, hence the new `H_edt_thread_handler` hazard |
| `EventQueue.push(q)` + `dispatchEvent` override | **migrator ports.** Invoking the override faithfully would mean synthesizing `AWTEvent`s our peer listeners never create; `vaadinx.awt.EventQueue.push`/`dispatchEvent` already `onUnimplemented`. The port is mechanical — the body of their `catch` becomes the session `ErrorHandler` |
| `sun.awt.exception.handler` | **migrator deletes.** Removed from the JDK (nothing in JDK 25's `src.zip` mentions it), so it was already doing nothing on their desktop; emulating JDK 6 would be inventing. Hence `H_sun_awt_exception_handler` |

**The split rule for a JVM-wide handler keys on the handler's *body*, not on why it was installed.**
(1) Move everything that touches Swing or the UI into `VaadinSession.setErrorHandler`. (2) Whatever
remains decides the registration: nothing left → delete the call; a UI-free remainder → keep it
registered, since nothing else in the migrated app covers a dying `new Thread()` or library thread.
Step 2 is what answers *"what if it was never a UI error handler?"* without having to recognise the
case — a JVM-wide handler is usually the EDT catch-all (it is *the* supported way to see an EDT throw,
since `sun.awt.exception.handler` was removed in JDK 7), but it can equally have been installed for a
CORBA/JMS reader or a `java.util.Timer`, whose thread dies on an uncaught throwable. Both testapps' handlers are hybrids of exactly this shape:
`crud`'s and `jlawyer-shape`'s `Main.showError` are `printStackTrace()` (step 2 keeps it) plus a
`JOptionPane` hopped onto the EDT (step 1 moves it).

### Why `Thread.getDefaultUncaughtExceptionHandler()` is *not* read back

The tempting one-liner: have `reportUncaught` consult the JVM-wide handler between the session handler
and `DefaultErrorHandler`. It is literally what `ThreadGroup.uncaughtException` does, and `main()`
survives migration (the guide's `S_split_main`), so the handler really is installed. Rejected on three
grounds. **It is dead code for every app that followed the guide** — `S_app_servlet` installs a session
`ErrorHandler` unconditionally, so the session step always wins; the migrator-facing promise "your hook
keeps working" would have been false for exactly the apps that did as they were told. **The one case it
would fire in is the case where firing is wrong** — an app whose JVM-wide handler is UI-free-only and
that installed no session handler has a dying-thread logger, not a UI error handler, and invoking it for
a caught-and-recovered UI error invents behaviour the desktop never had. **And it shrinks the change**:
no injected error reporter in the blocking-dialog runner,
no `instanceof DefaultErrorHandler` discrimination, no lookup order at all. The residual cost is one
case — an app with a JVM handler and no session handler stays silent — mitigated by
`H_uncaught_handler` being grep-complete and by the scaffold installing a session handler anyway.
`UncaughtErrorRoutingTest.jvmWideHandlerIsNotConsulted` pins the negative: without it, someone later
re-adds the read as an obvious improvement and nothing goes red.

**The handler is invoked in two worlds once kept**, which is the hazard the split leaves behind: from a
dying pool thread there is no `UI.getCurrent()`, no session and no lock, so a UI-touching body throws
from inside the uncaught-exception handler. The guide's Phase 4 listing already models the defence
(`if (UI.getCurrent() != null)`), and the hazard's *Fix* names it. The other three "a JVM-wide handler
interferes with the JVM" worries are each gated elsewhere — `System.exit` by the guardrails' JVM-exit
gate, mutable state by the Phase 1 static sweep, and clobbering a container's own default only in a
shared deployment (with Vaadin Boot the app's `main()` owns the JVM).

### `EHelper.reportUncaught`, and the `UiScheduler` guard

**`reportUncaught(session, throwable)`** is the one route to the session's handler. With no lookup order
left it is small, and what it exists for is the lock: `VaadinSession.getErrorHandler()` calls
`checkHasLock()`, which delegates to the session's `SessionLockCheckStrategy` — **`ASSERT` by default,
not `THROW`** — so an unlocked read blows up under `-ea` and passes silently in production. Both are
wrong, so callers holding the lock take the fast path and a lock-less caller is wrapped in
`session.access`. A dying session's report is logged here rather than dropped: unlike
`onSessionLiveUI`'s callbacks, this *is* the error report.

`getErrorHandler()` has exactly two call sites on the UI path and **both already hold the lock**, which
is what keeps the blocking-dialog library out of it: `UIFibers`' report is behaviourally identical to
`reportUncaught`'s fast path (a UI fiber holds the lock whenever it runs) and stays the library's own,
since the library cannot depend on `:emulators`; `JFrame.dispatchShutdownClosing` routes through the
helper.

**A throwing `UiScheduler` task is reported and keeps repeating.** The pool's own contract is the
opposite — a task that throws has its future cancelled and the throwable discarded — which would strand
a repeating `Timer` forever with no log, no handler and nothing to grep for, while a JDK `Timer`
demonstrably keeps firing because the EDT catches and keeps pumping. So every submitted body is wrapped
once: report, then swallow so the repeat survives. `forSession` is private for that reason — a caller
holding the raw executor submits an unguarded body. Two shapes that look equivalent and are not: the
wrap is a `Runnable` decorator, because an `afterExecute` hook sees a periodic task only once it has
already been cancelled; and it sits *outside* whatever the body does, because `Timer`'s reaches
`EHelper.onSessionLiveUI`, which already absorbs `RuntimeException` at DEBUG one level down.

### Out of scope, tracked elsewhere

Three siblings, each its own slice: [D_attach_aware_hop](#D_attach_aware_hop) (landed; its open questions in [`ideas/withpeer-shape.md`](../ideas/withpeer-shape.md)),
[D_modal_from_background](#D_modal_from_background) (landed),
and [D_invoke_from_background](#D_invoke_from_background) (landed) — the last found by this audit,
and a capability bug rather than an error-routing one: `invokeAndWait` could never succeed.

<a id="D_peer_access_chokepoint"></a>
## D_peer_access_chokepoint — one narrow waist between an emulator and its peer, so the off-UI-thread report cannot be forgotten

**The problem is that we cannot see it.** Swing's documented policy forbids touching components off
the event dispatch thread (`javax/swing/package-info.java`: *"All Swing components and related
classes, unless otherwise documented, must be accessed on the event dispatching thread"* — the
pre-1.4 "only once realised" rule was withdrawn around 2004). The JDK enforces none of it: there is
no check in `JComponent` or `java.awt.Component`, the only two methods documented safe off-EDT are
`repaint()` and `revalidate()` (the latter visibly re-dispatching via `invokeLater`), and container
mutation happens to be `synchronized` on the AWT tree lock. So off-EDT access is undefined behaviour
that reliably *appears* to work, and real apps are full of it. [R_tolerate_off_ui_thread](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules)
says we tolerate it; this entry is how we stop tolerating it *silently*.

**`EHelper.checkUIThread()` reports once per JVM**, with a diagnostic `Throwable` so the first
offending call site has a stack. It never throws and changes no behaviour.

**Where it is wired is the whole decision.** Calling it from "every UI method" was the first
proposal and would rot: a 265-class sweep that a new emulator method silently forgets, with no gate
to catch the omission. It hangs off `vaadinx.awt.Component.getPeer()` instead — the one place an
emulator can reach its peer — and `Component.peer` was narrowed from `protected` to **private** so
the waist cannot be stepped around. That narrowing is the bulk of the change: 126 field reads across
49 files, each rewritten at javac's own reported line and column so comments, javadoc and locals
named `peer` stayed untouched. One site was outside `:emulators` entirely — `third-party/jcalendar-1.4`'s
`JDateChooser.picker()` — which is the evidence that a `protected` field here was a live cross-module
seam rather than an implementation detail.

**Over-firing is free and under-firing is the failure**, which is what settles accessor-vs-mutator:
because the report is once per JVM, a read or a piece of internal plumbing tripping it costs
nothing, while a missed write path costs the whole signal. So the check sits on the accessor and not
on a curated list of writes.

Three call sites inside `Component` keep field access on purpose: the **constructor** (construction
off the UI thread is precisely the tolerated case, and the ctor's own peer wiring should not report),
**`toString()`** (logging a component must never itself warn), and `getPeer()`. Everything else in
the class, including `setVisible` / `setForeground` / `setBackground` / `setLocale`, goes through the
accessor — which is why `new JButton()` reports at all: `JComponent.installDefaults()` calls
`setBackground()`, so off-thread *construction* is observed, not only mutation.

**Deliberately not on `EHelper.warnHook`.** That is the stub-WARN channel the per-route
`WarnInventoryTest` exit gates assert on; routing thread hygiene through it would redden a gate for
a property of *the migrator's* code rather than an SB-Emulators gap.

**One answer to "what is the UI thread".** The check defers to
`vaadinx.swing.SwingUtilities.isEventDispatchThread()` — itself `UI.getCurrent() != null` — rather
than re-deriving it, so the emulator and the migrator calling that method themselves cannot get
different answers.

**The shutdown carve-out had to be made lock-safe, and finding out cost a test.** A UI-less teardown
thread is expected (R_callswing_envelope), so the check asks `isShuttingDown()` — but that flag lives
in a session attribute and `VaadinSession`'s default `SessionLockCheckStrategy` **asserts the session
lock on every attribute read**, on exactly the unlocked background threads this exists to observe.
The naive guard failed with `AssertionError: Cannot access state in VaadinSession or UI without
locking the session`. It now asks only when a session is current *and* `hasLock()`; an unlocked
caller reports, which is correct, because it is not in the teardown dispatch.

**Placed on `EHelper`, not as a `protected` member of `Component`.** [R_no_vaadin_in_api](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules)
names `EHelper` as the home for invented API, and a protected method lands in every migrator
subclass's namespace, where a same-named method of theirs becomes an accidental override.

`vaadinx.CheckUIThreadTest` covers it: silent on the UI thread, reports off it, the latch gates the
report and re-arms, shutdown is silent, and a locked session with no UI outside shutdown still
reports. Across the whole suite the warning fires only from that test and from
`WindowTest.setVisibleTrueWithNoCurrentUiThrowsIllegalStateException`, which constructs a no-UI
condition on purpose — no false positives in 277 test classes.

**Cost of the narrowing, stated plainly:** `Component.peer` was a `protected` field a migrator
subclass could read, and it is now private. `getPeer()` remains public and is the sanctioned seam,
so the replacement is one call away; the jcalendar site is what it looks like in practice.

<a id="D_sync_ui_hop"></a>
## D_sync_ui_hop — a Swing→peer write hops to the UI thread synchronously, never via `UI.access()`

**Measured, on `testapps/inventory`.** Save wraps `handleSaveAction()` in a `SwingWorker` (upstream
code — byte-identical in `testapps/inventory/swing/`), whose `doInBackground()` reaches a validator
constructing `new JLabel(imageIcon)`. That threw `IllegalStateException: No currently active UI
found` from three frames below anything SB-Emulators wrote: an `ImageIcon` becomes a Vaadin `Image`,
whose ctor calls `setSrc`, which resolves a `StreamResource` URI, which needs the current UI to build
the URL. The throw was then swallowed by `SwingWorker` ([D_uncaught_handler_chain](#D_uncaught_handler_chain)),
so the journey stopped with no message at all.

**The requirement is latent in Vaadin, not in our source**, so the scope was established by running
it rather than reading it: every `vaadinx` class constructed on a thread with no current UI. All 265
scanned; every one of the 81 with a public no-arg ctor constructed fine. The failures are one family
— resource URIs, whose sole construction-time site in the whole main tree is
`Icons.imageIconToVaadinImage` — plus `setVisible(true)` (the JDK's own realisation boundary, and a
separate slice) and `JComboBox.addItem`, whose JDK-faithful `ItemEvent` reached `EHelper.callSwing`
with no UI — since fixed on the surrogate side,
[SD_background_model_hop](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_background_model_hop). That measurement is what retired
the "defer peer construction until attach" shape: one construction path cannot justify changing peer
lifetime, `getPeer()`'s public seam and the whole bare-peer test corpus.

**`EHelper.runInUIThread(Runnable)` runs the body on the UI thread and returns only once it has
run** — inline when a UI is current, otherwise acquiring the session lock through
`accessSynchronously` and running under the live UI resolved per hop (never captured, so
[D_session_scoped_pools](#D_session_scoped_pools)'s F5 teleport property is untouched).

**Synchronous is the decision, and `UI.access()` is the rejected alternative.** Three reasons, in
order of weight:

- **Sync reproduces a Swing failure mode; async invents a non-Swing one.** An app whose EDT blocks
  waiting on a worker that needs the EDT deadlocks on real Swing too. If blocking deadlocks, the app
  was already broken and we reproduced the JDK. Deferring would *avoid* a deadlock Swing has and pay
  with an execution order Swing never had — the unrequested kindness
  [R_no_silent_improvements](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules) exists to forbid.
- **`access()` never runs inline, even for a caller already holding the lock.** Verified in
  flow-server 25.2.6: `VaadinService.ensureAccessQueuePurged` — *"if the lock is held by the current
  thread, we just release it knowing that the queue gets purged once the lock is ultimately
  released"* — and `UI.access`'s own javadoc, *"`accessSynchronously()` runs the task right away
  whereas `access()` defers the task to a later point in time."* So an async hop would push every
  write past the end of the request, and reorder background writes against inline ones. The orderings
  multiply with the number of hopping threads, and any order-dependent mutation becomes a subtle bug.
- **One contract.** Synchronous makes both branches mean the same thing — *the body has run by the
  time the call returns* — where async would give one method two timings. It also retires the
  idempotency trick considered along the way (having the deferred body re-read the Swing field rather
  than capture the value): that exists only to defuse the inline-beats-queued hazard, which sync does
  not have.
