It is also what this codebase already is: `callSwing` parks a virtual thread and drains
synchronously, `callOnLiveUISync` already does background→UI round-trips for `BridgedPreferences`,
and `SwingWorker.get()` from the EDT already throws (R_match_swing_errors case (1)) to head off the
worst version of this deadlock.

**Take the lock, rather than `callOnLiveUISync`'s queue-and-wait.** Both are "synchronous" and their
failure profiles differ: `accessSynchronously` waits on the `ReentrantLock` and nothing else, while
the queue shape waits for *someone else* to drain it, which additionally needs Push wired or
`MockVaadin.runUIQueue` to purge. The lock wins on the property that motivated choosing sync at all —
a thread parked on a lock names its owner in a thread dump (*"parking to wait for … owned by thread
X"*); one parked on a `CountDownLatch` shows one end and no hint of who should have drained the
queue. It is also reentrant, so a caller already holding the lock runs inline for free.

**Unbounded on purpose.** Bounding it means a hand-rolled `tryLock` plus the current-instance dance
`accessSynchronously` does for us, which is likelier to be wrong than the deadlock is to happen.
Instead a hop that waited ≥1s WARNs with the duration — which also surfaces the realistic cost here,
which is **lock contention, not deadlock**: a worker touching components in a loop ping-pongs the
session lock against the request thread, and that shows up as latency long before anything hangs.
Swing has the same shape in EDT contention, so it should at least be familiar; batching is the escape
hatch if it bites.

**Degrades rather than throws** on the two no-UI paths that remain soft — no live UI (teardown;
DEBUG, since it is routine) and the session invalidated while waiting. The caller has by then stored
its Swing-side state and will still fire its event, so only the *effect* is dropped, per
[R_decline_effect_only](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules). Throwing would be swallowed by `SwingWorker`
anyway. This is the one place it differs from `callOnLiveUISync`, which throws because it is a
value-returning read with nothing sensible to return. The third path — **no `EmulatorContext` at
all** — was soft here too and no longer is; see D_no_context_throws below.

**The hop must hold the lock *and* a current UI — though not necessarily a live one.** Most peer
work needs only the lock, so "take the lock, UI or no UI" looks like a free simplification. The
resource-URI family refutes it: `Image`'s ctor resolves a `StreamResource` URI through
`UI.getCurrentOrThrow`, so a lock-only hop reproduces the inventory stack trace exactly. Measured
2026-09-18 under Karibu, the UI half is weak: `setIcon` succeeds with a closed UI made current by
hand, even one already removed from its session — `getURI` builds a URL string off the UI object
and consults neither liveness nor the session. Only *no* current UI throws. Any widening or
relaxation of the hop keeps both halves.

**Falling back to the `AppTab`'s last-known UI when none is live was rejected, 2026-09-18.** It is
the obvious fix for the drop below, and the measurement above makes it look free. It is not: on
flow-server 25.2.8, `ui.accessSynchronously` works on a UI that is closing but still attached and
throws `UIDetachedException` once it has left the session, so past detach the fallback would mean a
hand-rolled `UI.setCurrent(deadUi)` around Flow's own detach guard. The legal half is
[D_shutdown_lifecycle](#D_shutdown_lifecycle)'s teardown window, where nobody reads the writes and
`isShuttingDown()` exists to do *less* work.

**The reversal — make it throw on *every* no-UI path — was proposed and rejected, 2026-09-18**, and
is recorded so it is not proposed again. Its argument was that if no UI is live then everything the
thread does afterwards is dead work, so no taxonomy of load-bearing-versus-cosmetic peer writes would
ever be needed. Two independent refutations, either sufficient:

- **The premise is false, and its counterexample is the common case.** `label.setText("saving…");
  saveToDatabase();` inside a worker is not dead work once the tab closes — the save is the worker's
  whole point, and on the desktop closing a window does not kill it. An unconditional throw unwinds
  at the first write and the save never happens, so the reversal does not dissolve the taxonomy; it
  resolves it by fiat in the direction that loses data. Nor is the exposed window an edge case: it is
  a browser tab closing on a worker mid-flight, the ordinary end of a user's visit.
- **It does not deliver what it was wanted for.** The case it existed for is a modal `show()` whose
  tab closes while the thread is *already parked* — by then this method has already succeeded and is
  never called again, so no amount of throwing inside it fires; only draining parked waiters on the
  tab-close cascade reaches it. The reversal would have paid the first refutation's price and left
  the hang standing.

**A different axis is decidable, and it is what shipped instead:** not *which peer writes are
cosmetic* — that taxonomy is genuinely unfinishable, and refusing it was right — but **whether the
emulator method is about to block until the browser sends something back.** Usually that is the fact
that the user clicked Yes; it is equally the clipboard's contents, or any other round-trip. What
those share is the failure: **if the browser is gone the interaction can never complete
meaningfully, so the thread stays blocked for ever.** That endless block is the harm. A dialog having
no `int` to return is merely why it cannot be papered over with a default — the symptom, not the
reason.

The calling method always knows the answer, so nothing in the migrator's code needs classifying, and
the members are nameable: every modal show (`Dialog.setVisible(true)`, and so `JOptionPane.show*` /
`JFileChooser.show*` / `JColorChooser.showDialog`) through `Dialog.parkUntilClose`;
`SwingUtilities.invokeAndWait` on its own latch; `WebClipboard.getContents` **and** `setContents`,
both parking on the `executeJs` promise; and `java.util.prefs` through
[D_preferences](#D_preferences)'s `callOnLiveUISync`. **Nameable, not closed** — the clipboard and
prefs members were missed when this was first written and the modal case was the only one in view,
so a new round-trip is added to the list rather than counting against it. And **the list is what the
criterion picks out, not what passes `true` today**: the clipboard and `java.util.prefs` reach the
browser through their own seams, not through `runInUIThread`, so the flag below does not reach them
and they carry their own no-UI answers.

So `runInUIThread` and `vaadinx.awt.Component.withPeerOnLiveUI` take a **mandatory
`callerPlansToBlockAfterwards` flag**: `false` is this entry's degrade-and-carry-on, unchanged;
`true` throws `vaadinx.BrowserSessionClosedError` (an `AWTError`, so a migrated worker's
`catch (Exception e)` does not swallow it) rather than let the caller park on a round-trip that was
dropped. The flag sits on this seam rather than in `parkUntilClose` so that *"did I reach a UI?"* has
one implementation instead of two that can drift. **Nothing passes `true` yet** — the
modal-from-a-background-thread path was unwritten — so this shipped as preparation. Both halves have
since landed in [D_modal_from_background](#D_modal_from_background): the first `true` caller is a
modal show's peer write, the unpark throw covers an interrupted background park, and the
[R_match_swing_errors](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules) case-(8) entry is written.

<a id="D_no_context_throws"></a>
### D_no_context_throws — a peer write from a thread carrying no `EmulatorContext` throws

**Decision.** `runInUIThread`'s first leg — `EmulatorContext.getOrNull()` returns null, so there is
no session to reach a UI through — throws `IllegalStateException` naming the fix
(`EmulatorContext.wrap(executor)`, or `ctx.run(...)` for a hand-rolled `Thread`) instead of WARNing
and dropping the write. R_match_swing_errors case (7).

**Why this leg and not the other two.** The three no-UI conditions look alike at the call site and
are not alike at all:

- **No context** is a *migrator configuration error with a one-line fix at a site the message can
  name* — the same shape as the enumerated cases (3) and (5). It is also **static**: a thread either
  carries a context for its whole life or never does, so the throw is deterministic and shows up on
  the first run rather than intermittently in production.
- **No live UI** is a *race with the user's browser* — they closed the tab. Nothing to fix, and
  throwing on it rests on `AppTab.liveUI()` never being transiently null across an F5 — designed for,
  and since measured (~490k polls, 14 real rebinds, zero transient nulls; see
  [D_modal_from_background](#D_modal_from_background)), which cleared the pre-park check rather than
  this leg.
- **Session invalidated while waiting** is the same, one layer down, and additionally loses data: a
  worker doing `label.setText("saving…"); saveToDatabase();` would unwind at the first write and
  never save, where today it limps through — a divergence from Swing, since closing a desktop window
  does not kill a worker. Carried as a cost to accept until 2026-09-18, when it turned out to be the
  *refutation* of the blanket reversal above rather than its price.

Throwing only the first leg buys the diagnosis without taking on either of the others. **What it does
not buy is what the reversal was wanted for** — a modal `show()` from a background thread still
parks forever when the *tab* is gone, because that is the second leg; the
`callerPlansToBlockAfterwards` seam above is half of the answer and the unpark half is still open.

**Why the old WARN was the wrong shape.** It fired at the *write* and told the reader about the
write; the defect is at the *submit*, in a different file, often a different class. Worse, it
recommended `UI.access(...)` — not a stage-2 migrator's API, and R_no_silent_improvements' wrong
answer besides (D_sync_ui_hop rejects `access()` for this hop). A dropped peer write is also
invisible in the way that matters: the Swing-side state is correct, `getIcon()` returns what was
set, the listener fired, and only the browser disagrees.

**Precondition, and why it now holds.** This is only fair because reaching a context is cheap:
`getOrNull()` synthesises one from any current `VaadinSession` (so every request thread and every
`callSwing` virtual thread has one), `SwingWorker` captures at construction, and since
D_emulator_context_wrap a migrator's own pool needs one line. What is left un-served is a hand-rolled
`Thread`, which is a `ctx.run(...)` away and which R_tolerate_off_ui_thread already treats as
something to report rather than tolerate silently.

<a id="D_submit_site"></a>
**D_submit_site — a contextless submit through a wrapped executor remembers where it was submitted
from.** The throw above names the fix, but not *which* submit needs it — the stack it throws on is
the task's, and the submit is gone from it. `EmulatorContext.capturing(...)` already branches on
exactly the right condition (`ctx == null` is both "this submit will produce a task that throws" and
the branch that otherwise passes through untouched), so six frames are snapshotted there, carried on
a `ThreadLocal` for the task's duration, and appended to the message.

- **`StackWalker` with `limit`, not `new Throwable()`** — the latter walks the whole stack at
  construction where this stops after six. Frames are formatted during the walk because a
  `StackFrame` is only valid inside it. Six is a starting point, not a finding.
- **The message changes shape, not just detail.** With no recorded site the generic advice stands
  ("wrap the pool"). With one, it says the *submitter* had no context either and wrapping the pool
  was not enough — which is the case where the generic advice is actively misleading, because the
  migrator has already done what it asks. That, rather than finding unwrapped pools, is what this
  buys: **an unwrapped executor never reaches our code, so it cannot be seen here at all.**
- **Cost is unmeasured, and the branch is not as narrow as it looks.** A contextless submit is also
  what a legitimately UI-free pool does — a log flusher, a background indexer — forever. A submit
  that *has* a context pays nothing. If the walk ever shows up in a profile, the fallbacks are a
  system property (off by default) or 1-in-N sampling; neither is wired today.
- **The drop-our-own-frames predicate matches exactly, never by prefix.** A `startsWith` on the class
  name also swallows a sibling whose name merely extends ours — caught by `EmulatorContextTest`,
  whose own frames vanished — so it is an equality test plus a `$` nested-class check.
- **`ThreadLocal.remove()`, not `set(null)`, on restore.** A pooled thread that retained a site would
  misattribute a later task's failure to an unrelated earlier submit.

**Blast radius, measured.** `:emulators`' 2124-test suite passes with no change beyond the one test
asserting the old behaviour, and all 13 reactor modules build green. Nothing inside SB-Emulators
reaches `runInUIThread` without a context:
the UI thread returns inline above this leg, and the live-UI hop's only call site then was
`JLabel.setIcon`. The shape that does break is a component built **pre-boot** — in a `static`
initializer or in `main()` before `VaadinBoot.run()` — which the stage-2 static sweep and
`MigrationGuardrails`' no-component-in-a-static-field gate already forbid, so the throw lands on code
that was already out of contract.

**Virtual threads carry no new JDK floor.** `doInBackground` runs on a VT, which unmounts cleanly
parking on a `ReentrantLock`, and since [JEP 491](https://openjdk.org/jeps/491) (JDK 24) even from
inside a `synchronized` block — which this case needs, because the inventory app's `Validator.addTask`
*is* `synchronized`. The project's existing JDK-24 floor already pays for it.

**Call sites go through `vaadinx.awt.Component.withPeerOnLiveUI`, not `runInUIThread` directly**,
and the reason is structural rather than cosmetic: a hop has to wrap the mutation, and an accessor
returns before the mutation happens. A hopping `getPeer()` would take the lock, hand back the peer,
release, and let the caller mutate off-thread anyway. So `getPeer()` can never carry a threading
strategy and `withPeerOnLiveUI` can — reads stay on the accessor, where a hop buys nothing and a deferral is
unimplementable. A body wraps one Swing method's worth of peer work, not one DOM write, or a
three-style setter becomes three lock acquisitions.

**Two call sites at first, deliberately few**, so the cost of a hop stayed observable: `JLabel.setIcon`, and
`Window.applyVisibleToPeer`, forced by [D_modal_from_background](#D_modal_from_background).
In both, state and
`firePropertyChange` stay on the calling thread and only the peer push hops, so the migrator's
listener still fires at their point in their code — R_decline_effect_only's decomposition falling
out of the design rather than being imposed on it. [D_attach_aware_hop](#D_attach_aware_hop) widened
the hop to every peer write; these two sites keep this entry's live-UI hop, now named
`withPeerOnLiveUI`. A pluggable-strategy knob stays parked — *enqueue* is unreachable as a global
setting, because the seam cannot tell which bodies tolerate deferral.

<a id="D_attach_aware_hop"></a>
### D_attach_aware_hop — every emulator peer write hops to the UI that owns the peer's state tree

**Decision.** Every Swing→peer write in `:emulators` goes through
`vaadinx.awt.Component.withPeer(Consumer)` → `SHelper.runOnSession`. That runs the body inline when a
UI is current. Otherwise it takes the lock of the session the component captured, and only then
resolves the UI owning the peer's state tree and makes it current. It runs inline when no session is
known at all, which means the node has never been attached. It is synchronous, needs no
`EmulatorContext`, never drops a write and never throws for the thread it runs on. R_tolerate_off_ui_thread limb 3,
widened from two call sites to the whole surface. Measured on `testapps/inventory`: the Save buttons
run their whole save inside `doInBackground()`, and after the `JLabel` icon hop the next unhopped
write (`Validator`'s `setBackground`) threw Vaadin's lock ISE, which `SwingWorker` swallowed.

**The target is the peer's own UI, not the session's live UI.** `runInUIThread` (D_sync_ui_hop) takes
the session off the thread's context and hops to `AppTab`'s live UI, which is right for its callers.
A plain write is a write to one tree, and the UI to serialise against is the one holding it. This
takes the context requirement off plain writes, so a setter on any component from any thread
behaves the same. With the live-UI hop everywhere, every setter on a *never-attached* component,
called from a thread with no context, would have started throwing (D_no_context_throws): a migrated
app's plain JUnit test building a panel without Karibu, or a component touched in a static
initializer. Those writes need no lock at all, so the throw would have been invented.
[R_match_swing_errors](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules) case (7) keeps covering the live-UI hop's callers.

**A captured session, and nothing read unlocked.** The hop first asked `Component.getUI()`, then the
node's owning `StateTree`. Both are fields the UI thread writes under the lock, so a worker reading
them races an attach and can see a stale "never attached". `Composite.getElement()` even initialises
content lazily. So each component captures its session instead, into a `volatile` field written once
and never changed, since a component never leaves its session:
- at construction, when one is current;
- handed down by an emulator from its `EmulatorContext` (an emulator built in `doInBackground()`
  builds its surrogate there, where no session is current);
- at first attach, which runs on the UI thread.

Each surrogate root declares a private `hopSession` field, which `SHelper.sessionOf` reads by
reflection. `vaadinx.awt.Component` keeps its own copy, because a bare `Div` / `Span` peer has
nowhere to store one. Only under that session's lock is the node's owning tree read, so a peer
detached after attach, which Flow still guards, is resolved correctly: a disposed `JInternalFrame`
failed every setter while reporting itself detached. And an F5 `@PreserveOnRefresh` teleport, which
moves the tree to a new UI in the same session, resolves to whichever UI holds it now. A final UI
captured at construction would have gone stale at the first F5. Attach listeners fire after the node
joins the tree, so a component that learned no session at construction could be written inline while
its attach was in flight. `withPeer` therefore falls back to the writing thread's own context
session. The residue is a write from a thread with no context, to a component built with no session,
during its first attach — thread-unsafe code racing, as R_tolerate_off_ui_thread's last limb says.
Gated by `SessionCaptureTest` and `ModelCallbackHopMarkerTest` in `:surrogates`, and by
`PeerSessionTest` here.

**Two seams, chosen per body.** `withPeer` for a plain write, and `withPeerOnLiveUI(boolean, …)`, the
D_sync_ui_hop hop, for a body that needs a current UI even while its peer is detached. That second
kind is anything that resolves a resource URL (an `ImageIcon` becoming a Vaadin `Image`:
`JLabel.setIcon`, `AbstractButton.setIcon`, `JTabbedPane`'s tab icons) or shows an overlay
(`JInternalFrame.setVisible` / `setIcon`, and `Window.applyVisibleToPeer`, which calls
`runInUIThread` directly). Model-driven pushes hop surrogate-side instead, per
[SD_background_model_hop](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_background_model_hop), so a worker mutating
the model directly is covered too — but only inside the model callback, never in a surrogate setter
(`ModelCallbackHopMarkerTest`), so every setter hop is the emulator's. The emulator bridges such an
event reaches use `EHelper.relayModelEvent`, and so does the caret bridge, since a caret setter
hopped through `withPeer` fires its `CaretListener`s inside the hop.

**What stays outside the body** is R_decline_effect_only's split: Swing-side state,
`firePropertyChange`, `fire*` events, model mutations and user-listener fan-out run on the calling
thread; only the push hops. A body wraps one Swing method's worth of peer work; nested hops are
inline.

**Gate.** `vaadinx.OffUiThreadWriteTest` is reflective and allow-list-free, in the manner of
`R12ProvenanceTest`. It attaches every public concrete non-window emulator with a no-arg constructor,
calls every public one-argument setter whose argument type has a sample, twice with different values,
from a context-carrying background thread, and fails on Vaadin's unlocked-access assertion and on a
`callSwing` no-UI echo. It found 85 setters on its first run. Windows are not swept, since showing one
leaves the session in a state the next attach cannot reuse. Reads are not wrapped at all: getters stop
reading the peer instead ([D_emulator_owned_state](#D_emulator_owned_state)). The shape questions this
left open are in [`ideas/withpeer-shape.md`](../ideas/withpeer-shape.md).


<a id="D_emulator_owned_state"></a>
### D_emulator_owned_state — emulators own their state: no getter reads the peer

**Decision.** An emulator holds the state its JDK class holds and runs the JDK's bodies over it; the surrogate renders it. Five rules:

1. **A getter answers from emulator-owned state and never reads the peer.** Owned state is the JDK model the emulator holds (shared with the surrogate or not, below), or a Swing-side field under the JDK's name. So a getter works on any thread, with no hop, no lock and no browser context.
2. **The event engine lives where the JDK puts it.** For `BoundedRangeModel` / `SpinnerModel` that is the model's own fan-out, and the emulator's listener subscribes to the model, as the JDK's `setModel` does. For `JComboBox` and `JTree` it is the component, so the JDK bodies are ported (`contentsChanged` / `selectedItemChanged`, `setExpandedState` / `TreeModelHandler`). Either way the emulator does not relay the surrogate's fan-out; the surrogate keeps its own listener lists for stage-3 code, and events fire on the mutating thread, outside the surrogate's hop, as on the desktop.
3. **The surrogate never observes the emulator.** It listens to a JDK model it is given and receives scalar state through `withPeer` pushes ([D_attach_aware_hop](#D_attach_aware_hop)), some of them through a render-only setter added for the purpose (`SChoice` / `SList.setItemsAndSelection`, `renderSelection` on text components).
4. **Browser → Swing: where the JDK routes a user gesture through a public method, the browser event calls that method**, inside `EHelper.callSwing`, rather than writing the field — a JTree toggle runs `expandPath`, so `TreeWillExpandListener` can veto; a color pick runs `getSelectionModel().setSelectedColor`, as a desktop chooser panel does. State only the browser moves, with no JDK method behind it, is mirrored from a synchronized peer property (`JComboBox.isPopupVisible` ← `opened` — not through `setPopupVisible`, since a desktop mouse open calls `BasicComboPopup.show()` directly and the browser cannot tell a click from a key), or, with no such property, from a held debounced report ([D_emulator_caret](#D_emulator_caret)).
5. **Swing → peer is a flush of current state, not a replay of calls.** The push reads the fields inside the `withPeer` body, so racing writers leave the peer on the last state; a peer write that cannot run yet is skipped and an attach listener flushes instead.

**Rationale.** A getter reading the peer needs a UI, a lock or a browser round-trip, and a migrated app calls getters from its own threads — `JDateChooser.getDate()` in a `SwingWorker` reached `BrowserTimeZone` and threw, the measured failure that started this. Hopping reads onto the UI thread was the first proposal and is rejected: a lock per read, and still no answer on a thread with no context. Owning the state removes the read seam entirely, puts programmatic notifications on the caller's thread before any hop ([R_decline_effect_only](../CLAUDE.md#hard-rules)), and is the precondition for rendering the surrogates late and in batches ([ideas/vaadin-ui-thread-only.md](../ideas/vaadin-ui-thread-only.md)). It supersedes [D_surrogate_first](#D_surrogate_first)'s end state, an emulator "thinned down" to a delegating shell; the surrogate-first *ordering* stands. Porting the bodies also proved the most productive audit the emulators have had: every component converted had a delegation hiding divergences from the JDK — invented surface, dropped exceptions, notifications fired or skipped, constructor call graphs — each recorded in its own entry.

**Status: every emulator.** A source scan of every public or protected `get*` / `is*` / `has*` method under `vaadinx/` finds none reaching `surrogate()` / `getPeer()` outside a `withPeer` body (2026-09-29). The components converted, each with what its bodies restored: [D_jcombobox](#D_jcombobox), [D_jtree_row_path_bridge](#D_jtree_row_path_bridge), JSlider / JSpinner / JProgressBar ([SD_background_model_hop](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_background_model_hop) § *Emulator side*), `JDateChooser` (the jcalendar add-on), [D_jlist](#D_jlist), [D_jtable_thin_shell](#D_jtable_thin_shell), [D_jtabbedpane](#D_jtabbedpane), `JTextArea` / `JPasswordField` ([SD_sjtextarea](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjtextarea), [SD_sjpasswordfield](../surrogates/decisions.md#SD_sjpasswordfield)), [D_emulator_caret](#D_emulator_caret), [D_jtoolbar](#D_jtoolbar), [D_jseparator](#D_jseparator), [D_awt_label](#D_awt_label), [D_awt_scrollbar](#D_awt_scrollbar), [D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice), [D_awt_list](#D_awt_list), [D_dialog_state](#D_dialog_state), [D_jcolorchooser](#D_jcolorchooser), [D_setpage_fetch](#D_setpage_fetch).

**Applying it to a new emulator.**
1. **Read the JDK source** for every method touched (`$JAVA_HOME/lib/src.zip`), the Basic L&F's too where behaviour is observable through it. Note where state lives, where events fire, in which order.
2. **Measure the JDK** on what the tests will pin: a headless script (`java -Djava.awt.headless=true Probe.java`) printing events and getters, under `xvfb-run -a` for AWT widgets, which refuse a headless JVM. Every component measured so far had an existing test asserting a divergence.
3. **Diff the emulator's public and protected methods against the JDK class** before porting: delegation hides invented surface (`JComboBox.addListDataListener`, `JColorChooser.addChangeListener`), and the fix is removal.
4. **Port the bodies** under the JDK's field names and protected hooks, reached from the JDK's call sites (R_no_vaadin_in_api limb 2) — constructors included.
5. **Tests:** a replayed JDK script asserting the measured output verbatim; an entry in `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest` (reads the getters on a bare thread and asserts `checkUIThread`'s latch stays unarmed); browser state driven the way the browser drives it (Karibu's `_setValue` / `_clickItem`; `TreeGrid`'s protected `expand(Collection, boolean userOriginated)` works reflectively), with `UIFibers.isInUIFiber()` or a `JOptionPane` park inside a listener; the `*BackgroundModelTest` pair where a model is shared.
6. **Clean full-reactor build** — it runs Sampler's WARN gates and rebuilds every testapp stage, which subclass these components; both caught regressions no emulator test did.

**Traps, each hit once.**
- **Sharing a model with the surrogate.** The surrogate writes a browser change into a shared model through its inline `SHelper.callSwing`, which starts no UI fiber. The emulator's own model listener must then wrap its fan-out in `EHelper.relayModelEvent`, or a listener opening a modal cannot park (`JComboBoxTest.browserPickRunsInAUiFiber`). Where the JDK's listeners sit on the model itself, or where the surrogate writes the model on its own (`SJTabbedPane` shifts its selection on every insert), relaying cannot help: keep the emulator's model, flush into the surrogate's private one, and run the browser change as the JDK's model write inside `callSwing` ([D_jtabbedpane](#D_jtabbedpane), [D_jcolorchooser](#D_jcolorchooser)). Components still sharing are listed in [ideas/withpeer-shape.md](../ideas/withpeer-shape.md) § 3 (h).
- **Surrogate state scoped to its own fan-out does not survive a park.** A Grid click stash is restored when the surrogate's synchronous dispatch returns — exactly when a handler parks on a dialog. Read it inside the surrogate's dispatch and hold it on the emulator for the whole `callSwing` body ([D_jlist](#D_jlist)).
- **The JDK pushes to its peer inside `synchronized (this)`; this layer must not.** An off-thread push takes the session lock while a request thread holding it may wait on the same monitor. Write under the monitor, flush after it is released; where JDK mutators nest, only the outermost flushes ([D_awt_choice](#D_awt_choice)).
- **The JDK sometimes keeps state in its own peer.** `java.awt.List` reads its platform peer once displayable, by different rules; measure both branches and port the peer's rules too ([D_awt_list](#D_awt_list)).
- **Part of the observable behaviour is the L&F's.** `JToolBar.Separator`'s size, `JColorChooser`'s five default panels, `JList`'s selection shift: every desktop L&F inherits them from Basic, so they are reproduced, and the code says whose they are.
- **Constructors are call graphs.** Where the JDK constructor assigns a field, an emulator constructor calling the public setter is a divergence a subclass override observes; replay constructors with a subclass logging into a static list, since the super constructor runs first ([D_dialog_state](#D_dialog_state)).
- **Listener order.** The JDK notifies last to first almost everywhere; the delegating shells iterated forwards.
- **A JDK hook reached only from a listener this layer cannot afford** (a mouse or focus listener costs a round trip per event): decline the hook in `R12DeadHookTest`'s `DECLINED_TARGET` with the reason, and feed the state through the public methods that listener would have called ([D_emulator_caret](#D_emulator_caret)).
- **WARN stubs on the JDK's call graph.** `EventQueue.getCurrentEvent()` and `Component.getWidth()` are stubs; a ported body calling one trips every Sampler WARN gate. Skip the call with a comment.
- **The surface gates pair nested classes by name**, so a private inner class named like the JDK's (`JTabbedPane$Page`) is held to the JDK one's constants; a rename needs a clean build, since the gates scan class files.
- **`-pl emulators` resolves `:surrogates` from `~/.m2`**, which a parallel checkout can overwrite; build `-pl surrogates,emulators` while iterating.

**Accepted limitation.** A browser toggle cannot be vetoed before it renders, so a vetoed `JTree` toggle flickers. The structural gate that would replace the source scan and `EmulatorOwnedStateTest`'s per-component list is open ([ideas/withpeer-shape.md](../ideas/withpeer-shape.md) § 4).

**Validation.** `vaadinx.EmulatorOwnedStateTest` (a bare-thread read per converted component), and each component's replayed JDK script, cited in its entry.

<a id="D_modal_from_background"></a>
### D_modal_from_background — a modal dialog shown from a background thread shows, blocks and returns

**Decision.** `vaadinx.awt.Dialog.setVisible(true)` on a modal dialog works from a background thread
carrying an `EmulatorContext` — a `SwingWorker.doInBackground()`, or any executor wrapped per
D_emulator_context_wrap — instead of throwing. The dialog renders, the calling thread blocks, the
user's answer comes back out of the call. Real Swing apps do this constantly (a worker hits a problem
and puts a `JOptionPane` in front of the user), and R_tolerate_off_ui_thread's first limb forbids
making the off-thread-ness itself fatal.

**Three steps, and the same three on both threads:** show the peer on the UI thread; block *outside*
that hop on the modal latch; hide on the UI thread. **Step 2 is one line, `latch.await()`, already
correct on both threads**, because what it does depends on the caller. On the UI thread the caller is
a loom VT whose carrier is the request thread holding the session lock, so awaiting unmounts the
carrier, the lock goes and the response flushes (D_callswing_loom). On a background thread the caller
holds nothing, so awaiting simply blocks it while the request threads stay free to deliver the click.
There is no second waiting mechanism to build; only the entry conditions differ.

**This is the desktop's own shape**, read 2026-09-17 from `java.awt.Dialog.show()` and
`WaitDispatchSupport.enter()` in JDK 25's `src.zip`. `show()` runs `conditionalShow` first, so the
dialog is on screen, and only then enters the secondary loop; `enter()` branches on the calling
thread, and for a non-EDT caller it posts the pump to the EDT and blocks the caller alone on
`getTreeLock().wait()`. So real Swing blocks **exactly one** thread — the caller — and the EDT keeps
pumping. Vaadin's request threads play the EDT's part.

**The hop sits on `Window.applyVisibleToPeer`, not around `Window.show()`, and the difference is
R_decline_effect_only.** Wrapping the whole `show()` was written first and was wrong: when no UI is
reachable the hop drops its body, and that took the `visible` field write and the
`COMPONENT_SHOWN` / `WINDOW_OPENED` fan-out with it — the migrator's listener silently not firing,
which is the exact failure shape that rule exists to name. `Component.show()` already decomposes the
way the rule wants (`visible = true` → `applyVisibleToPeer(true)` → `fireComponentEvent`), so the hop
belongs on the middle line alone. Caught by a test asserting a *non-modal* background show still
keeps `isVisible()` true with the effect dropped. `applyVisibleToPeer` is now `final` and subclasses
override `applyVisibleToPeerImpl` (JFrame's strategy hook), so the hop and the `preventPeerEvents`
envelope cannot be bypassed by an override that forgets `super`.

**That siting widens the hop from one call site to two, which is forced rather than chosen.**
`runInUIThread` was reached only from `JLabel.setIcon` before this, deliberately, so the cost of a hop
could be observed at one site; `Window.applyVisibleToPeer` is shared by `Frame` / `JFrame` /
`JWindow` / `Dialog`, so every window's show and hide comes along. Hopping only when
`blocksAfterVisibilityChange` is true would avoid that at the price of one method meaning two things
on the same line. Nor was widening itself the risk: `live.accessSynchronously` always makes a UI
current, which is all [D_sync_ui_hop](#D_sync_ui_hop)'s resource-URI family needs, so a widened hop
cannot reproduce the icon stack trace.

**One observable consequence, caught by a test that had encoded the old behaviour.**
`Frame.setVisible(true)` with no current UI used to throw `IllegalStateException` — "nowhere to attach
the Dialog". It now takes the session off the `EmulatorContext` and lands on the app's live UI,
because "no current UI" is exactly the condition identifying a background caller and nothing
distinguishes it from a UI thread that cleared its own. R_tolerate_off_ui_thread limb 3 working as
intended; the carve-out survives where it is still true, since a thread carrying **no session at
all** still throws `IllegalStateException` (D_no_context_throws). `WindowTest` pins both halves.

**`blocksAfterVisibilityChange(b)` is how the seam learns a park follows** — `b && isModal()` on
`Dialog`, `false` everywhere else — feeding `callerPlansToBlockAfterwards` (D_sync_ui_hop). Without
it, a show whose effect was dropped for want of a live UI would be followed immediately by a park on
a latch nothing can ever count down: an indefinite hang, which is what the enumerated-case throw
exists to prevent, rather than a degradation. R_match_swing_errors **case (8)**.

**The UI-fiber check moves from the entry to the UI-thread branch.** It was the guard that
rejected this whole case, but it is still right for a *UI-thread* caller: one outside a UI fiber (route
entry, attach listener) would block the platform request thread and nothing could deliver the close. A
background caller has no such constraint, and reaches its session through `EmulatorContext` rather
than through `UI.getCurrent()`.

**The background park skips the UI fiber's rebind** (`Q_rebind_skip`) — it waits on a plain
`future.get()`, never through `awaitModal`. The rebind exists so a
chained dialog lands on the right UI across an F5; on a worker it would *install* a current UI that
`EmulatorContext` deliberately withholds, silencing `checkUIThread()`'s off-EDT WARN for the rest of
`doInBackground` and making every later peer write look like legitimate UI-thread access while
holding no lock.

**An interrupted park throws, on the background path only.** Returning normally is indistinguishable
from the user dismissing the dialog — `JOptionPane` would report `CLOSED_OPTION` — and "the user
declined" and "nobody will ever answer" are different facts, the second of which has the worker
running on against a browser that is gone. The wake-up already existed and was being swallowed:
session destroy → the session-scoped pool's `shutdownNow()` → `InterruptedException` → a `catch` that
re-set the flag and returned. So the work was stopping the swallow, not adding a mechanism.
`worker.cancel(true)` arrives identically and the message covers both readings, since the answer is
the same. **On the UI thread a dead wait throws the same `BrowserSessionClosedError`**, woken by its anchor's
detach at a tab close or session destroy ([D_blocking_dialogs_library](#D_blocking_dialogs_library)),
and `callSwing` ends the fiber quietly at its root — there is no caller left to tell, which is why
`ModalBlockingProbeTest`, which deliberately leaves two modals parked, reports nothing at teardown.
`DeadModalWaitTest` pins both deaths.

**The F5 precondition was measured before the throw was enabled**, since the pre-park check rests on
`AppTab.liveUI()` never being transiently null mid-refresh — if it could be, a modal from a worker
would throw on an app that was merely reloading. Probe: a background thread polling `liveUI()` under
the session lock at ~1 ms while real Firefox reloaded Sampler, 2026-09-18. **~490k polls, 14 real
rebinds, zero transient nulls.** The control matters as much as the signal, because without one
"zero nulls" is indistinguishable from a blind probe: Playwright's `page.close()` fires no unload
beacon and produced nothing, but navigating a page to `about:blank` made the same probe report a null
window that stayed null for 93,686 polls with no UIs left in the session. A refresh and a tab close
are opposite observations, not two shades of one.

**What is not claimed.** The thread-safety of the migrator's own app is unchanged
(R_tolerate_off_ui_thread's last limb): the Swing-side state writes still happen on the caller's
thread, unsynchronised, so two threads mutating one dialog still race exactly as they would on the
desktop. The promise is only that the peer write lands on the UI thread and that the park has a
browser that can answer it.

**Left open, deliberately:**

- **Widening beyond window visibility** landed separately as
  [D_attach_aware_hop](#D_attach_aware_hop), and Family B — a Swing→peer write whose peer event
  re-enters `callSwing` — as SD_background_model_hop's relay.

**Not open, though it was carried as a question until it was read back:** a second browser tab does
not complicate this. `singleLiveUI` **never throws and never guesses** — it returns the `AppTab`'s UI
or null — because the one-app-per-session invariant is enforced at *attach*, where a second tab gets
`MainWindowRoute`'s curtain and never becomes the `AppTab` (D_active_ui_pointer). So a worker's modal
always lands on the app's tab, which is the only tab running the app.
